> यदि । स्तोतारः । शतं । यत् । सहस्रं । गृणंति । गिर्वणसं । शं । तत् । अस्मै ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमिंद्रं धीतयः कर्माणि परिचरणानि न हिंसंति न बाधंते। वाणीर्वाण्यः
> स्तुतयश्च यं न बाधंते । दातुमसमर्थः पुरुषोऽन्यकृतैः परिचरणैः स्तुतिभिश्च
> भृशं खिद्यतेऽस्य चंद्रस्य बहुधनत्वादात्तृत्वाच्च तस्मिन्प्रयुज्यमानानि परिचरणानि
> स्तोत्राणि च बाधहेतवो नाभूवन्नित्यर्थः । किं तर्हित्यत आह । तमिंद्रं वर्धयंतीर्वर्धयंतोऽभि नक्षंति । अभिगच्छंति । अपि च गिर्वणसं गिरां संभक्तारमिंद्रं
> शतं शतसंख्याकाः स्तोतारो यदि गृणंति स्तुवंति । यद्यदि च सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याकाः स्तोतारः स्तुवंति तत्सर्वं स्तोत्रमस्मा इंद्राय शं सुखकरं भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra whom the dhītayaḥ, that is, rites and services, do not harm, do not oppress; and whom the vāṇīḥ, the words, the praises, do not oppress. A man who is unable to give is greatly distressed by services and praises made by others. But because of this Indra's abundance of wealth and his being a giver, the services and hymns offered to him do not become causes of distress. What then? Making that Indra grow, they reach him (अभि नक्षंति (*abhi nakṣaṃti*), they go to him). Moreover, if a hundred singers praise Gīrvaṇas, the sharer of praises (गिर्वणसं (*girvaṇasaṃ*)), and if a thousand singers praise him, all that praise is शं (*śaṃ*), that is, productive of happiness, for this Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं इंद्रं (*yaṃ iṃdraṃ*)—the Indra whom
- धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*)—the acts of worship
- न हिंसंति (*na hiṃsaṃti*)—do not harm
- वाणीः (*vāṇīḥ*)—the words of praise
- न (*na*)—do not harm
- वर्धयंतीः (*vardhayaṃtīḥ*)—making him grow
- अभि नक्षंति (*abhi nakṣaṃti*)—go and reach
- गिर्वणिसं (*girvaṇisaṃ*)—towards Indra, who is worthy of worship through praise
- शतं स्तोतारः (*śataṃ stotāraḥ*)—hundreds of singers
- यदि गृणंति (*yadi gṛṇaṃti*)—if they offer praise and extol
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—thousands of singers
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever praise they offer
- तत् (*tat*)—all that
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to Indra
- शं (*śaṃ*)—is productive of happiness

### Printed p. 42

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Whichever Indra neither the acts of worship nor the words of praise harm, going to that Indra and making him grow, all those praises reach him. The hundreds and thousands of praisers who extol that Indra and offer him praises of many kinds, all those praises are productive of happiness for that Indra.

##### English translation
All praises contributing to his exaltation proceed to Indra, whom no acts, no words can harm, since hundreds and thousands of adorers glorify him who is entitled to praise, and so afford him gratification.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्मै॑ ए॒तद्दि॒व्य१॒ं॑ र्च्छेव॑ मा॒सा मि॑मि॒क्ष इंद्रे॒ न्य॑यामि॒  ॑
> सोमः ।  
> जनं॒ न धन्व॑न्न॒भि सं यदापः॑ स॒त्रा वा॑वृधु॒र्हव॑नानि य॒ज्ञैः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्मै । एतत् । दिवि । अर्चा इव । मासा । मिमिक्षः । इंद्रे । नि । अयामि । सोमः ।  
> जनं । न । धन्वन् । अभि । सं । यत् । आपः । सत्रा । ववृधुः । हवनानि । यज्ञैः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एतदेतस्मिन्निवि दिवसे सौत्येऽहन्यर्चेवार्चनसाधनेन स्तोत्रेणेव मासा
> मानेनेंद्राय त्वा वृत्रघ्न इत्यादिमंत्रसाध्येन युक्तो मिमिषो वसतीवर्येकधनाख्याभिरद्भिरासिक्तः सोमोऽस्मै ॥ विभक्ति व्यत्ययः ॥ अस्मिन्निंद्रे न्ययामि ।
> नियतोऽभूत् । यद्वा । अस्मा इंद्रायैतत्तोत्रं ब्रवाणीति शेषः । दिवि
> द्युलोकेऽर्चेवार्कः सूर्य इव मासा । लुप्तोपममेतत् । माति परिच्छिन्नत्तीति
> मासश्चंद्रमाः । स इव मिमिषो वृष्ट्युदकानां सेक्ता य इंद्रो वर्ततेऽस्मिन्निंद्रेऽभिषुतः सोमो नियम्यते स्म । किंच तमिंद्रं यज्ञैर्यजनसाधनैः
> पुरोडाशादिभिर्हविर्भिः सार्धं हवनानि स्तोत्राणि सत्रा सह नावृधुः । अवर्धयन् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"On this day", that is, on the day of the pressing of Soma, अर्चेव (*arceva*), as if with a hymn that is the instrument of worship, मासा (*māsā*), with a measure, that is, joined with a mantra to be accomplished by the words beginning "Indrāya tvā vṛtraghne", the Soma, sprinkled with the waters called vasatīvarī and ekadhanā, is held fast in this Indra (a change of case is to be understood: अस्मै (*asmai*) for "in this"). Or else the meaning is: "To this Indra I would speak this hymn", the words "I would speak" being supplied. Another explanation: दिवि (*divi*), in the heavenly world, अर्चेव (*arceva*), like the sun; मासा (*māsā*) (the elliptical simile), the moon, which measures; like him, the sprinkler of rain and waters, who is Indra, in this Indra the pressed Soma is held fast. Moreover, the hymns together with the oblations, the puroḍāśa cakes and the rest, which are the means of sacrifice, made that Indra grow together.

### Printed p. 43

> तत्र दृष्टांतः । धन्वन्धन्वनि मरुदेशेऽभि अभिमुखं सं यत् सम्यग्यत्यो गच्छंत्य
> आपो जनं प्राणिनमिव । यथा मरुदेश उपलभ्यमाना आपः प्राणिनं वर्धयंति
> तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here is the illustration. धन्वन् (*dhanvan*), in a desert land, अभि (*abhi*), towards a man, the waters flowing together well, as a living being is, that is, as waters found in a desert land make a living being grow, so (the hymns make Indra grow).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अर्चेव (*arceva*)—like a hymn that is the instrument of worship
- मासा (*māsā*)—joined with a meditative mantra **NOTE**
- मिमिक्षः (*mimikṣaḥ*)—that which is joined with the vasatīvarī waters
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the Soma
- अस्मै इंद्रे (*asmai iṃdre*)—in this Indra
- एतत् दिवि (*etat divi*)—this day
- न्ययामि (*nyayāmi*)—is offered
- धन्वन् (*dhanvan*)—in a sandy desert
- अभि (*abhi*)—before the traveller
- सं यत् (*saṃ yat*)—flowing together
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the water
- जनं न (*janaṃ na*)—as it gladdens him
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—joined with oblations, the means of sacrifice
- हवनानि (*havanāni*)—the hymns
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—together
- यत् (*yat*)—that same Indra
- वावृधुः (*vāvṛdhuḥ*)—made to grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma, which is joined with a meditative mantra like a hymn that is the instrument of worship, and with the vasatīvarī waters, is offered today in this Indra. As the water flowing before a traveller in a sandy desert gladdens him, the hymns joined with oblations, the means of sacrifice, gathering together, made that Indra grow.

##### English translation
The mixed Soma juice has been prepared for Indra, (to be offered) on the day (of sacrifice), with reverence-like adoration, when praises, together with offerings, yield him increase, as when water (revives) a man in a desert waste.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्मा॑ ए॒तन्मह्यां॑गू॒षम॑स्मा॒ इंद्रा॑य स्तो॒त्रं म॒तिभि॑रवाचि ।  
> अस॒द्यथा॑ मह॒ति वृ॑त्र॒तूर्य॒ इंद्रो॑ वि॒श्वायु॑रवि॒ता वृ॒धश्च॑ ॥

> अस्मै । एतत् । महि । अंगूषं । अस्मै । इंद्राय । स्तोत्रं । मतिभिः । अवाचि ।  
> आसत् । यथा । महति । वृत्रतूर्ये । इंद्रः । विश्वआयुः । अविता । वृधः । च ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 44

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मा इंद्राय महि महदेतदांगूषं स्तोत्रं मतिभिः स्तोतृभिरवाचि ।
> उक्तमभूत् । अस्मा इंद्राय स्तोत्रमिति पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था । विश्वायुः सर्वत्र
> गंता स इंद्रो महति प्रभूते वृत्रतूर्ये संग्रामे यथा येन प्रकारेणास्माकमविता रक्षको वृधो वर्धयिता चासत् भवेत् तथावाचीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To this Indra this great (महि (*mahi*)) āṅgūṣa hymn has been spoken (अवाचि (*avāci*)) by the minds, that is, by the singers. The repetition "to this Indra the hymn" is for the sake of reverence. May that Indra, who goes everywhere (विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)), in the great, abundant vṛtratūrya, the battle, be our protector and the one who makes us grow, in such a manner (यथा (*yathā*)) was the hymn spoken: this is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)—going everywhere
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- महति (*mahati*)—in the great
- वृत्रतूरै (*vṛtratūrai*)—in the battle
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever manner
- अविता (*avitā*)—our protector
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—the one who makes us grow
- असत् (*asat*)—may he be (for that reason)
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—addressed to this Indra
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- एतत् आंगूषं (*etat āṃgūṣaṃ*)—this hymn
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—by the singers
- अवाचि (*avāci*)—has been recited
- अस्मा (*asmā*)—for this (Indra)
- स्तोत्रं (*stotraṃ*)—the hymn has been recited

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Because Indra, who goes everywhere, is our protector and the one who makes us grow in the great battle, this great hymn has been recited by the praisers, addressed to this Indra.

##### English translation
To this Indra has this earnest eulogy been addressed by the devout, in order that the all-pervading Indra may be our defender and exalter in the great conflict with (our) foes.

## Sūkta 35 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कदा भुवन्निति पंचर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं नरस्त्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । कथा
> चानुक्रांतं । कदा नरस्त्विति ॥ तृतीये छंदोमे महाव्रते च निष्केवल्य
> उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning कदा भुवन् (*kadā bhuvan*) has five Ṛks and is the twelfth sūkta. Its seer is Nara, in the Ārṣa (seer's) account; the metre is Triṣṭubh and the deity is Indra. So it is also listed in the Anukramaṇī: "Kadā naras tu". Its use is stated for the third Chandoma day and for the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya recitation.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "Kadā bhuvan", is the twelfth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nara, born in the family of Bharadvāja; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā: "कदा नरस्तु (*kadā narastu*)", thus

### Printed p. 45

has been said. It was said earlier that this sūkta is used for the third Chandoma mantras, and, in the Mahāvrata sacrifice, for the mantras of the Niṣkevalya śastra.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 35
- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 35
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 7; Varga 7
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: Nara
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क॒दा भु॑व॒न्रथ॑क्षयाणि॒ ब्रह्म॑ क॒दा स्तो॒त्रे स॑हस्रपो॒ष्यं॑ दाः।  
> क॒दा स्तोमं॑ वासयोऽस्य रा॒या क॒दा धियः॑ करसि॒  ॑
> वाजरत्नाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कदा । भुवन् । रथक्षयाणि । ब्रह्म । कदा । स्तोत्रे । सहस्रपोष्यं । दाः ।  
> कदा । स्तोमं । वासयः । अस्य । राया । कदा । धियः । करसि । वाज्ररत्नाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ब्रह्म ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राण्यस्मदीयानि रथक्षयाणि रथनिवासानि कदा
> कस्मिन्काले भुवन् । भवेयुः । रथेवस्थितं त्वां कदा प्राप्नुवंतीत्यर्थः । कदा
> कस्मिन्काले स्तोत्रे स्तुवते मह्यं सहस्रपोष्यं सहस्रसंख्याकपुरुषपोषकं
> गोसमूहं पुत्रं वा दाः । कदा चास्य मम स्तोतुः स्तोमं स्तोत्रं राया
> धनेन वासयः । व्यापयेः । धियः कर्माणि चाग्निहोत्रादीनि वाजरत्ना
> वाजैरन्नॆ रमणीयाः कदा कस्मिन्काले करसि कुर्याः । एवं स्तोता फलस्य
> विलंबमसहमान इंद्रमनया पृष्टवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when will our hymns (ब्रह्म (*brahma*), that is, our praises), which have the chariot for their dwelling (रथक्षयाणि (*rathakṣayāṇi*)), come to be? The meaning is: when will they reach you as you stand on the chariot? When will you give me, who praise you, the सहस्रपोष्यं (*sahasrapoṣyaṃ*), that is, a herd of cattle or a son that nourishes a thousand persons? When will you make this hymn of mine, the singer's, pervade (वासयः (*vāsayaḥ*)) with wealth? And when will you make my rites, such as the agnihotra and the rest (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)), delightful with food (वाजरत्नाः (*vājaratnāḥ*), delightful with vāja, that is, with food)? Thus the singer, unable to bear the delay of the fruit, asked Indra with this Ṛk.

### Printed p. 46

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—our hymns (O Indra)
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- रथक्षयाणि (*rathakṣayāṇi*)—as dwelling in your chariot (with you)
- भुवन् (*bhuvan*)—will they be?
- कदा (*kadā*)—at what time
- स्तोत्रे (*stotre*)—to me, the praiser
- सहस्रपोष्यं (*sahasrapoṣyaṃ*)—wealth that nourishes thousands of people
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—will you give?
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- अस्य (*asya*)—of me, the singer
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the hymn
- राया (*rāyā*)—with wealth
- वासयः (*vāsayaḥ*)—will you make it fruitful?
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—our rites
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- वाजरत्नाः (*vājaratnāḥ*)—delightful with food
- करसि (*karasi*)—will you make?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when will our hymns reach you, who stand on the chariot? When will you give to me, the singer, wealth that nourishes thousands of people? When will you make the praise of me, the singer, fruitful with wealth? When will you make our rites delightful with food?

##### English translation
When may our prayers (be with you) in your chariot? when will you grant to your adorer the i(means of) maintaining thousands? when will you recompense my adoration with riches? when will you render sacred rites productive of food?

### Printed p. 47

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> फलस्य विलंबमसहमान ऋषिरनयापींद्रं पृच्छति । हे इंद्र कर्हि स्वित्कदा
> खलु तद्ववेत् । नृभिरस्मदीयैः पुरुषैन्रन् शत्रुपुरुषान् तथा वीरैरस्मदीयैः
> पुत्रैर्वीराना शत्रुपुत्रांश्च यन्नीळयासे त्वं संश्लेषयेः संयोजयेः ॥
> नीळयतिः संश्लेषणकर्मा ॥ ईदृशं युद्दे यत्संश्लेषणं तत्कदा भवेदिति वितर्कः ।
> अपि चास्मदर्थं त्वमाजीन् संग्रामान् कदा जय । जयेः । कदा च गोष्टभिगंतृषु शत्रुषु विद्यमानास्त्रिधातु त्रिधातूनां क्षीरदधिघृतानां त्रयाणां
> धारयित्रिर्गा अधि जयासि । अधिकं जयेः । हे इंद्र त्वं स्वर्वत् व्याप्तिमत्
> द्युम्नं धनमस्मे अस्मासु कदा धेहि । धारयेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, unable to bear the delay of the fruit, asks Indra with this Ṛk also. O Indra, "when indeed" (कर्हि स्वित् (*karhi svit*)) would that be, that you bring together (नीळयासे (*nīḷayāse*)) with our men the enemy men, and with our heroes, that is, our sons, the enemy heroes and sons? The root नीळयतिः (*nīḷayatiḥ*) has the sense of joining. Such a joining in battle, when would it be? so runs the question. Moreover, when will you win the battles for us? And when will you win in addition (अधि जयासि (*adhi jayāsi*)) the cattle that are found among the enemies who approach the cow-pen, cattle that bear the three threefold products (त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*): milk, curds and ghee)? O Indra, when will you place among us pervading (स्वर्वत् (*svarvat*)) wealth (द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*), that is, riches)?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—with our men
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—(bringing face to face) the enemy men
- वीरैः (*vīraiḥ*)—with our heroic sons
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—(bringing face to face) the enemy heroes
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever effort for battle there is
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- कर्हि स्मित् (*karhi smit*)—when indeed
- नीळयासे (*nīḷayāse*)—will you bring about?
- आजीन् (*ājīn*)—the battles
- जय (*jaya*)—will you make us win?
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—among the opposing enemies
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—having the substance of milk and the rest
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cattle
- अधि जयिसि (*adhi jayisi*)—will you win for us?
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- स्वर्वत् (*svarvat*)—all-pervading
- द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*)—wealth
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—will you establish?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when will you bring our heroic men together with the enemy heroes and make ready for battle? And when, causing the effort for battle to be made, will you bring us victory? When will you win for us and bring the cattle that are among the enemies who oppose us, cattle that have the three substances beginning with milk? O Indra, when will you establish all-pervading wealth in us?

##### English translation
When, Indra, will you bring together leaders with leaders, heroes with heroes, and give us victory in battles? when will you conquer from the enemy the threefold food-supplying cattle? (when will you grant) us, Indra, diffusive wealth?

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कर्हि॑ स्वि॒त्तदिं॑द्र॒ यज्ज॑रि॒त्रे वि॒श्वप्सु॒ ब्रह्म॑ कृ॒णवः॑ शविष्ठ ।  
> क॒दा धियो॒ न नि॒युतो॑ युवासे क॒दा गोम॑घा॒ हव॑नानिगच्छाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कर्हि । स्वित् । तत् । इंद्र । यत् । जरित्रे । विश्वप्सु । ब्रह्म । कृणवः । शविष्ठ ॥  
> तदा । धियः । न । नियुतः । युवासे । कदा । गोऽमघा । हवनानि । गच्छाः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयापि कतिचित् प्रश्नाः क्रियंते । हे इंद्र कर्हि स्वित्कदा खलु तद्भवेत् ।
> हे शविष्ठ बलवत्तमेंद्र त्वं जरित्रे स्तोत्रे विश्वप्सु बहुविधरूपं ब्रह्मान्नं कृणवः
> करोषीति यत् तत्कदा भवेदिति वितर्कः । कदा च धियः कर्माणि । नेति समुच्चये ।
> नियुतः स्तुतीश्च युवासे । आत्मनि योजयेः । कदा च त्वं गोमघा गोमघानि
> गवां दातृणि । मंहतेर्दानार्थस्य रूपमुत्तरपदं ॥ हवनानि स्तोत्राणि गच्छाः ।
> अभिगच्छेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk also some questions are put. O Indra, when indeed would that be? O Śaviṣṭha, most mighty Indra, that you make (कृणवः (*kṛṇavaḥ*)) for the singer, the praiser, food (ब्रह्म (*brahma*)) of many forms (विश्वप्सु (*viśvapsu*)): when would that be? so runs the question. And when will you join (युवासे (*yuvāse*)) to yourself our rites (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)) and the praises (नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)), the word न (*na*) being in the sense of combination? And when will you approach (गच्छाः (*gacchāḥ*)) our hymns (हवनानि (*havanāni*)), which are givers of cattle (गोमघा (*gomaghā*))? The word मघा (*maghā*) is a form of the root meaning "to give", standing as the last member of the compound. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शविष्ठ (*śaviṣṭha*)—O powerful one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- जरित्रे (*jaritre*)—for the praiser
- विश्वप्सु (*viśvapsu*)—of many kinds
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—food
- कृणवः (*kṛṇavaḥ*)—that you will make
- यत् (*yat*)—which matter is famed
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- कर्हि स्मित् (*karhi smit*)—when indeed (will you bring about)
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—our rites
- न (*na*)—and
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—the praises
- युवासे (*yuvāse*)—will you unite to yourself?
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- हवनानि (*havanāni*)—our hymns
- गोमघा (*gomaghā*)—fruitful with riches
- गच्छाः (*gacchāḥ*)—will you make?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mighty Indra, the matter that is famed, that you make for him who praises you a wealth of food of many forms: when will you bring it about? When will you unite our rites and our praises in yourself? When will you make our hymns fruitful with the gift of wealth?

When most vigorous Indra, will you grant your worshipper that food which is all-sufficing ? whea will you combine (in yourself) worship and praises ? when will you render oblations productive of cattle ?

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स गोम॑घा जरि॒त्रे अश्व॑श्चंद्रा॒ वाज॑श्रवसो॒ अधि॑ धेहि॒ पृक्षः॑।  
> पी॒पि॒हीषः॑ सु॒दुघा॑मिंद्र धे॒नुं भ॒रद्वा॑जेषु सु॒रुचो॑  
> रुरुच्याः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । गोमघाः । जरित्रे । अश्वचंद्राः । वाजश्रवसः । अधि । धेहि । पृक्षः ।  
> पीपिहि । इषः । सुदुघां । इंद्र । धेनुं । भरत्वाजेषु । सुरुचः । रुरुच्याः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स त्वं जरित्रे स्तोत्रे गोमघा गवां दात्रीरश्वश्चंद्रा अश्वैराह्लादयंतीर्वाजश्रवसो वाजैर्बलैः प्रसिद्धा एवंभूताः पृक्षोऽन्नानि भरद्वाजेषु
> भरद्वाजपुत्रेष्वस्मास्वधि धेहि । धारय । तथेषस्तान्यन्नानि सुदुघां शोभनदोग्ध्रीं
> धेनुं गां च हे इंद्र पीपिहि । प्यायय । आपि च ता इषो गौश्च सुरुचः
> शोभनदीप्तयो यथा भवंति तथा त्वं रुरुच्याः । दीपयेः । शोभनदीप्तियुक्ताश्च ताः संत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you, for the singer, the praiser, place (धेहि (*dhehi*), bestow) in us, the sons of Bharadvāja, foods (पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*)) that are givers of cattle (गोमघा (*gomaghā*)), delighting with horses (अश्वश्चंद्रा (*aśvaścaṃdrā*)) and famed for strength (वाजश्रवसः (*vājaśravasaḥ*)). And, O Indra, nourish (पीपिहि (*pīpihi*), make swell) those foods and the cow, the well-milking one (सुदुघां धेनुं (*sudughāṃ dhenuṃ*)). And make them shine (रुरुच्याः (*rurucyāḥ*)) in such a way that they become of beautiful radiance (सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*)): the meaning is, let them be endowed with beautiful radiance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः (*saḥ*)—you (O Indra)
- जरित्रे (*jaritre*)—for the praiser
- गोमघाः (*gomaghāḥ*)—those that furnish wealth of cattle
- अश्वश्चंद्राः (*aśvaścaṃdrāḥ*)—those delightful with horses
- वाजश्रवसः (*vājaśravasaḥ*)—those famed for strength
- पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*)—the foods
- भरद्वाजेषु (*bharadvājeṣu*)—in us, the sons of Bharadvāja
- अधि धेहि (*adhi dhehi*)—fill
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—those foods
- सुदुघां धेनुं (*sudughāṃ dhenuṃ*)—the cows that are excellent milkers
- पीपिहि (*pīpihi*)—make thrive
- सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*)—so that they shine exceedingly
- रुरुच्याः (*rurucyāḥ*)—make them radiant

### Printed p. 50

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, fill in us, the sons of Bharadvāja, for the singer, the foods that furnish wealth of cattle, are delightful with horses and are famed for strength. O Indra, make those foods and the cows that are excellent milkers thrive. Make them radiant, so that they shine exceedingly.

##### English translation
Grant Indra, to your adorer (abundant) food, productive of cattle, pleasant with horses, and renowned for vigour: multiply nourishment, and (cherish) the cows easily milked, and render them so that they may be resplendent.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमा नू॒नं वृ॒जन॑म॒न्यथा॑ च॒च्चूरो॒ यच्छ॑क्र॒ वि दुरो॑  ॒
> गृणी॒षे ।  
> मा निर॑रं शुक्र॒दुघ॑स्य धे॒नोरां॑गिर॒सान्ब्रह्म॑णा विप्र  
> जिन्व ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । आ । नूनं । वृजनं । अन्यथा । चित् । शूरः । यत् । शक्र । वि । दुरः । गृणीषे ।  
> मा । निः । अरं । शुक्रदुघस्य । धेनोः । अंगिरसान् । ब्रह्मणा । विप्र । जिन्व ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं नूनमद्यतनं वृजनं बाधकमस्मदीयं शत्रुमन्यथा चिदन्येनैव प्रकारेण योजय । येन प्रकारेण सर्वॆ जीवंति तद्विलक्षणं प्रकारं
> मरणाख्यं प्रापयेत्यर्थः । आकारः पूरकः । हे शक्र सर्वकार्येषु शक्तेंद्र कूरः
> शौर्यपेतो वि दुरो विशेषेण दारयिता शत्रूणां । यद्वा । दुरो द्वाराणि
> शत्रुसंबंधीनि वि घटयंस्तं यद्यस्मादृणीषे अस्माभिः स्तूयसे तस्मात्कारणात्
> शुक्रदुघस्य शुक्राणां निर्मलानां दोग्धुरिंद्रस्य धेनोर्वाचः स्तोत्रान्मा निररं ।
> मा निर्गच्छेयं । यद्वा । शुक्रस्य पयसो दोग्धा धेनोस्त्वया दत्ताया

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you now (नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)) bring our present obstructing enemy (वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)) to a different (अन्यथा (*anyathā*)) manner: that is, to a manner unlike that in which all live, the one called death. The syllable आ (*ā*) is a filler. O Śakra, Indra, capable in all works, brave and endowed with heroism, tearing the enemies apart in an especial manner (वि दुरः (*vi duraḥ*)). Or else: breaking open the doors belonging to the enemy. Since you are praised (गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)) by us, for that reason may I not go away (मा निररं (*mā niraraṃ*)) from the hymn, the speech, the cow of Indra, the milker of the pure and spotless (शुक्रदुघस्य (*śukradughasya*)). Or else: the milker of the pure milk, of the cow given by you.

### Printed p. 51

> गोः सकाशान्मा निर्गच्छेयं ॥ अरमित्याख्यातमृ गतावित्यस्य रूपं ॥ सा सर्वदास्मासु निवसत्त्व्यर्थः । हे विप्र प्राज्ञेंद्र आंगिरसानंगिरोगोत्रजानस्मान् ब्रह्मणान्नेन जिन्व । प्रीणय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(So that) I may not depart from the vicinity of the cow. The word "aram" is a verb, a form of the root meaning "to go". The meaning is: may she always dwell among us. O Vipra, wise Indra, gratify (जिन्व (*jinva*), that is, please) with food (ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)) us, the Āṅgirasas, those born in the lineage of Aṅgiras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूनं (*sūnaṃ*)—that which is of this time
- तं वृजनं (*taṃ vṛjanaṃ*)—that enemy
- अन्यथा चित् आ (*anyathā cit ā*)—make him one whose attention is elsewhere, or make him dead
- शक्र (*śakra*)—O almighty Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—mighty
- विदुरः (*viduraḥ*)—and destroyer of enemies, you are (therefore)
- गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)—you are praised (therefore indeed)
- शुक्रमघस्य (*śukramaghasya*)—of Indra, whose wealth is pure
- धेनोः (*dhenoḥ*)—by praise (I)
- मा निररं (*mā niraraṃ*)—may I not become averse
- विप्र (*vipra*)—O wise Indra
- अंगिरसान् (*aṃgirasān*)—us, who are born in the lineage of Aṅgiras
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—joining with food
- जिन्व (*jinva*)—satisfy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, turn the enemies who are present at this time of the sacrifice in another direction. O almighty Indra, for whatever reason you are mighty and the destroyer of enemies, for that very reason you are praised. For that reason, may I not become averse to the praise of Indra, whose wealth is pure. O wise Indra, make us, who are born in the lineage of Aṅgiras, rich in food, and satisfy us.

##### English translation
Direct him who is actually our adversary into a different (course): mighty Indra, you are a hero, the destroyer (of enemies). therefore are you glorified : never may I desist from the praise of the giver of pure (gifts): satisfy ; sage Indra, the Angirasas with food.

## Sūkta 36 (Maṇḍala 6)
**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्रा मदास इति पंचर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं नरस्त्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमृंद्रं ।
> सत्रेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ पृष्टस्य पंचमेऽहनि निष्केवल्य एतत्सूक्तं शस्यं । सूत्रितं च ।
> प्रेदं ब्रह्मेंद्रो मदाय सत्रा मदास इति निष्केवल्यं ॥ आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥ विश्वजिति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning सत्रा मदासः (*satrā madāsaḥ*) has five Ṛks and is the thirteenth sūkta. Its seer is Nara, in the Ārṣa (seer's) account; the metre is Triṣṭubh and the deity is Indra. It is listed in the Anukramaṇī as "सत्र (*satra*)". Its use: on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya (rite) this sūkta is to be recited in the Niṣkevalya. It is also taught in the sūtra: "प्रेदं (*predaṃ*) …", the Niṣkevalya (Ā. Sū. 7-12). In the Viśvajit (rite), (the passage continues below).

### Printed p. 52

> माध्यंदिनसवने प्रशास्तुः शस्त्र इदं सामसूक्ताख्यं शंसनीयं । सूत्रितं च । सत्रा
> मदासो यो जात एवाभूरेक इति सामसूक्तानि । आ. ८-७ । इति । महाव्रतेऽपि
> निष्केवल्य उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the midday pressing, in the śastra of the Praśāstṛ priest, this sūkta, which is called a Sāma-sūkta, is to be recited. It is also taught in the sūtra: "सत्रा मदासो यो जात एवाभूरेक इति सामसूक्तानि (*satrā madāso yo jāta evābhūreka iti sāmasūktāni*)" (Ā. Sū. 8-7). In the Mahāvrata also its use in the Niṣkevalya is stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Satrā madāsaḥ" is the thirteenth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nara; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said to begin with "Satrā". That this sūkta is used for the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭha sacrifice is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra प्रेदं ब्रह्मेंद्रो मदाय सत्रा मदास इति निष्केवल्यं (*predaṃ brahmeṃdro madāya satrā madāsa iti niṣkevalyaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-12). That in the śastra mantras that the priest called Praśāstṛ recites at the midday pressing of the Viśvajit iṣṭi this sūkta is to be recited as a Sāma-sūkta is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra सत्रा मदासो यो जात एवाभूरेक इति सामसूक्तानि (*satrā madāso yo jāta evābhūreka iti sāmasūktāni*) (Ā. Sū. 8-7). It was said before that this sūkta is used for the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras in the Mahāvrata also.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 36
- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 36
- Ṛṣi: Nara
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒त्रा मदा॑स॒स्तव॑ वि॒श्वज॑न्याः स॒त्रा रायोऽध॒ ये पार्थि॑वासः ।  
> स॒त्रा वाजा॑नामभवो विभ॒क्ता यद्दे॒वेषु॑ धा॒रय॑था  ॒॑
> असुर्यं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्रा । मदासः । तव । विश्वजन्याः । सत्रा । रायः । अध । ये । पार्थिवासः ।  
> सत्रा । वाजानां । अभवः । विभक्ता । यत् । देवेषु । धारयथाः । असुर्यं । १॥

### Printed p. 53

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तव त्वदीया मदासः सोमपानजनिता मदाः सत्रा । सत्यनामैतत् ।
> सत्यं विश्वजन्याः सर्वजनहिता भवंति । यद्वा। सत्रेति महन्नाम । महांतस्तव मदा
> इति योज्यं । अधापि च पार्थिवासः पृथिव्युपलक्षिते लोकत्रये भवास्त्वदीया
> ये रायो धनसमूहाः संति तेऽपि सत्रा सत्यं विश्वजनहिता भवंतीत्यन्वयः । किं
> च त्वं वाजानामन्नानां सत्रा सत्यं विभक्ता दाताभवः । भवसि । यद्वा। सत्रा महतां
> वाजानामिति योज्यं । यद्यस्मात्त्वं देवेषु मध्येऽसुर्यं बलं धारयथा
> अतः कारणात्त्वमेवं करोषीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, your intoxications (मदासः (*madāsaḥ*)) produced by the drinking of Soma are सत्रा (*satrā*), which is a name for "truth": truly they are beneficial to all people (विश्वजन्याः (*viśvajanyāḥ*)). Or else: सत्रा (*satrā*) is a name for "great", and the construction is "your intoxications are great". Moreover, the riches (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)), the masses of wealth that are yours and are पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*), that is, found in the three worlds designated by the earth, they too truly are beneficial to all people: this is the construction. Further, you truly are (अभवः (*abhavaḥ*), you become) the distributor (विभक्ता (*vibhaktā*)), the giver, of foods (वाजानां (*vājānāṃ*)). Or else the construction is "of great foods". Since you hold strength (असुर्यं (*asuryaṃ*)) among the gods, for that reason you act so: this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तव (*tava*)—your
- मदासः (*madāsaḥ*)—the satisfactions born of drinking Soma
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—truly
- विश्वजन्याः (*viśvajanyāḥ*)—are beneficial to all people
- अध (*adha*)—and
- पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*)—those that are in the three worlds
- ये रायः (*ye rāyaḥ*)—whatever riches of yours there are (those also)
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—truly beneficial to the world
- यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness of yours
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- असुरं (*asuraṃ*)—strength
- धारयथाः (*dhārayathāḥ*)—you hold (for that very reason)
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—truly
- वाजानां (*vājānāṃ*)—of foods
- विभक्ता अभवः (*vibhaktā abhavaḥ*)—you become the distributor

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the satisfaction born of your drinking of Soma brings benefit to the whole world. Your riches, spread through the three worlds, are truly beneficial to the world. By that greatness of yours by which you hold strength among the gods, for that very reason you are truly the distributor of foods.

##### English translation
Truly are your exhilarations beneficial to all men: truly are the riches which exist on earth (beneficial to all men): truly are you the distributor of food ; therefore you maintain vigour amongst the gods.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अनु॒ प्र ये॑जे॒ जन॒ ओजो॑ अस्य स॒त्रा द॑धिरे॒ अनु॑ वी॒र्या॑य।  
> स्यू॒म॒गृभे॒ दुध॒येऽर्व॑ते च॒ क्रतुं॑ वृंजं॒त्यपि॑ वृत्र॒हत्ये॑ ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 54

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनु । प्र । येजे । जनः । ओजः । अस्य । सत्रा । दधिरे । अनु । वीर्याय ।  
> सूम्यगृभे । दुधये। अर्वते । च । क्रतुं । वृंजंति । अपि । वृत्रहत्ये ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रसौजो बलं जनो यजमानोऽनु प्र येजे । संततं प्रकर्षण
> यजते । पूजयति । अपि च तमिंद्रं वीर्याय वीरकर्म कर्तुं सत्रा सत्यमनु
> दधिरे । पुरोदधिरे यजमानाः । यद्वा । सत्रा महांतमिंद्रमिति योज्यं । अपि
> च सूमगृभे सूम्नः सूतानविच्छेदेन वर्तमानान् शत्रून् गृह्णते दुधये ।
> दुधिर्हिंसाकर्मा । तेषां हिंसकायार्वते शत्रूणामभिगंत्रे च तस्मा इंद्राय
> क्रतुं कर्म परिचरणात्मकं वृंजंति । निष्पादयंति । किमर्थं । वृत्रहत्ये वृत्रस्य
> वारकस्य शत्रोर्हनननिमित्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The worshipper (जनः (*janaḥ*)), the sacrificer, continually and eminently worships (अनु प्र येजे (*anu pra yeje*)) the strength (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)) of this Indra. Moreover, the sacrificers truly place him before them (अनु दधिरे (*anu dadhire*)) in order to perform a heroic deed. Or else the construction is "the great Indra". And further, to him who seizes (सूमगृभे (*sūmagṛbhe*)) the enemies that go on without interruption, to the destroyer (दुधये (*dudhaye*); the root has the sense of harming: दुधिर्हिंसाकर्मा (*dudhirhiṃsākarmā*)) of them, and to the one who goes against the enemies (अर्वते (*arvate*)), to that Indra they perform (वृंजंति (*vṛṃjaṃti*), accomplish) the rite (क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)) consisting of service. For what purpose? For the slaying (वृत्रहत्ये (*vṛtrahatye*)) of Vṛtra, the obstructing enemy. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of Indra
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—the strength
- जनः (*janaḥ*)—the sacrificer
- अनु प्र येजे (*anu pra yeje*)—worships always
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—for the performance of heroic deeds
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—truly
- अनु दधिरे (*anu dadhire*)—they worship, setting him as the model
- सूमगृभे (*sūmagṛbhe*)—who seizes the enemies that come in succession
- दुधये (*dudhaye*)—the harmer of enemies
- अर्वते (*arvate*)—the one who defeats the enemies; (addressing) that Indra
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—the rite of worship
- वृत्रहत्ये (*vṛtrahatye*)—for the destruction of enemies
- वृंजंति (*vṛṃjaṃti*)—they accomplish (perform)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer always worships the strength of Indra. The sacrificers, in order to perform heroic deeds, worship Indra truly, setting him as the model. They offer worship to that Indra, who takes captive the enemies that press on without a break, who harms the enemies and defeats the enemies, for the destruction of the enemies.

##### English translation
The worshipper praises especially the strength of that Indra, verily they rely upon him for heroic deeds: they offer sacrifices to him as the seizer of an uninterrupted series of foes their assailant, their subduer, and also for their destruction.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं स॒ध्रि ची॑रू॒तयो॒ वृष्ण्या॑नि॒ पौंस्या॑नि नि॒युतः॑ सश्चु॒रिंद्रं॑।  
> स॒मु॒द्रं न सिंध॑व उ॒क्षशु॑ष्मा उरु॒व्यच॑सं॒ गिर॒ आ वि॑शंति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । सध्रीचीः । ऊतयः । वृष्ण्यानि । पौंस्यानि । नियुतः । सश्चुः । इंद्रं ।  
> समुद्रं । न । सिंधवः । उक्तशुष्माः । उरुव्यचसं । गिरः । आ । विशंति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तमिंद्रमूतये मरुतः सध्रीचीः सहांचंत्यः संगता भूत्वा सश्चुः ।
> सचंते । सेवंते । यद्वा । ऊतयस्तर्पकाण्यन्नानि सह वर्तमानानि भूत्वा सेवंते ।
> तथा वृष्ण्यानि वीर्याणि पौंस्यानि बलानि च नियुतो रथे युज्यमाना वडवाश्च
> तमिंद्रं सेवंते । अपि चोक्षशुष्माः । उक्तं शस्त्रं । तदेव बलं यासां तादृशा
> गिरः स्तुतयश्चोरुव्यचसं विस्तीर्णव्याप्तिकं तमिंद्रमा विशंति । प्रविशंति । तत्र
> दृष्टांतः । समुद्रं न सिंधवः । यथा स्यंदनशीला नद्यः समुद्रमाविशंत्याविश्य च
> विभक्ततया न दृश्यंते एवं सर्वा आपि स्तुतय इंद्रेणैकीभवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra the Maruts, moving together (सध्रीचीः (*sadhrīcīḥ*)), that is, assembled, attend (सश्चुः (*saścuḥ*), serve) for his protection. Or else: the ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*), the satisfying foods, being together, serve him. Likewise the virile powers (वृष्ण्यानि (*vṛṣṇyāni*)) and strengths (पौंस्यानि (*pauṃsyāni*)), and the mares (नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)) yoked to the chariot, serve that Indra. Moreover the praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) whose strength is the recitation (उक्षशुष्मा (*ukṣaśuṣmā*): उक्तं (*uktaṃ*) is the śastra, and that itself is their strength) enter (आ विशंति (*ā viśaṃti*)) that Indra, who is of wide extent (उरुव्यचसं (*uruvyacasaṃ*)). Here is an illustration: as rivers (सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)), which are flowing by nature, enter the ocean (समुद्रं न (*samudraṃ na*)) and, having entered, are no longer seen as distinct, so all the praises become one with Indra: this is the meaning.
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सध्रीचीः (*sadhrīcīḥ*)—the companions of Indra
- ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*)—the Maruts
- वृष्ट्यानि (*vṛṣṭyāni*)—the virile powers
- पौंस्यानि (*pauṃsyāni*)—the strengths
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—the horses of Indra
- तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*)—that same Indra
- सच्चुः (*saccuḥ*)—serve together
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—the rivers
- समुद्रं न (*samudraṃ na*)—as they go and join the ocean
- उक्तशुष्माः (*uktaśuṣmāḥ*)—the recited mantras full of strength
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises
- उरुव्यचसं (*uruvyacasaṃ*)—Indra, who pervades widely
- आ विशंति (*ā viśaṃti*)—go and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, the companions of Indra, the virile powers, the strengths and the horses of Indra serve Indra together. As rivers enter the ocean, the recited mantras full of strength and the praises go and join the widely pervading Indra.

### Printed p. 56

##### English translation
The associated Maruts, heroic energies, virile strength, and the Niyut steeds, attend upon Indra, and praises powerful in sacred song centre in him as rivers flow into the ocean.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स रा॒यस्सामुप॑ सृजा गृणा॒नः पु॑रुश्चं॒द्रस्य॒ त्वमिं॑द्र॒ वस्वः॑ ।  
> पति॑र्बभू॒थास॑मो॒ जना॑ना॒मेको॒ विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य॒ राजा॑ ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । रायः । खां । उप । सृज । गृणानः । पुरुचंद्रस्य । त्वं । इंद्र । वस्वः ।  
> पतिः । बभूथ । असमः । जनानां । एकः । विश्वस्य । भुवनस्य । राजा ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र गृणानः स्तूयमानः स त्वं रायो धनस्य खां । नदीनामैतत् ।
> अत्र तत्संबद्धा धारा लक्ष्यते । धारामुप सृज । विमुंच । अस्माभिः संयोजयेत्यर्थः । कीदृशस्य धनस्य । पुरुश्चंद्रस्य बहूनामाह्लादकस्य वस्वो निवासकस्य ।
> आपि चासमोऽनुपमः सर्वोतृष्टस्त्वं जनानां सर्वेषां प्राणिनां पतिरधिपतिर्बभूथ । तथा विश्वस्य सर्वस्य भुवनस्य भूतजातस्यैकोऽसाधारणो राजेश्वरश्च
> बभूविथ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)), of wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) the खां (*khāṃ*): खा (*khā*) is a name for rivers, and here the stream connected with it is meant. उप सृज (*upa sṛja*): release the stream, join it with us. Of what kind of wealth? पुरुश्चंद्रस्य (*puruścaṃdrasya*), which gladdens many, and वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*), which gives dwelling. Moreover you, incomparable (असमः (*asamaḥ*)) and supreme, have become the lord, the overlord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)), of all people, all beings (जनानां (*janānāṃ*)); and likewise of the whole world (विश्वस्य भुवनस्य (*viśvasya bhuvanasya*)), of all that is born, you have become the one, the unique, king and ruler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—who are praised
- सः त्वं (*saḥ tvaṃ*)—that same you
- पुरुश्चंद्रस्य (*puruścaṃdrasya*)—which gives joy to many
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—and is the cause of dwelling
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- खां (*khāṃ*)—the stream in the form of a flood
- उप सृज (*upa sṛja*)—cause to flow
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- असमः (*asamaḥ*)—as the one without a second
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—of beings
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—as lord
- बभूथ (*babhūtha*)—you have become
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all
- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—of the whole creation
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the unique
- राजा (*rājā*)—you have become the ruler

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are praised by all, cause to flow the stream, in the form of a flood, of wealth that gives joy to many and is the cause of dwelling. You, the one without a second

### Printed p. 57

and lord of creatures. You are the sole master of the whole of created beings.

##### English translation
Glorified by us. Indra, let flow the stream of much-delighting, home-conferring affluence, for you are the unequalled lord of men, the sole sovereign of all the world.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स तु श्रु॑धि॒ श्रुत्या॒ यो दु॑वो॒युद्यार्न भूमा॒भि रायो॑  ॒
> अर्यः ।  
> असो॒ यथा॑ नः॒ शव॑सा चका॒नो यु॒गेयु॑गे॒ वय॑सा॒ चेकि॑तानः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । तु । श्रुधि । श्रुत्या । यः । दुवःयुति । द्यौः । न । भूम । अभि । रायः । अर्यः।  
> असः । यथा । नः । शवसा । चकानः । युगेऽयुगे । वयसा । चेकितानः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र श्रुत्या श्रुत्यानि शोतव्यानि स्तोत्राणि तु क्षिप्रं श्रुधि ! शृणु ।
> यस्त्वं दुवोयुरस्मदीयं परिचरणमात्मन इच्छन् अर्योरेः संबंधीनि
> रायो धनानि भूम बहुतराणि द्यौर्न सूर्य इवाभि भवसि स त्वं श्रुधीत्यन्वयः ।
> अपि च शवसात्मीयेन बलेन स्तोतव्येन युक्तश्चकानः स्तूयमानो युगे युगे
> काले काले वयसा हनिर्लक्षणेनान्नेन चेकितानः प्रज्ञायमानस्त्वं यथा येन
> प्रकारेण नोऽस्माकमसाधारणोऽसि तथासः । स्याः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, listen quickly to the praises that are fit to be heard (श्रुत्या (*śrutyā*) is explained as श्रुत्यानि शोतव्यानि (*śrutyāni śotavyāni*), praises to be heard); you who, desiring our service, overcome like the sun the abundant riches belonging to the enemy, be that one and hear." The construction is: you who do so, listen. Further: you, endowed with your own strength and being praised, and made known age after age by the offered food, the oblation; as you are not common but peculiarly ours, so may you be. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—O Indra, you who
- दुवोयुः (*duvoyuḥ*)—desiring our acts of worship
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—of the enemy
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—the riches
- भूम (*bhūma*)—abundantly
- द्यौर्न (*dyaurna*)—like the sun
- अभि (*abhi*)—seize
- सः (*saḥ*)—such a you
- श्रुत्या (*śrutyā*)—our praises
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—as one endowed with strength
- चकानः (*cakānaḥ*)—and praised by us
- युगे युगे (*yuge yuge*)—in all times
- वयसा (*vayasā*)—by the food in the form of the oblation
- चेकितानः (*cekitānaḥ*)—and made known by us
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever way
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- असः (*asaḥ*)—be favourable; be in that way

### Printed p. 58

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who, desiring our acts of worship, seize abundantly the riches of the enemy like the sun, listen quickly to our praises. Being endowed with strength, praised by us, and made known by us at all times through food in the form of the oblation, be in whatever way is favourable to us.

##### English translation
Hear, Indra, (the praises) that may be heard (by you), who, are gratified by our adoration, and, like the sun, (prevail) over the ample riches of the enemy : endowed with strength, being glorified in every age rendered comprehensible by (sacrificial) food, be to us no other (than such as you have been.)

## Sūkta 37 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आर्वाग्रथमिति पंचर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमृंद्रं।
> आर्वाग्रथमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning आर्वाग्रथमिति (*ārvāgrathamiti*) has five Ṛks and is the fourteenth sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja (Ārṣa), its metre is Triṣṭubh, and its deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇī records it with the words आर्वाग्रथमित्यनुक्रांतं (*ārvāgrathamityanukrāṃtaṃ*). Its use, as stated before, is in the Niṣkevalya (śastra) of the Mahāvrata.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "अर्वाग्रथं (*arvāgrathaṃ*)" is the fourteenth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta, Indra is the deity, and the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said to begin "Arvāgratham". It has already been stated that this sūkta is used for the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras in the Mahāvrata sacrifice.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 37
- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 37
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 7; Varga 9
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: Triṣṭup

### Printed p. 59

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒र्वाग्रथं॑ वि॒श्ववा॑रं त उ॒ग्रेंद्र॑ यु॒क्तासो॒ हर॑यो  
> वहंतु ।  
> की॒रिश्चि॒द्धि त्वा॒ हव॑ते॒ स्व॑र्वानृधी॒महि॑ सध॒माद॑स्ते अ॒द्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अर्वाक् । रथं । विश्ववारं । ते । उग्र । इंद्र । युक्तासः । हरयः । वहंतु ।  
> कीरिः । चित् । हि । त्वा । हवते । स्वःवान् । ऋधीमहि । सध्वमादः । ते । अद्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उग्रोद्गूर्णबलेंद्र युक्तासो रथेन युक्ता हरयोऽश्वास्ते
> त्वदीयं विश्ववारं विश्वैर्वणेयं रथमर्वागस्मदभिमुखं वहंतु । आनयंतु ।
> हि यस्मात् स्वर्वान् । स्वः सुष्करणेयं गुणजातं । तद्वान् कीरिश्चित् स्तोता
> भरद्वाज ऋषिस्त्वा त्वां हवते आह्वयति तस्मात्कारणात्त्वदीयं रथमभिमुखं
> वहंतित्यर्थः । वयं चाद्येदानीं ते त्वया सधमादः सह माद्यंत ऋधीमहि ।
> समृद्धा भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O fierce Indra, of uplifted strength, may your horses, yoked to the chariot, bring your chariot, which all desire (विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*), to be chosen by all), towards us. For (हि (*hi*)) the praiser, the seer Bharadvāja, who possesses स्वः (*svaḥ*) (explained as a group of qualities, and he is endowed with it), invokes you; for that reason may they bring your chariot towards us. And we also, today, rejoicing together with you, would prosper. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्र (*ugra*)—possessed of fearful power
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- युक्तासः (*yuktāsaḥ*)—yoked to your chariot
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—the horses
- ते (*te*)—your
- विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)—worthy of the regard of all
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—towards us
- वहंतु (*vahaṃtu*)—let them carry and bring
- हि (*hi*)—because
- स्वर्वान् (*svarvān*)—one endowed with devotion
- कीरिश्चित् (*kīriścit*)—Bharadvāja, the praiser
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- हवते (*havate*)—calls
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- ते (*te*)—with you
- सधमादः (*sadhamādaḥ*)—experiencing common joy
- ऋधीमहि (*ṛdhīmahi*)—may we attain prosperity

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, of fearful power, may the horses yoked to your chariot bring your chariot, which is worthy of the regard of all, towards us. Bharadvāja, who is endowed with devotion and is the praiser, calls you. May we too, experiencing common joy with you, attain prosperity.

### Printed p. 60

##### English translation
Fierce Indra, let your harnessed steeds bring down your all-desired chariot : your devoted adorer verily invokes you: may we to-day, partaking of your exhilaration, increase to-day (in prosperity).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रोद्रोणे॒ हर॑यः॒ कर्मा॑ग्मन्नुना॒नास॒ ऋज्यं॑तो अभूवन् ।  
> इंद्रो॑ न अ॒स्य पू॒र्व्यः प॑पीयाद्दु॒क्षो मद॑स्य सो॒म्यस्य॒  ॑
> राजा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रो इति । द्रोणे । हरयः । कर्म । अग्मन् । पुनानासः । ऋज्यंतः । अभूवन् ।  
> इंद्रः । नः । अस्य । पूर्व्यः । पपीयात् । म्युक्षः । मदस्य । सोम्यस्य । राजा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तृतीये पर्यायेच्छावाकस्य प्रो द्रोण इत्येषा शस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रितं
> च । प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या । आ-६-४ । इति ॥
> हरयो हरितवर्णाः सोमा नः कर्मास्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रो अग्मन् । प्रकर्षेण
> गच्छंति । प्राप्नुवंति । प्राप्य च पुनानासः पूयमाना द्रोणे द्रोणकलश ऋज्यंत
> ऋजु गच्छंतोऽभूवन् । भवंति । पूर्व्यः पुरातनो द्युक्षो दीप्तेर्निवासभूतो
> द्युस्थानो वा मदस्य मदकरस्य सोम्यस्य सोमस्य राजेश्वर एवंभूत इंद्रश्चास्येमं सोमं पपीयात् । पिबतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third paryāya, this Ṛk, प्रो द्रोण (*pro droṇa*), is the śastra-yājyā of the Acchāvāka priest. It is also taught in the sūtra: "प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या (*pro droṇe harayaḥ karmāgmanniti yājyā*)", with the reference Ā. 6-4. The green Soma juices (हरयः (*harayaḥ*)) come forward to our rite (कर्म (*karma*), our sacrifice); having come they are purified in the pitcher (द्रोणे (*droṇe*), the Droṇa vessel) and, flowing straight (ऋज्यंतः (*ṛjyaṃtaḥ*)), become so. The ancient (पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)) Indra, who abides in radiance or dwells in the heavenly region, and who is the lord of the exhilarating Soma, may drink this Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—the Soma juices of green hue
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- कर्म (*karma*)—the sacrifice
- प्रो अग्मन् (*pro agman*)—come forward and join
- पुनानासः (*punānāsaḥ*)—purified here
- द्रोणे (*droṇe*)—in the Droṇa vessel
- ऋज्यंतः (*ṛjyaṃtaḥ*)—joined together
- अभूवन् (*abhūvan*)—they become
- पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)—the ancient one
- द्युक्षः (*dyukṣaḥ*)—the radiant dweller of the heavenly region
- मदस्य (*madasya*)—of the gladdening
- सोम्यस्य (*somyasya*)—Soma juice
- राजा (*rājā*)—the lord
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma
- पपीयात् (*papīyāt*)—may he drink

### Printed p. 61

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma juices of green hue come forward to our sacrifice. Then, purified, they join together in the Droṇa vessel. May Indra, the ancient one, the radiant dweller of the heavenly region, the lord of the gladdening Soma juice, drink this Soma.

##### English translation
The green Soma juices flow at our sacrifice, and, purified, proceed direct into the pitcher: may the ancient. illustrious Indra, the sovereign of the exhilarating Soma libation, drink of this our offering.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the third paryāya the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this Ṛk, प्रो द्रोणे (*pro droṇe*), as the śastra-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या (*pro droṇe harayaḥ karmāgmanniti yājyā*) (Ā. Sū. 6-4).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒स॒स्रा॒णासः॑ शवसा॒नमच्छेंद्रं॑ सुच॒क्रे र॒थ्या॑सो॒ अश्वाः॑ ।  
> अ॒भि श्रव॒ ऋज्यं॑तो वहेयु॒नूर्चि॒न्नु वा॒योर॒मृतं॒ वि  ॑
> दस्यॆत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आसस्राणासः । शवसानं । अच्छै । इंद्रं । सुचक्रे । रथ्यासः । आश्वाः ।  
> अभि । श्रवः । ऋज्यंतः । वहेयुः । नु । चित् । नु । वायोः । अमृतं । वि । दस्येत् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> असस्राणासः परितो गच्छंतो रथ्यासो रथे युक्ता अश्वा ऋज्यंत
> यजुगमनाः संतः सुचक्रे शोभनचक्रे रथेवस्थितं शवसानं बलमिवाचरंतमिंद्रं
> श्रवः श्रवणीयमस्मदीयं हविरच्छाभिमुख्येनाभि वहेयुः । आवहेयुः । नू
> चिदिति निपातो निषेधेऽत्र वर्तते । अमृतममरणहेतुभूतं सोमलक्षणं हवि_

### Printed p. 62

> र्वायोर्हेतोनु इदानीं नू चित् नैव वि दस्येत् । क्षयं न प्राप्नुयात् ।
> पात्रे गृहीतः सोमो वायुना शुष्यति ततः पुरैव तत्पानार्थमश्वा इंद्रमभिवहेयुरित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The horses yoked to the chariot (रथ्यासः (*rathyāsaḥ*)), going about on every side (आसस्राणासः (*āsasrāṇāsaḥ*)), moving straight (ऋज्यंतः (*ṛjyaṃtaḥ*), going directly), should carry towards our oblation, which is to be heard of (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)), Indra, who stands in the chariot with fair wheels (सुचक्रे (*sucakre*)) and acts like strength itself (शवसानं (*śavasānaṃ*)). The word नू चित् (*nū cit*) is a particle used here in the sense of negation. The immortal (अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)), that is the oblation consisting of Soma, which is not the cause of death, should not be wasted, should not come to destruction by the wind: Soma taken in a vessel dries up through the wind; therefore, before that happens, the horses should bring Indra to drink it. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आसस्राणासः (*āsasrāṇāsaḥ*)—moving about on all sides
- रथ्यासः (*rathyāsaḥ*)—yoked to the chariot
- अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*)—the horses
- ऋज्यंतः (*ṛjyaṃtaḥ*)—going straight
- सुचक्रे (*sucakre*)—in the chariot with excellent wheels
- शवसानं (*śavasānaṃ*)—who is the representative of strength
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- श्रवः अच्छ (*śravaḥ accha*)—towards the oblation
- अभि वहेयुः (*abhi vaheyuḥ*)—may they bring
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—the Soma, which is like ambrosia
- वायोः (*vāyoḥ*)—by the force of the wind
- नु (*nu*)—now
- नू चित् (*nū cit*)—certainly
- विदस्यॆत् (*vidasyèt*)—let it not be dried up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the horses, moving about everywhere and yoked to the chariot, going straight, bring Indra, the representative of strength, in the chariot with excellent wheels, towards the oblation. May the Soma, which is like ambrosia, not be dried up and wasted by the force of the wind.

##### English translation
May the everywhere-going, straight-proceeding, chariot-bearing steeds, bring the mighty Indra in his strong-wheeled car to our rite : let not the ambrosial Soma waste in the wind.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the companionship of Indra and Vāyu is described. In many contexts Indra and Vāyu have the same kind of epithets. To support this point Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk:
आसस्यवांसोऽभिबलायमानमिंद्रं कल्याणचक्रे रथे योगाय रथ्या अश्वा रथस्य वोढार ऋज्यंत ऋजुगामिनोऽन्नमभिवहेयुर्नवं च पुराणं च । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयत इति सतः । वायोश्चास्य भक्षो यथा न विदस्येदिति । इंद्रप्रधानेत्येके नैघुंटुकं नायुकर्मोभयप्रधानेत्यपरं ॥ (*āsasyavāṃso 'bhibalāyamānamiṃdraṃ kalyāṇacakre rathe yogāya rathyā aśvā rathasya voḍhāra ṛjyaṃta ṛjugāmino 'nnamabhivaheyurnavaṃ ca purāṇaṃ ca | śrava ityannanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ | vāyoścāsya bhakṣo yathā na vidasyediti | iṃdrapradhānetyeke naighuṃṭukaṃ nāyukarmobhayapradhānetyaparaṃ ‖*)
(Ni. 10-3)

### Printed p. 63

That is: the horses that draw Indra's chariot, ever moving about, bring Indra, who is exceedingly mighty and sits in the chariot with excellent wheels, to partake of the old and the new food (the Soma). Indra's horses are by nature ones that go straight, that is, without turning this way or that, only facing forward. The intention is: that the Soma juice prepared for Indra may not dry up and be wasted through the drying power of the wind, may the horses bring Indra here quickly and straight. The word श्रवः (*śravaḥ*) is a synonym among the names of food. Because food is well known, food is also called श्रवः (*śravaḥ*). May the Soma not dry up and be wasted through the drying power of the wind. Some hold that in this Ṛk the matter of Indra is presented as the principal one; others hold that it is the action of Vāyu that is presented, and that both are praised.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वरि॑ष्ठो अस्य॒ दक्षि॑णामिय॒र्तींद्रो॑ म॒घोनां॑ तुविकू॒र्मित॑मः ।  
> यया॑ वज्रवः परि॒यास्यंहो॑ म॒घा च॑ धृष्ट्णो॒ दय॑से॒ वि  ॒
> सूरीन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वरिष्ठः । अस्य । दक्षिणां । इयर्ति । इंद्रः । मघोनां । तुविकूर्मितमः ।  
> यया । वज्रीवः । परियासि । अंहः । मघा । च । धृष्णो इति । दयसे । वि ।  
> सूरीन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरिष्ठ उरुतमस्तुविकूर्मितमोऽतिशयेन बहुविधकर्मेंद्रो मघोनां
> मघवतां हनिर्लक्षणधनोपेतानां मध्येऽस्य यजमानस्य दक्षिणां यज्ञे
> दातव्यामियर्ति । प्रेरयति । यद्वा । मघोनामित्यस्येत्यनेन समानाधिकरणं ॥
> वचनव्यत्ययः ॥ मघोनो हविष्मतोऽस्य यजमानस्येत्यर्थः । शेषः प्रत्यक्षकृतः ।
> हे वज्रिवो वज्रवन्निद्र यया दक्षिणया दत्तयांहः पापं यज्ञसंबंधि परियासि
> विनाशयसि हे धृष्टो धर्षक मघा मघानि धनानि सूरीन् स्तोत्थान् पुत्रांश्च
> यया च दक्षिणया वि दयसे प्रयच्छसि तादृशीं दक्षिणां प्रेरयसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is वरिष्ठ (*variṣṭha*), the most excellent, and तुविकूर्मितमः (*tuvikūrmitamaḥ*), one who performs exceedingly many kinds of deeds. Among the wealthy (मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*), those possessed of wealth in the form of oblations) he sends forth (इयर्ति (*iyarti*), impels) the fee (दक्षिणां (*dakṣiṇāṃ*)) that is to be given at the sacrifice of this sacrificer. Or else: मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*) agrees with अस्य (*asya*) through a change of number, so that the sense is: of this sacrificer, who is rich in oblations; the rest is evident. O wielder of the thunderbolt, by the fee given you remove the sin connected with the sacrifice (परियासि (*pariyāsi*) means: you destroy it). O bold one, the destroyer of enemies, with which fee you grant riches and सूरीन् (*sūrīn*), praisers and sons, such a fee you send forth. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—O wielder of the thunderbolt
- धृष्णो (*dhṛṣṇo*)—and humbler of the pride of enemies, O Indra
- यया (*yayā*)—with which wealth
- अ०हः (*a0haḥ*)—sin
- परियासि (*pariyāsi*)—you destroy (and)
- यया (*yayā*)—by which act of giving
- मघा (*maghā*)—riches
- सूरीन् (*sūrīn*)—and sons who are praisers
- वि दयसे (*vi dayase*)—you favour; such
- दक्षिणां (*dakṣiṇāṃ*)—wealth fit to be given
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—among the wealthy
- अस्य (*asya*)—to this sacrificer
- वरिष्ठः (*variṣṭhaḥ*)—most excellent
- तुविकूर्मितमः (*tuvikūrmitamaḥ*)—doer of manifold deeds
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—and lord of all, you
- इयर्ति (*iyarti*)—provide

### Printed p. 64

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt and humbler of enemies, by what giving of wealth you destroy sin, and by what act of giving you favour us with riches and with sons who are praisers, such wealth fit to be given you, the most excellent, the doer of manifold deeds, the lord of all, provide for this sacrificer among the wealthy.

##### English translation
The very strong Indra, the performer of many great deeds, instigates the donation of this (institutor of the ceremony) amongst the opulent, whereby, wielder of the thunderbolt, you remove sin, and, firm of purpose, bestow riches upon the worshippers.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॒ वाज॑स्य॒ स्थवि॑रस्य दा॒तेंद्रो॑ गी॒र्भिर्व॑र्धतां वृ॒द्धम॑हाः ।  
> इंद्रो॑ वृ॒त्रं हनि॑ष्ठो अस्तु॒ सत्वा ता सू॒रिः पृ॑णति॒ तूतु॑जानः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । वाजस्य । स्थविरस्य । दाता । इंद्रः । गीःभिः । वर्धतां । वृद्धमहाः ।  
> इंद्रः । वृत्रं । हनिष्ठः । अस्तु । सत्वा । आ । ता । सूरिः । पृणति । तूतुजानः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 65

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रः स्थविरस्य वाजस्यान्नस्य बलस्य ना दाता भवतु । स चेंद्रो
> वृद्धमहाः प्रवृद्धतेजस्कः सन् गीर्भिरस्मदीयाभिः स्तुतिभिर्वर्धतां । सत्वा शत्रूणां
> शाशयिता स इंद्रो वृत्रमावरकं शत्रुं हनिष्ठो हंतृतमोऽस्तु । भवतु । अपि
> च सूरिः प्रेरकः स इंद्रस्तूतुजानस्वरमाणस्ता तानि धनान्या पृणति । अस्मभ्यं
> प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this Indra be the giver of स्थविरस्य वाजस्य (*sthavirasya vājasya*), abiding food, that is, strength. And may that Indra, of greatly increased splendour (वृद्धमहाः (*vṛddhamahāḥ*)), grow by our praises. सत्वा (*satvā*) means the chastiser of enemies: may that Indra be हनिष्ठः (*haniṣṭhaḥ*), the best slayer, of Vṛtra, the enemy who obstructs. And the impeller (सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)), that Indra, hastening (तूतुजानः (*tūtujānaḥ*) is explained as one who hurries), fills up those riches: may he give them to us. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- स्थविरस्य (*sthavirasya*)—of abiding
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—food
- दाता (*dātā*)—let him be the giver
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वृद्धमहाः (*vṛddhamahāḥ*)—being of exceeding splendour
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—by our praises
- वर्धतां (*vardhatāṃ*)—let him grow
- सत्वा (*satvā*)—the destroyer of enemies
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the enemy
- हनिष्ठः (*haniṣṭhaḥ*)—a swift destroyer
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let him be
- सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)—Indra the impeller
- तूतुजानः (*tūtujānaḥ*)—hastening
- ता (*tā*)—those well-known riches
- आ पृणति (*ā pṛṇati*)—let him give to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra be the giver of abiding food. And, being of exceeding splendour, may he grow by our praises. May Indra, the destroyer of enemies, destroy the enemy in the form of Vṛtra. May Indra, the impeller, hastening, give us the well-known riches.

##### English translation
Indra is the donor of substantial food: may the very illustrious Indra increase (in glory) through our praises: may Indra, the destroyer (of enemies), be the especial slayer of Vritra : may he, the animator, the quick-mover, grant us those (riches which we desire).

## Sūkta 38 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपादित इति पंचर्चं पंचदशं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं ।
> अपादित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्य उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अपादित इति (*apādita iti*) has five Ṛks and is the fifteenth sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja (Ārṣa), its metre is Triṣṭubh, and its deity is Indra. It is listed in the Anukramaṇī with the words अपादित्यनुक्रांतं (*apādityanukrāṃtaṃ*). Its use, as stated before, is in the Niṣkevalya (śastra) of the Mahāvrata.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "अपादितः (*apāditaḥ*)" is the fifteenth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta, Indra is the deity, and the metre is

### Printed p. 66

Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said to begin with "Apāt". It has already been stated that this sūkta is used for the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras in the Mahāvrateṣṭi.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 38
- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 38
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 7; Varga 10
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: Bhāradvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अपा॑दि॒त उदु॑ नश्चि॒त्रत॑मो म॒हीं भ॑र्षद्दु॒मती॒मिंद्र॑हूतिं।  
> पन्य॑सीं धी॒तिं दैव्य॑स्य॒ याम॒ञ्जन॑स्य रा॒तिं व॑नते सु॒दानुः॑ ॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपात् । इतः । उत् । ऊं इति । नः । चित्रतमः । महीं । भर्षत् । द्युमतीं ।  
> इंद्रहूतिं ।  
> पन्यसीं । धीतिं । दैव्यस्य । यामन् । जनस्य । रातिं । वनते । सुदानुः ॥ १ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चित्रतमश्चायनीयतम आश्चर्यतमो वा स इंद्रो नोऽस्मदीयादितोऽस्माद्ग्रहचमसादेरपात् । सोमं पिबतु । यद्वा । इतोऽस्माच्छत्रोर्नोऽस्मानपात् । पातु । रक्षतु । उदु इत्येत् पूरणौ । तथा महीं महतीं द्युमतीं
> दीप्तिमतीमिंद्रहूतिमिंद्रस्य स्तुतिं भर्षत् । स इंद्रो बिभर्तु । धारयतु ।
> दैव्यस्य देवसंबंधिनो जनस्य यामन् यामनि यज्ञे क्रियमाणां पत्यसीं
> स्तुत्यतमां धीतिं परिचरणरूपां क्रियां रातिं दाशव्यं हविश्च सुदानुः शोभनदान
> इंद्रो वनशे । संभजतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra, who is चित्रतमः (*citratamaḥ*) (the most worthy of being gathered to, or the most wonderful), अपात् (*apāt*): may he drink Soma from this vessel of ours, the grahacamasa and the like (इतः (*itaḥ*)). Or else: may he protect us (अपात् (*apāt*) is पातु (*pātu*), रक्षतु (*rakṣatu*)) from this enemy. उदु (*udu*) are two expletives. Likewise may that Indra bear (भर्षत् (*bharṣat*) is बिभर्तु (*bibhartu*), धारयतु (*dhārayatu*)) the great, shining invocation of Indra, that is, praise. In the course (यामन् (*yāman*)) of the sacrifice of the devout man (the one belonging to the gods), may Indra, the good giver (सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)), enjoy (संभजतु (*saṃbhajatu*)) the most praiseworthy rite performed in the sacrifice, in the form of service (धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)), and the gift (रातिं (*rātiṃ*)), the oblation fit to be offered. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चित्रतमः (*citratamaḥ*)—Indra, the most attractive
- नः (*naḥ*)—by us
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from our cups and other vessels
- अपात् (*apāt*)—let him drink the Soma
- महीं (*mahīṃ*)—great
- द्युमशीं (*dyumaśīṃ*)—and radiant

### Printed p. 67

- इंद्रहूतिं (*iṃdrahūtiṃ*)—the praise addressed to Indra
- भर्षत् (*bharṣat*)—let him bear
- सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)—Indra, the excellent giver
- दैव्यस्य (*daivyasya*)—belonging to the gods
- जनस्य (*janasya*)—of the sacrificer
- यामन् (*yāman*)—in the sacrifice
- पन्यसीं (*panyasīṃ*)—the praiseworthy
- धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)—act of worship
- राशिं (*rāśiṃ*)—and the oblation fit to be given
- वनते (*vanate*)—he enjoys

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, the most attractive, drink from our cups and other vessels the Soma offered by us. May he bear the great and radiant praise addressed to Indra. Indra, the excellent giver, enjoys in the sacrifice of the sacrificer who belongs to the gods the praiseworthy act of worship and the oblation fit to be given.

##### English translation
May the most marvellous Indra drink from this (our cup) : may he acknowledge our earnest and brilliant invocation: may the munificent (Indra) accept the offering and the praiseworthy adoration at the sacrifice of the devout worshipper.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दू॒राच्चि॒दा व॑सतो अस्य॒ कर्णा॒ घोषा॒दिंद्र॑स्य तन्यति  ॒
> ब्रुवा॒णः ।  
> वियमे॑नं दे॒वहू॑तिर्ववृत्यान्म॒द्र्य१॒ं॑ गिंद्र॑मि॒यमृ॒च्यमा॑  
> ना ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दूरात् । चित् । आ । वसतः । अस्य । कर्णा । घोषात् । इंद्रस्य । तन्यति । ब्रुवाणः ।  
> आ । इयं । एनं । देवहूतिः । ववृत्यात् । मद्र्यक् । इंद्रं । इयं । ऋच्यमाना॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रस्य कर्णा कर्णौ दूराच्चित् दूरदेशादप्या वसतः । स्तोत्रश्रवणार्थमागच्छतः । इंद्रस्य घोषात् घोषणीयात् स्तोत्राद्धेतोर्ब्रुवाणः स्तुवन्
> स्तोता तन्यति । शब्दं करोति । यद्वा ! सर्वत्र विस्तारयति । देवहूतिर्देवस्येंद्र-

### Printed p. 68

> स्याह्वानरूपेयं स्तुतिश्च ऋच्यमाना स्वयं प्रेर्यमाणा सत्येनमिंद्रं मद्यक्
> मदभिमुखमा ववृत्यात् । आवर्तयतु । पुनरियमिति पूरणः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two ears of this Indra, even from a distant place, come (आ वसतः (*ā vasataḥ*): they come to hear the praise). Because of the praise to be proclaimed (घोषात् (*ghoṣāt*)) of Indra, the praiser, reciting (ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*), praising), makes sound (तन्यति (*tanyati*)); or else: he spreads it everywhere. देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*) is this praise, in the form of an invocation of the god Indra, and being herself urged on (ऋच्यमाना (*ṛcyamānā*)), may she turn this Indra to face me (मद्यक् (*madyak*), towards me); इयं (*iyaṃ*) is to be repeated. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दूराच्चित् (*dūrāccit*)—from very far away
- आ वसतः (*ā vasataḥ*)—though dwelling
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Indra
- कर्णा (*karṇā*)—to touch the ears
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—addressed to Indra
- घोषात् (*ghoṣāt*)—for the sake of the praise
- ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*)—reciting the praise, the praiser
- तन्यति (*tanyati*)—makes sound
- देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)—that which invokes the god Indra
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this praise
- ऋच्यमाना (*ṛcyamānā*)—self-impelled
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this Indra
- मद्रक् (*madrak*)—towards me
- आ ववृत्यात् (*ā vavṛtyāt*)—let it make him turn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Though Indra is very far away, the praiser, reciting praise, makes sound addressed to him, so as to touch Indra's ears. May this praise that invokes the god Indra, self-impelled, make this Indra turn towards me.

##### English translation
Reciting (his praise, the worshipper) calls aloud, that by the sound he may reach the ears of Indra, although abiding afar off: may this invocation of the deity, inducing him (to come). bring Indra to my presence.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं वो॑ धि॒या प॑र॒मया॑ पुरा॒जाम॒जर॒मिंद्र॑म॒भ्य॑नूष्क॒र्कैः।  
> ब्रह्मा॑ च॒ गिरो॑ दधि॒रे सम॑स्मिन्म॒हांश्च॒ स्तोमो॒ अधि॑  ॒॑
> वर्धदिंद्रॆ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । व ॥ धिया । परमया । पुराजां । अजरं । इंद्रं । अभि । अनूषि । अकैः ।  
> ब्रह्म । च । गिर ॥ दधिरे । सं । अस्मिन् । महान् । च । स्तोमः । अधि । वर्धत् ।  
> इंद्रे ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 69

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तं तादृशमिंद्रं वस्तां ॥ व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं ॥ परमयोत्कृष्टतमया धिया स्तुत्यार्कैरर्चनसाधनैर्हविर्भिः सार्धमभ्यनूषि । अभिष्टौमि ।
> कीदृशं । पुराजां पूर्वस्मिन् काले जातं चिरंतनमजरं जरारहितं नित्यं ।
> अतः कारणादस्मिन्निंद्रॆ ब्रह्म ब्रह्माणि हविर्लक्षणान्यन्नानि गिरः स्तुतयश्च सं दधिरे ।
> संधीयंते । संश्लिष्यंते । महान् प्रवृद्धः स्तोमश्चाधि वर्धत् । अधिकं वर्धते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, that such Indra" तं (*taṃ*): the plural वः (*vaḥ*) stands by a change of number. I praise (अभ्यनूषि (*abhyanūṣi*)) him with the most excellent praise (परमयोत्कृष्टतमया धिया (*paramayotkṛṣṭatamayā dhiyā*)) together with oblations (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*), the means of worship). Of what kind is he: पुराजां (*purājāṃ*), born in former time, ancient; अजरं (*ajaraṃ*), free from old age, eternal. For that reason, in this Indra the oblations in the form of food (ब्रह्म (*brahma*)) and the praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) are joined together (सं दधिरे (*saṃ dadhire*), they are put together, they cling), and the great, swelling praise (स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)) grows further. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुराजां (*purājāṃ*)—the ancient
- अजरं (*ajaraṃ*)—the free from old age
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the lord
- तं वः (*taṃ vaḥ*)—that same you
- परमया (*paramayā*)—with the most excellent
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—praise
- अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—and with oblations, the means of worship
- अभ्यनूषि (*abhyanūṣi*)—I worship
- अस्मिन् इंद्रे (*asmin iṃdre*)—in this very Indra
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the food in the form of oblation
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—and the praises
- सं दधिरे (*saṃ dadhire*)—have come together
- महान् (*mahān*)—very great
- स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)—praise also
- अधि वर्धत् (*adhi vardhat*)—grows exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are ancient, free from old age and lord, that same you I worship with the most excellent praise and with oblations that are the means of worship. In this very Indra the food in the form of oblation and the praises have come together. Very great praise also grows exceedingly.

##### English translation
I glorify you with hymns and with pious worship, the ancient undecaying Indra, for in him are oblations and praises concentrated, and great adoration is enhanced (when addressed to him).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वर्धा॒द्यं य॒ज्ञ उ॒त सोम॒ इंद्रं॒ वर्धा॒द्ब्रह्म॒ गिर॑ ॒ ॒॑
> उ॒क्था च॒ मन्म॑ ।  
> वर्धाहै॑नमु॒षसो॒ याम॑न्न॒ क्तोर्वर्धा॒न्मासाः॑ श॒रदो॒ द्याव॒  ॑
> इंद्रं ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 70

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वर्धात् । यं । यज्ञः । उत । सोमः । इंद्रं । वर्धान् । ब्रह्म । गिरः । उक्था ।  
> च । मन्म ।  
> वर्ध । अह । एनं । उषसः । यामन् । अक्टोः । वर्धान् । मासाः । शरदः । द्यावः।  
> इंद्रं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमिंद्रं यज्ञो यागो वर्धात् वर्धयति । उतापि च तत्साधनभूतः
> सोमश्च यमिंद्रं वर्धयति । तथा ब्रह्म हविर्लक्षणमन्नं च पुरोडाशादिकं
> यमिंद्रं वर्धात् वर्धयति । गिरः स्तोत्राणि मन्म मननीयान्कुक्षोकशस्त्राणॆ च
> यं वर्धयंति एनमिंद्रमुषसश्चाक्तो रात्रेर्यामन् यामनि गमने सति
> वर्ध । वर्धयंति । मासाः शरदः संवत्सराश्च द्यावो दिवसाश्चैनमिंद्रं वर्धान् ।
> वर्धयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra whom the sacrifice (यज्ञो (*yajño*), the rite) makes grow (वर्धात् (*vardhāt*)); and also Soma, the means of it, makes that Indra grow. So too ब्रह्म (*brahma*), food in the form of the oblation, such as the sacrificial cake and the like, makes that Indra grow. The praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) and the मन्म (*manma*), the thoughtful recitations of the śastra kind, make him grow. This Indra the Dawns (उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)) cause to grow when the night (अक्टोः (*akṭoḥ*)) goes on (यामन् (*yāman*)). The months, the autumns, that is, the years, and the days make this Indra grow. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं इंद्रं (*yaṃ iṃdraṃ*)—the Indra whom
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- वर्धात् (*vardhāt*)—makes strong
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—and the food in the form of oblation
- वर्धात् (*vardhāt*)—make full-grown
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises
- मन्म (*manma*)—which are means of meditation
- उक्ता (*uktā*)—and the recited mantras, make whom strong
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—that same Indra
- अक्टोः (*akṭoḥ*)—of the night
- यामन् (*yāman*)—in the time of its passing
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the Dawns
- वर्ध (*vardha*)—make grow
- मासाः (*māsāḥ*)—the months
- शरदः (*śaradaḥ*)—the years
- द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*)—the days
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- वर्धान् (*vardhān*)—make grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra whom the sacrifice, the Soma that is its means, and the food in the form of oblation make full-grown, and whom the praises and the recited mantras that serve meditation make strong: that same Indra the Dawns make grow in the time of the night's passing. The months, the years and the days are causes of Indra's growth.

### Printed p. 71

##### English translation
Indra, whom the sacrifice, whom the libation exalts, whom the oblation, the praises, the prayers, the adoration exalt, whom the course of day and night exalts, whom months, and years, and days exalt.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा ज॑ज्ञा॒नं सह॑से॒ असा॑मि वावृधा॒नं राध॑से च श्रु॒ताय॑।  
> म॒हामु॒ग्रमव॑से विप्र नू॒नमा वि॑वासेनु वृत्र॒तूर्ये॑षु ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । जज्ञानं । सहसे । आसामि । ववृधानं । राधसे । च । श्रुताय ।  
> महां । उग्रं । अवसे । विप्र । नूनं । आ । विवासेम । वृत्रतूर्येषु ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हॆः विप्र मेधाविन्निंद्र एवैवं जज्ञानं प्रादुर्भवंतं सहसे शत्रूणामभिभवार्थमसामि बहुलं वावृधानं वर्धमानं महां महांतमुग्रमुद्गूर्णबलं
> त्वां नूनमद्य वृत्रतूर्येषु श्रुताय विश्रुताय राधसे धनाय चावसे रक्षणाय
> चा विवासेम । परिचरेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wise (विप्र (*vipra*), intelligent) Indra, you who are thus (एव (*eva*)) being born, manifesting yourself (जज्ञानं (*jajñānaṃ*)), for the overcoming of enemies (सहसे (*sahase*)), असामि (*asāmi*), abundantly, growing (वावृधानं (*vāvṛdhānaṃ*)), great (महां (*mahāṃ*)), mighty (उग्रं (*ugraṃ*), of uplifted strength): you do we serve (विवासेम (*vivāsema*), परिचरेम (*paricarema*)) today in the battles in which Vṛtra is slain (वृत्रतूर्येषु (*vṛtratūryeṣu*)), for renowned (श्रुताय (*śrutāya*)) wealth (राधसे (*rādhase*)) and for protection (अवसे (*avase*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्र (*vipra*)—O wise Indra
- एव (*eva*)—in this manner
- जज्ञानं (*jajñānaṃ*)—one who has come into being
- सहसे (*sahase*)—to defeat the enemies
- आसामि (*āsāmi*)—exceedingly
- वावृधानं (*vāvṛdhānaṃ*)—one who has grown
- महां (*mahāṃ*)—and a great soul
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—and one of fearful strength, you
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- वृत्रशूरेषु (*vṛtraśūreṣu*)—in the battles
- श्रुताय (*śrutāya*)—for fame
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for wealth
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- आ विवासेम (*ā vivāsema*)—we worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Indra, you who have thus come into being, who have grown exceedingly in order to defeat the enemies, a great soul, one of fearful strength, we worship in the battles, for fame, for wealth and for protection.

### Printed p. 72

##### English translation
So, wise Indra, may we to-day propitiate you who are manifested. to overcome (our foes), you who are greatly augmenting, mightly and free, for (the sake of) wealth, fame, and protection, and for the destruction of (our) enemies.

## Sūkta 39 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मंद्रस्य कवेरिति पंचर्चं षोडशं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार્ષं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं ।
> मंद्रस्येत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning मंद्रस्य कवेरिति (*maṃdrasya kaveriti*) has five Ṛks and is the sixteenth sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja (Ārṣa), its metre is Triṣṭubh, and its deity is Indra. It is listed in the Anukramaṇī with the word मंद्रस्येत्यनुक्रांतं (*maṃdrasyetyanukrāṃtaṃ*). Its use has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "मंद्रस्य कवेः (*maṃdrasya kaveḥ*)" is the sixteenth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta, Indra is the deity, and the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said to begin with "Mandrasya". The use has been stated before.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 39
- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 3; Sūkta 39
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 7; Varga 11
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Indra
- Chandas: Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मं॒द्रस्य॑ क॒वेर्दि॒व्यस्य॒ वह्ने॒र्विप्र॑मन्मनो वच॒नस्य॒ मध्वः॑ ।  
> अपा॑ न॒स्तस्य॑ सच॒नस्य॑ दे॒वेषो॑ युवस्व गृण॒ते गोअ॑ग्राः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मंद्रस्य । कवेः । दिव्यस्य । वह्नेः । विप्रमन्मनः । वचनस्य । मध्वः ।  
> अपाः । नः । तस्य । सचनस्य । देव । इषः । युवस्व । गृणते । गोऽअग्राः ॥ १ i

### Printed p. 73

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मंद्रस्य मोदनस्य मदकरस्य वा कवेर्विक्रांतस्य दिव्यस्य दिवि भवस्य
> वह्नेर्वोढुर्विप्रमन्मनः । विप्रा मेधाविनो मन्मनः स्तोतारो यस्य स तथोक्तः ।
> तस्य वचनस्य वचनीयस्य स्तुत्यस्य तस्य सर्वत्र प्रसिद्धस्य सचनस्य सेव्यस्य एवंभूतस्य
> मध्वो मधुनः सोमस्य ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी ॥ एवंभूतं नोऽस्मदीयं सोमं हे इंद्र त्वमपाः । पिब । अपि
> च हे देव द्योतमानेंद्र गृणते स्तुवते ॥ तृतीयार्थे चतुर्थी ॥ स्तुवता
> मया गोअग्राः । गावोऽग्री प्रमुखे यासां तादृशा इषोऽन्नानि युवस्व ।
> संयोजय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मंद्रस्य (*maṃdrasya*) is delighting or intoxicating; कवेः (*kaveḥ*), the powerful; दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*), born in heaven; वह्नेः (*vahneḥ*), the bearer; विप्रमन्मनः (*vipramanmanaḥ*) is one whose praisers (मन्मनः (*manmanaḥ*)) are the wise (विप्रा (*viprā*)); वचनस्य (*vacanasya*), that which is to be spoken of, to be praised; that which is famed everywhere; सचनस्य (*sacanasya*), to be served; the sweet Soma (मध्वो मधुनः सोमस्य (*madhvo madhunaḥ somasya*)) of such a kind, our Soma, O Indra, you drink (अपाः (*apāḥ*), पिब (*piba*)). The genitive here stands in the sense of the dative, since the act of taking is to be performed on it as the thing given. And, O shining god Indra, to me who praise (गृणते (*gṛṇate*); the dative stands for the instrumental), join (युवस्व (*yuvasva*), संयोजय (*saṃyojaya*)) foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*), foods) that have cattle at their head. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नः (*naḥ*)—offered by us
- मंद्रस्य (*maṃdrasya*)—intoxicating
- कवेः (*kaveḥ*)—life-giving
- दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*)—born in the heavenly world
- वह्नेः (*vahneḥ*)—bearing fruit
- विप्रमन्मनः (*vipramanmanaḥ*)—meditated on by the praisers
- वचनस्य (*vacanasya*)—praiseworthy
- तस्य (*tasya*)—well known
- सचनस्य (*sacanasya*)—fit to be served
- मध्यः (*madhyaḥ*)—sweet Soma juice
- अपाः (*apāḥ*)—drink
- देव (*deva*)—O shining Indra
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—with me, the praiser
- गो अग्राः (*go agrāḥ*)—having cattle as the chief part
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods
- युवस्व (*yuvasva*)—join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink the sweet Soma juice, offered by us, intoxicating, life-giving, born in the heavenly world, bearing fruit, meditated on by the praisers, praiseworthy, well known and fit to be served. O shining Indra, join to me, the praiser, foods that have cattle as their chief part; that is, fill me with all of them.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra, of that our sweet, exhilarating, inspiring, celestial, fruit-yielding Soma, commended by the wise, and entitled to praise and preparation: bestow upon him who glorifies you, divine (Indra), food, the chiefest of which is cattle.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यमु॑शा॒नः पयद्रि॑मु॒स्रा ऋ॒तधी॑तिभिर्ऋत॒युग्यु॑जा॒नः ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आयमिंद्रोऽद्रिं वलेन गोपिधानाय निर्मितं शिलोच्चयं परि परितः
> पर्वतसमीपे विद्यमाना उस्रा गा उशानः कामयमान ऋतधीतिभिः सत्यकर्मभिरंगिरोभिर्युजानः संगच्छमान ऋतयुक् ऋतेन तत्कृतेन स्तोत्रेण युक्तश्च
> भूत्वा वलस्यासुरस्य स्वभूतं सानुमुच्च्रितं पर्वतमरुग्णमन्मैरभग्नं वि रुजत् ।
> व्यभांक्षीत् । किं च पणीन्वलानुचरानेतत्संज्ञानसुरांश्च वचोभिः स्तुत्यैरायुध्यैः
> संतर्जनरूपैर्वाक्यैरेव वायमिंद्रोऽभि योधत् । अभ्ययुध्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra, desiring (उशानः (*uśānaḥ*)) the cows (उस्रा (*usrā*)) that were near the mountain (अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)), the mass of rock made by Vala to enclose the cows, joining (युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)) the Aṅgirases whose acts were true (ऋतधीतिभिः (*ṛtadhītibhiḥ*)), and being joined with the praise (ऋतयुक् (*ṛtayuk*)) made by them, broke (वि रुजत् (*vi rujat*)) the unbroken (अरुग्णं (*arugṇaṃ*)) summit (सानुं (*sānuṃ*)), the high mountain belonging to the asura Vala. And further, the Paṇis, the asuras of that name who were Vala's followers, Indra fought (अभि योधत् (*abhi yodhat*)) with words alone (वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)), words that were praiseworthy and warlike, in the nature of संतर्जन (*saṃtarjana*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं इंद्रः (*ayaṃ iṃdraḥ*)—this Indra
- अद्रिं परि (*adriṃ pari*)—around the mountain
- उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)—the cows
- उशानः (*uśānaḥ*)—wishing to obtain
- यतधीतिभिः (*yatadhītibhiḥ*)—with the Aṅgirases, whose acts are true
- युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)—joining
- यतयुक् (*yatayuk*)—being furnished with praise
- वलस्य (*valasya*)—of the asura Vala
- अरुग्णं (*arugṇaṃ*)—which others could not enter
- सानुं (*sānuṃ*)—the high part of the mountain
- वि रुजत् (*vi rujat*)—split apart
- पणीन् (*paṇīn*)—the Paṇis, followers of Vala
- वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)—with harsh words alone
- अभि योधत् (*abhi yodhat*)—he confronted

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Wishing to obtain the cows that were around the mountain made by Vala to confine the cows, Indra joined the Aṅgirases, whose acts are true, and, furnished with praise, split apart the high part of the mountain of the asura Vala, which others could not enter. He confronted the Paṇis, the followers of Vala, with harsh words alone.

##### English translation
Determined (to recover) the cattle hidden in the mountain, associated with the celebrators of pure rites, (the Angirasas), and animated by (their) veracious (praise), this (Indra) fractured the infrangible rock of Vala. and overwhelmed the Panis with reproaches.
