##### English translation
Whom, therefore, we all, who are the profferers and bestowers of praise ever commend, as the pious Bribu, the donor of thousands (of cattle) the recciver of thousands (of laudations).

## Sūkta 46 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वामिद्दीति चतुर्दशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं बृहस्पतिपुत्रस्य शंयोरार्षमैंद्रं।
> प्रथमातृतीयाद्या आयुजो बृहत्यो द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्याद्या युजः सतोबृहत्यः ।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । त्वामिद्दि षळूना प्रागाथमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ यदि
> ज्योतिःष्टोमो बृहत्पृष्ठः स्यात्तदानीं निष्केवल्यस्याद्यः प्रगाथः स्तोत्रियः ।
> सूत्रितं च । यद्यु वै बृहत्वामिद्दि हवामहे । आ. ५-१५ । इति ॥ महाव्रतेऽपि
> निष्केवल्येयं प्रगाथः शंसनीयः । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । त्वामिद्दि
> हवामहे त्वं हैहि चेरव इति बृहतः स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ । ऐ. आ. ५-२-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The third sūkta, of fourteen Ṛks, beginning त्वामिद्दीति (*tvāmiddīti*), has as its seer Śaṃyu, son of Bṛhaspati; its deity is Indra. The first, third and the following odd Ṛks are Bṛhatī; the second, fourth and the following even Ṛks are Satobṛhatī. So the Anukramaṇī says: त्वामिद्दि षळूना प्रागाथमिति (*tvāmiddi ṣaḷūnā prāgāthamiti*) **GLOSS** The use of the sūkta is by indication. If the Jyotiṣṭoma is Bṛhatpṛṣṭha, then at that time the first pragātha of the niṣkevalya is the stotriya. It is also laid down in the sūtra यद्यु वै बृहत्वामिद्दि हवामहे (*yadyu vai bṛhatvāmiddi havāmahe*) (Ā. 5-15). In the Mahāvrata too this pragātha is to be recited in the niṣkevalya. So also in the fifth Āraṇyaka it is laid down: त्वामिद्दि हवामहे त्वं हैहि चेरव इति बृहतः स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*tvāmiddi havāmahe tvaṃ haihi cerava iti bṛhataḥ stotriyānurūpau*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, त्वामिद्दि (*tvāmiddi*), is the third sūkta in the fourth Anuvāka. It has fourteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Śaṃyu, son of Bṛhaspati; Indra is the deity. In this sūkta the Ṛks of odd number, 1, 3, 5 and so on, are in the Bṛhatī metre; the Ṛks of even number, 2, 4, 6 and so on, are in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: त्वामिद्दि पळूना प्रागाथं (*tvāmiddi paḷūnā prāgāthaṃ*) **GLOSS** **NOTE** The use of the sūkta is by indication. In the variety of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice called Bṛhatpṛṣṭha, at the time of reciting the niṣkevalya-śastra mantras, the use of this sūkta for the stotriya mantras called the pragātha at the beginning is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, यद्यु वै बृहत्वामिद्दि हवामहे (*yadyu vai bṛhatvāmiddi havāmahe*) (Ā. 5-15). In the Mahāvratesṭi too, when the niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited, this sūkta is to be recited as a pragātha sūkta; this is indicated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya-Āraṇyaka by the sentence त्वामिद्दि हवामहे त्वं हैहि चेरव इति बृहतः स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*tvāmiddi havāmahe tvaṃ haihi cerava iti bṛhataḥ stotriyānurūpau*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2).

### Printed p. 164

##### Particulars

Sūkta 46. Maṇḍala 6. Anuvāka 4. Aṣṭaka 4. Adhyāya 7. Vargas 27, 28, 29. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 14. Seer: Śaṃyu Bārhaspatya. Deity: Indra. Metre: Prāgātha.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वामिद्धि हना॑महे सा॒ता वाज॑स्य का॒रवः॑ ।  
> त्वां वृ॒त्रेस्विं॑द्र॒ सत्प॑तिं॒ नर॒स्त्वां काष्ठा॒ स्वर्व॑तः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वां । इत् । हि । हवामहे । साता । वाजस्य । कारवः ।  
> त्वां । वृत्रेषु । इंद्र । सर्त्पतिं । नरः । त्वां । काष्ठासु । अर्वतः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कारवः स्तोतारो वयं वाजस्यान्नस्य साता सात् संभजने निमित्तभूते सति
> हे इंद्र त्वामिद्दि त्वामेव हवामहे । स्तुतिभिराह्वयामः । हे इंद्र सत्पतिं सतां
> पालयितारं श्रेष्ठं त्वां नरोऽन्येऽपि मनुष्या वृत्रेष्वावरकेषु शत्रुषु सत्तु
> हवंते । आह्वयंति तज्जयार्थं । अपि चार्वतोऽश्वस्य संबंधिनीषु काष्ठासु
> यत्राश्वः क्रांता तिष्ठति तासु काष्ठाः संग्रामेषु युद्धकामाश्च त्वामेवाह्वयंति ।
> आतो वयं त्वामेवाह्वयाम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We singers (कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)), for the sake of the sharing of food (साता (*sātā*), that is, when there is a cause for sharing), call on you alone, O Indra, with praises. O Indra, protector of the good and the best, other men too call on you in the encounters with enemies (वृत्रेषु (*vṛtreṣu*), the obstructing foes) for the conquest of them. And in the battles (काष्ठासु (*kāṣṭhāsu*)) connected with the horse, where the horse stands having advanced, those who desire to fight call on you alone. Therefore we too call on you alone: this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)—we who are praisers
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food
- साता (*sātā*)—for the gain
- त्वामिद्दि (*tvāmiddi*)—you alone
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call, praying
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—the protector of good men and the best
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—other men also
- वृत्रेषु (*vṛtreṣu*)—at the time of fighting with enemies (they call you for help)
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—accompanied by horses
- काष्टासु (*kāṣṭāsu*)—in battles also
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—they call you alone

### Printed p. 165

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who are praisers call on you alone, praying, for the gain of food. Other men too call on you alone for help, when they are fighting with enemies in battles accompanied by horses, you who are the protector of good men and the best.

##### English translation
We worshippers invoke you for the acquirement of food; you, Indra, the protector of the good, (do) men (invoke for aid) against enemies, and in places where horses (enconnter).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स त्वं न॑श्चित्र वज्रहस्त धृष्णु॒या म॒हः स्त॑वा॒नो अ॑द्रिवः ।  
> गामश्वं॑ र॒थ्य॑मिंद्र॒ सं कि॑र स॒त्रा वाजं॒ न जि॒ग्युषे॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । त्वं । नः । चित्र । वज्रहस्त । धृष्टुया । महः । स्तवानः । अद्रिवः ।  
> गां । अश्वं । रथ्यं । इंद्र । सं । किर । सत्रा । वाजं । न । जिग्युषे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे चित्र चायनीय वज्रहस्त वज्रबाहो आद्रिवो वज्रवन् । यद्वा ।
> अदृणात्यनेनेत्यद्रिरशनिः । तद्वन् । एवंभूतेंद्र धृष्णुया धृष्णुः शत्रूणां धर्षयिता महो महान् स तादृशस्त्वं स्तवानोऽस्माभिः स्तूयमानः सन् गां रथ्यं
> रथवाहनमश्वं च सं किर । सम्यक् प्रयच्छ । जिग्युषे जितवते पुरुषाय भोगार्थं
> सत्रा महत्पभूतं वाजं नान्नमिव । यथा शत्रून् जितवते भोर्गार्थं बह्वन्नं
> प्रयच्छसि तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wonderful (चित्र (*citra*), worthy of admiration) Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt in your hand (vajra-armed), possessor of the thunderbolt, or else, since the thunderbolt is that by which one tears, the possessor of that; such an Indra, bold (धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*), the assailer of enemies) and great: being praised by us, grant us (सं किर (*saṃ kira*), bestow well) the cow and the horse that draws the chariot. As you give abundant food (सत्रा (*satrā*), much) for enjoyment to a man who has conquered (जिग्युषे (*jigyuṣe*)), so do you give: this is the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चित्र (*citra*)—wonder-working
- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—holding the thunderbolt in the hand
- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—holding the thunderbolt **NOTE**
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*)—assailer of enemies
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great-souled
- सः (*saḥ*)—and renowned
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you

### Printed p. 166

- स्तवानः (*stavānaḥ*)—being praised by us
- जिग्युषे (*jigyuṣe*)—to a man who is victorious, for enjoyment
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—abundant
- वाजं न (*vājaṃ na*)—as you give food
- गां (*gāṃ*)—cattle
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—and horses
- सं किर (*saṃ kira*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wonder-working and holding the thunderbolt in your hand, you who are the assailer of enemies, great-souled and renowned, being praised by us, provide us too with cattle and horses, as you give abundant food to a man who is victorious, for enjoyment.

##### English translation
Wonderful wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra, the lord of clouds, mighty in resolution, being glorified by us. grant us cattle, and horses fit for chariots, as (you grant) abundant food to him who is victorious (in battle).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यः स॑त्रा॒हा विच॑र्षणि॒रिंद्रं॒ तं हू॑महे व॒यं ।  
> सह॑स्रमुष्क॒ तुवि॑नृम्म॒ सत्प॑ते॒ भवा॑ स॒मत्सु॑ नो वृ॒धे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । सत्राहा । विचर्षणिः । इंद्रं । तं । हूमहे । वयं ।  
> सहस्रमुष्क । तुविनृम्म । सत्पते । भव । समत्सु । नः । वृधे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये यः सत्राहेत्यादिसूक्तशेषः शंसनीयः । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिरिति शेषोऽयं ते अस्तु हर्यत इति सूक्ते । ऐ. आ. ५-२-४ ।
> इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने यः सत्राहेति प्रगाथो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । यः सत्राहा विचर्षणः स्वादोरित्था विषूवतः । आ. ७-४ ॥ इति ॥
> य इंद्रः सत्राहा महतां शत्रूणां हंता विचर्षणिर्विशेषेण सर्वस्य द्रष्टा
> तमिंद्रं वयं हूमहे । स्तुतिपदैराह्वयामः । उत्तरार्धः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे
> सहस्रमुष्क सहस्रशेफ । यां कां च स्त्रियं संभवन्निंद्रो भोगलोलुपतया

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Mahāvrata, in the niṣkevalya, the remainder of the sūkta beginning with यः सत्राहा (*yaḥ satrāhā*) is to be recited. For it is laid down: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिरिति शेषोऽयं ते अस्तु हर्यत इति सूक्ते । (*yaḥ satrāhā vicarṣaṇiriti śeṣo 'yaṃ te astu haryata iti sūkte |*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4) **GLOSS** On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the pragātha यः सत्राहेति (*yaḥ satrāheti*) is an optional anurūpa. And it is laid down in the sūtra: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणः स्वादोरित्था विषूवतः । (*yaḥ satrāhā vicarṣaṇaḥ svādoritthā viṣūvataḥ |*) (Ā. 7-4) **GLOSS** **NOTE** The Indra who is the slayer (सत्राहा (*satrāhā*)) of mighty enemies and the all-seer (विचर्षणिः (*vicarṣaṇiḥ*), he who sees everything in particular): that Indra we call (हूमहे (*hūmahe*)), summoning him with words of praise. The latter half is in the direct address. O thousand-organed one (सहस्रमुष्क (*sahasramuṣka*), with a thousand members), whatever woman Indra met, in his eagerness for enjoyment

### Printed p. 167

> स्वशरीरे पर्वणि पर्वणि शेफान् ससर्जेति कौषीतकिभिराम्नातं । तदभिप्रायेणेदं
> संबोधनं । हे तुविनृम्म बहुधन सत्पते सतां पालयितरिंद्र समत्सु संग्रामेषु
> नोऽस्माकं वृधे वर्धनाय भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

he sent forth organs in his own body, at every joint: so the Kauṣītakins have handed down. With this in mind the address is made. O you of much wealth (तुविनृम्म (*tuvinṛmma*)), O protector of the good (सत्पते (*satpate*)), Indra, be in battles (समत्सु (*samatsu*)) for our increase (वृधे (*vṛdhe*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who
- सत्राहा (*satrāhā*)—is the destroyer of enemies
- विचर्षणिः (*vicarṣaṇiḥ*)—is able to see everything
- तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*)—that same Indra
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- हूमहे (*hūmahe*)—call, praying
- सहस्रमुष्क (*sahasramuṣka*)—O you who have thousands of organs of enjoyment
- तुविनृम्म (*tuvinṛmma*)—who have many kinds of wealth
- सत्पते (*satpate*)—and are the protector of good men, O Indra
- समत्तु (*samattu*)—in battles
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- वृधे (*vṛdhe*)—as the increaser
- भव (*bhava*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who is the destroyer of enemies and is able to see everything, that same Indra we call, praying. O Indra, who have thousands of organs of enjoyment, who have many kinds of wealth and are the protector of good men, be the increaser for us in battles.

##### English translation
We invoke that Indra who is the destroyer of mighty foes, the supervisor (of all things): you, the many-organed, the protector to the good, the distributor of wealth, be unto us (the ensurer of) successs in combats.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśaka, at the time of the midday pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin may recite, optionally, for the anurūpa Ṛk, the Ṛk (pragātha) इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भर (*iṃdra jyeṣṭhaṃ na ā bhara*); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरा त्वा सहस्रमा शतं (*iṃdra jyeṣṭhaṃ na ā bharā tvā sahasramā śataṃ*) (Ā. 7-4).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बाध॑से॒ जना॑वृष॒भेव॑ म॒न्युना॒ फृषौ॑ मी॒ळ्ह ऋ॑चीषम ।  
> अ॒स्माकं॑ बोध्यवि॒ता म॑हाध॒ने त॒नूष्व॒प्सु सूर्ये॑ ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 168

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बाधसे । जनान् । वृषभा इव । मन्युना । फृष् । माळ्ही । ऋचीषम ।  
> अस्माकं । बोधि । अविता । महाधने । तनूषु । अप्सु । सूर्ये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋचीषम ऋचा सम ऋग्यादृशं रूपं प्रतिपादयति तादृग्रूपेंद्र
> घृषौ शत्रूणां घर्षके बाधके माळ्वे संग्रामे जनानस्मदीयान् शत्रून् वृषभेव
> वृषभेणेव बलवता मन्युना क्रोधेन बाधसे । बाधस्व । तथा महाधने महतो
> धनस्य निमित्तभूते संग्रामे चास्माकमविता रक्षिता बोधि । बुध्यस्व । रक्षितृत्वेनात्मानं
> जानीहि । रक्षको भवेति यावत् । किमर्थं । तनूषु तनयेष्टप्पूडकेषु सूर्ये
> च लब्धव्येषु सत्त्वतेषां लाभार्थं । सूर्यस्य लाभः संदर्शनं । तदर्थमित्यर्थः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ऋचीषम (*ṛcīṣama*), one who is like the Ṛk, that is, whose form is such as the Ṛk sets forth: such an Indra, in battle (माळ्वे (*māḷve*)), the crusher and harasser of enemies (घृषौ (*ghṛṣau*)), you assail (बाधसे (*bādhase*), assail!) the people, our enemies, with strong anger (मन्युना (*manyunā*)), as a bull would. And in the battle that is the cause of great wealth, be our protector (अविता (*avitā*)); बोधि (*bodhi*) means know yourself as protector, that is, be our protector. For what purpose? For the gain of those things that are to be obtained, among them the offspring (तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)), the waters, and the sun (सूर्ये (*sūrye*)); the gain of the sun is its sight; for that, is the meaning. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋचेषम (*ṛceṣama*)—O Indra, whose form is set forth by the Ṛk and the other mantras
- फृषौ (*phṛṣau*)—who assail enemies
- माळ्वे (*māḷve*)—in battle
- जनान् (*janān*)—the enemy people
- वृषभेव (*vṛṣabheva*)—like a bull
- मन्युना (*manyunā*)—with powerful anger
- बाधसे (*bādhase*)—destroy
- महाधने (*mahādhane*)—in the battle which is the cause of abundant wealth
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- अविता (*avitā*)—that you should be the protector
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know
- तनूषु (*tanūṣu*)—for the gain of sons and the rest
- अप्पु (*appu*)—and for the gain of water
- सूर्ये (*sūrye*)—and for our obtaining the light of the sun (be our protector)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whose form is set forth by the Ṛk and the other mantras, in the battle fought with enemies destroy the enemy people with anger as powerful as a bull's. Know that you should be our protector in the battle that is the cause of abundant wealth. And be our protector for the gain of sons and the rest for us, for the gain of water, and for our obtaining the light of the sun.

##### English translation
Such, Indra, as you are represented in holy texts, assail (our) adversaries with fierceness like (that of) a bull in close conflict: regard yourself as our defender in war, (that we may long enjoy) posterity, water, and the (sight of the) sun.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒ ज्येष्ठं॑ न॒ आ भ॑र॒ ओजि॑ष्ठं॒ पपु॑रि॒ श्रवः॑ ।  
> येने॒मे चि॑त्र वज्रहस्त॒ रोद॑सी॒ ओभे सु॑तिप्र॒ प्राः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । ज्येष्ठं । नः । आ । भर । ओजिष्ठं । पपुरि । श्रवः ।  
> येन । इमे इति । चित्र । वज्रहस्त । रोदसी इति । आ । उभे इति । सुशिप्र । प्राः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरेति
> प्रगाथो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरा त्वा सहस्रमा
> शतं । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र ज्येष्ठं प्रशस्यतममोजिष्ठमोजस्वितममतिशयेन बलकरं पपुरि
> पूरकं श्रवोऽन्नं नोऽस्मभ्यमा भर । आहर । प्रयच्छ । हे चित्र चायनीय
> वज्रहस्त वज्रबाहो हे सुशिप्र शोभनहनुक एवंभूत हे इंद्र येनान्नेनेमे
> परिदृश्यमाने उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावा प्रा आपूरयसि तदन्नमा भरेत्यन्वयः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the pragātha of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरेति (*iṃdra jyeṣṭhaṃ na ā bhareti*), is an optional anurūpa; this is laid down in the sūtra इंद्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरा त्वा सहस्रमा शतं (*iṃdra jyeṣṭhaṃ na ā bharā tvā sahasramā śataṃ*) (Ā. 7-4). O Indra, bring (आ भर (*ā bhara*), fetch, give) to us the food that is the best (ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*), the most praiseworthy), most vigorous (ओजिष्ठं (*ojiṣṭhaṃ*), exceedingly strengthening) and filling (पपुरि (*papuri*), that which fills). O wonderful one (चित्र (*citra*), worthy of admiration), holder of the thunderbolt in your hand, O fair-jawed one (सुशिप्र (*suśipra*), having a beautiful jaw), such an Indra: the food with which you fill (प्राः (*prāḥ*)) these two visible worlds, heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), bring us that food: this is the construction. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चित्र (*citra*)—attractive one
- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—you who have a hand holding the thunderbolt
- सुशिप्र (*suśipra*)—you who have an excellent jaw
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- येन (*yena*)—with which food
- इमे (*ime*)—these visible
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- आ प्राः (*ā prāḥ*)—you protect; such
- ज्येष्ठः (*jyeṣṭhaḥ*)—praiseworthy
- ओजिष्ठं (*ojiṣṭhaṃ*)—endowed with vigour
- पपुरि (*papuri*)—and the giver of creation
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring and give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, attractive, with a hand holding the thunderbolt and with an excellent jaw, bring and give us such praiseworthy food, endowed with vigour and the giver of nourishment, with which you protect these two visible worlds, heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 170

##### English translation
Indra, bring to us most excellent, most invigorating and nutritious food, wherewith, wonderful wielder of the thunderbolt, the handsome-chinned, you sustain both heaven and earth.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वामु॒ग्रमव॑से चर्षणी॒सहं॒ राज॑न्दे॒वेषु॑ हूमहे ।  
> विश्वा॒ सु नो॑ विधु॒रा पि॑ब्ब॒ना व॑सो॒ऽमित्रा॑न्तु॒षहा॑न्कृधि ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वां । उग्रं । अवसे । चर्षणीसहं । राजन् । देवेषु । हूमहे ।  
> विश्वा । सु । नः । विधुरा । पिब्बना । वसो इति । अमित्रान् । सुसहान् । कृधि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजन् राजमानेंद्र देवेषु देवानां मध्य उग्रमुद्गूर्णबलं
> चर्षणीसहं चर्षणीनां शत्रुभूतानां प्रजानामभिभवितारं त्वामवसे रक्षणाय
> हूमहे । आह्वयामः । त्वं विश्वा सर्वाणि पिब्बना पिब्बनानि रक्षांसि । पिहितमव्यक्तं
> शब्दयंत इति पिब्बनानि । पृषोदरादिः । तानि सु सुष्टु विथुरा व्यथितानि बाधितानि
> कुरु । हे वसो वासकेंद्र नोऽस्मदीयानमित्रान् शत्रुंश्च सुषहान् सुखेनाभिभवितुं शक्यान् कृधि । कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining (राजन् (*rājan*)) Indra, among the gods you are fierce (उग्रं (*ugraṃ*), of uplifted strength) and the overcomer (चर्षणीसहं (*carṣaṇīsahaṃ*)) of the carṣaṇīs, the peoples who are enemies; you we call (हूमहे (*hūmahe*), we summon) for protection. Make all the पिब्बना (*pibbanā*), the rākṣasas (so called because they utter muffled, indistinct sounds), well afflicted and hindered. O Vasu, giver of dwellings, Indra, make our enemies easy to overcome (सुषहान् (*suṣahān*)), that is, such as can be overcome with ease.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—O shining Indra
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—you who have exceedingly great strength
- चर्षणीसहं (*carṣaṇīsahaṃ*)—and who destroy enemy armies
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- हूमहे (*hūmahe*)—we call
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwellings
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- पिब्बना (*pibbanā*)—the rākṣasas
- सु (*su*)—completely
- विधुरा (*vidhurā*)—make them afflicted
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemies
- सुषहान् (*suṣahān*)—so that we may conquer them easily
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—help

### Printed p. 171

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Indra, you who among the gods have exceedingly great strength and who destroy enemy armies, we call you for protection. O Indra, giver of dwellings, make all the rākṣasas completely afflicted. Help us so that we may conquer our enemies easily.

##### English translation
We invoke for proteetion you, royal Indra, who are mighty amongst the gods, the subduer of men; granter of dwellings, repel all evil spirits, and render our enemies easy of discomfiture.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिं॑द्र॒ नाहु॑षी॒ष्वा ओजो॑ नृ॒ण्मं च॑ कृ॒ष्टिषु॑ ।  
> यद्वा॒ पंच॑ क्षिती॒नां द्यु॒म्नमा भ॑र स॒त्रा विश्वा॑नि॒ पौंस्या॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्र । नाहुषेषु । आ । ओजः । नृम्मं । च । कृष्णिषु ।  
> यत् । वा । पंच । क्षितीनां । द्युम्नं । आ । भर । सत्रा । विश्वानि । पौंस्या ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र नाहुषीषु । नहुष इति मनुष्यनाम । तत्संबंधिनीसु कृष्णिषु
> प्रजासु । आकारः समुच्चये । यच्चौजो बलं नृम्मं धनं च विद्यते । यद्वा
> यच्च पंच पंचानां क्षितीनां । निषादपंचमाश्चत्वारो वर्णाः पंच क्षितयः ।
> तेषां स्वरूपं द्युम्नं द्योतमानमन्नं तत्सर्वमस्मभ्यमा भर । आहर । प्रयच्छ
> तथा सत्रा महांति विश्वानि सर्वाणि पौंस्यानि बलानि चास्मभ्यमाहर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, among the Nāhuṣī (नाहुषीषु (*nāhuṣīṣu*)): Nahuṣa is a name for man, so the word means those connected with him, the peoples (कृष्णिषु (*kṛṣṇiṣu*)); the particle आ (*ā*) expresses combination. Whatever strength (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)) and wealth (नृम्मं (*nṛmmaṃ*)) there is among them; or else whatever there is of the five peoples (क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)), the four classes with the Niṣādas as the fifth being the five peoples, their own nature, the shining (द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*)) food: all that bring to us, give to us. And likewise bring to us all the great manly powers (पौंस्यानि (*pauṃsyāni*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नाहुषीषु (*nāhuṣīṣu*)—connected with man
- कृष्णिषु (*kṛṣṇiṣu*)—among the peoples
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—strength
- नृम्णं च (*nṛmṇaṃ ca*)—and wealth also there is
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or
- पंच क्षीतीनां (*paṃca kṣītīnāṃ*)—among the five peoples beginning with the Niṣādas
- द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*)—whatever shining food there is
- all that: आ भर (*ā bhara*)—provide for us
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—great
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—and all: give all the powers

### Printed p. 172

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whatever strength and wealth there is among the peoples connected with man, or whatever shining food there is among the five peoples beginning with the Niṣādas, provide all that for us. Give all the great and entire powers.

##### English translation
Whatever strength and opulence (exist) amongst human beings, whatever be the sustenance of the five classes of men, bring Indra to us, as well (as) all great manly energies.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद्वा॑ तृ॒क्षौ म॑घवन्नुद्रु॒ह्यावा जने॒ यत्पू॒रौ कच्च॒वृष्ण्यं॑ ।  
> अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ तद्रि॑रीहि॒ सं नृ॒षाह्ये॒ऽमित्रा॑न्पृ॒त्सु तु॒र्वणे॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । वा । तृक्षौ । मघवन् । द्रुह्यौ । आ । जने । यत् । पूरौ । कत् । च । वृष्टं ।  
> अस्मभ्यं । तत् । रिरीहि । सं । नृसह्ये । अमित्रान् । पृत्सु । तुर्वणे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र तृक्षावेतत्संज्ञॆ राजनि यद्वा यच्च बलं विद्यते
> द्रुह्यावा द्रुह्यौ चैतत्संज्ञॆ च जने यद्बलमस्ति । पूरावेतत्संज्ञॆ नृपे च यत्कच्च
> यत्किंचन वृष्ट्यं वीर्यं विद्यते तत्सर्वमस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यः सं सम्यग्रिरीहि ।
> प्रयच्छ । कदा । नृसह्ये नृभिर्योद्धृभिः सोढव्ये युद्धे प्रवृत्ते । किमर्थं ।
> पृत्सु पृतनासु संग्रामेष्टमित्रान् शत्रून् तुर्वणे तुर्वितुं हिंसितुं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra: whatever strength there is in Tṛkṣu (तृक्षावेतत्संज्ञॆ (*tṛkṣāvetatsaṃjñè*), the king of this name); or in Druhyu, of this name, and in the people (जने (*jane*)) whatever strength there is; and in Pūru, the king of this name, whatever manly vigour (वृष्ट्यं (*vṛṣṭyaṃ*)) there is: all that give fully (सं रिरीहि (*saṃ rirīhi*), give completely) to us who are your praisers. When? When a battle is undertaken (नृसह्ये (*nṛsahye*)), one to be endured by men, by warriors. For what purpose? In the encounters (पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*), in battles), to crush (तुर्वणे (*turvaṇe*), to destroy) the enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, possessor of wealth
- तृक्षौ (*tṛkṣau*)—in the king named Tṛkṣu
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or
- द्रुह्यौ (*druhyau*)—named Druhyu
- आ जने (*ā jane*)—in the multitude of people too
- पूरौ (*pūrau*)—in the king named Pūru too
- यत् कच्च (*yat kacca*)—of whatever kind

### Printed p. 173

- वृष्ट्यं (*vṛṣṭyaṃ*)—manly vigour there is, तत् (*tat*)—all that
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us who are praisers
- नृसह्ये (*nṛsahye*)—in confronting enemies
- पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*)—in battles
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemies
- तुर्वणे (*turvaṇe*)—to destroy
- सं रिरीहि (*saṃ rirīhi*)—give fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, possessor of wealth, whatever kind of vigour there is in the king named Tṛkṣu, or in the king named Druhyu, or in the king named Pūru, give all that fully to us, who are praisers, in battles in which enemies are confronted, so that we may destroy the enemies.

##### English translation
Whatever vigour, Maghavan, (existed) in Trikshu, in Druhyu, in Puru, bestow fully upon us in conflicts wish foes, so that we may destroy our enemies in war.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑ त्रि॒धातु॑ शर॒णं त्रि॒वरू॑थं स्वस्ति॒मत् ।  
> छ॒र्दिर्य॑च्छ म॒घव॑द्भ्यश्च॒ मह्यं॑ च या॒वया॑ दि॒द्युमे॑भ्यः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । त्रिधातु । शरणं । त्रिवरूथं । स्वस्तिमत् ।  
> छर्दिः । यच्छ । मघवत्भ्यः । च । मह्यं । च । यवय । दिद्युं । एभ्यः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि निष्केवल्ये इंद्र त्रिधात्विति वैरूपस्य सामप्रगाथः शंसनीयः।
> सूत्रितं च । इंद्र त्रिधातु शरणं त्वमिंद्र प्रशूर्तिषु । आ ७ ३ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र त्रिधातु त्रिप्रकारं त्रिभूमिकं त्रिवरूथं त्रयाणां शीतातपवर्षाणां
> वारकं स्वस्तिमदविनाशयुक्तं छर्दिश्चदिष्टिच्छादनयुक्तमेवंगुणविशिष्टं शरणं गृहं
> मघवद्भ्यश्च । मघं हविर्लक्षणं धनं । तद्वद्भ्यश्चास्मदीयेभ्यो मह्यं
> भरद्वाजाय च यच्छ । देहि । अपि चैभ्यः सकाशाद्विद्युं शत्रुप्रेरितं द्योतमानमायुधं यवय । पृथक्कुरु ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, in the niṣkevalya, the sāma-pragātha of the Vairūpa beginning इंद्र त्रिधातु (*iṃdra tridhātu*) is to be recited. It is laid down in the sūtra: इंद्र त्रिधातु शरणं त्वमिंद्र प्रशूर्तिषु (*iṃdra tridhātu śaraṇaṃ tvamiṃdra praśūrtiṣu*) (Ā. 7 3). **NOTE** O Indra, give a dwelling (शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*), a house) that is threefold (त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*): of three kinds, of three storeys), a warder-off of three things, cold, heat and rain (त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)), secure (स्वस्तिमत् (*svastimat*), free from destruction), furnished with a covering (छर्दिः (*chardiḥ*)) **NOTE**; a house of such qualities: give it to those of ours who are possessed of wealth (मघवद्भ्यश्च (*maghavadbhyaśca*): magha is wealth in the form of oblations) and to me, Bharadvāja. And separate from them (यवय (*yavaya*), put apart) the flaming (दिद्युं (*didyuṃ*)) weapon sent by the enemy.

### Printed p. 174

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—which is of three kinds
- त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)—which can protect from cold, sunshine and rain
- स्वस्तिमत् (*svastimat*)—which is auspicious
- छर्दिः (*chardiḥ*)—which is protective
- शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*)—a house
- मघवद्ध्यः (*maghavaddhyaḥ*)—to our kinsmen, who have wealth in the form of oblations
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—and to me, Bharadvāja
- यच्छ (*yaccha*)—grant
- एभ्यः (*ebhyaḥ*)—from these houses
- दिद्युं (*didyuṃ*)—the flaming (and enemy-sent) weapons
- यवयॆ (*yavayè*)—put apart

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, grant a house that is of three kinds, that can protect from cold, sunshine and rain, that is auspicious and protective, to our kinsmen, who are ready to offer oblations, and to me, Bharadvāja. Keep far from these houses the flaming weapon of the enemies, sent by the enemy, so that no harm may come to it.

##### English translation
Give, Indra, to the affluent, and to me also, a sheltering and prosperous dwelling, combining three elements, and defending in three ways, and keep from them the blazing (weapon of our foes).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśaka, when the niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited, this Ṛk, इंद्र त्रिधातु (*iṃdra tridhātu*), is to be recited for the sāma-pragātha mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, इंद्र त्रिधातु शरणं त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु (*iṃdra tridhātu śaraṇaṃ tvamiṃdra pratūrtiṣu*) (Ā. 7-3).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये ग॑व्य॒ता मन॑सा॒ शत्रु॑माद॒भुर॑भिप्र॒घ्नंति॑ धृष्णु॒या ।  
> अध॑ स्मा नो मघवन्निंद्र गिर्वणस्तनू॒पा अंत॑मो भव ॥ ०॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । गव्यता । मनसा । शत्रुं । आदभुः । अभिप्रघ्नंति । धृष्णुया ।  
> अध । स्म । नः । मघवन् । इंद्र । गिर्वणः । तनूपाः । अंतमः । भव ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 175

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये जना गव्यता शत्रुणां गा इच्छता मनसा युक्ताः संतः शत्रुं शायितारं
> वैरिणमादभुः अहिंसिषुः । ये च धृष्टया धृष्टवो धृष्टाः संतोऽस्मानभिलक्ष्य
> प्रघ्नंति प्रकर्षेण हिंसंति हे मघवन् धनवन् गिर्वणो गिरां संभक्तरिंद्र अध
> स्मास्मिन्काले तेभ्यः सकाशात् नोऽस्माकं तनूपास्तनूनां शरीराणां रक्षिता सन्
> अंतमोऽन्तिकतमो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those men who, endowed with a mind that desires the cows (गव्यता (*gavyatā*)) of their enemies, slew (आदभुः (*ādabhuḥ*), did violence to) the enemy, the foe (शायितारं (*śāyitāraṃ*)); and those who, bold (धृष्टया (*dhṛṣṭayā*)), aiming at us, strike (प्रघ्नंति (*praghnaṃti*), hurt violently): O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, sharer of songs (गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)), at this time, from those, be the protector of our bodies (तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)) and be nearest to us (अंतमः (*aṃtamaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy
- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—and one to be reached by praise
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—Indra
- ये (*ye*)—those men who
- गव्यता (*gavyatā*)—desiring to obtain cows (from the enemies)
- मनसा (*manasā*)—endowed with such a mind
- शत्रुं (*śatruṃ*)—the enemy
- आदभुः (*ādabhuḥ*)—have slain (and who)
- धृष्णुया (*dhṛṣṇuyā*)—with a mind that assails enemies
- प्रघ्नंति (*praghnaṃti*)—strike (like such men)
- अध स्मै (*adha smai*)—at this time
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)—as the protector of the body
- अंतमः (*aṃtamaḥ*)—exceedingly near
- भव (*bhava*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, one to be reached by praise, like those men who, endowed with a mind that desires to obtain cows from the enemies, have slain the enemy, and who strike with a mind that assails enemies, be exceedingly near to us at this time.

##### English translation
Affluent Indra, propitiated by praise, be near to us, the defender of our persons (against those) who assail (us as) enemies, with a mind bent upon carrying off (our) cattle, or who assault us with arrogance.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अध स्म तदानीं नोऽस्माकं वृधे वर्धनाय भव । आपि च नायं
> योऽस्माकं नयो नेता युधि युद्धे तमप्यव । रक्ष । तदेत्युक्तं कदेत्यत आह ।
> पर्णिनः पक्षवंतस्तिग्ममूर्धानस्तीक्ष्णास्या दिद्यवो दीप्ता वाहा यद्यदांतरिक्षे
> व्योम्मि पतयंति शत्रुभिर्विसृष्टाः पतंति तदानीं वृधे भवेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, at that time be for our growth, and protect in battle whoever is our leader. Sāyaṇa supplies the answer to "at what time?": when the feathered, sharp-pointed, shining वाहा (*vāhā*) **NOTE** ones, let loose by the enemies, fall through the sky, then be for our growth. This is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- पर्णिनः (*parṇinaḥ*)—the feathered ones
- तिग्ममूर्धानः (*tigmamūrdhānaḥ*)—the ones with sharp points
- दिद्यवः (*didyavaḥ*)—and shining ones, the arrows (sent by the enemies)
- अंतरिक्षे (*aṃtarikṣe*)—from the sky
- पतयंति (*patayaṃti*)—fall (upon us)
- अध स्म (*adha sma*)—immediately then
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वृधे (*vṛdhe*)—as one who brings increase
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- युधि (*yudhi*)—in battle
- नायं (*nāyaṃ*)—our leader
- अव (*ava*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when the feathered, sharp-pointed and shining arrows of the enemies, sent by the enemies, fall upon us from the sky, be to us one who brings increase (a protector). Protect our leader in battle.

##### English translation
Indra, be (favourable) at present to our success: protect our leader in battle when the feathered, sharp-pointed, shining shafts fall from the sky.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्र॒ शूरा॑सस्त॒न्वो॑ वितन्व॒ते प्रि॒या शर्म॑ पित्ृ॒णां ।  
> अध॑ स्मा यच्छ त॒न्वे॒३॒॑३ तने॑ च छ॒र्दिर॒चित्तं॑ या॒वय॒ द्वेषः॑॥१२।  
> । चदचा ।  
> यत्र । शूरासः । तन्वः । वितन्वते । प्रिया । शर्म । पित्ृणां ॥  
> अध॑ । स्म । यच्छ । त॒न्वे॒३॒॑ । तने॑ । च । भ॒र्दिः । अ॒चित्तं॑ । य॒वय॒ । द्वेषः॑ ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 177

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र यस्मिन्काले शूरासः शूराः शौर्यवंतो योद्धारस्तन्नः स्वकीयानि
> शरीराणि वितन्वते विस्तारयंति स्वामिनो जयाय शत्रुणां पुरतो दर्शयंति ।
> तथास्मिन्काले प्रिया प्रियाणि शर्म शर्माणि स्थानानि पित्ृणां जनकानां संबंधीनि ।
> तैरर्जितानीति यावत् । एतानि च वितन्वते शत्रुणां पुरस्ताद्वि स्तरयंति । परित्यजंतीति
> यावत । अध स्मास्मिन्काले तन्ने शरीराय तने तनयाय च छर्दिश्वादनमायुधानां
> निवारकं कवचमचित्तं शत्रुभिरज्ञातं यथा भवति तथा यच्छ । प्रयच्छ । शत्रुज्ञानातूर्वमेव देहीत्यर्थः । अपि च द्वेषो द्वेष्टान् शत्रुन्यावय । तेभ्यो
> वियोजय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the time when the brave warriors spread out their own bodies, that is, show them before the enemies for their master's victory, at that time they leave behind the pleasant dwellings that belong to their fathers, that is, that were acquired by them; they spread these out before the enemies, which means they abandon them. Then, at this time, for the body (तन्ने (*tanne*)) and for the offspring (तने (*tane*)) grant armour (छर्दिः (*chardiḥ*)), a covering that wards off weapons, in such a way that it is unknown to the enemies, that is, give it before the enemies know of it. And drive away the haters, the enemies: separate them from us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यत्र (*yatra*)—at which time
- शोरासः (*śorāsaḥ*)—valiant warriors
- तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—their bodies
- वितन्वते (*vitanvate*)—spread out on the battlefield (for the master's victory), at that time
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—pleasant ones
- पितृणां (*pitṛṇāṃ*)—and inherited from fathers
- शर्म (*śarma*)—dwellings (they abandon)
- अध स्म (*adha sma*)—in that circumstance
- तन्ने (*tanne*)—for the protection of their bodies
- तने (*tane*)—and of sons and others
- छर्दिः (*chardiḥ*)—the armour that protects their bodies
- अचित्तं (*acittaṃ*)—so that the enemies do not know it
- यच्छ (*yaccha*)—cause to be given
- द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)—the enemies
- यावय (*yāvaya*)—conquer and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, at the time when valiant warriors spread out their bodies on the battlefield for their master's victory, they abandon their own houses, which are pleasant, inherited from their fathers and protective. At that time give armour, unknown to the enemies, for the protection of their bodies and of their sons and others. And destroy the enemies.

##### English translation
When heroes rest their persons (until abandoning) the pleasant abodes of their progenitors: grant us, for ourselves and our posterity, an unsuspected defence, and scatter our enemies.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिं॑द्र॒ सर्गे॒ अर्व॑तश्चो॒दया॑से महाध॒ने ।  
> अ॒स॒म॒ने अध्व॑नि वृजि॒ने प॒थि श्ये॒नाइ॑व श्रवस्य॒तः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 178

> यत् । इंद्र । सर्गे । अर्वतः । चोदयासे । महाधने ।  
> असमने । अध्वनि । वृजिने । पथि । श्येनान् इव । श्रवस्यतः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र महाधने जेतव्यस्य महतो धनस्य निमित्ते महति संग्रामे
> सर्ग उद्योगे सत्यसमने विषमेऽध्वनि मार्गेऽर्वतोऽस्मदीयानश्वान्यद्यदा
> चोदयासे प्रेरयसि । वृजिने कुटिले पथि मार्गेऽंतरिक्षलक्षणे श्रवस्यतः
> श्रवोऽन्नमामिषरूपमात्मन इच्छतः श्येनानिव यथामिषार्थिन श्येना अंतरिक्षे
> शीघ्रं गच्छंति तथास्मदीयानश्वान्यदा त्वं शीघ्रं गमयसि तदानीमस्माकं तन्ने
> तनयाय च छर्दिर्यच्छेति पूर्वस्यामृचि संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when in a great battle (महाधने (*mahādhane*)), that is, a battle fought for the sake of great wealth that is to be won, at the time of the effort (सर्गे (*sarge*), that is, exertion) you urge our horses along an uneven, rough road, and along the crooked path that is the sky, as falcons that desire food in the form of flesh (श्रवस्यतः (*śravasyataḥ*): śravaḥ is food, flesh) fly swiftly in the sky for the sake of that food, so, when you make our horses go swiftly, then give armour for our body and our offspring: this is the connection with the preceding Ṛk. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृजिने (*vṛjine*)—on the crooked
- पथि (*pathi*)—path that is the sky
- श्रवस्यतः (*śravasyataḥ*)—seeking food in the form of flesh
- श्येनानिव (*śyenāniva*)—as falcons fly swiftly
- महाधने (*mahādhane*)—in a battle for the sake of abundant wealth
- सर्गे (*sarge*)—at the time of the effort
- असमने (*asamane*)—uneven, full of pits and mounds
- अध्वनि (*adhvani*)—on the road
- अर्वशः (*arvaśaḥ*)—our horses
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- चोदयासे (*codayāse*)—you urge (to run swiftly) (then give protective armour)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when, in a battle for the sake of abundant wealth, at the time of the effort, you urge our horses to run swiftly on a road full of pits and mounds and uneven, as falcons that seek food in the form of flesh fly swiftly on the crooked path of the sky, then give protective armour.

##### English translation
(At the time) when, in the effort (made) in an arduous conflict; urge our horses over an uneven road, like falcons darting upon their food through the difficult path (of the firmament).

### Printed p. 179

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सिंधू॑रिव प्रव॒ण आ॑शु॒या य॒तो यदि॒ क्लोश॒मनु॒ स्वणि॑ ।  
> आ ये वयो॒ न वर्वृ॑त॒त्यामि॑षि गृभी॒ता बा॒ह्वर्गवि॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सिंधून् इव । प्रवणे । आशुया । यतः । यदि । क्लोशं । अनु । स्वनि ।  
> आ । ये । वयः । न । वर्वृतति । आमिषि । गृभीताः । बाह्वोः । गवि ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उक्तस्यैवार्थस्यातिशयप्रतिपादनार्थेयं । प्रवणे निम्म देशे सिंधूनिव
> स्यंदमाना नदीरिवाशुयाशु शीघ्रं यतो गच्छतोऽश्वान् हे इंद्र यदि
> चोदयासे प्रेरयसि । कदा । क्लोशमनु । क्लोश इति भयनाम । भयमनुलक्ष्य
> स्वनि स्वन आक्रोशे सति । कीदृशास्तेऽश्वाः । बाह्वोर्बाहुमूलयोर्गृभीताः
> कक्षया बद्धा येऽश्वा गवि गोरूपे धने जेतव्ये सत्या वर्वृतति पुनः पुनरावर्तंते । आमिष्यामिषे मांसे ग्रहीतव्ये सति वयो न यथा श्येनादयः दक्षिणः
> पुनः पुनरावर्तंते तद्वत् । एवंभूतानश्वान् भयेन क्रोशे सति यदा त्वं
> प्रेरयसि तदानीमस्मदीयेभ्यश्वर्दिः प्रयच्छेति संबंधः । यद्यप्यषेयूर्द्धे
> प्रसक्तिर्नास्ति तथापि राजपुरोहितत्वेन राजकीयानां पुरुषाणां जयः प्रार्थ्यत
> इति न कश्चिद्विरोधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is meant to establish with emphasis the meaning already stated. O Indra, if you urge horses that go swiftly (आशुया (*āśuyā*)), like streams (सिंधूनिव (*siṃdhūniva*)) flowing down a slope (प्रवणे (*pravaṇe*)); when? क्लोशमनु (*klośamanu*): क्लोश (*klośa*) is a name for fear; with regard to fear, when there is a cry (स्वनि (*svani*), in the sense of a cry). What kind are those horses? Those that are held (गृभीताः (*gṛbhītāḥ*)) at the arm-roots (बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)), that is, bound by the girth, and that, when wealth in the form of cattle (गवि (*gavi*)) is to be won, turn back again and again (वर्वृतति (*varvṛtati*)); when flesh (आमिषि (*āmiṣi*)) is to be seized they turn again and again, like birds (वयो न (*vayo na*)) such as falcons. When you urge such horses while there is a cry through fear, then give armour for those who belong to us: this is the connection. And though the ṛṣi has no occasion in war **NOTE**, yet, since he is the king's chief priest, victory is prayed for the king's men, so there is no contradiction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) आमिषि (*āmiṣi*)—to obtain flesh
- वयो न (*vayo na*)—as falcons and other birds come running again and again
- बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)—at the arm-roots
- गृभीताः (*gṛbhītāḥ*)—which are bound with a girth
- ये (*ye*)—those horses
- गवि (*gavi*)—for the sake of cattle
- आ वर्वृतति (*ā varvṛtati*)—which come again and again
- क्लोशमनु (*klośamanu*)—from fear
- स्वनि (*svani*)—even though they are neighing
- प्रवणे (*pravaṇe*)—in low-lying places
- सिंधूनिव (*siṃdhūniva*)—like rapidly flowing rivers
- आशुया (*āśuyā*)—very swiftly
- यतः (*yataḥ*)—as they run
- यदि (*yadi*)—when you urge (then give armour for war)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, those horses which are bound with a girth at the arm-roots, and which come back again and again for the sake of cattle, as falcons and other birds come running again and again to obtain flesh, even though those horses are neighing through fear, when you urge them to run very swiftly, like rivers flowing rapidly in low-lying places, then give armour for war.

### Printed p. 180

##### English translation
Rushing rapidly like rivers in their downward course, and although neighing loudly through terror, they yet, tight-girthed, return repeatedly (to the conflict) for cattle, like birds darting on their prey.

## Sūkta 47 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वादुरित्येकत्रिंशदृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तं भरद्वाजपुत्रस्य गर्गस्यार्षं। प्रस्तोक
> इन्नित्येषा त्रिष्टुप् दशाश्वानित्यनुष्टुप् दश रथानिति गायत्री महि राध इति द्विपदा
> द्वैकादशका युजानो हरितेत्येषा बृहती दिवस्पृथिव्या इति जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः ।
> आदितः पंचानामृचां सोमो देवता । अगव्यूति क्षेत्यमित्यर्धर्चप्रथमपादे
> देवा उत्तरस्य भूमिस्कृतीयस्य बृहस्पतिश्चतुर्थस्येंद्रः । प्रस्तोक इत्याद्याश्चतस्रः
> सृंजयपुत्रस्य राज्यो दानस्तुतिरूपत्वात्तद्देवताकाः । वनस्पते वीड्वंग इत्ययं
> तृचो रथदेवत्यः । उप श्वासयेति तृचो दुंदुभिदेवत्यः । समश्वपर्णा इत्यर्धर्च
> ऐंद्रः । शिष्टा इंद्रदेवताकाः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । स्वादुरेकत्रिंशद्गर्गः पंचादौ
> सौम्योऽगप्यूत्यर्धर्चो लिंगोक्तदेवतः प्रस्तोक इति त्रिष्टुबनुष्टुब्जायत्री
> द्विपदा सार्ङ्मयस्य प्रस्तोकस्य दानस्तुतिः परौ तृचौ रथदुंदुभिदेवत्यावैंद्रोऽत्यर्थर्चो युजानो बृहती दिवस्पृथिव्या जगती ॥ अग्निमारुत
> आदितश्चतस्रः शंसनीयाः । सूत्रितं च । स्वादुष्किलायमिति चतस्रो मध्यॆ जाह्वानं ।
> अ. ५-२० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fourth sūkta, beginning स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*), has thirty-one Ṛks; its seer is Garga, son of Bharadvāja. The Ṛk प्रस्तोक इन्नु (*prastoka innu*) is in the triṣṭubh metre, दशाश्वान् (*daśāśvān*) in anuṣṭubh, दश रथान् (*daśa rathān*) in gāyatrī, महि राधः (*mahi rādhaḥ*) a dvipadā of two lines of eleven syllables, युजानो हरित (*yujāno harita*) a bṛhatī, दिवस्पृथिव्याः (*divaspṛthivyāḥ*) a jagatī, and the rest are triṣṭubh. The deity of the first five Ṛks is Soma. In the first line of the half-verse अगव्यूति क्षेत्रं (*agavyūti kṣetraṃ*) the deities are the gods named in it; the next line has Bhūmi, the third Bṛhaspati and the fourth Indra. The four Ṛks beginning प्रस्तोक (*prastoka*) are in praise of the gift of the king Prastoka, son of Sṛñjaya, and so have that as deity. The three beginning वनस्पते वीड्वंगः (*vanaspate vīḍvaṃgaḥ*) have the chariot as deity; the three beginning उप श्वासय (*upa śvāsaya*) have the drum (dundubhi) as deity. The half-verse समश्वपर्णाः (*samaśvaparṇāḥ*) is addressed to Indra; the rest have Indra as deity. He quotes the Anukramaṇī to the same effect. He adds that it is prescribed in the sūtra: the four Ṛks beginning स्वादुष्किलायं (*svāduṣkilāyaṃ*) are recited in the middle (of the invocations), reference A. 5-20. **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the fourth Anuvāka. It has thirty-one Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Garga, son of the ṛṣi Bharadvāja. Of this sūkta, the Ṛk beginning "Prastoka inn" (the 22nd) is in the triṣṭubh metre; the Ṛk beginning "daśāśvān" (the 23rd) is in the anuṣṭubh metre; the Ṛk beginning "daśa rathān" (the 24th) is in the gāyatrī metre; the Ṛk beginning "mahi rādhaḥ" (the 25th) is in the metre called dvipadā, with two lines of eleven syllables; the Ṛk beginning "yujāno daritā" (the 19th) **NOTE** is in the bṛhatī metre; the Ṛk beginning "divaspṛthivyāḥ" (the 27th) is in the jagatī metre. The remaining Ṛks are in the triṣṭubh metre. The deity of the first five Ṛks of this sūkta is Soma. For the first line of the first half of the twentieth Ṛk, "agavyūti kṣetram", the deities are those mentioned in it; for the second line the deities are Bhūmi, for the third line Bṛhaspati, and for the fourth line Indra. In the four Ṛks beginning with "Prastoka" (22-25) there is praise of the gift of the king named Prastoka, son of Sṛñjaya, so the deity of those four Ṛks is the praise of Prastoka's gift. For the three Ṛks beginning with "vanaspate vīḍvaṅgaḥ" (26-28) the chariot is the deity. For the three beginning with "upaśvāsaya" (24-31) **NOTE**, except the latter half of the last Ṛk, the drum is the deity. For the latter half of the thirty-first Ṛk, "samaśvaparṇāḥ", Indra is the deity. For all the remaining Ṛks Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: स्वादुरेकत्रिंशद्गर्गः पंचादौ सौम्योऽगव्यूत्यर्धर्चो लिंगोक्तदेवतः प्रस्तोक इति त्रिष्टुबनुष्टुब्बायत्री द्विपदा सांजयस्य प्रस्तोकस्य दानस्तुतिः परौ तृचौ रथदुंदुभिदेवत्यावैंद्रोऽन्त्यर्थर्चो युजानो बृहती त्रिष्टुम्महि द्विपदा दिवस्पृथिव्या जगती (*svādurekatriṃśadgargaḥ paṃcādau saumyo 'gavyūtyardharco liṃgoktadevataḥ prastoka iti triṣṭubanuṣṭubbāyatrī dvipadā sāṃjayasya prastokasya dānastutiḥ parau tṛcau rathaduṃdubhidevatyāvaiṃdro 'ntyartharco yujāno bṛhatī triṣṭummahi dvipadā divaspṛthivyā jagatī*). That the first four Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited for the Āgnimāruta śastra mantras is made clear by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, स्वादुष्किलायमिति चतस्रो मध्यॆ चाह्वानां (*svāduṣkilāyamiti catasro madhyè cāhvānāṃ*) (Ā. 5-20).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वा॒दुष्किला॒यं मधु॑मा उ॒तायं ती॒व्रः किला॒यं रस॑वा  ॒
> उतायं ।  
> उ॒तो न्व१॒ं॑स्य प॑पि॒वांस॒मिंद्रं॒ न कश्च॒न स॑हत आह॒वेषु॑ ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 182

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वादुः । किल । अयं । मधुमान् । उत । अयं । तीव्रः । किल । आयं । रसवान् ।  
> उत । अयं ।  
> उतो इति । नु । अस्य । पपिवांसं । इंद्रं । न । कः । चन । सहते । आहवेषु ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमभिषुतः सोमः स्वादुरास्वादनीयः किल भवति । उतापि च मधुमान्माधुर्यवांश्चायं सोमो भवति ! तथायं सोमस्तीव्रः किल मदोत्पादने
> तीक्ष्णः खलु भवति । उतापि चायं सोमो रसवान् सारवांश्च भवति । अनेन
> वाक्यचतुष्टयेन सोमस्य माधुर्यातिशयत्वं च प्रतिपादितं ! उतो आपि चास्य
> सोमस्य !! द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी ॥ इमं सोमं पपिवांसं पीतवंतमिंद्रमाहवेषु
> संग्रामेषु न कश्चन न कोऽपि सहते अभिभवति । नु इति पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This pressed Soma is indeed sweet to the taste (स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*)). It is also honeyed (मधुमान् (*madhumān*)), that is, full of sweetness. This Soma is likewise keen (तीव्रः (*tīvraḥ*)): in producing intoxication it is sharp. And it is full of juice (रसवान् (*rasavān*)), that is, full of essence. By these four statements the surpassing sweetness of Soma is set forth. Further, no one in battles can overcome Indra, who has drunk (पपिवांसं (*papivāṃsaṃ*)) this Soma. The word नु (*nu*) is a mere filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this pressed Soma
- स्वादुः किल (*svāduḥ kila*)—is certainly savoury
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this
- मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—is endowed with sweetness
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this same Soma juice
- तीव्रः किल (*tīvraḥ kila*)—has a sharpness that causes intoxication
- उत (*uta*)—moreover
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this same Soma
- रसवान् (*rasavān*)—is full of essence
- उतो (*uto*)—and
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma
- पपिवांसं (*papivāṃsaṃ*)—who drinks
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- आहवेषु (*āhaveṣu*)—in battles
- कश्चन (*kaścana*)—no one at all
- न सहते नु (*na sahate nu*)—can withstand and defeat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This pressed Soma is certainly savoury. It is endowed with sweetness and full of juice, and moreover has a sharpness that causes intoxication. No one in battles can withstand and defeat Indra who drinks this Soma juice.

##### English translation
Savoury indeed is this (Soma); sweet is it, sharp, and full of flavour: no one is able to encounter Indra in battles after he has been quaffing this (beverage).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं स्वा॒दुरि॒ह मदि॑ष्ट आस॒ यस्येंद्रो॑ वृत्र॒हत्ये॑ म॒माद॑ ।  
> पु॒रूणि॒ यश्चा॒त्ना शंब॑रस्य॒ विन॑व॒तिं नव॑ च दे॒ह्यो॒३॒॑३ हन्॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । स्वादुः । इह । मदिष्टः । आस । यस्य । इंद्रः । वृत्रहत्ये । ममाद ।  
> पुरूणि । यः । च्यौत्ना । शंबरस्य । वि । नवतिं । नव । च । देह्यः । हन् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इहास्मिन्यज्ञेयं सोमः स्वादुरास्वादितः पीतः सन् मदिष्टोऽतिशयेन
> मदयितास । बभूव । यस्य सोमस्य पानेनेंद्रो वृत्रहत्ये वृत्रहननकाले
> ममाद मत्तो बभूव । यः सोमः शंबरस्यासुरस्य पुरूणि बहूनि च्यौत्ना
> च्यौत्नानि बलानि जघान । तथा देहो दिग्धा उपचिता आसुरीः पुरीः तदीयान्
> देहान् वा नवतिं नव च नवोत्तरनवतिसंख्याका यः सोमो वि हन् व्यहन् अयं
> सोम इति प्रथमपादेन संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here, in this sacrifice, this Soma, tasted, that is, drunk, has become most intoxicating, intoxicating to the highest degree. By drinking this Soma Indra became exhilarated at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra. This Soma also destroyed the many strengths (च्यौत्ना (*cyautnā*)) of the asura Śambara. Likewise, the Soma destroyed ninety-nine (नवतिं नव च (*navatiṃ nava ca*)) of the demons' strongholds, built-up and accumulated ones (देहो (*deho*)), or else their bodies. This is connected with अयं सोमः (*ayaṃ somaḥ*), "this Soma", of the first line.

- and (यस्य (*yasya*)—by drinking which Soma)
- नवतिं नव च (*navatiṃ nava ca*)—ninety-nine in number

- asura cities

- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this Soma

- स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*)—is savoury
- मदिष्टः (*madiṣṭaḥ*)—and intoxicating
- आस (*āsa*)—is

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By drinking which Soma Indra obtained exhilaration at the time of slaying the asura Vṛtra, which Soma became the means of killing the numerous armies of the asura Śambara, and by drinking which he slew the ninety-nine firm cities of the asuras, this Soma is, in this sacrifice, savoury and intoxicating.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं मे॑ पी॒त उदि॑यर्ति॒ वाच॑म॒यं म॑नी॒षामु॑श॒तीम॑जीगति ।  
> अ॒यं षु॒र्वीर॑मिमित॒ धीरो॒ न याभ्यो॒ भुव॑नं॒ कच्च॒नारे॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । मे । पीतः । उत् । इयर्ति । वाचं । अयं । मनीषां । उशतीं ।  
> अजीगरिति ।  
> अयं । षट् । उर्वीष । अमिमात । धीरः । याभ्यः । भुवनं । कत् । चन । आरे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सोमः पीतः सन् मे मम वाचमुदियर्ति । उद्गमयति ।
> अयमेव सोम उशतीं कांतां मनीषां बुद्धिमुदजीगः । उद्गारयति ।
> प्रकाशयति ॥ गृ निगरण इत्यस्माण्ण्यंताल्लुजि चजा रूपं ॥ अपि चायं धीरो धीमान्
> सोमः सळुर्विः षण्मोर्वीरंहसस्पांतु द्यौष्ट पृथिवी चाहश्च रात्रिश्चापश्चाधयश्चेति प्रतिपादिता द्युपृथिव्याद्याः षडमिमीत । निर्मितवान् । याभ्य उर्विभ्य आरे
> दूरे विप्रकृष्टे देशे कच्चन किंचन भुवनं भूतजातं न भवति अपि त्वास्वेव सर्वं
> भूतजातं वर्तते तावृशीरुर्निर्निर्मितवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, when drunk, brings forth, that is, makes manifest, my speech (वाचं (*vācaṃ*)). This same Soma brings forth and makes manifest the desired (उशतीं (*uśatīṃ*)), lovely intelligence (मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)). And this wise Soma created the six wide ones **NOTE**, which are set forth as heaven and earth, day and night, the waters and the plants. Than these wide ones, far away, in a distant place, there is no other being or world whatever; rather, all beings exist in these very ones. Such wide ones he created.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this same Soma
- उततीं (*utatīṃ*)—attractive
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—intelligence
- अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)—makes grow sharp
- याभ्यः (*yābhyaḥ*)—than which principles

- आरे (*āre*)—surpassing
- कच्चन भुवनं (*kaccana bhuvanaṃ*)—any other world

- षट्.उर्विः (*ṣaṭ.urviḥ*)—six worlds beginning with the heavenly world
- धीरः (*dhīraḥ*)—wise

- अमिमीत (*amimīta*)—created

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma juice, when drunk, makes my speech manifest. This same Soma makes the attractive intelligence grow sharp. This wise Soma king created the six principles, the heavenly world, the earth, day, night, waters and plants, beyond which there is no other world.

##### English translation
This beverage inspires my speech; this develops the desired intelligence: this sagacious (Soma) has created the six vast conditions, from which no creature is distinct.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अयं । पीयूषं । तिसृषु । प्रवत्सु । सोमः । दाधार । उरु । अंतरिक्षं ॥ ४ ॥

> तथोरु विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षं च धारयति । कथा च मंत्रातरं । त्वमिमा ओषधीः
> सोम विश्वास्त्वमपो अजनयस्त्वं गाः । त्वमा ततंथोर्वंतरिक्षं ऋग्वे.
> १-९१-२२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is that Soma who made the extent (वरिमाणं (*varimāṇaṃ*)), the wideness and expansion, of the earth. Likewise this Soma made the compactness (वर्ष्णाणं (*varṣṇāṇaṃ*)), the firmness, of the heaven. **NOTE** This Soma also holds the juice, the ambrosia (पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)), in the three **NOTE**, in these excellent ones (प्रवत्सु (*pravatsu*)). And he holds up the wide firmament. He quotes another mantra: त्वमिमा ओषधीः सोम विश्वास्त्वमपो अजनयस्त्वं गाः । त्वमा ततंथोर्वंतरिक्षं (*tvamimā oṣadhīḥ soma viśvāstvamapo ajanayastvaṃ gāḥ | tvamā tataṃthorvaṃtarikṣaṃ*) (Ṛgve. 1-91-22) **GLOSS** **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth

- अकृणोत् (*akṛṇot*)—has made
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- आयं सोमः (*āyaṃ somaḥ*)—is this Soma king
- आयं सः (*āyaṃ saḥ*)—this same Soma
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- वर्ष्णाणं (*varṣṇāṇaṃ*)—the firmness (he made)
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Soma
- प्रवत्सु (*pravatsu*)—in the excellent
- तिसृषु (*tisṛṣu*)—plants, waters and cows
- पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)—the juice of the nature of ambrosia
- दाधार (*dādhāra*)—has filled
- उरु (*uru*)—the wide
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—firmament (he has upheld)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

He who made the earth exceedingly wide, he who made the heavenly world stand firm, is this Soma king. This same Soma has filled the most excellent plants, waters and cows with the juice of the nature of ambrosia. And he has upheld the wide firmament.

##### English translation
This it is which has formed the earth, the compactness of the heaven : this soma has deposited the ambrosia in its three principal (receptacles). and has upheld the spacious firmament.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं वि॑दच्चित्र॒दृशी॑क॒मर्णः॑ शु॒क्रस॑द्मनामु॒षसा॒मनी॑के ।  
> अ॒यं म॒हान्म॑ह॒ता स्कंभ॑ने॒नोद्द्याम॑स्तभ्नाद्वृष॒भोः  ॒॑
> मरुत्वान् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । विदत् । चित्रदृशीकं । अर्णः । शुक्रसद्मनां । उषसां । अनीके ।  
> अयं । महान् । महता । स्कंधनेन । उत् । द्यां । अस्तभ्नात् । वृषभः । मरुत्वान् ॥

### Printed p. 187

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सोमश्चित्रदृशीकं विचित्रदर्शनं यद्वाश्चर्यत्वेन दर्शनीयमर्णः
> सर्वस्य प्रेरकं सौरं ज्योतिर्विदत् । लंभयति । कस्मिन्काले ! शुक्रसद्मनां शुक्रं
> निर्मलमंतरिक्षं सद्म सदनं यासां तासामुषसामनीके प्रमुखे । उषःकाल
> इत्यर्थः । अपि च महान् प्रवृद्योयं सोमो महता स्थविष्ठेन स्कंभनेन
> स्तंभनसाधनेन मध्यवर्तिनांतरिक्षेण द्यां द्युलोकमुदस्तभ्नात् । ऊर्ध्वमस्थापयत् । यथाधो न पतति तथांतरिक्षं तस्याधारत्वेन कृतवानित्यर्थः । कीदृशः
> सोमः । वृषभो वृष्टेर्जनयिता । सोमाहुत्या हि वृष्टिर्जन्यते । मरुत्वान्मरुद्धिर्युक्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma obtains (विदत् (*vidat*)), that is, causes to be obtained, the wonderfully visible (चित्रदृशीकं (*citradṛśīkaṃ*)), or marvellously beautiful, solar light (अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)), the impeller of all. At what time? At the front, at the head, of the dawns (उषसां (*uṣasāṃ*)) whose seat is the pure firmament; that is, at the time of dawn. And this great (महान् (*mahān*)), grown Soma has propped up (उदस्तभ्नात् (*udastabhnāt*)) the heavenly world with a great, most massive prop, namely the firmament that stands in the middle: he set it upright, and made the firmament its support so that it does not fall downward. What kind of Soma? A bull (वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)), the producer of rain; for by the oblation of Soma rain is produced. He is accompanied by the Maruts (मरुत्वान् (*marutvān*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुक्रसद्मनां (*śukrasadmanāṃ*)—those whose dwelling is the shining firmament
- उषसां (*uṣasāṃ*)—of the dawns
- अनीके (*anīke*)—at the time of their appearing
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this Soma king
- चित्रदृशीकं (*citradṛśīkaṃ*)—the most attractively visible
- अर्ण (*arṇa*)—solar light
- विदत् (*vidat*)—makes manifest
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the producer of rain
- मरुत्वान् (*marutvān*)—accompanied by the Maruts
- महान् (*mahān*)—and great-souled
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this Soma king
- महता (*mahatā*)—by the most firm
- स्कंभनेन (*skaṃbhanena*)—firmament that is like a supporting pillar
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heavenly world
- उदस्तभ्नात् (*udastabhnāt*)—has established and made to stand

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of the appearing of the dawns, whose dwelling is the shining firmament, this Soma king makes manifest the most attractively visible light of the sun. This Soma king, the producer of rain, accompanied by the Maruts, and great-souled, has established and made to stand the heavenly world with the help of the firmament, which is like a most firm supporting pillar.

##### English translation
This makes known the wonderfully beautiful and inspiring (solar radiance) at the appearance of the dawns, whose dwelling is the firmament : this mighty (Soma) has sustained the heaven with a powerful support, the sender of rain, the leader of the winds.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धृ॒षत्पि॑ब क॒लशे॒ सोम॑मिंद्र वृत्र॒हा शू॑र सम॒रे वसू॑नां ।  
> माध्यं॑दिने॒ सव॑न॒ आ वृ॑षस्व रयि॒स्थानो॑ र॒यिम॒स्मासु॑ धेहि ॥६॥

### Printed p. 188

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धृषत् । पिब । कलशे । सोमं । इंद्र । वृत्रहा । शूर । संअरे । वसूनां ।  
> माध्यंदिने । सवने । आ । वृषस्व । रयिस्थानः । रयिं । आस्मासु । धेहि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर शौर्यवन्निंद्र वृत्रहा वृत्राणामावरकाणां शूत्रूणां हंता त्वं
> वसूनां धनानां समरे संग्रामे निमित्तभूते सति कलशे द्रोणकलशेवस्थितं
> सोमं धृषत् धृष्टं यथा । भवति तथा पिब । अपि च माध्यंदिने सवन आ वृषस्व ।
> आसिंचस्व । जठरं सोमेन पूरय ! सर्वैंद्रं हि माध्यंदिनं सवनं । किं च
> रयिस्थानो रयीणां धनानां स्थानभूतस्त्वं रयिं धनमस्मासु धेहि । धारय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O hero, O Indra, you who slay the Vṛtras, the enemies who obstruct, when a battle for wealth has come about, drink boldly (धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*)), that is, in such a way that you become bold, the Soma standing in the Droṇa-kalaśa (कलशे (*kalaśe*)). Also pour in (आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*)), that is, fill your belly with Soma at the midday pressing; for the midday pressing belongs wholly to Indra. And, as the abode of riches (रयिस्थानः (*rayisthānaḥ*)), place riches in us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—you, the slayer of Vṛtra
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—that is fought for riches
- समरे (*samare*)—in order to take part in the battle
- कलशे (*kalaśe*)—which is in the Droṇa-kalaśa
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*)—so that strength and courage are filled
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- माध्यंदिने सवने (*mādhyaṃdine savane*)—also at the time of the midday pressing
- आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*)—fill the belly fully with Soma
- रयिस्थानः (*rayisthānaḥ*)—you, the place of origin of riches
- अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—in us
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—riches
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, you, the slayer of Vṛtra, drink the Soma that is in the Droṇa-kalaśa, so that you are filled with strength and courage, in order to take part in the battle that is fought for riches. At the time of the midday pressing also fill your belly fully with Soma. You, the place of origin of riches, fill us fully with riches.

##### English translation
Hero, Indra, you are the slayer of foes in contests for (the acquirement of) treasures, drink boldly from the pitcher : drink copiously at the noon-day rite : receptacle of riches, bestow riches upon us.
