##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ श्वासय पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्यां पु॑रु॒त्रा ते॑ मनुतां॒ विस्मि॑तं॒  ॑
> जगत् ।  
> स दुं॑दुभे स॒जूरिंद्रे॑ण दे॒वैर्दू॒राद्दवी॑यो॒ अप॑ सेध॒  ॑
> शत्रून् ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । श्वासय । पृथिवीं । उत । द्यां । पुरुत्रा । ते । मनुतां । विस्मितं । जगत् ।  
> सः । दुंदुभे । सजूः । इंद्रेण । देवैः । दूरात् । दवीयः । अप । सेध ।  
> शत्रून् ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परेण तृचेन संग्रामे दुंदुभिरभिमर्शनीयः । सूत्रितं च । उप श्वासय
> पृथिवीमुत द्यामिति तृचेन दुंदुभिमभिमृशेत् । आ. गृ. ३-१२-१७ । इति ॥
> हे दुंदुभे पृथिवीमुतापि च द्यां दिवमुप श्वासय । आत्मीयेन जयघोषेणाश्वासय । यथा लोकद्वयं त्वदीयेन शब्दीनापूरितं भवति तादृशं शब्दं
> कुर्वित्यर्थः । अपि च विस्थितं विशेषेण स्थितं स्थावरं जंगमं चोभयविधं
> प्राणिजातं ते त्वदीयं शब्दं पुरुत्रा बहुधा मनुतां । मन्यतां । जानातु ।
> हे दुंदुभे स त्वमिंद्रेणान्वैर्देवैश्च सजूः सह दूराद्दवीयो दूरादपि
> दूरतॆरं शत्रुनस्मदीयानप सेध । आपगमय! अत्र निरुक्तं। दुंदुभिरिति शब्दानुकरणं
> द्रुमो भिन्न इति वा दुंदुभ्यतेर्वा स्याद्वधकर्मणः । नि. ९-१२ । इत्यादि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In battle the dundubhi is to be touched with the following tṛca. It is laid down in the sūtra: the dundubhi is to be touched with the tṛca beginning उप श्वासय (*upa śvāsaya*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-17)**NOTE**. O dundubhi, make the earth and also heaven draw breath: reassure them with your own cry of victory; make such a sound that both worlds are filled with your sound. This is the meaning. Further, all living beings, both the standing (the immovable) and the moving, who stand in their various ways, should in many ways (पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*), that is, बहुधा (*bahudhā*)) take note of your sound; let them know it. O dundubhi, you, united with Indra and the other gods, drive away our enemies from far, from farther than far; make them go away. Here the Nirukta says: शब्दानुकरणं द्रुमो भिन्न इति वा दुंदुभ्यतेर्वा स्याद्वधकर्मणः (*śabdānukaraṇaṃ drumo bhinna iti vā duṃdubhyatervā syādvadhakarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 9-12).**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दुंदुभे (*duṃdubhe*)—O dundubhi, special instrument of war so named
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यां उप (*dyāṃ upa*)—the world of heaven (so as to pervade it fully)
- श्वासय (*śvāsaya*)—make a loud sound
- विस्थितं (*visthitaṃ*)—that which stands firm
- जगत् (*jagat*)—that which is of the nature of the moving; the beings of the two kinds
- ते (*te*)—your sound
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many ways
- मनुतां (*manutāṃ*)—let them know; (O dundubhi)
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the famous one
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—with Indra
- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—with other gods

### Printed p. 223
- सजूः (*sajūḥ*)—united
- दूराद्दवीयः (*dūrāddavīyaḥ*)—even though at the greatest distance
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—the enemies
- अप सेध (*apa sedha*)—drive them away and make them vanish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O dundubhi, special instrument of war so named, make a loud sound so as to pervade fully the earth and the world of heaven. May the beings of the two kinds, the immovable and the moving, know your sound in many ways. O dundubhi, the famous one, united with Indra and the other gods, drive away the enemies and make them vanish, even though they be at the greatest distance.

##### English translation
War drum, fill with your sound both heaven and earth; and let all things, fixed or moveable, be aware of it: do you, who are associated with Indra and the gods, drive away our foes to the remotest distance.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In time of battle the dundubhi (the nagāri drum) is to be touched with the tṛca (three Ṛks) beginning उप श्वासय (*upa śvāsaya*), as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra: उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यामिति तृचेन दुंदुभिमभिमृशेत् (*upa śvāsaya pṛthivīmuta dyāmiti tṛcena duṃdubhimabhimṛśet*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-17)**NOTE**.

In the course of explaining the meaning of the word dundubhi, Yāska has given a nirvacana for this Ṛk:

दुंदुभिः । दुंदुभिरिति शब्दानुकरणं । द्रुमो भिन्न इति वा । दुंदुभ्यतेर्ना स्याच्छब्दकर्मणः ॥ तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*duṃdubhiḥ | duṃdubhiriti śabdānukaraṇaṃ | drumo bhinna iti vā | duṃdubhyaternā syācchabdakarmaṇaḥ ‖ tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*)

उप श्वासय पृथिवीं च दिवं च बहुधा ते घोषं मन्यतां विष्ठितं स्थावरं जंगमं च यत् स दुंदुभे सहजोषण इंद्रेण च देवेभ्यश्च दूरात् दूरतरमपसेध शत्रून् ॥ (*upa śvāsaya pṛthivīṃ ca divaṃ ca bahudhā te ghoṣaṃ manyatāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ ca yat sa duṃdubhe sahajoṣaṇa iṃdreṇa ca devebhyaśca dūrāt dūrataramapasedha śatrūn ‖*) (Ni. 9-13)**NOTE**

Dundubhi means the nagāri drum; because it makes the sound dhuṃ dhuṃ, it has come by the name dundubhi. Or else, drumas means a tree; because this is made by splitting and cutting it, it is named dundubhi. Or it may also be derived from the word दुंदुभ्य (*duṃdubhya*), which means making a sound.

### Printed p. 224
O dundubhi, with your sound make the earth and heaven pervaded and filled, that is, let your firm sound pervade the earth and the intermediate region. May all things, of the nature of the moving and the unmoving, or all beings, know you (your sound). And, O dundubhi, you, together with Indra and the gods, make our enemies flee far and farther, that is, very far. This is the main sense of the nirvacana.

> अप । प्रोथ । दुंदुभे । दुच्चुनाः । इतः । इंद्रस्य । मुष्टिः । असि । वीळयस्व । ३०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे दुंदुभे आ क्रंदय । अस्मच्छत्रून्नोदय । बलं सेनारूपमोजः
> शरीरबलं च नोऽस्मभ्यमा धाः । आधेहि । प्रयच्छ । कथा दुरिता दुरितानि दुर्गमनानि
> बाधमानो हिंसंस्त्वं निः स्तनिहि । नितरां शब्दं कुरु ॥ स्तन शब्द इति धातुः ॥
> हे दुंदुभे दुच्चना अस्मद्दुःखहेतुभूतं शुनं सुखं यासां तादृशीः शत्रुसेना
> इतोऽस्मत्स्थानादप प्रोथ । बाधस्व । त्वं चेंद्रस्य मुष्टिरसि । मुष्टिरिव शूत्रोणां
> हंता भवसि । अतोऽस्मान्वीळयस्व । दृढीकुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O dundubhi, आ क्रंदय (*ā kraṃdaya*): urge on our enemies. Give us (आ धाः (*ā dhāḥ*): bestow, grant) strength (बलं (*balaṃ*)) in the form of an army and bodily strength (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)). How? Harassing, that is, hurting, the दुरिता (*duritā*), the hard-to-traverse (misfortunes), you thunder aloud (निः स्तनिहि (*niḥ stanihi*): make a sound continuously). The root is स्तन (*stana*), in the sense of sound. O dundubhi, those armies of enemies (दुच्चना (*duccanā*)) whose happiness (शुनं (*śunaṃ*), that is, सुखं (*sukhaṃ*)) is the cause of sorrow to us, drive away (अप प्रोथ (*apa protha*): repel) from this, our place. And you are Indra's fist; like a fist you are the slayer of the enemies. Therefore make us firm, make us strong (वीळयस्व (*vīḷayasva*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दुंदुभे (*duṃdubhe*)—O dundubhi
- आ क्रंदय (*ā kraṃdaya*)—destroy our enemies
- बलं (*balaṃ*)—the strength in the form of an army
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—our bodily strength
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ धाः (*ā dhāḥ*)—bestow
- दुरिता (*duritā*)—the enemies of sinful mind
- बाधमानः (*bādhamānaḥ*)—harassing
- निः स्तनिहि (*niḥ stanihi*)—make a loud sound
- दुच्चुनाः (*duccunāḥ*)—the armies of enemies that cause us sorrow
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from this place
- अप प्रोथ (*apa protha*)—drive far away
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you indeed
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—for Indra
- मुष्टिः असि (*muṣṭiḥ asi*)—you are of the form of a fist
- वीळयस्व (*vīḷayasva*)—(therefore) make us strong

### Printed p. 225

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O dundubhi, make our enemies weep. Provide strength in the form of an army, and for our body power of its own. Harassing the enemies of sinful mind, make a loud sound. Drive far from this place the armies of enemies that cause us sorrow. O dundubhi, you are of the form of a fist for Indra. Therefore make us strong.

##### English translation
Sound loud against the (hostile) host : animate our prowess: thunder aloud, terrifying the evil-minded : repel, drum, those whose delight it is to harm us : you are the fist of Indra; inspire us with fierceness.

#### Ṛk 31

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आमूर॑ज प्र॒त्याव॑र्तये॒माः के॑तु॒मद्दुं॑दु॒भिर्वा॑वदीति ।  
> समश्व॑पर्णा॒श्चरं॑ति नो॒ नरो॒ऽस्माक॑मिंद्र र॒थिनो॑ जयंतु ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । अमूः । अज । प्रतिआवर्तय । इमाः । केतुमत् । दुंदुभिः । नावदीति ।  
> सं । अश्वपर्णाः । चरंति । नः । नरः । अस्माकं । इंद्र । रथिनः । जयंतु ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्याः पूर्वार्धो दुंदुभिदेवत्य उत्तरार्धश्चैंद्रः । यद्वा । उभावप्यर्धर्चावैंद्रौ । हे इंद्र अमूः शत्रुषु स्थितास्ता गा आज । आस्मान्प्रत्यागमय ।
> इमा अस्मदीया गाः शत्रुभिर्जिघृक्षिताः प्रत्यावर्तय । प्रतिनिवर्तय । अयं च
> दुंदुभिः केतुमत् प्रज्ञानवत् यथा सर्वैर्ज्ञायते तथा वावदीति । भृशं शब्दं
> करोति । अश्वपर्णा अश्वपतना अश्ववाहाश्च नोऽस्मदीयाश्च नरः पुरुषाः सं चरंति ।
> शत्रुभिर्युध्यमाना वर्तंते । तथा सति हे इंद्र अस्माकं रथिनो रथारूढाः
> पुरषाः शत्रून् जयंतु ॥
> XXI 15

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The first half of this Ṛk has the drum (dundubhi) as deity and the latter half is addressed to Indra. Or else both half-verses are addressed to Indra. O Indra, bring to us (आज (*āja*)) those cows of ours that stand among the enemies; make them come to us. Turn back (प्रत्यावर्तय (*pratyāvartaya*)) these cows of ours that the enemies wish to seize; make them return. And this dundubhi sounds loudly (वावदीति (*vāvadīti*): it makes a mighty sound), केतुमत् (*ketumat*), that is, so as to be known to all. Our men, अश्वपर्णा (*aśvaparṇā*), those who go with horses and who ride horses, move about together (सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)); they are engaged in fighting with the enemies. That being so, O Indra, may our men who are mounted on chariots conquer the enemies.

### Printed p. 226

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अमूः (*amūḥ*)—our cows that are among the enemies
- आ अज (*ā aja*)—make them come and join us
- इमाः (*imāḥ*)—these very cows of ours
- प्रत्यावर्तय (*pratyāvartaya*)—turn them back to us
- दुंदुभिः (*duṃdubhiḥ*)—this instrument of war
- केतुमत् (*ketumat*)—so as to come to the notice of all
- वावदीति (*vāvadīti*)—makes a sound
- अश्वपर्णाः (*aśvaparṇāḥ*)—mounted on horses
- नः (*naḥ*)—and belonging to us
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—men
- सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)—are moving about on the battlefield
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—belonging to us
- रथिनः (*rathinaḥ*)—men mounted on chariots
- जयंतु (*jayaṃtu*)—may they conquer the enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, make our cows that are among the enemies come and join us. Turn back to us these very cows of ours. This war-dundubhi also sounds so that all may know it. Our warriors, mounted on horses and on chariots, are moving about on the battlefield. May all of them be victorious over the enemies.

##### English translation
Recover these our cattle, Indra ; bring them back : the drum sounds repeatedly as a signal : our leaders, mounted on their steeds, assemble : may our warriors, riding in their cars, Indra, be victorious.

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके सप्तमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*) ओं तत्त्वत् (*oṃ tattvat*) **GLOSS**

Here ends the seventh adhyāya, in the fourth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, which has the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and a translation in the Kannada language.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्रहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrahīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stute ‖*) **GLOSS** शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*) मंगळ (*maṃgaḷa*)

ओं (*oṃ*) श्रीः (*śrīḥ*) श्री गणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī gaṇādhipataye namaḥ*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**

यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायिया सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyiyā sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*) **GLOSS**

The Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (with the explanation of the translation of the meaning in the Kannada language).

चतुर्थाष्टके अष्टमोऽध्यायः (*caturthāṣṭake aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ*)

The eighth adhyāya in the fourth aṣṭaka. The forty-eighth sūkta of the sixth maṇḍala.

## Sūkta 48 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथाष्टमाध्याय आरभ्यते । षष्ठमंडलस्य चतुर्थेऽनुवाके चत्वारि सूक्तानि
> व्याख्यातानि । यज्ञायज्ञेति द्वाविंशत्यृचं पंचमं सूक्तं बृहस्पतिपुत्रस्य
> शंयोरार्षं अत्रानुक्रम्यते । यज्ञायज्ञा द्वैधिका शंयुस्तृणपाणिकं
> प्रश्निसूक्तं प्रगाथौ बृहती महासतोबृहती महाबार्हतबार्हतौ प्रगाथावित्याग्नेय्यः काकुभः प्रगाथः पुरउष्णिग्बृहत्यतिजगतीति मारुत्योऽंत्यास्तिस्रो वासां
> लिंगोक्तदेवताः काकुभः प्रगाथः पुरउष्णिग्बृहतीति पौष्टो बृहती महाबृहती
> यवमध्यांत्यानुष्टुब्दावाभूम्योर्वा पृश्नेर्वेति । यज्ञायज्ञा व इत्येषा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now the eighth adhyāya begins. In the fourth anuvāka of the sixth maṇḍala four sūktas have been explained. Here is set out the fifth sūkta, beginning यज्ञायज्ञेति (*yajñāyajñeti*), of twenty-two Ṛks, whose seer is Śaṃyu, son of Bṛhaspati. The Anukramaṇī says: यज्ञायज्ञा द्वैधिका शंयुस्तृणपाणिकं प्रश्निसूक्तं प्रगाथौ बृहती महासतोबृहती महाबार्हतबार्हतौ प्रगाथावित्याग्नेय्यः काकुभः प्रगाथः पुरउष्णिग्बृहत्यतिजगतीति मारुत्योऽंत्यास्तिस्रो वासां लिंगोक्तदेवताः काकुभः प्रगाथः पुरउष्णिग्बृहतीति पौष्टो बृहती महाबृहती यवमध्यांत्यानुष्टुब्दावाभूम्योर्वा पृश्नेर्वेति । (*yajñāyajñā dvaidhikā śaṃyustṛṇapāṇikaṃ praśnisūktaṃ pragāthau bṛhatī mahāsatobṛhatī mahābārhatabārhatau pragāthāvityāgneyyaḥ kākubhaḥ pragāthaḥ purauṣṇigbṛhatyatijagatīti mārutyo 'ṃtyāstisro vāsāṃ liṃgoktadevatāḥ kākubhaḥ pragāthaḥ purauṣṇigbṛhatīti pauṣṭo bṛhatī mahābṛhatī yavamadhyāṃtyānuṣṭubdāvābhūmyorvā pṛśnerveti |*).**NOTE** Of these, the Ṛk यज्ञायज्ञा व (*yajñāyajñā va*) is a bṛhatī, since the mark of that metre is present: the third pāda has twelve syllables.

### Printed p. 228

> बृहती । तृतीयो द्वादशक इति तल्लक्षणसद्भावात् । द्वितीया सतोबृहती । आयुजौ
> जागतौ सतोबृहतीत्युक्तलक्षणोपेतत्वात् । तृतीयाचतुर्थि बृहतीसतोबृहत्यौ
> पंचमी बृहती षष्ठी महासतोबृहती । अष्टाक्षरास्त्रयः पादा द्वादशाक्षरा द्यौ
> पादौ सा महासतोबृहती । सप्तमी महाबृहती । अष्टाक्षराश्चत्वारः पादा एको
> द्वादशाक्षरः सा महाबृहती । अष्टमी महासतोबृहती । अष्टिनस्त्रयो द्यौ जागतौ
> सा महासतो बृहती । नवमी बृहती दशमी सतोबृहती । एता दशाग्नि देवत्याः ।
> एकादशी ककुप् । मध्यमो यदि द्वादशाक्षर उभयतोऽष्टकौ द्यौ पादौ सा ककुप् ।
> द्वादशी सतोबृहती त्रयोदशी पुरउष्णिक् । आद्यो जागतो द्वितीयतृतीयौ
> गायत्रौ सा पुरउष्णिक् । चतुर्दशी बृहती पंचदश्यतिजगती द्वापंचाशदक्षरा ।
> एकादश्याद्याः पंच मरुद्देवताकाः । त्रयोदश्यादीनां तिसृणां लिंगोक्ता
> इंद्रादयो ना देवताः । षोडशी ककुप् सप्तदशी सतोबृहत्यष्टादशी पुरउष्णिगेकोनविंशी बृहती । षोडश्यादीनां चतसृणां पूषा देवता । विंशी बृहत्येकविंशी
> यवमध्या महाबृहती । आद्यौ द्वावष्टकौ तृतीयो द्वादशकश्चतुर्थपंचमावष्टकौ
> सा यवमध्या महाबृहती । विंशैकविंश्योः पृश्नि सूक्तमित्युक्तत्वान्रुतां माता
> पृश्निर्देवता । द्वाविंश्यनुष्टुप् । स चापि पृश्नादेवत्या द्यावाभूमिदेवत्या वा ॥
> सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । अग्नि मारुते यज्ञायज्ञाव इत्ययं स्तोत्रियप्रगाथः ।
> सूत्रितं च । यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये देवो वो द्रविणोदा इति प्रगाथौ
> स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ ॥ आ. ५-२० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second Ṛk is a satobṛhatī, since it has the stated mark: its odd pādas (आयुजौ (*āyujau*)) are of the jagatī kind. The third and fourth are a bṛhatī and a satobṛhatī, the fifth a bṛhatī. The sixth is a mahāsatobṛhatī: three pādas of eight syllables and two of twelve. The seventh is a mahābṛhatī: four pādas of eight syllables and one of twelve. The eighth is a mahāsatobṛhatī: three of eight syllables and two of the jagatī kind. The ninth is a bṛhatī and the tenth a satobṛhatī. These ten are addressed to Agni. The eleventh is a kakubh: if the middle pāda has twelve syllables and the two pādas on either side eight. The twelfth is a satobṛhatī; the thirteenth a puraūṣṇih: the first pāda of the jagatī kind, the second and third of the gāyatrī kind. The fourteenth is a bṛhatī; the fifteenth an atijagatī of fifty-two syllables. The five Ṛks from the eleventh on have the Maruts as deity. For the three from the thirteenth on the deities are those stated by the indication, Indra and the others.**NOTE** The sixteenth is a kakubh, the seventeenth a satobṛhatī, the eighteenth a puraūṣṇih, the nineteenth a bṛhatī; for these four from the sixteenth on Pūṣan is the deity. The twentieth is a bṛhatī; the twenty-first a yavamadhyā mahābṛhatī: the first two pādas of eight syllables, the third of twelve, the fourth and fifth of eight. Because the twentieth and twenty-first are called a Pṛśni sūkta, Pṛśni, the mother of the Maruts, is their deity. The twenty-second is an anuṣṭubh, and it too is addressed to Pṛśni or to Heaven and Earth. The application of the sūkta is by indication: at the Agnimāruta this pragātha beginning यज्ञायज्ञाव (*yajñāyajñāva*) is the stotriya pragātha. This is laid down in the sūtra: the two pragāthas, stotriya and anurūpa (Ā. Sū. 5-20).

##### Anuvāda

Since the explanation of the seventh adhyāya of the fourth aṣṭaka in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā has ended, we now begin the explanation of the eighth adhyāya. The four sūktas of the fourth anuvāka of the sixth maṇḍala were explained in the previous adhyāya. The sūkta beginning यज्ञायज्ञा (*yajñāyajñā*) is the fifth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has twenty-two Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Śaṃyu, the son of Bṛhaspati. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: यज्ञायज्ञा द्व्यधिका शंयुस्तृणपाणिकं प्रश्निसूक्तं प्रगाथौ बृहती महासतोबृहती महाबार्हतबार्हतौ प्रगाथावित्याग्नेय्यः काकुभः प्रगाथः पुरउष्णिग्रहत्यतिजगतीति मारुत्योऽन्तास्तिस्रो वासां लिंगोक्तदेवताः काकुभः प्रगाथः पुरउष्णिग्रहतीति पौष्ठो बृहती महाबृहती यवमध्यांत्यानुष्टुप् द्यावाभूम्योर्वा पृश्नेर्वा (*yajñāyajñā dvyadhikā śaṃyustṛṇapāṇikaṃ praśnisūktaṃ pragāthau bṛhatī mahāsatobṛhatī mahābārhatabārhatau pragāthāvityāgneyyaḥ kākubhaḥ pragāthaḥ purauṣṇigrahatyatijagatīti mārutyo 'ntāstisro vāsāṃ liṃgoktadevatāḥ kākubhaḥ pragāthaḥ purauṣṇigrahatīti pauṣṭho bṛhatī mahābṛhatī yavamadhyāṃtyānuṣṭup dyāvābhūmyorvā pṛśnervā*). The first Ṛk of this sūkta, यज्ञायज्ञा वः (*yajñāyajñā vaḥ*), is of the bṛhatī metre. If the third pāda has twelve syllables and the remaining pādas eight each, that metre is called bṛhatī. If in a Ṛk there are five

### Printed p. 229
pādas, of which four pādas have eight syllables each and the remaining one pāda twelve syllables, it is called mahābṛhatī. The eighth Ṛk of this sūkta is of the mahāsatobṛhatī metre. If in a Ṛk there are five pādas, of which three pādas have eight syllables each and the remaining two pādas twelve each, it is called mahāsatobṛhatī. The ninth Ṛk is of the bṛhatī metre. The tenth Ṛk is of the satobṛhatī metre. The first ten Ṛks of this sūkta have Agni as deity. The eleventh Ṛk is of the kakubh metre. If in a Ṛk there are three pādas, of which the first and the last have eight syllables each and the middle one twelve, it is called kakubh. The twelfth Ṛk is of the satobṛhatī metre. The thirteenth is of the metre called puraūṣṇih. If in a Ṛk there are three pādas, of which the first has twelve syllables as in the jagatī metre, and the second and third have eight each as in the gāyatrī metre, it is called puraūṣṇih. The fourteenth Ṛk is of the bṛhatī metre. The fifteenth is of the metre called atijagatī. If in a Ṛk there are five pādas, the first three of twelve syllables each and the last two of eight each, fifty-two syllables in all, it is called atijagatī. The five Ṛks from the eleventh on have the Maruts as deity. For the three Ṛks from the thirteenth on the deities are those named by the indication, or Indra and the others. The sixteenth Ṛk is of the kakubh metre. The seventeenth is of the satobṛhatī metre. The eighteenth is of the puraūṣṇih metre. The nineteenth is of the bṛhatī metre. For the four Ṛks from the sixteenth on Pūṣan is the deity. The twentieth Ṛk is of the bṛhatī metre. The twenty-first Ṛk is of the metre called yavamadhyāmahābṛhatī. If in a Ṛk there are five pādas, with eight syllables each in the first two pādas, twelve in the third, and eight each in the last two, it is called yavamadhyāmahābṛhatī. Since the twentieth and twenty-first Ṛks are called the Pṛśni sūkta, Pṛśni, the mother of the Maruts, is the deity of those Ṛks. The twenty-second Ṛk is of the anuṣṭubh metre. Pṛśni or Bhūmi may be the deity of this Ṛk. The application of the sūkta is by indication. At the time of reciting the Agnimāruta śastra mantras, this tṛca beginning यज्ञायज्ञा वः (*yajñāyajñā vaḥ*) is to be recited as the stotriya pragātha tṛca, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये देवो वो द्रविणोदा इति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*yajñāyajñā vo agnaye devo vo draviṇodā iti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. Sū. 5-20).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒ज्ञाय॑ज्ञा वो अ॒ग्नये॑ गि॒रागि॑रा च॒ दक्ष॑से ।  
> प्रप्र॑ व॒यम॒मृतं॑ जा॒तवे॑दसं प्रि॒यं मि॒त्रं न शं॑सिषं ॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यज्ञायज्ञा । वः । अग्नये । गिरागिरा । च । दक्षसे ।  
> प्रप्र । वयं । अमृतं । जातवेदसं । प्रियं । मित्रं । न । शंसिषं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतारो वो यूयं यज्ञा यज्ञा यज्ञे यज्ञे सर्वॆषु यागेषु
> दक्षसे प्रवृद्धायाग्नये गिरा गिरा स्तुतिरूपया वाचा वाचा स्तोत्रं कुरुतेति
> शेषः । चशब्दो भिन्नक्रमो व इत्यस्मात्परो द्रष्टव्यः । यूयं च स्तोत्रं कुरुत ।
> वयमपि तमग्निं प्र शंसिषं ॥ प्रसमुपोदः पादपूरण इति प्रशब्दस्य द्विरुक्तिः
> पादपूरणार्था । व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । छांदसो लुज् ॥ प्रशंसाम । कीदृशं ।
> अमृतं मरणरहितं जातवेदसं जातानां वेदितारं जातप्रज्ञं जातधनं वा मित्रं
> न सखिभूतनिव प्रियमनुकूलं ॥ यद्वा । व्यत्ययेन त्वमित्यस्य वसादेशः । अग्निय
> इति च कर्मणि चतुर्थी । क्रियाग्रहणमपि कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वात् ।
> चशब्दश्चण्णिति निपातश्चेदर्थे वर्तते । दक्षस इति च दक्षेर्वृद्दिकर्मणोऽंतर्भानि-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praisers, in every sacrifice (यज्ञा यज्ञा (*yajñā yajñā*): in each and every rite) offer praise to Agni, अग्नये (*agnaye*), who is दक्षसे (*dakṣase*), grown great, with every praise (गिरा गिरा (*girā girā*): with speech after speech in the form of praise): this has to be supplied. The word च (*ca*) is to be seen after व (*va*), out of its order. And you offer praise; we too praise him. How is he? Immortal (अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*): free from death), जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*): the knower of all that is born, or one whose knowledge is born, or one whose wealth is born; dear and favourable, like a friend. Or else, by inversion, वो (*vo*) stands for त्वं (*tvaṃ*), you, and अग्नये (*agnaye*) is a dative in the sense of the object, since the object is an indirect recipient.

### Printed p. 231

> तण्यर्थाल्लट रूपं । चणा योगात् निपातैर्यद्यदिहंतेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥
> तत्रायमर्थः । हे स्तोतस्त्वं यज्ञे यज्ञ इममग्निं गिरा गिरा स्तुत्या दक्षसे च
> वर्धयसि चेत् वयमप्यमृतत्वादिगुणकं तं प्रशंसाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The particle च (*ca*) here has the sense of "if". The meaning is this: O praiser, if you in every sacrifice make this Agni grow with every praise, and make him thrive, then we too praise him, who has the qualities of immortality and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—(O praisers) you
- यज्ञा यज्ञा (*yajñā yajñā*)—in each and every sacrifice
- दक्षसे (*dakṣase*)—who has abundant power
- अग्नये (*agnaye*)—with reference to Agni
- गिरागिरा (*girāgirā*)—praise with many kinds of praise
- वयं च (*vayaṃ ca*)—we also
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—who is free from the nature of death
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—who is of born wisdom
- मित्रं न (*mitraṃ na*)—like a friend
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—and beneficent, Agni
- प्र शंसिषं (*pra śaṃsiṣaṃ*)—we praise and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, in every sacrifice praise with many kinds of praise Agni, who has abundant power. We also praise and worship Agni, who is free from the nature of death, of born wisdom, and beneficent like a friend.

##### English translation
At every sacrifice (honour) the mighty Agni with your reiterated praise, whilst we glorify him, the immortal, who knows, all things, our dear friend.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As has been said earlier in the application of this sūkta, this Ṛk beginning यज्ञा यज्ञा (*yajñā yajñā*) is to be recited as the stotriya pragātha mantra in the Agnimāruta śastra mantras.

The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says thus in this matter:

यज्ञायज्ञावो अग्नये देवो वो द्रविणोदा इति मध्ये योनिं चानुरूपं च शंसति तद्यन्मध्ये योनिं चानुरूपं च शंसति तस्मान्मध्ये योनिर्धृता । यदु द्वे सूक्ते शस्त्रा शंसति प्रतिष्ठयोरेव तदुपरिष्टात्पृजननं दधाति प्रजात्यै प्रजायुते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥ (*yajñāyajñāvo agnaye devo vo draviṇodā iti madhye yoniṃ cānurūpaṃ ca śaṃsati tadyanmadhye yoniṃ cānurūpaṃ ca śaṃsati tasmānmadhye yonirdhṛtā | yadu dve sūkte śastrā śaṃsati pratiṣṭhayoreva tadupariṣṭātpṛjananaṃ dadhāti prajātyai prajāyute prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1-35)

The hotṛ recites at the beginning of the Agnimāruta śastra mantras the sūkta of the nature of Agni Vaiśvānara, वैश्वानराय पृथुपाजसे (*vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3). After that he recites, addressed to the Maruts, the sūkta of the nature of the Marut deities, प्रत्वक्षसः प्रतवसः (*pratvakṣasaḥ pratavasaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-87). For the śastra mantras, after

### Printed p. 232
these two sūktas have been recited, the hotṛ recites the stotriya and the anurūpa pragātha mantras. Here the Ṛk now in hand, यज्ञायज्ञावो आग्नये (*yajñāyajñāvo āgnaye*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-1), is the stotriya mantra. This is the first pragātha mantra. The Ṛk देवो वो द्रविणोदा (*devo vo draviṇodā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-16-11), recited as corresponding to it, is the anurūpa pragātha mantra. This is the second. In the first pragātha, the tṛca beginning यज्ञायज्ञा (*yajñāyajñā*), there are three Ṛks. These are sung by the Sāmagas (Sāmaveda 35; 703). In response, the ṛtviks of the hotṛ class recite the anurūpa mantras देवो वो द्रविणोदाः (*devo vo draviṇodāḥ*). The reason for reciting these two mantras in the middle of the śastra mantras is this: the Ṛk यज्ञायज्ञा (*yajñāyajñā*), the stotriya mantra, is called the womb (yoni). The two sūktas mentioned above, वैश्वानराय (*vaiśvānarāya*) and प्रत्यक्षसः (*pratyakṣasaḥ*), are the two thighs. Since the womb-region of women lies between the two thighs, in the middle region of the body, these stotriya and anurūpa mantras, of the form of the womb, are put in the middle of the śastra mantras, after the recitation of the two sūktas. By doing so the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice is helped to obtain offspring. The man who knows this also rejoices, furnished with offspring and wealth of cattle.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒र्जो नपा॑तं॒ स हि॒नायम॑स्म॒युदाशे॑म ह॒व्यदा॑तये ।  
> भुव॒द्वाजे॑ष्ववि॒ता भुव॑द्वृ॒ध उ॒त त्रा॒ता त॒नूनां॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊर्जः । नपातं । सः । हिन । अयं । अस्मयुः । दाशेम । हव्यदातये ।  
> भुवत् । वाजेषु । अविता । भुवत् । वृधः । उत । त्राता । तनूनां ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऊर्जोऽन्नस्य बलस्य वा नपातं पुत्रं प्र शंसिषमित्यनुषंगात् प्रशंसामेत्यर्थः । हिनेति निपातद्वयसमुदायो हीत्यस्यार्थे । स खल्वयमग्निरस्मयुरस्मान्कामयमानो भवति । वयं च हव्यदातॆये हव्यानां हविषां देवेभ्यो
> दात्रे तस्मा आग्नये दाशेम । हवींषि दद्याम । स चाग्निर्वाजेषु संग्रामेष्टविता
> रक्षिता वृधो वर्धकश्चास्माकं भुवत् । भवतु । उतापि च तनूनां तनयानामस्मत्पुत्राणां च त्राता रक्षिता भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*): of food or of strength; नपातं (*napātaṃ*): the son. "We praise" is to be supplied from the preceding Ṛk by continuation; the meaning is: we praise the son of strength. हिन (*hina*) is a combination of two particles in the sense of हि (*hi*), "for". This Agni indeed is अस्मयुः (*asmayuḥ*), one who desires us. And we would give (दाशेम (*dāśema*): may we give oblations) to that Agni, हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*), the giver of oblations, of offerings, to the gods. And may that Agni be, in battles (वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*): in conflicts), our protector (अविता (*avitā*)) and our increaser (वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)). And may he also be the protector of our bodies (तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)), that is, of our children, our sons.

### Printed p. 233

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*)—to strength
- नपातं (*napātaṃ*)—the son, Agni (we praise him)
- हि न (*hi na*)—certainly
- सः आयं (*saḥ āyaṃ*)—this same Agni
- अस्मयुः (*asmayuḥ*)—desires us
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to Agni, who distributes the oblation to the gods
- दाशेम (*dāśema*)—let us offer the oblation
- सः (*saḥ*)—(that same Agni)
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles
- अविता (*avitā*)—as our protector
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—as the cause of our increase
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—may he be
- उत (*uta*)—and
- तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)—of our sons, grandsons and the rest
- त्राता (*trātā*)—may he be the protector

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise Agni, the son of strength. This same Agni certainly desires us, for the good of the gods. To Agni, who distributes the oblation to the gods, let us offer the oblation. May that same Agni be our protector in battles and the cause of our increase. And may he also be the protector of our sons, grandsons and the rest.

##### English translation
The son of strength, for he verily is propitious to us ; to whom let us offer oblations as to the conveyer of them (to the gods) : may he be our defender and of our offspring.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॒ ह्य॑ग्ने अ॒जरो॑ म॒हान्वि॒भास्य॒र्चिषा॑ ।  
> अज॑स्रेण शो॒चिषा॒ शोशु॑चच्चुचे सुदी॒तिभिः॒ सु दी॑दिहि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषा । हि । अग्ने । अजरः । महान् । विभासि । अर्चिषा ।  
> अजस्रेण । शोचिषा । शोशुचत् । शुचे । सुदीतिभिः । सु । दीदिहि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने वृषा वर्षिता कामानां वृष्टेः कर्ता वाजरो जरारहितो महान्
> गुणैरधिक एवंभूतस्त्वमर्चिषा दीप्त्या विभासि हि। विशेषेण प्रकाशसे खलु। हे शुचे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are वृषा (*vṛṣā*), the showerer of desires, or the maker of rain; अजरः (*ajaraḥ*), free from decay; महान् (*mahān*), greater in qualities. Being such, you shine forth (विभासि (*vibhāsi*)) with your flame (अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)), that is, with your light: you indeed shine in a special way.

### Printed p. 234

> दीप्ताग्ने अजस्रेणाविच्छिन्नेन शोचिषा तेजसा शोशुचत् भृशं दीप्यमानस्त्वं
> सुदीतिभिः सुदीप्तिभिः सु दीदिहि । सुष्पस्मान्दीपय । प्रकाशय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O bright Agni (शुचे (*śuce*)), you who blaze exceedingly (शोशुचत् (*śośucat*)) with unceasing (अजस्रेण (*ajasreṇa*)), unbroken splendour (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*): brilliance), shine well (सु दीदिहि (*su dīdihi*)) with beautiful radiances (सुदीतिभिः (*sudītibhiḥ*)): light us up and illuminate us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—showerer of desires
- अजरः (*ajaraḥ*)—free from decay
- महान् (*mahān*)—having exceedingly great qualities, you
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—with your radiance
- विभासि हि (*vibhāsi hi*)—do you not shine exceedingly
- शुचे (*śuce*)—O Agni, full of splendour
- अजस्रेण (*ajasreṇa*)—unceasing
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with brilliance
- शोशुचत् (*śośucat*)—you who blaze exceedingly
- सुदीतिभिः (*sudītibhiḥ*)—with excellent radiance
- सु दीदिहि (*su dīdihi*)—blaze exceedingly and spread your light everywhere

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, showerer of desires, free from decay, having exceedingly great qualities, do you not shine exceedingly with your brilliance? O Agni, full of splendour, you who blaze exceedingly with unceasing brilliance, blaze exceedingly with excellent radiance and spread your light everywhere.

##### English translation
Agni, you are the showerer (of benefits), mighty, and exempt from decay, you shine with (great) splendour ; you are resplendent, brilliant (Agni), with unfading lustre : shine forth with glorious rays.

> अ॒र्वाचः॑ सीं कृणुह्य॒ग्नेऽव॑से॒ रास्व॒ वाजो॒त वं॑स्व ॥ ४ ॥

> अर्वाचः । सीं । कृणुहि । अग्ने । अवसे । रास्व । वाजा । उत । वंस्व ॥ ४ ॥

> हे अग्ने त्वं महो महतो देवान्यजसि । यजमानानां यज्ञे हविर्भिः
> पूजयसि । अतोऽस्माकमपि यज्ञ आनुषक् अनुषक्तं संततं यथा भवति तथा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you worship (यजसि (*yajasi*)) the great gods: at the sacrifices of the sacrificers you honour them with oblations. Therefore at our sacrifice also, आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*), continuously, in such a way that it goes on without a break,

> यक्षि । तान्देवान्यज । तदर्थं तव क्रत्वा प्रज्ञयोतापि च दंसना कर्मणा च ।
> सीमिति परिग्रहार्थीयः । तान् सर्वान्देवानर्वाचोऽस्मदभिमुखान् कृणुहि
> कुर्ववसेऽस्मद्रक्षणार्थं । तथा वाजा वाजान् हविर्लक्षणान्यन्नानि रास्व । तेभ्यो
> देवेभ्यो देहि । उतापि च त्वमपि वंस्व । तुभ्यं प्रत्तानि हवींषि संभजस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

worship (यक्षि (*yakṣi*)) those gods. For that purpose, with your wisdom (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) and also with your action (दंसना (*daṃsanā*)). The word सीं (*sīṃ*) is used in the sense of comprehension: make all those gods face us (अर्वाचः (*arvācaḥ*)), for our protection (अवसे (*avase*)). So also give (रास्व (*rāsva*)) वाजा (*vājā*), foods that are of the nature of oblations; give them to those gods. And you also partake (वंस्व (*vaṃsva*)): enjoy the oblations that have been given to you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- देवान् (*devān*)—gods
- यजसि (*yajasi*)—you worship
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—without a break
- यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—worship the gods (in our sacrifices also)
- तव (*tava*)—your
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—with wisdom
- उत (*uta*)—and
- दंसना (*daṃsanā*)—with acts
- सीं (*sīṃ*)—all those gods
- अवसे (*avase*)—for our protection
- अर्वाचः (*arvācaḥ*)—so that they face us
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—the foods in the form of oblation

- उत (*uta*)—and
- वंस्व (*vaṃsva*)—you also eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you worship the great gods. Therefore worship them without a break in our sacrifice also. With your wisdom and with your acts make all those gods face us, for our protection. Offer to them the foods in the form of oblation, and partake of them yourselves as well.

##### English translation
You sacrifice to the mighty gods : sacrifice (for us) continually, for (sacrifice is perfected) by your wisdom and your acts : bring them down, Agni, for our salvation : present (to them) the sacrificial food, partake of it yourself.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आपो वसतीवर्याख्या अद्रयो ग्रावाणो वना वनानि काष्ठानि च ऋतस्य
> यज्ञस्योदकस्य वा गर्भं गर्भवदंतर्वर्तमानं यमग्निं पिप्रति पूरयंति ।
> यॆद्वा । आपः समुद्रिया अद्रयो मेघा वनान्यरण्यानि च ऋतस्य गर्भं वाडववैद्युतदावरूपेण वर्तमानं यमग्निं पिप्रति पूरयंति । यश्चाग्निर्नृभिर्नेकृभिर्युत्विग्निः सहसा बलेन मथितः सन् पृथिव्या अधि भूमेरुपरि सानवि समुच्च्रित
> उत्कृष्टे देवयजनदेशे जायते प्रादुर्भवति स त्वं वंस्वेत्यन्वयः । यद्वा । यः
> पप्रावित्यनया संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The waters called vasatīvarī, the stones (अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*): the pressing-stones), and the forests, that is, woods and timber (वना (*vanā*)), fill (पिप्रति (*piprati*): make full) that Agni who is within, like an embryo (गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)), of the sacrifice or of the water (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)). Or else: the waters of the sea, the clouds (अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*): मेघा (*meghā*)) and the forests fill that Agni who exists as the embryo of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*) in the form of the submarine fire, lightning and forest fire. And that Agni who, churned (मथितः (*mathitaḥ*)) with force (सहसा (*sahasā*): with strength) by the men (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*): by the leaders, the ṛtviks), is born (जायते (*jāyate*): appears) on the earth (पृथिव्या अधि (*pṛthivyā adhi*): on the surface of the earth), in the elevated (सानवि (*sānavi*)) and excellent place of the divine sacrifice: you are he, and वंस्व (*vaṃsva*) is to be construed with it. Or else the connection is with यः पप्रौ (*yaḥ paprau*) of the following Ṛk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—the clouds
- वना (*vanā*)—the forests
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—to the sacrifice
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—who is of the form of the embryo
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Agni
- पिप्रति (*piprati*)—they nourish
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the ṛtviks
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—with force
- मथितः (*mathitaḥ*)—being churned and kindled
- पृथिव्या अधि (*pṛthivyā adhi*)—on the earth
- सानवि (*sānavi*)—in the elevated place of sacrifice
- जायसे (*jāyase*)—is born (may such an Agni partake of our oblation)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The waters, the clouds and the forests nourish that Agni who is the embryo of the sacrifice; that Agni who, churned with force by the ṛtviks and kindled, is born on the earth at the elevated sacrificial altar: may such an Agni partake of our oblation.

##### English translation
(You are he) whom the waters, the mountains, the woods, nourish as the embryo of sacrifice : who, churned with strength by the performers (of the rite), are generated in the highest place of the earth.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ यः प॒प्रौ भा॒नुना॒ रोद॑सी उ॒भे धू॒मेन॑ धावते दि॒वि ।  
> ति॒रस्तमो॑ ददृश॒ ऊर्म्या॒स्वा श्या॒वास्व॑रु॒षो वृषा श्या॒वा ॒॑ ॑
> अरुषो वृषा ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । यः । पप्रौ । भानुना । रोदसी इति । उभे इति । धूमेन । धावते । दिवि ।  
> तिरः । तमः । ददृशे । ऊर्म्यासु । आ । श्यावासु । अरुषः । वृषा । आ । श्यावाः ।  
> अरुषः । वृषा ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निर्भानुना दीप्तोभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावा पप्रौ अपूरयति स
> धूमेन दिव्यंतरिक्षे धावते । गच्छति । धूमो हि मेघात्मना परिणतः सन् अंतरिक्षे
> गच्छति । कार‍्यकारणयोरभेदविवक्षया तद्गमनमग्नावुपचर्यते। अपि चायमरुष
> आरोचमानो वृषा वर्षिता कामानामेवंगुणकोऽग्निः श्यावासु श्यावर्णासु
> कृष्णा सूर्म्यासु । रात्रिनामैतत् । निशासु तमोऽंधकारं तिरस्कृत्या समंताद्ददृशे ।
> दृश्यते । श्यावाः श्यावर्णा रात्रीश्चा तिष्ठति । अरुषा वृषेति पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था
> पादपूरणार्था वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who, shining with his radiance (भानुना (*bhānunā*)), fills (पप्रौ (*paprau*): अपूरयति (*apūrayati*)) both worlds (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), heaven and earth, moves (धावते (*dhāvate*): goes) with smoke (धूमेन (*dhūmena*)) in the sky, that is, the atmosphere. For smoke, transformed into the nature of a cloud, goes in the atmosphere; with the intention of not distinguishing cause and effect, that going is figuratively ascribed to Agni. Further, this अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*), the shining one, वृषा (*vṛṣā*), the showerer of desires, Agni of such qualities, is seen (ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)) on all sides, having put aside (तिरः (*tiraḥ*)) the darkness (तमः (*tamaḥ*)), in the dark-coloured (श्यावासु (*śyāvāsu*)) nights (ऊर्म्यासु (*ūrmyāsu*): this is a name of night). And he stands over the dark-coloured nights (श्यावाः (*śyāvāḥ*)). The repetition अरुषो वृषा (*aruṣo vṛṣā*) is for respect or for filling out the pāda.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- भानुना (*bhānunā*)—with his radiance
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- आ पप्रौ (*ā paprau*)—he who stands pervading them
- धूमेन (*dhūmena*)—in the form of smoke
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the atmosphere
- धावते (*dhāvate*)—moves about
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—possessed of an attractive colour
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—and the showerer of desires, Agni
- श्यावासु (*śyāvāsu*)—in the dark-coloured
- ऊर्म्यासु (*ūrmyāsu*)—nights
- तमः तिरः (*tamaḥ tiraḥ*)—thrusting the darkness aside
- आ ददृशे (*ā dadṛśe*)—is seen on all sides
- अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*)—shining
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—showerer of desires, Agni
- श्यावाः (*śyāvāḥ*)—the dark-coloured nights
- आ (*ā*) (तिष्ठति (*tiṣṭhati*))—stands, having occupied them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who stands pervading heaven and earth with his radiance moves about in the atmosphere in the form of smoke. Agni, possessed of an attractive colour and showerer of desires, thrusting aside the darkness in the dark-coloured nights, is seen on all sides. Agni, the shining one, the showerer of desires, stands having occupied the dark-coloured nights (he shines).

##### English translation
He who fills both heaven and earth with light, who mounts with sm ke into the sky, this radiant showerer (of benefits) is beheld in the dark

### Printed p. 238
nights dispersing the gloom : this radiant showerer (of benefits) presides over the dark nights.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बृ॒हद्भि॑रग्ने अ॒र्चिभिः॑ शु॒क्रेण॑ देव शो॒चिषा॑ ।  
> भ॒रद्वा॑जेसमिधा॒नो य॑विष्ठ्य रे॒वन्नः॑ शुक्र दीदिहि द्यु॒मत्पा॑वक दीदिहि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बृहत्भिः । अग्ने । अर्चिभिः । शुक्रेण । देव । शोचिषा ।  
> भरत् वाजे । संइधानः । यविष्ठ्य । रेवत् । नः । शुक्र । दीदिहि । द्युमत् । पावक ।  
> दीदिहि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देव दानादिगुणयुक्त यविष्ठ्य युवतम शुक्र दीप्ताग्ने शुक्रेण
> निर्मलेन शोचिषा तेजसा भरद्वाजेऽस्मद्धातरि समिधानः समिध्यमानस्त्वं
> बृहद्भिर्महद्दिरर्चिभिस्तेजोभिर्नोऽस्मदर्थं रेवद्धनयुक्तं यथा भवति तथा
> दीदिहि । दीप्यस्व । तथा पावक हे शोधकाग्ने द्युमत् द्योतमानेन च युक्तं
> यथा भवति तथा दीदिहि । दीप्यस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O divine one (देव (*deva*)), endowed with the qualities of giving and the rest, O youngest (यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*)), O bright (शुक्र (*śukra*)) and shining Agni, you who are kindled (समिधानः (*samidhānaḥ*)) with pure (शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*): निर्मलेन (*nirmalena*)) splendour (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*): lustre) in भरद्वाजेऽस्मद्धातरि (*bharadvāje 'smaddhātari*),**NOTE** shine (दीदिहि (*dīdihi*): be kindled) for our sake, with great (बृहद्भिः (*bṛhadbhiḥ*)) flames (अर्चिभिः (*arcibhiḥ*): lustres), so as to be endowed with wealth (रेवत् (*revat*)). So also, O purifier (पावक (*pāvaka*)), O Agni who cleanses, shine so that you are joined with brilliance (द्युमत् (*dyumat*): shining).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—divine one
- यविष्य (*yaviṣya*)—exceedingly young
- शुक्र (*śukra*)—and radiant
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*)—pure
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with radiance
- भरद्वाजे (*bharadvāje*)—by Bharadvāja
- समिधानः (*samidhānaḥ*)—you who have been kindled
- बृहद्भिः (*bṛhadbhiḥ*)—great
- अर्चिभिः (*arcibhiḥ*)—with lustres
- नः (*naḥ*)—to our share
- रेवत् (*revat*)—so as to be rich and a bestower of wealth
- दीदिहि (*dīdihi*)—shine
- पावक (*pāvaka*)—O Agni, the purifier
- द्युमत् (*dyumat*)—with splendid radiance
- दीदिहि (*dīdihi*)—shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, divine one, exceedingly young and radiant, kindled by Bharadvāja with pure radiance, shine with great lustres so that you are rich and a bestower of wealth to our share. O Agni, the purifier, shine with splendid radiance.

### Printed p. 239

##### English translation
Divine, resplendent Agni, youngest (of the gods), when kindled by Bharadwaja, shines with many flames, with pure lustre, (conferring) riches upon us ; shine, resplendent purifier.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वा॑सां गृ॒हप॑तिर्वि॒शाम॑सि॒ त्वम॑ग्ने॒ मानु॑षीणां ।  
> श॒तं पू॒र्भिय्य॑विष्ठ पा॒ह्यंह॑सः समे॒द्धारं॑ श॒तं हिमाः॑  
> स्तो॒तृभ्यो॒ ये च॒ दद॑ति ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वासां । गृहपतिः । विशां । असि । त्वं । अग्ने । मानुषीणां ।  
> शतं । पूःभिः । यविष्ठ । पाहि । अंहसः । संविद्द्धारं । शतं । हिमाः । स्तोतृभ्यः ।  
> ये । च । ददति ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं मानुषीणां मनोरपत्यभूतानां विश्वासां सर्वासां विशां
> प्रजानां गृहपतिरसि । गृहस्वामी भवसि । हे यविष्ठ युवतमाग्ने आतस्तं शतं
> हिमाः शतं हेमंतान् संवत्सरान् समेद्धारं त्वां सम्यगिद्दं कृतवंतं मां शतं
> शतेन शतसंख्याकैः पूर्भिः पालकैरंहसः पापादाहंतुः शत्रोर्वा पाहि । रक्ष ।
> ये च स्तोतृभ्यो ददति धनं तव समिंधनस्य कर्तरि प्रयच्छंति तांश्च पाहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are the lord of the house (गृहपतिः (*gṛhapatiḥ*)) of all the human (मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*): born of Manu) peoples (विशां (*viśāṃ*): the subjects); you are the master of the house. Therefore,**NOTE** O youngest Agni, protect (पाहि (*pāhi*): guard) me, who have well kindled you (समेद्धारं (*sameddhāraṃ*)), for a hundred winters (शतं हिमाः (*śataṃ himāḥ*): a hundred years), with a hundred (शतं (*śataṃ*)) guardians (पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*): protectors), from sin (अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)) or from the enemy who strikes. And protect also those who give wealth to the praisers (स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)), who give it to the one who makes you kindled.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*)—born in the line of Manu
- विश्वासां विशां (*viśvāsāṃ viśāṃ*)—of all the peoples
- गृहपतिः (*gṛhapatiḥ*)—as lord of the house
- आसि (*āsi*)—you are
- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O Agni, exceedingly young
- समेद्धारं (*sameddhāraṃ*)—me, who have made you kindled
- शतं हिमाः (*śataṃ himāḥ*)—for a hundred years
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—numbering a hundred
- पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*)—with protections
- अं हसः (*aṃ hasaḥ*)—from sins
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect
- ये च (*ye ca*)—whoever
- स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)—to your praisers
- ददति (*dadati*)—give wealth (protect them also)

### Printed p. 240

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you are the lord of the house for all the people born in the line of Manu. O exceedingly young Agni, protect me, who have kindled you, from sins for a hundred years, together with protections numbering a hundred. Protect also those who give wealth to those who praise you.

##### English translation
You, Agni, are the lord of the dwelling and of all men the descendents of Manu: protect me, youngest (of the gods), when kindling you, with a hundred defences against iniquity : (grant me) a hundred winters, (as well as to those) who bestow gifts upon your worshippers.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं न॑श्चि॒त्र ऊ॒त्या वसो॒ राधां॑सि चोदय ।  
> अ॒स्य रा॒यस्त्वम॑ग्ने र॒थीर॑सि वि॒दा गा॒धं तु॒चे तु नः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । न । चित्रः । ऊत्या । वसो इति । राधांसि । चोदय ।  
> अस्य । रायः । त्वं । अग्ने । रथीः । असि । विदाः । गाधं । तुचे । तु । नः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो वासकाग्ने चित्रो दर्शनीयस्त्वमूत्या रक्षया सह राधांसि धनानि
> नोऽस्मभ्यं जोदय । प्रेरय । अस्य सर्वत्र लोके परिदृश्यमानस्य रायो धनस्य
> त्वं रथीरसि । रंहिता नेता भवसि । अतः कारणादस्मभ्यं धनानि प्रेरयेत्यर्थः ।
> अपि च नोऽस्माकं तुचे । अपत्यनामैतत् । अपत्यायापतनहेतुभूताय पुत्रादये गाधं प्रतिष्ठां तु क्षिप्रं विदाः । लंभय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasu, Agni who makes others dwell, wonderful and worth beholding, urge riches towards us together with your protection. Of this wealth that is seen everywhere in the world you are the conveyer and leader; for that reason, urge wealth to us. And further: for our offspring (the word used here is a name for offspring), for sons and the rest who are the cause of the family's not falling, quickly obtain a firm footing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसो (*vaso*)—O giver of dwelling
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- चित्रः (*citraḥ*)—of attractive form
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- ऊत्या (*ūtyā*)—with protections
- राधांसि (*rādhāṃsi*)—riches
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us

- चोदय (*codaya*)—urge

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this well-known
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you yourself
- रथीः आसि (*rathīḥ āsi*)—are the leader
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- तुचे (*tuce*)—to sons, grandsons and the rest
- गाधं (*gādhaṃ*)—lasting condition and state
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- विदाः (*vidāḥ*)—cause to obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, giver of dwelling, you of attractive form, urge towards us riches accompanied by protections. For you are the leader of all well-known wealth. Quickly cause our sons, grandsons and the rest to obtain a lasting condition and state.

##### English translation
Wonderful (Agni), giver of dwellings, encourage us by (your) protection, and (the gift of) riches, for you are the conveyer, Agni, of this wealth : quickly bestow permanence upon our progeny.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पर्षि॑ तो॒कं तन॑यं प॒र्तृभि॒ष्त्वमद॑भै॒रप्र॑युत्वभिः ।  
> अग्ने॒ हेळां॑सि॒ दैव्या॑ युयोधि॒ नोऽदे॑वानि॒ ह्वरां॑सि च ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पर्षि । तोकं । तनयं । पर्तृभिः । त्वं । आदभ्यैः । अप्रयुत्त्वभिः ।  
> अग्ने । हेळांसि । दैव्या । युयोधि । नः । अदेवानि । ह्वरांसि । च ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वमदभ्यैः केनाप्यहिंसितैरप्रयुत्वभिः । यौतिरत्र पृथग्भावार्थः ।
> अपृथग्भूतैः संहतैः पर्तृभिः पालनसाधनैस्तोकं पुत्रं तनयं पौत्रं च पर्षि ।
> पालय । दैव्या देवसंबधीनि च हेळांसि क्रोधान्नोऽस्मत्तो युयोधि । पृथक्कुरु।
> आदेवानि मनुष्यसंबंधीनि च ह्वरांसि हिंसनानि चास्मत्तः पृथक्कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you protect our son (toka) and grandson (tanaya) with means of protection that are unharmed by anyone and are unseparated, that is, united (here the root has the sense of separation, and the word is taken as meaning not separated). Remove from us the wraths that belong to the gods, and likewise the injuries that belong to men; set them apart from us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- आदभैः (*ādabhaiḥ*)—those that are non-injurious, or those that are not injured by anyone
- अप्रयुत्वभिः (*aprayutvabhiḥ*)—those that are always kept together

- पर्तृभिः (*partṛbhiḥ*)—with protections
- तोकं (*tokaṃ*)—our son
- तनयं (*tanayaṃ*)—and grandson
- पर्षि (*parṣi*)—protect
- दैव्याः (*daivyāḥ*)—belonging to the gods
- हेळांसि (*heḷāṃsi*)—wraths
- नः (*naḥ*)—from us
- युयोधि (*yuyodhi*)—remove far away
- आदेवानि च (*ādevāni ca*)—and also those belonging to men
- ह्वरांसि (*hvarāṃsi*)—drive them far from us and make them flee

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, protect our son and grandson with protections that are non-injurious and not injured by anyone. Remove from us the wraths that belong to the gods. Make it so that, if men become angry with us, the effect of it does not touch us.

##### English translation
You protect with uninjurable, irremoveable defences (our) sons and grandsons : remove far from us celestial wrath and human malevolence.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ स॑खायः सब॒र्दुघां॑ धे॒नुम॑जध्व॒मुप॒ नव्य॑सा॒ वचः॑ ।  
> सृ॒जध्व॒मन॑पस्फुरां ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अ । सखायः । सबःदुघां । धेनुं । अजध्वं । उप । नव्यसा । वचः ।  
> सृजध्वं । अनपस्फुरां ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सखायः समानख्याना अध्वर्यवः सबर्दुघां । सबरिति पयसो नाम ।
> अमरणहेतुभूतस्य पयसो दोग्धीं धेनुं गामाजध्वं । अभिगच्छत । प्राप्नुत्त ।
> केन साधनेन । नव्यसा नवीयसा नवतरेण वचो वचसाह्वानरूपेण कद्देन ।
> तदनंतरमनपस्सुरां । स्पुरतिर्वधकर्मा । अनपबाध्यां तां धेनुमुप सृजध्वं ।
> वत्सेनोपसृष्टां कुरुत । मरुद्देवत्यत्वात् मरुतां यागाय पयो दोग्सुमिति
> शेषः । अथवा मरुतां माता पृश्नाख्या माध्यमिका वाग्गेनुः । हे सखायः
> स्तोतारः सबर्दुघां मरुज्जनहेतुभूतस्य पयसो दोग्धीं धेनुं पृश्चिं
> नव्यसा नवतरेण वचसा स्तोत्रेणोपाजध्वं उपागच्छत । अनपस्सुरामनपबाध-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O friends, adhvaryus who share one name, approach the cow that yields sabar (sabar is a name for milk), the cow that gives milk that is the cause of immortality. By what means? With a newer, fresher speech, in the form of a calling-out. After that, set free that cow, the unobstructed one (here the root meaning "to throb" has the sense of killing, so she is one who is not to be hindered), and let her go to her calf. Because the verse is addressed to the Maruts, what is to be supplied is that the milk is to be milked for the sacrifice of the Maruts. **NOTE**. Or else: the cow is the mother of the Maruts, the speech of the middle region called Pṛśni. O friends, praisers, approach with newer praise that Pṛśni, the cow who yields the milk that causes the birth of the Maruts; and release the unobstructed one.

### Printed p. 243

> नीयां तां सृजध्वं । बंधनाद्विसृजत । मुंचत । ईदृशी महती धेनुर्मरुतां
> माता किमु वक्तव्यं तेषां माहात्म्यमिति मरुत्सुतिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Release her from bondage; set her free. Such a great cow is the mother of the Maruts; what need then to speak of their greatness? Thus this is praise of the Maruts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—O friendly priests
- सबर्दुघां (*sabardughāṃ*)—who milks abundant milk
- धेनुं (*dhenuṃ*)—the cow
- नव्यसा (*navyasā*)—newly composed
- वचः (*vacaḥ*)—with words of praise
- आ अजध्वं (*ā ajadhvaṃ*)—approach
- अनहस्पुरां (*anahaspurāṃ*)—her who is free of hindrance (release her from bondage)
- उप सृजध्वं (*upa sṛjadhvaṃ*)—join her with her calf

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O friendly priests, approach with newly composed words of praise the cow who milks abundant milk. Join her, who is free of hindrance, with her calf.

##### English translation
Approach, friends, the milk-yielding cow with a new song, and let her loose unharmed.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या शर्धा॑य॒ मारु॑ताय॒ स्वभा॑नवे॒ श्रवोऽमृ॑त्यु॒ धुक्ष॑त ।  
> या मृ॑ळी॒के म॒रुतां॑ तु॒राणां॒ या सु॒म्मॆरे॑व॒याव॑री ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । शर्धाय । मारुताय । स्वभानवे । श्रवः । अमृत्यु । धुक्षत ।  
> या । मृळीके । मरुतां । तुराणां । या । सुम्नैः । एव्ययावरी ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या धेनुरमृत्युमरणहेतु श्रवोऽन्नं पयोलक्षणं मारुताय
> मरुत्संघाय धुक्षत अधुक्षत् । कीदृशाय । शर्धाय प्रसहनशीलाय स्वभानवे
> स्वायत्तदीप्तये । या च तुराणां क्षिप्रकारिणां मरुतां मृळिके सुखे तत्परा
> वर्तते । या च सुम्मैः सुखैर्हेतुभूत्यैरेवयावर्यॆवैर्गंतृभिरश्वैर्मध्यमस्थानैरुदकैर्वा सह यांत्यन्येषामपि सुखार्थं वृष्टिजलैः सहागच्छंती तां
> धेनुमुपाजध्वमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । अत्रापि पूर्ववन्मरुत्तुतिरधिगंतव्या ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The cow who has milked for the host of the Maruts immortal-making food in the form of milk, a host that is overpowering and self-luminous; and who stays intent on the happiness of the swift Maruts, who act quickly; and who goes along with happiness-bringing waters of the middle region for the sake of the happiness of others too, coming with the rain-waters (the words describing what she goes with are damaged in the print: horses that go, or waters of the middle region) **NOTE**: approach that cow; this is the connection with the preceding verse. Here also, as before, a praise of the Maruts is to be understood.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒रद्वा॑जा॒याव॑ धुक्षत द्वि॒ता ।  
> धे॒नुं च॑ वि॒श्वदो॑हस॒मिषं॑ च वि॒श्वभो॑जसं ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भरत् वाजाय । अव । धुक्षक । द्विता ।  
> धेनुं । च । विश्वदोहसं । इषं । च । विश्वभोजसं ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो भरद्वाजायास्मद्भात्रे द्विता द्वितयमव धुक्षत । किं तद्वितयं ।
> धेनुं च गां चेषं चान्नं च ! कीदृशीं धेनुं । विश्वदोहसं विश्वस्य व्याप्तस्य
> बहुलस्य दोग्ध्रीं । कीदृशमन्नं । विश्वभोजसं सर्वेषां भोगपर्याप्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, milk for Bharadvāja, our brother, the twofold. What is that twofold? The cow and food. What kind of cow? One that yields all, that is, one that milks what is pervasive and abundant. What kind of food? Food that is sufficient for the enjoyment of all.

O Maruts, milk for the sage Bharadvāja two kinds of sources of food. They are these: first, the cow who milks so as to pervade the world; second, the food that serves for the enjoyment of the whole world. (Milk both of these fully.)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word "na" is used in the sense of "now". Now I praise (the verb "I praise" is to be supplied) the might of the host of the Maruts: brilliant, loud-sounding, unassailed, that is, not met by enemies, nourishing, a might in the form of the host of the Maruts. And that host of the Maruts, in the manner in which it would make (the sentence continues on the next page).

> शतसंख्याकानि धनानि सं सहैव चर्षणिभ्यो मनुष्येभ्योऽस्मभ्यं कारिषत् कुर्यात् ।
> आकारः समुच्चये । ऋथा वा सहस्रा सहस्रसंख्याकानि धनानि च सं सहैव कारिषत्
> कुर्यात् तथा सौमाति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । अपि च स मरुद्धणो गूढा गूढानि

> सुवेदा सुलभानि च नोऽस्माकं करत् । करोतु । यदा तु लिंगादियं पौष्टी
> तदा मारुतं शर्ध इव त्वेषं पूषणं पूषकमेतत्संज्ञं देवं सौमाति
> योजनीयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

It would make for us men, together, hundreds of riches; the particle "ā" is in the sense of conjunction. Or else: in the way that it would make thousands of riches together, so I praise; this is connected with what precedes. And further: may that host of the Maruts bring to light for us the hidden, concealed riches, and may it make riches easy to find for us. But when this Ṛk is taken as addressed to Pūṣan, by its gender, then the connection is: I praise the god named Pūṣan, the nourisher, brilliant like the might of the Maruts.

- शता (*śatā*)—hundreds of riches
- सं (*saṃ*)—at one time
- चर्षणिभ्यः (*carṣaṇibhyaḥ*)—for us, the sacrificers
- कारिषत् (*kāriṣat*)—come into being
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—and thousands of riches
- सं (*saṃ*)—come into being at one time (for that purpose)
- न (*na*)—now
- तेषं (*teṣaṃ*)—the radiant
- तुविष्टणि (*tuviṣṭaṇi*)—the loud-sounding
- अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*)—the unassailed
- पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*)—the nourishing
- मारुतं (*mārutaṃ*)—of the host of Maruts
- शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)—the might (I praise)
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same host of Maruts
- गूळ्हा (*gūḷhā*)—hidden
- वसु (*vasu*)—riches

- वसु (*vasu*)—riches
- सुवेदा (*suvedā*)—so as to be easily known
- करत् (*karat*)—help

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In order that riches in hundreds and in thousands may come into being for us, the sacrificers, for that very purpose I now praise the might of the host of the Maruts: radiant, loud-sounding, unassailed and nourishing.

##### English translation
I now (glorify) the brilliant vigour of the company of the Maruts, loud-sounding, irresistible, cherishing, whereby hundreds and thousands (of treasures) are bestowed collectively upon men ; may that (company) make hidden wealth manifest; may it render the wealth easily accessible to us.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् मा मामा द्रव रक्षणार्थमभिगच्छ । हे अघृणे आगतदीप्ते
> अघा आहंत्रीरर्योऽरीरभिगंत्रीररातयः शत्रुभूताः प्रजा उप द्रव । बाधस्व ॥

> तै. सं १-५-१-४ । इति ॥ अहं च ते तवापिकर्णॆ कर्णावपिगते सविापदेशे स्थितः
> सन् नु क्षिप्रं शंसिषं । प्रशंसामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, run to me; come towards me for protection. O Aghṛṇi, of arrived radiance, run upon the enemy people: those who are slayers, who come against us, who are hostile; oppress them. The root "dru" with the prefix "upa" has the sense of oppressing, as in the passage "as it ran upon the offspring and the cattle of the sacrificer" (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-4). And I, standing at your ear, close beside you, quickly praise you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan, the nourishing god
- मा (*mā*)—facing me
- आ द्रव (*ā drava*)—be kind, for protection
- आघ्रणे (*āghraṇe*)—O god of exceeding radiance
- अघाः (*aghāḥ*)—the most sinful
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—who fall upon us and injure us
- अरातयः (*arātayaḥ*)—the enemies
- उप (द्रव) (*upa (drava)*)—oppress and drive them away
- ते (*te*)—your
- अपिकर्णे (*apikarṇe*)—standing right beside the ear
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- शंसिषं (*śaṃsiṣaṃ*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, be kind and turn towards me for protection. O god of exceeding radiance, oppress and drive away the enemies, the most sinful, who fall upon us and injure us. Standing right beside your ear, I quickly praise you.

##### English translation
Hasten, Pushan, to me: (repel), bright deity, (all) deadly assailing foes : close at your side I repeat your praise.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मोत सूरो॒ अह॑ ए॒वा च॒न ग्री॒वा आ॒दध॑ते॒ वेः ॥ १७ ॥

### Printed p. 249

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । काकंबीरं । उत् । वृहः । वनस्पतिं । अशस्तीः । वि । हि । नीनशः ।  
> मा । उत । सूरः । अहरिति । एव । चन । ग्रीवाः । आदधते । वेरिति वेः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यषिः पुत्रपौत्रसहितमात्मानं बहुपक्ष्याश्रयवनस्पतित्वेन रूपयन् तस्यानुद्वारमाशास्ते । हे पूषन् मा काकंबीरं काकानां भर्तारं वनस्पतिं वृक्षं
> मोद्वहः । उद्धर । मा बाधस्व । पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः सखीभूतैरुपेतमन्मैश्च बहुभिराश्रितं मां मा हिंसीरित्यर्थः । हितब्धश्चार्थे । अशस्तीरशंसनीया अशंसनीयस्य
> दुःखस्य कीर्तयित्रिर्वा शत्रुभूताः प्रजा वि नीनशो हि । विनाशय च । उतापि च
> सूरः प्रेरकः शत्रुरेवैवं माहः । आस्मान्मा हार्षित् ॥ एवमित्यभिसंबंधादाख्यातस्योदात्तवत्त्वाच्चाश्रुतोऽपि यथेत्येतद्वाक्येऽध्याह्रियते ॥ ग्रीवाः । गिरं
> त्यंतरवस्थापयंति बध्वंतीति ग्रीवा दामानि । यथा व्याधा वेः पक्षिणो हरणार्थं
> ग्रीवा दामानि जालरूपाण्यादधते भूम्यां निदधते तैश्च निहितैः पक्षिणो
> हरंत्येवमस्मान् बंधनोपायैः शत्रुर्मा हार्षिदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, picturing himself together with his sons and grandsons as a tree that is the resort of many birds, asks that it not be uprooted. O Pūṣan, do not uproot the tree that supports crows; do not oppress me, who am sheltered by many, joined by sons, grandsons and others who are my friends and by many other people: this is the meaning. The particle "hi" is in the sense of "and". Destroy completely the hostile people who are unpraiseworthy, or who proclaim unpraiseworthy sorrow. And further: may the enemy, the impeller, not carry us off. The word "so" (as, in the manner that) is supplied in this sentence, though not heard, because of the connection with "evam" and because the verb is accented. "Grīvāḥ" are the nooses that bind. As hunters lay on the ground snares in the form of nets, nooses, in order to catch birds, and birds are caught by them when so laid, so may the enemy not carry us off by means of devices for binding: this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- काकंबीरं (*kākaṃbīraṃ*)—that supports crows
- वनस्पतिं (*vanaspatiṃ*)—this tree
- मा उद्वहः (*mā udvahaḥ*)—do not overturn
- अशस्तिः (*aśastiḥ*)—the unpraiseworthy enemy peoples
- वि नीनशः हि (*vi nīnaśaḥ hi*)—destroy completely
- उत (*uta*)—and
- ग्रीवाः (*grīvāḥ*)—nets made of ropes
- वेः (*veḥ*)—spread out for the catching of birds
- आदधते (*ādadhate*)—in the way in which they catch birds
- एव चन (*eva cana*)—in the same way
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—the enemy who is bent on it
- मा (*mā*)—me
- अहः (*ahaḥ*)—let him not carry off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, do not overturn me, who am the giver of shelter and the nourisher of sons, grandsons and all the rest, like a tree that gives shelter to crows and all other birds, as one fells a tree. Destroy completely the unpraiseworthy enemy peoples. And as nets made of ropes, spread out for the catching of birds, catch the birds, in the same way may the enemy who is bent on seizing me not carry me off.

### Printed p. 250

##### English translation
Uproot not, Pushan, the forest lord, with its progeny of crows: utterly destroy those who are my revilers: let not the adversary ensnare me, as (fowlers) set snares for birds.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दृते॑रिव तेवृ॒कम॑स्तु स॒ख्यं ।  
> अच्छि॑द्रस्य दध॒न्वतः॒ सुपू॑र्णस्य दध॒न्वतः॑ ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दृतेः इव । ते । अवृकं । अस्तु । सख्यं ।  
> अच्छिद्रस्य । दधन् ऽवतः । सुपूर्णस्य । दधन् ऽवतः ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् ते तव सख्यं सखित्वमवृकं बाधकरहितं सर्वदैकरूप्येण
> वर्तमानमस्माकमस्तु । सर्वदा भवतु । दृतेरिव । यथा दृतेस्तदीयं सख्यमविच्छिन्नं तद्वत् । कीदृशो दृतिः । अच्चिद्रस्य छिद्ररहितस्य संश्लिष्टस्य दधन्वतो दधिमतः
> सुपूर्णस्य दध्ना सुष्टु पूरितस्य । पुनर्दधन्वत इति दध्नोऽधिकत्वद्योतनार्थः ।
> ईदृशो दृतिः सर्वदा पूष्टो रथे वर्तते । स इव वयमपि तव सखायो
> भवेमेत्यृषिराशास्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, may your friendship with us be free of hindrance, always continuing in one form; may it be so always. "Like that of the leather bag": as the friendship of the bag with its owner is unbroken, so may it be. What is the bag like? Without a hole, closely joined, containing curds, well filled with curds; the repetition of "containing curds" is to show the abundance of curds. Such a bag is always on the chariot of Pūṣan. Like it, may we also be your friends: thus the seer wishes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अच्चिद्रस्य (*accidrasya*)—without a break
- दधन्वतः (*dadhanvataḥ*)—holding curds
- सुपूर्णस्य (*supūrṇasya*)—and full of curds
- दृतेः इव (*dṛteḥ iva*)—as your bag is secure
- ते (*te*)—with you
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—my friendship
- अवृकं (*avṛkaṃ*)—without obstacle and everlasting
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, as your bag, without a break, holding exceeding curds and full of curds, is secure, so may my friendship with you be without obstacle and everlasting.

### Printed p. 251

##### English translation
May your frindship be unbroken, like (the surface) of a skin without a flaw, containing curds.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒रो हि मत्यै॒रसि॑ स॒मो दे॒वैरु॒त श्रि॒या ।  
> अ॒भि ख्यः॑ पूष॒न्कृत॑नासु न॒स्त्वमवा॑ नू॒नं यथा॑ पु॒रा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परः । हि । मर्त्यैः । असि । समः । देवैः । उत । श्रिया ।  
> अभि । ख्यः । पूषन् । पृतनासु । नः । त्वं । अव । नूनं । यथा । पुरा ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् मर्त्यैर्मर्त्येभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यः परः परस्तात्स्थितोऽसि । श्रिया
> संपदा देवैरुत सर्वैर्देवैश्च समः समानोऽसि । अतस्त्वं पृतनासु संग्रामेषु
> नोऽस्मानभि ख्यः । अभिपश्यानुग्रहदृष्ट्या विलोकय । यथा पुरा येन प्रकारेण
> पूर्वकालीनान्पुरुषान्ररक्षिथ एवं नूनमद्येदानीमव । आस्मान्रक्ष ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, you stand beyond mortals, that is, men; and by your wealth you are equal to all the gods. Therefore, in battles, look upon us: regard us with a look of favour. In the way in which you protected men of former times, so now, today, protect us.

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan, you
- मर्त्यैः (*martyaiḥ*)—than men
- परः (*paraḥ*)—greatly superior
- असि हि (*asi hi*)—you are
- श्रिया (*śriyā*)—by your wealth
- देवैः उत (*devaiḥ uta*)—with all the gods
- समः (*samaḥ*)—you are equal (therefore)
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)—in battles
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अभि ख्यः (*abhi khyaḥ*)—look with a favouring eye
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way
- पुरा (*purā*)—in former times
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- अव (*ava*)—protect us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, you are greatly superior to men. By your wealth you are equal to all the gods. Therefore look upon us with a favouring eye in battles. As in former times you protected those who worship you, so protect us now also.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वस्य॑ वा मरुतो॒ मर्त्य॑स्य वेजा॒नस्य॑ प्रयज्यवः ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वामीा । वामस्य । धूतयः । प्रनीतिः । अस्तु । सूनृता ।  
> देवस्य । वा । मरुतः । मर्त्यस्य । वा । ईजानस्य । प्रयज्यवः ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे धूतयः कंपयितारः प्रयज्यवः प्रकर्षेण यष्टव्या मरुतः सा सूनृता
> प्रियसत्यात्मिका माध्यमिका युष्मदीया वाक् प्रणीतिरस्तु । अस्मदर्थं धनानां
> प्रणेत्री भवतु । देवस्य वा मर्त्यस्य मनुष्यस्य वेजानस्यॆष्टवत उभयविधस्य
> पुरुषस्य वामिन् प्रशस्ता या वाक् वामस्य वननीयस्य धनस्य प्रणीतिः प्रणीत्रि सा
> सूनृतेत्यन्वयः । प्रणीतिरस्त्वस्मदर्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shakers, O Maruts to be especially worshipped, may that pleasant and true speech of yours, the speech of the middle region, be our guide; may she be the conductor of riches for us. Whether of a god or of a mortal man, of a sacrificer, of a person of either kind, the speech that is praised and that is the guide to desirable wealth is that pleasant and true speech: this is the construction. May she be the guide for us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धूतयः (*dhūtayaḥ*)—who make trees and the rest tremble
- प्रयज्यवः (*prayajyavaḥ*)—exceedingly worthy of worship
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- सूनृता (*sūnṛtā*)—the pleasant and true speech of the middle region
- प्रणीतिः अस्तु (*praṇītiḥ astu*)—may she be, in our case, the guide to wealth
- ईजानस्य (*ījānasya*)—of the worshipper
- देवस्य वा (*devasya vā*)—whether of a god
- मर्त्यस्य वा (*martyasya vā*)—or of a man
- वामी (*vāmī*)—this worshipful speech
- वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—may she point the way to the desired wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, who make trees and the rest tremble and who are exceedingly worthy of worship, may your pleasant and true speech of the middle region be for us a guide to wealth. May this speech, worthy of worship, whether for a god who worships or for a man, point the way to the desired wealth.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वे॒षं शवो॑ दधिरे॒ नाम॑ य॒ज्ञियं॑ म॒रुतो॑ वृत्र॒हं शवो॒

> त्वेषं । शवः । धदिरे । नाम । यज्ञियं । मरुतः । वृत्रहं । शवः । ज्येष्ठं ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्य च मरुद्दणस्य चर्कृतिः कर्म सद्यश्चित्सद्य एव द्यां पर्योति परिगच्छति
> दिव्यंतरिक्षे परितो वर्तते देवो न देवो द्योतमानः सूर्य इव तादृशगणात्मका
> मरुतस्वेषं दीप्तं नाम शत्रूणां नमयितृ यज्ञियं यज्ञार्हं शवो बलं

> वृत्रहं शवो ज्येष्ठं सर्वेभ्यः प्रशस्ततमं भवति ॥

That strength is the slayer of Vṛtra and other asuras; and that Vṛtra-slaying strength is the eldest, the most praised of all.

- नाम (*nāma*)—destroying enemies
- यज्ञियं (*yajñiyaṃ*)—worthy of worship

- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—that same strength
- वृत्रहं (*vṛtrahaṃ*)—becomes the destroyer of enemies

- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—that same strength
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—is the most praiseworthy of all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, the excellent work of whose host pervades the sky all around, continually, like the shining sun, have obtained a strength that is peaceful, that destroys enemies and that is worthy of worship. That same strength becomes the destroyer of enemies. That same enemy-destroying strength is the most praiseworthy of all. **NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पृश्न्याः । दुग्धं । सकृत् । पयः । तत् । अन्यः । न । अनु । जायते ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सकृद्द सकृदेव द्यौरजायत । उदपद्यत । सकृदुत्पन्नैव स्थिता भवति । न
> पुनस्तस्यां नष्टायामन्या तत्सदृशी द्यौर्जायते । भूमिश्च सकृदेवाजायत ।
> पृश्ना मरुतां मातुर्गोः पयश्च सकृदेकवारमेव दुग्धं यस्मात्पयसो
> मरुतो जज्जिरे । पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः । तै. सं. २-२-११-४ । इति
> तैत्तिरीयकं । यथा द्यावापृथिव्यौ सकृदेवोत्पद्येते एवं पृश्निरपि सकृद्दुग्धेनैव
> पयसा मरुतोऽजीजनत् । तत्ततः परमन्यः पदार्थो नानु जायते । तत्सदृशो
> नोत्पद्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Heaven was born once only; having been produced once, it stands, and when it is destroyed no other like it is born. The earth too was born once only. The milk of Pṛśni, the cow who is the mother of the Maruts, was milked once only; the Maruts were born from that milk. "From the milk of Pṛśni the Maruts were born": so the Taittirīya (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4). As heaven and earth are produced once only, so Pṛśni also generated the Maruts with milk milked once only. Beyond that, no other thing is born after it; nothing like it is produced.

- सकृत् ह (*sakṛt ha*)—once only
- अजायत (*ajāyata*)—was born
- भूमिः (*bhūmiḥ*)—the earth also
- सकृत् (*sakṛt*)—at one time
- अजायत (*ajāyata*)—was born

### Printed p. 255

- पृश्न्याः (*pṛśnyāḥ*)—of the cow named Pṛśni
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—the milk
- सकृत् (*sakṛt*)—once only
- दुग्धं (*dugdhaṃ*)—was milked
- तत् अन्यः (*tat anyaḥ*)—anything other than this
- न अनु जायते (*na anu jāyate*)—was not born in this way

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sky was born once only. The earth too was born once only. The milk of the cow named Pṛśni was milked once only. Nothing other than this was born in this way.

##### English translation
Once, indeed, was the heaven generated ; once was the earth born ; once was the milk of Prisni drawn : other than that was not similarly generated.

## Sūkta 49 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्तुषे जनमिति पंचदशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं भारद्वाजस्य ऋजिश्वन आर्षं
> वैश्वदेवं । अंत्या षट्पंचाशदक्षरा शक्वरी शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । स्तुषे
> पंचोन ऋजिश्वा ह वैश्वदेवं ह शक्वर्यंतमिति ॥ व्यूळ्हे दशरात्रे पंचमेऽहनीदं
> वैश्वदेवनिविद्धानं । सूत्रितं च । ऋर्भुर्विभ्वा स्तुषे जनमिति वैश्वदेवं । आ. ८-८ ।
> इति । आद्या महानामिव्रते जप्या ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning "Stuṣe janam" has fifteen Ṛks and is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is Ṛjiśvā, of the line of Bharadvāja; its deity is the Viśvedevas. The last Ṛk is a Śakvarī of fifty-six syllables; the rest are Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī states. On the fifth day of the Vyūḍha Daśarātra this is the Vaiśvadeva nivid-dhāna sūkta. It is laid down in the sūtra ऋर्भुर्विभ्वा स्तुषे जनमिति वैश्वदेवं (*ṛrbhurvibhvā stuṣe janamiti vaiśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 8-8). The first Ṛk is to be recited silently in the Mahānāmnī vrata.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Stuṣe janam" is the sixth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It contains fifteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Ṛjiśvā, born in the line of Bharadvāja. The deity is the Viśvedevas. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the metre called Śakvarī, of fifty-six syllables. All the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre. The Anukramaṇī says: स्तुषे पंचोन ऋजिश्वा ह वैश्वदेवं ह शक्वर्यंतमिति ॥ व्यूळ्हे दशरात्रे पंचमेऽहनीदं वैश्वदेवनिविद्धानं । सूत्रितं च । ऋर्भुर्विभ्वा स्तुषे जनमिति वैश्वदेवं । आ. ८-८ । इति । आद्या महानामिव्रते जप्या ॥ अनुवादवु—स्तुषे जनं ऎंब ई सूक्तवु नाल्कनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि आरनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि हदिनैदु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ भरद्वाजवंशोत्पन्ननाद ऋजिश्वा ऎंबवनु ऋषियु. विश्वेदेवतॆगळु देवतॆयु. ई सूक्तद कॊनॆय ऋक्कु ऐवत्तारु अक्षरगळुळ्ळ शक्वरी ऎंब छंदस्सिनदु. उळिद ऋक्कुगळॆल्ला त्रिष्टुप्‌छंदस्कवु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—स्तुषे पंचोन ऋजिश्वा ह वैश्वदेवं ह शक्वर्यंतं (*stuṣe paṃcona ṛjiśvā ha vaiśvadevaṃ ha śakvaryaṃtamiti ‖ vyūḷhe daśarātre paṃcame 'hanīdaṃ vaiśvadevanividdhānaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | ṛrbhurvibhvā stuṣe janamiti vaiśvadevaṃ | ā. 8-8 | iti | ādyā mahānāmivrate japyā ‖ anuvādavu—stuṣe janaṃ èṃba ī sūktavu nālkanèya anuvākadalli āranèya sūktavu. idaralli hadinaidu ṛkkugaḷiruvavu. ī sūktakkè bharadvājavaṃśotpannanāda ṛjiśvā èṃbavanu ṛṣiyu. viśvedevatègaḷu devatèyu. ī sūktada kònèya ṛkku aivattāru akṣaragaḷuḷḷa śakvarī èṃba chaṃdassinadu. uḷida ṛkkugaḷèllā triṣṭupchaṃdaskavu. anukramaṇikèyalli—stuṣe paṃcona ṛjiśvā ha vaiśvadevaṃ ha śakvaryaṃtaṃ*). On the fifth day of the ten-night sacrifice called Vyūḍha, this sūkta is to be recited as the nivid-dhāna sūkta in the middle of the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva śastra, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, ऋभुर्विभ्वा स्तुषे जनमिति वैश्वदेवं (*ṛbhurvibhvā stuṣe janamiti vaiśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 8-8). This sūkta is to be recited in the Mahānāmnī vrata as well.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्तु॒षे जनं॑ सुव्र॒तं नव्य॑सीभिर्गि॒र्भिर्मि॒त्रावरु॑णा सुम्म॒यंता॑ ।  
> त आ ग॑मंतु॒ त इ॒ह श्रु॑वंतु सुक्ष॒त्रासो॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो  ॒
> अग्निः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्तुषे । जनं । सुव्रतं । नव्यसीभिः । गीभिः । मित्रावरुणा । सुम्नयंता ।  
> ते । आ । गमंतु । ते । इह । श्रुवंतु । सुक्षत्रासः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अग्निः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुव्रतं सुकर्माणं जनं दैव्यं जनं देवसंघं नव्यसीभिर्नवतराभिर्गिर्भिः
> स्तुतिभिः स्तुषे । अहं स्तुवे । तथा मित्रावरुणा । मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायको वरुणः
> पापान्निवारयिता । एतावपि देवौ सौमि । कीदृशौ । सुम्नयंता सुम्मं सुखं
> स्तोत्कृणामिच्छंतौ । सुक्षत्रासः शोभनबलास्ते वरुणादयः सर्वॆ देवा इहास्मिन्यज्ञ
> आ गमंतु । आगच्छंतु । ते तादृशाः श्रुवंतु । अस्मदीयाः स्तुतीः शृण्वंतु च । अत्र
> मित्रादीनां परिगणनमुपलक्षणं । सूक्तस्य सर्वदेवताप्रतिपादकत्वात् । अत एव
> पूर्वं जनमिति सामान्यनिर्देशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I praise the people of good works, that is, the host of the gods, with newer songs of praise. So too I praise Mitra and Varuṇa: Mitra the protector from death, Varuṇa the warder-off of sins; I praise both these gods. What are they like? They desire happiness for those who praise. May those of good strength, Varuṇa and the rest, all the gods, come here to this sacrifice; and may they, such as they are, hear our praises. Here the enumeration of Mitra and the others is only indicative, since the sūkta teaches all the deities; for that reason the word "people" is used first as a general designation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुकृतं (*sukṛtaṃ*)—of excellent works
- जनं (*janaṃ*)—the divine people
- नव्यसीभिः (*navyasībhiḥ*)—new
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with praises
- स्तुषे (*stuṣe*)—I praise
- सुम्नयंता (*sumnayaṃtā*)—who bring happiness
- मित्रा वरुणा (*mitrā varuṇā*)—I praise Mitra and Varuṇa
- सुक्षत्रासः (*sukṣatrāsaḥ*)—of excellent strength

- ते (*te*)—those
- वरुणादिगळु (*varuṇādigaḷu*)—Varuṇa and the others
- इह (*iha*)—to this place of sacrifice
- आ गमंतु (*ā gamaṃtu*)—may they graciously come
- ते (*te*)—all of them (that is)
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- श्रुवंतु (*śruvaṃtu*)—may they hear our prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise with new praises the divine people of excellent works. I praise also Mitra and Varuṇa, the bringers of happiness. May Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni, of excellent strength, all come together to our sacrifice. May all of them hear our praises and prayers.

##### English translation
I commend with new hymns the man observant of his duty, and the beneficent Mitra and Varuna: may they, the mighty ones. Varuna, Mitra, Agni, come to our rite, and listen (to our praises).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒शोवि॑श॒ ईड्य॑मध्व॒रेष्वदृ॑प्तक्रतुमर॒तिं यु॑व॒त्योः ।  
> दि॒वः शिशुं॒ सह॑सः सू॒नुम॒ग्निं य॒ज्ञस्य॑ के॒तुम॑रु॒षं यज॑ध्यै ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विशःविशः । ईड्यं । अध्वरेषु । अदृप्तक्रतुं । आरतिं । युवत्योः ।  
> दिवः । शिशुं । सहसः । सूनुं । अग्निं । यज्ञस्य । केतुं । अरुषं । यजध्यै ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विशो विशः सर्वस्याः प्रजाया अध्वरेषु यज्ञेष्टीड्यमृत्तिग्निः स्तुत्यमदृप्तक्रतुं दर्परहितकर्माणममूढप्रज्ञं वा युवत्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योररतिमभिगंतारमर्यं स्वामिनं दिवो द्युलोकस्य शिशुं पुत्रं । दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे
> अग्निः। ऋग्वे १०-४५-१। इति निगमः। यद्वा। दिवः स्तोतुः पुत्रभूतं । तथापि निगमो
> भवति । त्वं पुत्रो भवसि यस्तेऽविधत् । ऋग्वे. २-१-९ । इति । सहसो बलस्य सूनुं
> पुत्रं यज्ञस्य यागस्य केतुं प्रज्ञापकमरुषमारोचमानमेवंगुणकमग्निं
> यजध्यै यष्टुं । स्तुष इत्यनुषज्यते । स्तुषे । स्तुवे ॥
> XXI 17

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the priest, is to be praised in the sacrifices of every people. He is of undaunted action, that is, of work free of pride, or of unconfused wisdom. He is the goer, the lord, of the two young women, heaven and earth. He is the child, the son, of heaven. "Agni was born first from heaven" (Ṛgve. 10-45-1): thus the Nigama. **NOTE** Or else: he is the son of the one who praises; so too there is a Nigama: "You become a son to the one who served you" (Ṛgve. 2-1-9). **NOTE** He is the son of strength, the sign of the sacrifice, shining; Agni, of such qualities, I praise, in order to worship him. The word "I praise" is carried over from the first Ṛk.
