- विशोविशः (*viśoviśaḥ*)—of every worshipper
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—in the sacrifices also
- ईड्यं (*īḍyaṃ*)—the one to be praised
- आदृप्तक्रतुं (*ādṛptakratuṃ*)—the one whose action is free of pride
- युवत्योः (*yuvatyoḥ*)—to the two young women, heaven and earth
- अरतिं (*aratiṃ*)—the lord
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the world of heaven
- शिशुं (*śiśuṃ*)—the son
- सहसः (*sahasaḥ*)—of strength
- सूनुं (*sūnuṃ*)—the son
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the one who makes it known
- अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*)—the one of attractive golden colour
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—in order to worship, I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise Agni, in order to worship him: he who is to be praised in the sacrifices of every worshipper, whose action is free of pride, who is the lord of the two young women, heaven and earth, the son of the world of heaven, the son of strength, the one who makes the sacrifice known, of attractive golden colour.

##### English translation
(I incite the worshipper) to offer worship to Agni, who is to be adored at the sacrifices of every man; whose acts are free from arrogance; the lord of two youthful (brides, heaven and earth); the child of heaven, the son of strength, the brilliant symbol of sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒रु॒षस्य॑ दुहि॒तरा॒ विरू॑पे॒ स्तृभि॑र॒न्या पि॑पि॒शे सूरो॑ अ॒न्या ।  
> मि॒थ॒स्तुरा॑ वि॒चरं॑ती पाव॒के मन्म॑ श्रु॒तं न॑क्षत ऋ॒च्यमा॑ने ॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरुषस्य । दुहितरा । विरूपे इति विरूपे । स्तृभिः । अन्या । पिपिशे । सूरः । अन्या ।  
> मिथःतुरा । विचरंती इति विचरंती । पावके इति । मन्म । श्रुतं । नक्षतः ।  
> ऋच्यमाने इति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमहोरात्रयोः स्तुतिः । अरुषस्यारोचमानस्य सूर्यस्य दुहितरा
> दुहितरौ । सूर्येण ह्यहोरात्रयोर्विभागः क्रियते । अतस्तदधीनात्मलाभत्वात्तस्य
> दुहितरावित्युच्येते । विरूपे शुक्लकृष्णतया नानारूपे । तयोरनैका रात्रिः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is a praise of Day and Night. "Of the shining (Sun)", that is, of the radiant Sun, there are two daughters. By the Sun the division of day and night is made; therefore, since they gain their very existence in dependence on him, they are called his two daughters. They are "of various form" विरूपे (*virūpe*), that is, of different forms, by being white and black. Of the two, one is Night.

### Printed p. 259

> स्त्रृभिर्नक्षत्रैः पिपिशे । पिश्यते । संश्लिष्यते ॥ पिश अवयव इति धातुः ॥ अन्याहरात्मिका
> दुहिता सूरः सूर्येण पिपिशे । संश्लिष्यते । ते च नक्षत्रैः सूर्येण चालंकृते
> भवत इत्यर्थः । मिथस्तुरा परस्परं बाधयंत्यौ । अह्ना रात्रिर्निवर्त्यते रात्रा
> चाहरिति परस्परं बाधः । अत एव विचरंती विविधं पृथक्वरंत्यौ पावके सर्वस्य
> शोधयित्र्यौ । एवंभूते अहश्च रात्रिश्च ऋच्यमाने अस्माभिः स्तूयमाने सत्यौ
> श्रुतं श्रोतव्यं मन्म मननीयं स्तोत्रमस्मत्कृतं नक्षतः । व्याप्नुतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Night "is joined" पिपिशे (*pipiśe*) with the stars, that is, she is adorned; the other, whose nature is day, is joined with the Sun. Thus both are adorned, the one with the stars, the other with the Sun. "Mutually opposed" मिथस्तुरा (*mithasturā*): they obstruct each other; night is driven back by day, and day by night, which is their mutual obstruction. Therefore they are "proceeding diversely", moving apart in various ways; "purifying", cleansing everything. Day and Night, being thus, are praised by us: may the praise made by us, worthy to be heard and pondered, pervade them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विरूपे (*virūpe*)—the two of white and black form, of various colours
- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of the Sun of golden colour
- दुहितरा (*duhitarā*)—of the two daughters, Day and Night
- अन्या (*anyā*)—one, Night
- स्तृभिः (*stṛbhiḥ*)—with the shining stars
- पिपिशे (*pipiśe*)—she shines
- अन्या (*anyā*)—the other, Day
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—she is joined with the Sun
- मिथस्तुरा (*mithasturā*)—the two who obstruct each other's state
- विचरंती (*vicaraṃtī*)—the two who move about in different ways
- पावके (*pāvake*)—the two who purify
- ऋच्यमाने (*ṛcyamāne*)—the two Day and Night, who are praised by us
- श्रुतं (*śrutaṃ*)—the well-known
- मन्म (*manma*)—the meditative
- नक्षतः (*nakṣataḥ*)—may they pervade our praise (may they hear it and be satisfied)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Of the two daughters of the Sun of golden colour, who are of various colours, white and black, Day and Night, the one, Night, shines with the shining stars. The other, Day, is joined with the Sun. Obstructing each other in their respective states, moving about in different ways, purifying, praised by us, may Day and Night hear our praise, well known and meditative, and be satisfied.

##### English translation
May the two daughters of the radiant (sun) of various form, of whom one glitters with stars, the other (is bright) with the sun, mutually opposed, proceeding diversely, purifying (all things), and entitled to our laudation, be pleased by the praise they hear (from us).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वा॒युमच्छा॑ बृह॒ती म॑नी॒षा बृ॒हद्र॑यिं वि॒श्ववा॑रं  ॒
> रथप्रां ।  
> द्यु॒तद्या॑मा नि॒युतः॒ पत्य॑मानः क॒विः क॒विमि॑यक्षसि प्रयज्यो ॥

### Printed p. 260

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वायुं । अच्छ । बृहती । मनीषा । बृहत्कयं । विश्ववारं । रथप्रां ।  
> द्युतशयामा । नियुतः । पत्यमानः । कविः । कविं । इयक्षसि । प्रयज्यो इति  
> प्रयज्यो ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहती महती मनीषास्मदीया स्तुतिर्वायुमच्छाभिमुख्येन प्र गच्छतु ॥
> उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ कीदृशं वायुं । बृहद्रयिं महाधनं
> विश्ववारं विश्वैर्वर्णनीयं संभजनीयं रथप्रां रथस्यात्मीयस्य प्रातारं पूरयितारं । यद्वा । स्तोत्यणां रथं धनैः पूरयितारं । अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । हे
> प्रयज्यो प्रकर्षेण यष्टव्य वायो द्युतद्यामा प्रदीप्तयानो नियुत
> आत्मीयरथयोज्या वडवास्ताः पत्यमानोऽभिहतन्नभिगच्छन् । यद्वा । पत्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । तासां वडवानामीश्वरः कविः क्रांतदर्शि । एवंभूतस्त्वं कविं मेधाविनं
> स्तोतारमियक्षसि । धनेन पूजय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May our great praise go forward, face to face, to Vāyu; the verb is supplied, as suited to the preposition. What sort of Vāyu? One of great wealth; to be chosen and shared in by all; the filler of his own chariot, or, alternatively, the one who fills the chariots of the praisers with wealth. Then comes the direct address: O Vāyu, to be worshipped in the highest degree, whose chariot shines, your "Niyut" are your own mares yoked to your chariot; you approach them, or else (the root meaning lordship) you are the lord of those mares; you are far-seeing. Being such, you honour the sage, the wise praiser, with wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—of great qualities
- मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—our praise
- बृहद्रयिं (*bṛhadrayiṃ*)—the one of very great wealth
- विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)—the one desired by all
- रथप्रां (*rathaprāṃ*)—the one who fills the chariot of the praiser with wealth
- वायुं अच्छ (*vāyuṃ accha*)—facing Vāyu
- प्र (गच्छतु) (*pra (gacchatu)*)—may it go forth and reach
- प्रयज्यो (*prayajyo*)—O Vāyu, worthy of the highest worship
- द्युतद्यामा (*dyutadyāmā*)—the one of radiant lustre
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the one of far-reaching wisdom, you
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—your horses
- सत्यमानः (*satyamānaḥ*)—driving (and coming)
- कविं (*kaviṃ*)—the sage, the praiser
- इयक्षसि (*iyakṣasi*)—satisfy with wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May our praise, of great qualities, go forth and reach Vāyu, who has very great wealth, is desired by all, and fills the praiser's chariot with wealth. O Vāyu, worthy of the highest worship, you of radiant lustre and far-reaching wisdom, come driving your horses and satisfy the sage, the praiser, with wealth.

### Printed p. 261

##### English translation
May our earnest praise proceed to the presence of Vayu, the possessor of vast riches, the desired of all, the filler of his chariot (with wealth for his worshippers): most adorable (Vayu) you are riding in a radiant car, and driving your Niyut (steeds); you, are far-seeing, show favour to the sage, (your adorer).

> अश्विनोः स्वभूतः स रथो मे मदीयं वपुः शरीरं छदयत् । छादयतु ।
> तेजसाच्छादयतु । यो रथो विरुक्मान् विरोचनवान् विशेषेण दीप्यमानो
> मनसा मनोव्यापारमात्रेण युजानोऽश्वैः संप्रयुज्यमानो भवति । हे नरा
> नेतार् हे नासत्या सत्यस्वभावौ सत्यस्य नेतार् नासिकाप्रभवौ वाश्विन् येन रथेन
> वर्तिः स्तोतृगृहं तनयाय पुत्राय त्मने तत्पित्रॆ स्तोत्रे चेषयध्यॆ कामान्प्रापयितुं याथो गच्छथः स रथ इति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May that chariot, belonging to the Aśvins, clothe my body, that is, clothe it with radiance. That chariot is shining, brilliantly bright, and is yoked with horses by a mere act of the mind. O leaders, O Nāsatyas, who are true in nature, leaders of the true, or born from the nose: by which chariot you go to the house of the praiser, to bring about the desires of his son and of the father, the praiser himself; that chariot, as in the first part, is to be connected with the beginning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरा (*narā*)—O leaders
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—O Aśvin gods
- येन (*yena*)—with which chariot
- तनयाय (*tanayāya*)—for the son of the praiser
- त्मने च (*tmane ca*)—and also for the praiser himself
- इषयध्यै (*iṣayadhyai*)—in order to fulfil the desired object
- वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*)—towards the house of the praiser
- याथः (*yāthaḥ*)—you go
- अश्विनोः (*aśvinoḥ*)—of you, the Aśvin gods
- यः रथः (*yaḥ rathaḥ*)—which chariot
- विरुक्मान् (*virukmān*)—shining brilliantly

### Printed p. 262

- मनसा (*manasā*)—by mere intention of its own
- युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)—is joined with the horses
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same chariot
- मे वपुः (*me vapuḥ*)—my body
- छदयत् (*chadayat*)—may it cover with its radiance

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, leaders, may that same chariot of yours, which shines brilliantly and is joined with the horses by mere intention of its own, and with which you go towards the house of the praiser in order to fulfil the desired object for the praiser's son and for the praiser, cover my body with its radiance.

##### English translation
May that splendid car of the Aswins, which is harnessed at a thought, clothe my form (with radiance): that (car) with which, Nasatyas, leaders of (rites), you go to the dwelling (of the worshipper) to fulfil his desires for his posterity and himself.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पर्ज॑न्यवाता वृषभा पृथि॒व्याः पुरी॑षाणि जिन्वत॒मप्या॑नि ।  
> सत्य॑श्रुतः कवयो॒ यस्य॑ गी॒र्भिर्जग॑तः स्थात॒र्जग॒दा कृ॑णुध्वं॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पर्जन्यवाता । वृषभा । पृथिव्याः । पुरीषाणि । जिन्वतं । अप्यानि ।  
> सत्यश्रुतः । कवयः । यस्य । गीभिः । जगतः । स्थातः । जगत् । आ । कृणुध्वं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पर्जन्यवाता पर्जन्यवायू वृषभा वृष्टेः कर्तारौ पृथिव्याः । अंतरिक्षनामैतत् । अंतरिक्षादप्यान्याप्तव्यानि पुरीषाणि पूरकाण्युदकानि जिन्वतं । प्रेरयतं ।
> उत्तरोऽर्धर्चो मारुतः । हे सत्यश्रुतः सत्यस्य स्तोत्रस्य श्रोतारः कवयो
> मेधाविनो मरुतो यस्य स्तोतुर्गिर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्यूयं स्तुता भवथ तस्य
> स्तोतुर्जगत्सावरजंगमात्मकं सर्वं प्राणिजातमा कृणुध्वं । अभिमुख्येन कुरुत ।
> हे जगतः स्थातः । गणाभिप्रायमेकवचनं । स्थावरजंगमात्मकस्य जगतोऽवस्थापक
> हे मरुद्धणेति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Parjanya and Vāta, that is, Parjanya and Vāyu, makers of rain, send forth the waters from the "earth", a name of the firmament: the waters that are to be obtained from the firmament, that fill. The latter half of the Ṛk is addressed to the Maruts. O hearers of true praise, sages, Maruts: by the praises of whichever praiser you are praised, for that praiser make favourable the whole world, all beings, moving and unmoving. O "stander" of the world: the singular is meant for the host; O establisher of the world of the moving and the unmoving, O host of Maruts: so it is to be construed.

### Printed p. 263

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पर्जन्यवाता (*parjanyavātā*)—O Parjanya and Vāyu gods
- वृषभा (*vṛṣabhā*)—you, makers of rain
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—from the firmament
- अप्यानि (*apyāni*)—that are to be obtained
- पुरीषाणि (*purīṣāṇi*)—the waters
- जिन्वतं (*jinvataṃ*)—send them forth and pour them down
- सत्यश्रुतः (*satyaśrutaḥ*)—you who hear true praises
- जगतः (*jagataḥ*)—of the moving world
- स्थातः (*sthātaḥ*)—O givers of stability
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—O sages, O Maruts
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of the praiser whose
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—by whose praises you are pleased, of such a praiser
- जगत् (*jagat*)—all the wealth, moving and unmoving
- आ कृणुध्वं (*ā kṛṇudhvaṃ*)—cause it to increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Parjanya and Vāyu, makers of rain, send forth and pour down the waters that are to be obtained from the firmament. O Maruts, hearers of true praises, givers of stability to the moving world, sages: cause to increase all the wealth, moving and unmoving, of that praiser by whose praises you are pleased.

##### English translation
Parjanya and Vata, showerers of rain, send from the firmament available waters : sage Maruts, hearers of truth, establishers of the world, multiply the moveable (wealth of him) by whose praises (you are propitiated).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पावी॑रवी क॒न्या॑ चि॒त्रायुः॒ सर॑स्वती वी॒रप॑त्नी॒ धियं॑ धात् ।  
> ग्नाभि॒रच्छि॑द्रं शर॒णं स॒जोषा॑ दुरा॒धर्षं॑ गृण॒ते शर्म॑  
> यंसत् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पावीरवी । कन्या । चित्रआयुः । सरस्वती । वीरपत्नी । धियं । धात् ।  
> ग्नाभिः । अच्छिद्रं । शरणं । सजोषाः । दुःआधर्षं । गृणते । शर्म । यंसत् ॥७॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अन्वारंभणीयायां सारस्वतस्य हविषो याज्या पावीरवीत्येषा । सूत्रितं
> च । पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः । आ. २-८ । इति ॥ एकादशिने

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Anvārambhaṇīyā, the verse पावीरवी (*pāvīravī*) is the Yājyā for the oblation to Sarasvatī. It is so put in the Sūtra: पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ pīpivāṃsaṃ sarasvataḥ*) (Ā. 2-8). Further, for the एकादशिने (*ekādaśine*)

### Printed p. 264

> सारस्वते पशावेषैव पुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुर्यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूः । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥ अग्निमारुते शस्त्रेऽप्येषा ।
> सूत्रितं च । राकामहमिति द्वे पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः । आ. ५-२० । इति ॥
> पावीरवी शोधयित्रि कन्या कमनीया चित्रायुश्चित्रगमना चित्रान्ना वा
> वीरपत्नी । वीरः प्रजापतिः पतिर्यस्यास्तादृशी । यद्वा । वीराणां पालयित्रि ।
> एवंभूता सरस्वती धियमस्मदीयं कर्म यज्ञाख्यं धात् । दधातु । धारयतु ।
> ददातु ना । शब्देन प्रतिपादितो ह्यर्थोऽनुष्ठीयते । अपि च ग्नाभिर्देवपत्नीभिः
> सजोषाः सह प्रीयमाणा । यद्वा । ग्ना गायत्र्यादीनि छंदांसि । छंदांसि वै ग्ना
> इति श्रुतेः । तैः सह प्रीयमाणा गृणते स्तुवते मह्यमच्छिद्रं छिद्ररहितं दुराधर्षं
> शत्रुभिः शीतवातादिभिश्च धर्षितुमशक्यं शरणं गृहं शर्म सुखं च यंसत् ।
> प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse is also the Yājyā for the cake offered in the animal sacrifice to Sarasvatī. So it is put in the Sūtra: पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुर्यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuryaste stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūḥ*) (Ā. 3-7). It is used also in the Agnimāruta Śastra. So it is put in the Sūtra: राकामहमिति द्वे पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः (*rākāmahamiti dve pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ*) (Ā. 5-20). "Pāvīravī" is the purifier; "kanyā" is the lovely one; "citrāyuḥ" is the one of wondrous motion, or of wondrous food; "vīrapatnī" is she whose husband is Vīra, that is Prajāpati; or else she is the protectress of heroes. May Sarasvatī, such as she is, "grant", bestow, bear, give our rite called the sacrifice. **NOTE** The meaning conveyed by a word is indeed carried out. Further, she is "sajoṣāḥ" with the "gnā", that is, pleased together with the wives of the gods; or else "gnā" are the metres, the Gāyatrī and the rest, according to the Śruti छंदांसि वै ग्ना इति (*chaṃdāṃsi vai gnā iti*) **GLOSS**; pleased together with these, may she grant to me who praise a dwelling that is free of breach and cannot be assailed by enemies, nor by cold wind and the like, and happiness as well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पावीरवी (*pāvīravī*)—the purifier
- कन्या (*kanyā*)—the one of lovely form
- चित्रायुः (*citrāyuḥ*)—the one with food of many kinds
- वीरपत्नि (*vīrapatni*)—the protectress of heroes
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—to us the understanding that teaches the rite
- धात् (*dhāt*)—may she bestow
- ग्नाभिः (*gnābhiḥ*)—with the wives of the gods
- सजोषा (*sajoṣā*)—that same Sarasvatī, who is joined with them
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—to me, the praiser
- अच्छिद्रं (*acchidraṃ*)—that which is free of breach
- दुराधर्षं (*durādharṣaṃ*)—that which cannot be struck by enemies
- शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*)—a house
- शर्म (*śarma*)—and happiness
- यंसत् (*yaṃsat*)—may she favour us by giving

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddess Sarasvatī, who is the purifier, of lovely form, with food of many kinds, the protectress of heroes, bestow on us the understanding that teaches the rite. May that same Sarasvatī, joined with the wives of the gods, favour me, the praiser, by giving a house free of breach and not to be struck by enemies, and happiness.

##### English translation
May the purifying, amiable, graceful Saraswati, the bride of the hero, favour our pious rite: may she, together with the wives of the gods, well pleased, bestow upon him who praises her a habitation free from defects, and impenetrable (to wind and rain), and (grant him) felicity.

### Printed p. 265

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice, in the oblation made to the deity Sarasvatī, this Ṛk beginning पावीरवी (*pāvīravī*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ pīpivāṃsaṃ sarasvataḥ*) (Ā. 2-8). In the sacrifice called एकादशिन् (*ekādaśin*), in the animal oblation addressed to the deity Sarasvatī, this Ṛk is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra when the cake is offered: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुर्यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuryaste stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūḥ*) (Ā. 3-7); and that this Ṛk is to be recited also in the mantras of the Agnimāruta Śastra is set forth by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra राकामहमिति द्वे पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः (*rākāmahamiti dve pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ*) (Ā. 5-20).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒थस्प॑थः॒ परि॑पतिं वच॒स्या कामे॑न कृ॒तो अ॒भ्या॑नळ॒र्कं ।  
> सनो॑ रासच्चु॒रुध॑श्चं॒द्राग्रा॒ धियं॑धियं सीषधाति॒ प्र  ॒
> पूषा ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पथःपथः । परिपतिं । वचस्या । कामेन । कृतः । अभि । आनट् । अर्क० ।  
> सः । नः । रासत् । शुरुधः । चंद्रग्राः । धियंधियं । सीसधाति । प्र । पूषा॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकादशिने पौष्णे पश् पथस्पथ इति हविषो याज्या । सूत्रितं च । पथस्पथः
> परिपतिं वचस्या बृहस्पते या परमा परावदिति । आ ३-७ । इति ॥
> पथस्पथः सर्वस्य मार्गस्य परिपतिमधिपतिमर्कमर्चनीयं पूषणं कामेन
> काम्यमानेन फलेन कृतो वशीकृतः स्तोता वचस्या स्तुत्याभ्यानट् । अभ्यश्नुतां ।
> प्राप्नोतु । स च पूषा नोऽस्मभ्यं शुरुधः शुचो रोधयित्रीर्गाश्चंद्राग्राः ।
> चंद्रमिति हिरण्यनाम । हिरण्यप्रमुखा यद्वा स्वर्णशृंगा रासत् । ददातु ॥
> रा दाने । आस्माल्लोटि रूपं ॥ तथा धियं धियं सर्वमस्मदीयं कर्म स पूषा
> प्र सीषधाति । प्रसाधयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Ekādaśinī, in the animal sacrifice to Pūṣan, पथस्पथः (*pathaspathaḥ*) is the Yājyā for the oblation. So it is put in the Sūtra: पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या बृहस्पते या परमा परावदिति (*pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā bṛhaspate yā paramā parāvaditi*) (Ā. 3-7). Pūṣan is the lord of every path, the worshipful one. The praiser, who has been brought under his power by the fruit he desires, is to reach him with his praise. And may that Pūṣan give us cows, the ones that check sorrow, "candrāgrāḥ": "candra" is a name of gold, so they are gold-fronted, or gold-horned. And may that Pūṣan carry through every rite of ours.

### Printed p. 266

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पथस्पथः (*pathaspathaḥ*)—of all paths
- परिपतिं (*paripatiṃ*)—the excellent protector
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—and the worshipful god Pūṣan
- कामेन (*kāmena*)—by the desire to obtain the fruit
- कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)—the praiser who has brought him under his power
- वचस्या (*vacasyā*)—with his praise
- अभ्यानट् (*abhyānaṭ*)—may he approach and reach him
- सः पूषा (*saḥ pūṣā*)—that same god Pūṣan
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- चंद्राग्राति (*caṃdrāgrāti*)—those with golden horns
- शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*)—cows
- रासत् (*rāsat*)—may he give
- धियंधियं (*dhiyaṃdhiyaṃ*)—all our rites
- प्र सीषधाति (*pra sīṣadhāti*)—may he adorn completely (make fruitful)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the praiser, who by the desire to obtain the fruit has brought under his power the god Pūṣan, the excellent protector of all paths and the worshipful one, approach him with his praise and reach him. May that same god Pūṣan give us cows with golden horns. May he adorn all our rites completely.

##### English translation
May (the worshipper), influenced by the hope (of reward), approach with praise the adorable (Pushan), protector of all paths : may he bestow upon us cows with golden horns: may Pushan bring to perfection our every rite.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifice called एकादशिन् (*ekādaśin*), when the oblation is offered in the animal homa addressed to Pūṣan, this Ṛk beginning पथस्पथः (*pathaspathaḥ*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या बृहस्पते या परमा परावदिति द्वे (*pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā bṛhaspate yā paramā parāvaditi dve*) (Ā. 3-7).

Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk:
पथस्पथोऽधिपतिं वचनेन कामेन कृतोऽभ्यानदर्कमभ्यापन्नोऽकर्मिति वा स नो ददातु चायनीयाग्राणि धनानि कर्मकर्म च नः प्रसाधयतु पूषेति ॥ (*pathaspatho 'dhipatiṃ vacanena kāmena kṛto 'bhyānadarkamabhyāpanno 'karmiti vā sa no dadātu cāyanīyāgrāṇi dhanāni karmakarma ca naḥ prasādhayatu pūṣeti ‖*) (Ni. 12-18)

This god Pūṣan is the lord of all paths and is to be worshipped by all. May the praiser approach such a god with praise, that is, praise him, for the obtaining of his desired objects. May that god

### Printed p. 267

give us, and favour us with, wealth of many kinds and of the best kind, in every act, that is, in all acts such as the sacrifice and the offering: this is the main sense of the explanation.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒थ॒म॒भाजं॑ य॒शसं॑ वयो॒धां सु॑पा॒णिं दे॒वं सु॒गभ॑स्ति॒मृभ्वं॑ ।  
> होता॑ यक्षद्यज॒तं प॒स्त्या॑नाम॒ग्निस्वष्टा॑रं सु॒हवं॑ वि॒भावा॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रथमभाजं । यशसं । वयोधां । सुपाणिं । देवं । सुगभस्तिं । ऋभ्वं ।  
> होता । यक्षत् । यजतं । पस्त्यानां । अग्निः । त्वष्टारं । सुहवं । विभावा ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वाष्टे पशौ प्रथमभाजमिति हविषो याज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्रथमभाजं
> यशसं वयोधां सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> प्रथमभाजं प्रथम उत्पत्तिकाल एव विभक्तारं जंतूनां । यावच्चो वै
> रेतसः सिक्तस्य त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति तावच्चो वै तत्प्रजायत । शै. सं. १-५-९-१ ।
> इति श्रुतेः । यशसं यशस्सिनं वयोधां वयस्सोऽन्नस्य हविर्लक्षणस्य धातारं
> धारयितारं यद्वा स्तोतृभ्योऽन्नप्रदं सुपाणिं । हस्तस्य मणिबंधादूर्ध्वप्रदेशः
> पाणिः । शोभनपाणिकं देवं दानादिगुणयुक्तं सुगभस्तिं । गभस्तिरिति बाहुनाम ।
> शोभनदोर्दंडमृभ्वमुरु भासमानं महांतं वा पस्त्यानां । पस्त्यमिति
> गृहनाम । तत्स्थानां यजतं यष्टव्यं । गृहस्थैर्यजनीयमित्यर्थः । सुहवं
> सुखेन हातुं शक्यं । एवंभूतं त्वष्टारं होता देवानामाह्वाता विभावा
> दीप्यमानोऽग्निर्यक्षत् । यजत् । अनेन हविषा यजतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ, प्रथमभाजं (*prathamabhājaṃ*) is the Yājyā for the oblation. So it is put in the Sūtra: प्रथमभाजं यशसं वयोधां सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां (*prathamabhājaṃ yaśasaṃ vayodhāṃ somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇāṃ*) (Ā. 3-8). "Prathamabhāj" is the divider of the living beings at the very time of their first origin; so according to the Śruti: यावच्चो वै रेतसः सिक्तस्य त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति तावच्चो वै तत्प्रजायत । (*yāvacco vai retasaḥ siktasya tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti tāvacco vai tatprajāyata |*) (Śai. Saṃ. 1-5-9-1) **NOTE** **GLOSS**. "Yaśasam" is the glorious one; "vayodhām" is the giver, the bearer, of "vayas", food in the form of the oblation, or else the giver of food to the praisers. "Supāṇi": the part of the hand above the wrist is the "pāṇi"; so he is the god with beautiful hands, endowed with the qualities of giving and the rest. "Sugabhasti": "gabhasti" is a name for the arm; so he has beautiful arms. "Ṛbhvam" is the one who shines widely, or the great one. "Pastyānām": "pastya" is a name for the house; so, of those who dwell in it, he is "yajata", to be worshipped: that is, to be worshipped by householders. "Suhavam" is the one who can be invoked with ease. May Agni, the Hotṛ, the summoner of the gods, the shining one, worship Tvaṣṭṛ, such as he is; may he worship him with this oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमभाजं (*prathamabhājaṃ*)—the one who at the time of origin itself makes the divisions of all living beings
- यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*)—the one whose action gives fame
- वयोधां (*vayodhāṃ*)—the giver of food
- सुपाणिं (*supāṇiṃ*)—the one with excellent hands
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—the one who is divine in nature
- सुगभस्तिं (*sugabhastiṃ*)—the one with excellent arms

### Printed p. 268

- यभ्वं (*yabhvaṃ*)—the one of surpassing radiance
- पस्त्यानां (*pastyānāṃ*)—for all the householders, the worshippers
- यजतं (*yajataṃ*)—the one to be worshipped
- सुहवं (*suhavaṃ*)—the one with excellent invocation
- त्वष्टारं (*tvaṣṭāraṃ*)—the god Tvaṣṭṛ
- होता (*hotā*)—the one who calls the gods
- विभावा (*vibhāvā*)—the one of surpassing radiance
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- यक्षत् (*yakṣat*)—may he worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni, the divine Hotṛ of the whole sacrifice, of surpassing radiance, worship the god Tvaṣṭṛ, who at the time of origin itself makes the divisions of all living beings, whose action gives fame, who is the giver of food, with excellent hands, of surpassing radiance, to be worshipped by all householders, the worshippers, and with excellent invocation.

##### English translation
May the illustrious Agni, the invoker of the gods, worship (with this oblation), Twashtri, the first divider (of forms), the renowned, the giver of food, the well-handed, the vast, the adored of householders, the readily invoked.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice addressed to the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, when the oblation is offered, this Ṛk beginning प्रथमभाजं (*prathamabhājaṃ*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्रथमभाजं यशसं वयोधां सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणामिति सूक्तं (*prathamabhājaṃ yaśasaṃ vayodhāṃ somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇāmiti sūktaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भुव॑नस्य पि॒तरं॑ गी॒र्भिरा॒भी रु॒द्रं दिवा॑ व॒र्धया॑ रु॒द्रम॒क्त्य ।  
> बृ॒हंत॑मृ॒ष्टम॒जरं॑ सुषु॒म्न मृध॑ग्घुवेम क॒विने॑षि॒तासः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भुवनस्य । पितरं । गीःभिः । अभिः । रुद्रं । दिवा । वर्धय । रुद्रं । अक्त्वा ।  
> बृहंतं । ऋष्वं । अजरं । सुसुम्नं । यधक् । हुवेम । कविना । इषितासः ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 269

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य पितरं पालयितारं रुद्रं । रुद्दुःखं । तद्दावयितारमीश्वरमाभिर्गिर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्दिवाहनि हे स्तोतर्वर्धय । अक्त्वा
> रात्र्यां च तमेव रुद्रं स्तुतिभिर्वर्धय । वयं च कविना प्राज्ञेन रुद्रेणेषितासः
> प्रेरिताः संतो बृहंतं महांतमृष्टं दर्शनीयमजरं जरारहितं सुषुम्नं
> शोभनसुखमेवंगुणविशिष्टं रुद्रमृधक् युद्धं समृद्धं यथा भवति तथा
> हुवेम । स्तवाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Rudra is the "father", that is, the protector, of the world, of all that is born. "Rud" is sorrow; he who drives it away is the lord. O praiser, by day, with these praises, make this Rudra grow; and at night too make that same Rudra grow with praises. And we, impelled by Rudra the wise, great, fair to see, free of old age, of beautiful happiness, such as he is, may we invoke Rudra, praise him, so that it may be "ṛdhak", in a prosperous manner. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—(O praiser) of all that is born
- पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—the protector
- रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—Rudra
- आभिः गीर्भिः (*ābhiḥ gīrbhiḥ*)—with these praises
- दिवा (*divā*)—by day
- वर्धय (*vardhaya*)—make him grow
- अक्तौ (*aktau*)—at times of night also
- रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—that same Rudra (make him grow)
- कविना (*kavinā*)—by Rudra the wise himself
- इषितासः (*iṣitāsaḥ*)—impelled
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—the one of great nature
- ऋष्टं (*ṛṣṭaṃ*)—the one of fair form
- अजरं (*ajaraṃ*)—the one free of decay
- सुषुम्नं (*suṣumnaṃ*)—the one of excellent qualities, that same Rudra
- ऋधक् (*ṛdhak*)—so that he may be prosperous
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—may we praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, make Rudra, the protector of all that is born, grow by day with these praises. Make him grow at times of night also. Impelled by Rudra the wise himself, may we praise that same Rudra, of great nature, of fair form, free of decay, of excellent qualities, so that he may be prosperous.

##### English translation
Exalt Rudra, the parent of the world, with these hymns by day ; (exalt) Rudra (with them) by night ; animated by the far-seeing, we invoke him, mighty, of pleasing aspect, undecaying, endowed with felicity, (the source of) prosperity.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ यु॑वानः कवयो यज्ञियासो॒ मरु॑तो गं॒त गृ॑ण॒तो  ॒॑
> वरस्यां ।  
> अ॒चि॒त्रं चि॒द्दि जिन्न॑था वृ॒धंत॑ इ॒त्था नक्षं॑तो नरो अंगिर॒स्वत् ॥

### Printed p. 270

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । युवानः । कवयः । यज्ञियासः । मरुतः । गंत । गृणतः । वरस्यां ।  
> अचित्रं । चित् । हि । जिन्नथः । वृधंतः । इत्था । नक्षंतः । नरः । अंगिरस्वत् ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे युवानो नित्यतरुणाः कवयः प्राज्ञा यज्जियासो यज्ञार्हा
> एवंभूता हे मरुतो गृणतः स्तुवतो वरस्यां वरणीयां स्तुतिं प्रत्या गंत ।
> आगच्छत । अपि च हे नरो नेतारो मरुत इत्थेत्ममनेन प्रकारेण वृधंतो
> षर्धमानाः । यद्वा । इत्यामुत्रांतरिक्षे नक्षंतो व्याप्नुवंतोऽंगिरस्वत् । अंगिरसो
> गमनशीला रश्मयः । ते यथा शीघ्रं नभस्तलं व्यापुवंति तद्वत् । यद्वा । ऋषय
> एवांगिरसः । तद्वच्छीघ्रगामिनः । एवंभूता यूयमचित्रं चित् । ओषधिवनस्पतिभिर्निविडो देशश्चित्रं । तद्विलक्षणमोषध्यादिभिर्वियुक्तमपि देशं जिन्पथ । वृष्टा तर्पयथ ।
> हीति पूरणः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ever-young, wise Maruts, worthy of the sacrifice, such as you are, come to the praise of the praiser, the one to be chosen. And, O leaders, Maruts, growing thus in this manner; or else, pervading there in the firmament like the Aṅgirases: the Aṅgirases are the swift-moving rays, and as these quickly fill the expanse of the sky, so you do; or else the Aṅgirases are the seers themselves, and you are swift-going like them. **NOTE** Such as you are, you gladden by rain a "not-wondrous" place: a place thickly covered with herbs and trees is "citra", wondrous; in contrast to it, a place devoid of herbs and the rest you satisfy by raining. The word "hi" is a filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवानः (*yuvānaḥ*)—ever-young
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—wise
- यज्जियासः (*yajjiyāsaḥ*)—worthy of the sacrifice
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—of the praiser
- वरस्यां (*varasyāṃ*)—towards his venerable praise
- आ गंत (*ā gaṃta*)—be so kind as to come
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—O Maruts, the leaders
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this manner
- वृधन्तः (*vṛdhantaḥ*)—you who grow
- नक्षंतः (*nakṣaṃtaḥ*)—and pervading all regions
- अंगिरस्वत् (*aṃgirasvat*)—swift like the rays
- अचित्रं चित् (*acitraṃ cit*)—even the regions devoid of herbs and the rest
- जिन्वथ हि (*jinvatha hi*)—gladden with rain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, ever-young, wise, worthy of the sacrifice, be so kind as to come towards the venerable praise of the praiser. O Maruts, leaders, you who grow in this manner, pervading all regions and swift like the rays, gladden with rain even the regions devoid of herbs and the rest.

### Printed p. 271

##### English translation
Ever youthful, wise, and adorable Muruts, come to the praise of your adorer : thus augmenting, leaders (of rites), and spreading (through the firmament), like rays (of light) refresh the scanty woods (with rain).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वी॒राय॒ प्र त॒वसे॑ तु॒रायाजा॑ यू॒थेव॑ पशु॒रक्षि॒रस्तं॑ ।  
> स पि॑स्पृशति त॒न्वि॑ श्रु॒तस्य॒ स्तृभि॒र्न नाकं॑ वच॒नस्य॒ विपः॑ ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वीराय । प्र । तवसे । तुराय । अज । यूथाइव । पशुरक्षिः । अस्तं ।  
> सः । पिस्पृशति । तन्वि । श्रुतस्य । स्तृभिः । न । नाकं । वचनस्य । विपः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वीराय विक्रांताय विविधं शत्रूणामीरकाय ना मरुद्दणाय प्राज ।
> हे स्तोतः स्तुतिं प्रगमय । तथा तवसे बलिने तुराय क्षिप्रगमनाय च तस्मै
> गणाय प्राज । तत्र दृष्टांतः । पशुरक्षिः पशुपालको यूथेव । स यथा
> गोयूथानि सायंकालेस्तं गृहं शीघ्रं गमयति तद्वत् शीघ्रं स्तुतिं प्रेरयेत्यर्थः । स च मरुद्दणो वचनस्य वक्तुर्विपो विप्रस्य मेधाविनः स्तोतुः श्रुतस्य ॥
> क्रियाग्रहणमपि कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी ॥ श्रुतं
> श्रोतव्यं स्तोत्रं तन्वात्मीये शरीरे पिस्पृशति । स्पर्शयतु । संश्लेषयतु ।
> तत्सोत्रं हृद्धतं भवत्त्व्यर्थः । स्पर्शने दृष्टांतः । स्तृभिर्न नाकं । यथा
> नक्षत्रैर्नाकमंतरिक्षं स्पर्शयति संश्लेषयति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Vīra" is the valiant one, the one who in various ways drives out enemies: to the host of the Maruts of this kind, O praiser, send forth the praise. So too to the mighty one, and to the swift one, the quick-going: to that host send it. An illustration follows: as a herdsman drives herds, and as he at evening time makes the herds go quickly to the stall, to the house, so send the praise quickly: this is the meaning. And may that host of the Maruts, of the speaker, the sage, the praiser, the praise that is heard, the praise that is to be heard, touch his own body, cling to it; may that praise reach the heart. An illustration of the touching: "as the stars the firmament": as the stars touch the firmament, cling to it, so.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—(O praiser) to the host of the valiant Maruts
- प्र अज (*pra aja*)—offer the praise
- तवसे (*tavase*)—to the host of the Maruts that is mighty
- तुराय (*turāya*)—and swift-going

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, offer praise to the host of the valiant Maruts. To the host of the Maruts, mighty and swift-going, offer praises quickly, as a herdsman sends the cattle to the cattle-shed. As the firmament shines, reached by the stars, so may that same host of the Maruts touch throughout its body the praiseworthy hymn of the praiser, who is a reciter of praise and wise, and be fully delighted.

##### English translation
Offer adoration to the valiant, powerful, swift-moving (company of the Maruts), as the herdsman (drives his) herd to their stall ; may that company appropriate to its own body the praises of the pious worshipper, as the firmament (is studded) with stars.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viṣṇu, for the sake of Manu, the Prajāpati, who was harassed, injured, by the Asuras, measured the "terrestrial", earth-connected regions, that is, the three worlds, thrice; the word "cit" is for emphasis: he measured with three strides only. O Viṣṇu, of you, of such a kind

> च तना तनयेन पुत्रेण च मदेम । मोदेम । हृष्टा भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

While we dwell in the house or in happiness that is being given to us by you, may we rejoice with wealth, with a body free of disease and the like, and with offspring, a son: may we be delighted.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, you, the all-pervading, who for Manu harassed by the Asura measured in three parts all the worlds connected with the earth: dwelling in the houses given to us by you, may we attain joy, with wealth, with bodies free of disease and the like, and with sons, grandsons and the rest.

##### English translation
May we be happy in home, in riches, in person, in children, bestowed upon us by you, Vishnu, who with three (steps) made the terrestrial regions for Manu when harrassed (by the Asuras).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बुध्न्यः । बुध्नमंतरिक्षं । तत्र भवोऽहिः । एत्यंतरिक्ष इत्यहिः । उक्तं च ।
> अहिरयनादेत्यंतरिक्षे । नि. २-१७ । इति । एतत्पदद्वयाभिधेयो देवोऽर्कैरर्डनसाधनैर्मंत्रैः स्तूयमानः सन् नोऽस्मभ्यं तत् लोके प्रसिद्धं चनोऽन्नमद्भिरुदकैः सार्धं धात् । दधातु । विदधातु । प्रयच्छतु । पर्वतः पूरयिता ॥
> पर्व पूरण इति धातुः ॥ यद्वा । पर्ववद्वज्रं पर्वतः । तद्वान् । पर्वतस्य गिरीः
> शत्रुरिति वा पर्वतः । स च तच्चनो दधातु । तथा सविता प्रेरको देवश्च तच्चनो
> दधातु । अपि च रातिषाचः । रातिं दानं सचंते सेवंत इति रातिषाचो विश्वे देवाः ।
> ते चौषधीभिः । ओषः पाक आसु धीयत इत्योषधयस्तिलमाषाद्याः । ताभिः सार्धं
> तदन्नमभि प्रयच्छंतु । तथा पुरंधिर्बहुधीर्बहुप्रज्ञो वा बहुकर्मा वा भगो
> भजनीय एतत्संज्ञो देवश्च राये धनार्थं प्र जिन्वतु । अस्मान्मेरयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Budhnya": "budhna" is the firmament, and he who is born there is "ahi"; he who goes in the firmament is "ahi". It is said also: अहिरयनादेत्यंतरिक्षे (*ahirayanādetyaṃtarikṣe*) (Ni. 2-17) **GLOSS**. The god denoted by these two words, being praised with hymns, the means of worship, may give us the food well known in the world, together with the waters. "Parvata" is the filler; or else the one who has the joint-like thunderbolt, or the enemy of mountains. **NOTE** He too may give that food. So too Savitṛ, the impelling god, may give that food. Further, "rātiṣācaḥ" are the Viśvedevas, the gods who attend upon gifts; may they with the herbs, the sesame, beans and the rest, in which the ripening (oṣa) is placed, give that food. So too Purandhi, of much wisdom or of many works, Bhaga, the one to be shared, the god so called, may he urge us on towards wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहिर्बुध्न्यः (*ahirbudhnyaḥ*)—the god Ahirbudhnya
- अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—being praised with our hymns
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- तत् (*tat*)—the well-known
- चनः (*canaḥ*)—food
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—together with waters
- धात् (*dhāt*)—may he give
- पर्वतः (*parvataḥ*)—and the god Parvata
- तत् (*tat*)—may he give that food
- सविता (*savitā*)—and the god Savitṛ
- तत् (*tat*)—may he give that food
- रातिषाचः (*rātiṣācaḥ*)—all the gods who give generously
- ओषधीभिः (*oṣadhībhiḥ*)—that which is joined with herbs, trees and the rest
- तत् (*tat*)—that food
- अभि (*abhi*)—may they favour us
- पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)—of much wisdom
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—the god Bhaga
- राये (*rāye*)—for wealth
- प्र जिन्वतु (*pra jinvatu*)—may he urge us on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Ahirbudhnya, praised with our hymns, give us the well-known food together with waters. May the god Parvata too give that food. May the god Savitṛ too favour us with it. May all the gods who give generously give us that food, joined with herbs, trees and the rest. May the god Bhaga, of much wisdom, urge us on towards wealth.

##### English translation
May Ahirbudhnya (propitiated) by (our) hymns, and Parvata and Savitri give us food with water: may the bountiful (gods supply us), in addition, with vegetable (grains); and may the all-wise Bhaga be propitious (to us) for (acquirement of) riches.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सर्वॆ देवा नोऽस्मभ्यं रयिं धनं क्षयं गृहं च दात । प्रयच्छत ।

> मनुष्याः । तेषां पूरयितारं पुरुवीरं । वीर्याज्जायंत इति वीराः पुत्रादयः ।

> धनेन हि यज्ञो रक्ष्यते । मृतो यज्ञस्त्वदक्षिण इति वचनात् । कीदृशं क्षयं ।
> अजरं जरारहितं । येन रयिणा क्षयेण च जनान् शत्रून् स्पृधः स्पर्धमाना
> अदेवीरदेवसंबंधिनीरासुरीः सेनाश्चाभि क्रमाम अभिभवेम । तथादेवीः । अगता
> देवा यासु हविस्वीकारार्थं ता अदेव्यः । तादृशीश्च विशः प्रजा यज्ञानुष्ठायिनीर्येन धनेन गृहेण चाभ्यश्चनाम अभिप्राप्नवाम तादृशं धनं गृहं च
> दातेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O all gods, give us wealth and a dwelling. What kind of wealth? "Rathya": connected with the chariot, that is, furnished with chariots. "Carṣaṇiprā": the "carṣaṇayaḥ" are men; it is the filler of them. "Puruvīra": "vīrāḥ" are those born of virility, sons and the rest; so, accompanied by many heroes. It is the protector of the great "ṛta", the sacrifice; for the sacrifice is protected by wealth in the form of the fee, on the saying मृतो यज्ञस्त्वदक्षिण (*mṛto yajñastvadakṣiṇa*) **GLOSS**. What kind of dwelling? Ageless, free of old age. By which wealth and dwelling we may overcome the enemies, the rivals, and the hosts of the Asuras, who are "adevī", not belonging to the gods; and likewise the "ādevī", those among whom the gods have come to accept the oblation **NOTE**, that is, the peoples who perform the sacrifice, which we may reach, attain, by which wealth and dwelling: give such wealth and dwelling. So the construction runs.

- अभि क्रमाम (*abhi kramāma*)—may we become able to defeat
- आदेवी॥ (*ādevī‖*)—likewise, who worship the gods with oblations and the like
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—all the peoples
- अभ्यश्चनाम (*abhyaścanāma*)—may we satisfy; such
- रथ्यं (*rathyaṃ*)—furnished with chariots

- चर्षणिप्रां (*carṣaṇiprāṃ*)—nourishing all our people
- पुरुवीरं (*puruvīraṃ*)—accompanied by abundant heroes
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—for the sacrifice
- गोपां (*gopāṃ*)—a protector
- अजरं (*ajaraṃ*)—free of decay
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- क्षयं (*kṣayaṃ*)—and a dwelling

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśvedevas, certainly give us such wealth and dwelling, furnished with chariots, nourishing all our people, accompanied by abundant heroes, a protector of the great sacrifice, free of decay, by which we shall be able to defeat our enemy folk and the Asura folk who fight with us, and likewise satisfy the peoples who worship the gods with oblations and the like.

##### English translation
Grant us, (universal gods), riches, comprehending chariots, numerous dependants, many male offspring, (wealth) the giver of efficiency to the solemn rite. and a dwelling free from decay. wherewith we may overcome malevolent man and unrighteous (spirits), and afford support to those people who are devoted to the gods.

## Sūkta 50 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पंचमेऽनुवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि । तत्र हुवे व इति पंचदशर्चं प्रथमं
> सूक्तमृजिश्वन आर्षं बहुदेवताकं त्रैष्टुभं । हुवे व इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतः
> सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the fifth anuvāka there are twelve sūktas. Of these, the first sūkta, of fifteen Ṛks, beginning हुवे व (*huve va*), has Ṛjiśvā as its seer, many deities, and the metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: हुवे व (*huve va*). The use of the sūkta in ritual has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

In the fifth anuvāka of the sixth maṇḍala there are twelve sūktas. Of them, this sūkta "Huve vaḥ" is the first. It has fifteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Ṛjiśvā. The deities are the Viśvedevas. The metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as beginning "Huve vaḥ". The use of the sūkta in ritual has been stated before.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवा वो युष्माकं मातरं देवीं द्योतमानामदितिमखंडनीयामदीनां वा एतत्संज्ञां देवतां मृळीकाय सुखार्थं नमोभिर्नमस्कारैः स्तोत्रैर्वा
> हुवे । ह्वयामि । सौमि । तथा वरुणं वारकं मित्रं प्रमीतेस्त्रायकं देवमग्निं
> चैतांश्च देवान्नमोभिर्हुवे । तथाभिक्षदां । क्षदिर्हिंसाकर्मा । अभिक्षत्तारं
> शत्रुणां हिंसितारं सुशेवं सुसुखमर्यमणं च नमोभिर्हुवे । सवितारं
> भगं च नमोभिर्हुवे । किं बहुना त्रात्यन् पालयित्यन् सर्वान्देवान्नमोभिः
> स्तोत्रैर्हुवे । सौमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, I invoke your mother, the shining Aditi, the one not to be broken, or the deity so named, "of the not poor", for happiness, with salutations or with hymns. So too I invoke Varuṇa, the one who restrains, Mitra, the protector from death, and the god Agni; and these gods I invoke with salutations. So too "abhikṣad": the root "kṣad" has the sense of injuring; he is the one who injures enemies; and Aryaman, very happy: I invoke him with salutations. I invoke Savitṛ and Bhaga with salutations. What need of more? I invoke all the gods, the protecting, guarding ones, with salutations, with hymns.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—to you (the mother)
- देवीं (*devīṃ*)—the venerable
- अदितिं (*aditiṃ*)—the goddess Aditi
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—the god Varuṇa
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—Mitra
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*)—for our happiness
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with praises accompanied by salutation
- हुवे (*huve*)—I call, praying
- अभिक्षदां (*abhikṣadāṃ*)—the one who injures enemies
- सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)—the very happy-making

### Printed p. 278
- अर्यमणं (*aryamaṇaṃ*)—Aryaman, the god
- सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*)—Savitṛ
- भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—Bhaga
- त्रात्वान् (*trātvān*)—our protectors
- देवान् च (*devān ca*)—all the other gods as well (I invoke, praying)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, I invoke with salutation-accompanied hymns, for the sake of our happiness, the goddess Aditi, your venerable mother, and Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni; and Aryaman, the god who injures enemies and is exceedingly happy-making, and Savitṛ and Bhaga as well. In the same way I invoke, praying, all the other gods who are our protectors.

##### English translation
I invoke with adorations, for the sake of felicity, the divine Aditi and Varuna, Mitra and Agni, overthrower of foes, worthy of devotion, Savitri and Bhaga, and (all) protecting divinities.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> येषां ते दक्षपितरः । पितृशब्दो हि सामान्येन पूर्वपुरुषत्वमात्रं ब्रूते ।

> शोभनज्योतिष्कान्देवाननागास्त्वेऽनपराधत्वे वीहि । कामयस्व । यथास्माकमपराधं ते न कुर्वंति तथा कुर्या इत्यर्थः । ये देवा द्विजन्मानो द्वयोर्लोक-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Sumahas, well-radiant Sūrya, impeller of all, take pleasure in the gods who have Dakṣa as their forefather." Sāyaṇa explains that the word "father" in general denotes merely an ancestor, as in the mantra he cites (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-15-3); that these gods have Dakṣa as their forefather is known from another mantra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-5). Such well-lit gods, shining beautifully, are to be desired in respect of being free from offence: act so that they commit no offence against us. **NOTE** He goes on to describe these gods as those who are twice born, that is, appearing as born in the two worlds.

> योर्जायमानाः प्रादुर्भवंत ऋतसाप ऋतं यज्ञं स्पृशंतः सत्या अवितथाः
> सत्यवादीनो वा स्वर्वंतो धनवंतो यजता यष्टव्या अग्नि जिह्वाः । अग्नि र्जिह्वास्थानीयो येषां ते । एवंभूता ये देवाः संति तान्नेवान्वीहीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods are "ṛtasāpaḥ", touching the ṛta, the sacrifice; "satyāḥ", true, or speakers of truth; "svarvantaḥ", possessed of wealth; "yajatāḥ", to be worshipped; and "agnijihvāḥ", those whose tongue-equivalent is Agni. The construction is: be pleased with the gods who are of this kind.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुमहः (*sumahaḥ*)—O one of exceeding splendour
- सूर्य (*sūrya*)—O Sūrya
- ये (*ye*)—which gods
- द्विजन्मानः (*dvijanmānaḥ*)—those who are born in both worlds
- ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*)—those who touch the sacrifice
- सत्याः (*satyāḥ*)—those who are of true nature
- स्वर्वंतः (*svarvaṃtaḥ*)—the wealthy
- यजताः (*yajatāḥ*)—the venerable
- अग्निजिह्वाः (*agnijihvāḥ*)—those who have Agni for their tongue; such as are so
- दक्षपित्मान् (*dakṣapitmān*)—those who have Dakṣa for their father
- सुज्योतिषः (*sujyotiṣaḥ*)—those of exceeding radiance
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- अनागास्त्वे (*anāgāstve*)—so as to be free of harm
- वीहि (*vīhi*)—impel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sūrya, of exceeding splendour, impel the gods who are born in both worlds, who touch the sacrifice, who are of true nature, wealthy, venerable, and have Agni for their tongue, who have Dakṣa for their father and are of exceeding radiance, to be free of harm towards us.

##### English translation
Radiant Surya, render the deities, who have Daksha for their progenitor, void of offence towards us ; they who are twice born, desirous of sacrifice, observant of truth, possessors of wealth, deserving of worship whose tongue is Agni.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यावुरु विस्तीर्णं क्षत्रं बलं करथः ।
> कुरुतं । तथा रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य सुसुम्मे सुसुखे युवां । बृहन्महच्छरणं
> गृहं च करथः । कुरुतं । महो महद्वरिवो धनं नोऽस्माकं यथा स्यात्तथा

> चास्मे आस्माकं क्षयाय निवासार्थं कुरुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover, O Heaven and Earth, you two make wide, extensive strength. Likewise, O Rodasī, Heaven and Earth, you of good happiness, make a great, vast refuge, that is, a house. Do so that great wealth ("varivas") may be ours. Further, O Dhiṣaṇe, O sustainers, Heaven and Earth, make freedom from evil for us, for our dwelling.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—moreover
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—O Heaven and Earth
- उरु (*uru*)—exceeding
- क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)—strength
- करथः (*karathaḥ*)—produce
- सुसुम्मे (*susumme*)—you who bring about happiness
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—O Heaven and Earth
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great
- शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*)—a house (build it for us)
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—abundant
- वरिवः (*varivaḥ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever way it may be obtained, so favour us
- धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*)—O Heaven and Earth, sustainers of the world
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—for the sake of a dwelling-place
- अनेकः (*anekaḥ*)—produce also freedom from sin

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Heaven and Earth, who bring about happiness, produce exceeding strength for us. Build a great house for us. Favour us in such a way that abundant wealth is obtained by us. O Heaven and Earth, sustainers of the world, produce freedom from sin for us, for the sake of a dwelling-place.

##### English translation
Or bestow, Heaven and Earth, vast strength : give us, Earth and Heaven, a spacious habitation for our comfort : so arrange, that infinite wealth may be ours ; remove, beneficent deities, inquiry from our abode.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रुद्रस्य सूनवः पुत्रा मरुतोऽद्यास्मिन्काले हूतास अहूताः संतो
> नोऽस्मान्पत्या नमंतां । आनता भवंतु । आगच्छंतु । कीदृशाः । वसवो वासयितारोऽधृष्ट्वा अन्न्यैरहिंसिताः । यद्यदेमेनान्मरुतो देवानर्भेऽल्पे महति
> प्रभूते वा बाधे संग्रामे हितासो निहिताः स्थिताः संतो वयमह्वाम आह्वयाम
> तदानीमद्येत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts, the sons of Rudra, invoked today, at this time, are to bow to us, that is, to become inclined to us and come. **NOTE** They are of this kind: "vasavaḥ", causers of dwelling, and "adhṛṣṭāḥ", unharmed by others. The construction is: when we, placed in battle, whether it be small or great, call upon these Maruts, the gods, then, today, may they bow to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यॆत् (*yèt*)—when
- देवान् (*devān*)—who are of divine nature
- ईं मरुतः (*īṃ marutaḥ*)—these Maruts
- अर्भे (*arbhe*)—whether in a small one
- वा (*vā*)—or
- महति (*mahati*)—in a great one
- बाधे (*bādhe*)—in battle
- हितासः (*hitāsaḥ*)—we, who are engaged
- आह्वाम (*āhvāma*)—call for help
- अद्य (*adya*)—at that very time
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—the givers of dwelling
- आधृष्टाः (*ādhṛṣṭāḥ*)—the unassailed by enemies
- रुद्रस्य (*rudrasya*)—of Rudra
- सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*)—the sons
- हूतासः (*hūtāsaḥ*)—having been called by us
- नः (*naḥ*)—towards us
- आ नमंतां (*ā namaṃtāṃ*)—let them descend and come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When we, engaged in a battle, whether small or great, pray to these Maruts, the divine ones, for help, at that time may the Maruts, the givers of dwelling, unassailed by enemies, the sons of Rudra, having been called by us, descend and come towards us.

##### English translation
May the sons of Rudra, givers of dwellings, the unsubdued, invoked on the occasion, stoop down to us, inasmuch as we call upon the divine Maruts that they may be our helpers in difficulty, great or small.

> विम्यक्ष नु क्षिप्रं संगच्छते । तथाभ्यर्धयज्वा स्तोत्कन्यभ्यर्धयन् समृद्धान्कुर्वन्यो

> अभ्यर्धयज्वाभ्यर्धयन्यजति । नि. ६-६ । इति यास्कः । हे मरुतस्ते यूयं

> मार्गे प्रविक्ते गमनार्थं पृथक्कृते सति तत्र विद्यमानानि भूम भूतजातानि
> रेजंते । कंपंते । तथा च मंत्रांतरं । प्र वेपयंति पर्वतान्नि विंचंति वनस्पतीन् ।
> ऋग्वे. १-३९-५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among those Maruts, Rodasī, the wife of Rudra, the shining speech of the middle region, quickly joins; likewise Pūṣan, "abhyardhayajvā", who makes the praisers prosperous and worships, that is, honours with wealth, being the nourishing god, attends upon those Maruts. "Abhyardhayajvā" means one who, increasing, worships (Ni. 6-6), as Yāska says. O Maruts, when you, having heard our invocation, come, then on the path set apart for your going, all the beings that are there tremble. Another mantra says the same (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-39-5).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- येषु (*yeṣu*)—in whom
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—the wife of Rudra
- देवी (*devī*)—and the shining goddess of speech of the middle region
- नु (*nu*)—with
- मिम्यक्ष (*mimyakṣa*)—she is joined (and likewise)
- अभ्यर्धयज्वा (*abhyardhayajvā*)—he who makes the praisers prosper through the giving of wealth
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*)—attends upon you (such as you)
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—our invocation
- श्रुत्वा (*śrutvā*)—having heard
- यद्ध (*yaddha*)—when
- याथ (*yātha*)—you come (then)
- प्रविक्ते (*pravikte*)—divided and made ready for your travelling
- अध्वनि (*adhvani*)—on the path
- भूम (*bhūma*)—all beings
- रेजंते (*rejaṃte*)—tremble

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you with whom the shining goddess of speech of the middle region, the wife of Rudra, is joined, and whom likewise the god Pūṣan, who makes the praisers prosper through the giving of wealth, attends: when you, having heard our invocation, come, then all beings on the path made ready for your travelling tremble with fear.

### Printed p. 283

##### English translation
With whom the divine Heaven and Earth are associated ; whom Pushan, the rewarder (of his worshippers) with prosperity, honours : when Maruts, having heard our invocation, you come hither, then on your several paths all beings tremble.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has stated an etymology of the word "abhyardhayajvā" in this Ṛk, and has explained its meaning taking this very Ṛk as the example:
अभ्यर्द्धयज्वाभ्यर्द्धयन्यजति । सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्द्धयज्वा इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*abhyarddhayajvābhyarddhayanyajati | siṣakti pūṣā abhyarddhayajvā ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-6)
Durgācārya, commenting on this etymology, says: अभ्यर्द्धयज्वा इत्यनवगतं । अभ्यर्द्धयन् अभिवर्धयन् यो यजति । अभ्यर्द्धयतिरत्र दानार्थः । (*abhyarddhayajvā ityanavagataṃ | abhyarddhayan abhivardhayan yo yajati | abhyarddhayatiratra dānārthaḥ |*). The praise of Pūṣan's quality is stated here: he gives to the man who praises him wealth and the like that grow and increase, or he makes wealth and prosperity for the one who praises him so that he prospers. अभ्यर्द्धयतिरत्र दानार्थः (*abhyarddhayatiratra dānārthaḥ*): the word "abhyardhayan" has here the meaning of giving. If one asks what is given, the intention is that he gives things that are dear to the praiser, or wealth and the like that are desired. To make clear the meaning of this word, they have given this very Ṛk as the example.
युद्ध याथ प्रविक्ते अध्वनि भूमा रेजंते (*yuddha yātha pravikte adhvani bhūmā rejaṃte*): O Maruts, when you come, that is, move (blowing with violence), on the path specially marked out separately for your movement, all beings, that is, all creatures, tremble with fear. Describing thus the extraordinary power and might of the Maruts, the commentator has explained the meaning, giving as an example in this matter the Vedic sentence प्र वेपयंति पर्वतान् वि विंचंति वनस्पतीन् (*pra vepayaṃti parvatān vi viṃcaṃti vanaspatīn*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-39-5), whose meaning is: when the Maruts move with violence they make even the mountains, known as immovable, tremble; they bring down the great trees of the forest, roots and all.

> श्रवत् । इत् । हवं । उप । च । स्तवानः । रासत् । वाजान् । उप । महः । गृणानः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जरितः स्तोतस्यं तं प्रसिद्धं वीरं वीर्यवंतं विशेषेण शत्रूणामीरकं
> वा गिर्वणसं गिरां संभक्तारमेवंविधमिंद्रं नवेनाभिनवेन शोभनेन ब्रह्मणा
> स्तोत्रेणाभ्यर्च । अभिष्टुहि । स च स्तवानः स्तूयमानः सन् हवमस्मदीयं स्तोत्रमुप श्रवदित् । उपशृणुयादेव । अपि च गृणानः स्तूयमान इंद्रो महो
> महतः प्रभूतान्वाजानन्नानि चोप रासत् । प्रदेयात् । यत एवमतः स्तुहीत्यर्थः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, worship with a new, fresh, excellent hymn that well-known Indra, who is a hero, mighty, or one who specially impels enemies, and who is the lover of songs. And may he, being praised, hear our invocation, our hymn; and being lauded, may Indra give abundant food. Therefore, Sāyaṇa says, praise him. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—the well-known
- वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—the valiant
- गिर्वणसं (*girvaṇasaṃ*)—and pleased by praise
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- नवेन (*navena*)—with a new
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—hymn
- अभ्यर्च (*abhyarca*)—worship
- स्तवानः (*stavānaḥ*)—that same Indra, who has been praised
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—our hymn
- उप श्रवदित् (*upa śravadit*)—he does surely hear
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—Indra, who is praised by us
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—abundant
- वाजान् च (*vājān ca*)—foods too
- उप रासत् (*upa rāsat*)—let him graciously give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, worship with a new hymn that well-known, valiant Indra, who is pleased by praise. That same Indra, who has been praised, does surely hear our hymns. May Indra, who is praised by us, graciously give us abundant foods.

##### English translation
Praise, worshipper, with a new hymn, that hero, Indra, who is deserving of praise : may he, so glorified, hear our invocation : may he, so lauded, bestow upon us abundant food.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यूयं । हि । स्थ । भिषजः । मातृतमाः । विश्वस्य । स्थातुः । जगतः । जनित्रीः ॥ ७ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आपो मानुषीर्मनुष्यहिता यूयममृक्तमहिंसितमोमानं । अवति
> रक्षतीत्योमा रक्षकमन्नं । तोकाय पुत्राय तनयाय तत्पुत्राय च धात । धत्त ।
> प्रयच्छत । तथा शं शमनमुपद्रवाणां योर्यावनं पृथक्करणं च पृथक्कर्तव्यानां धत्त । प्रयच्छत । कुत इत्यत आह । हि यस्माद्यूयं मातृतमा मातृभ्योऽप्यधिका भिषजः स्थ भवध तस्माद्घातेत्यन्वयः । कथं मातृभ्योऽप्यधिकं
> भैषज्यमस्तीत्यत आह । विश्वस्य सर्वस्य स्थातुः स्थावरस्य जगतो जंगमस्य जनित्रीर्जनयित्र्यो भवथ । अतो यूयं भिषजः स्थ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O waters, friendly to men, you give to our son and to his son the unharmed, protecting food ("omāna"; "avati" means he protects, hence "omā" is protecting food). Give also "śam", the quieting of calamities, and "yoḥ", the keeping apart, the separating, of what is to be kept apart." Why? Because you are "mātṛtamāḥ", more than mothers, physicians. How can there be a remedy greater than that of mothers? He answers: you are the mothers, the begetters, of the whole world, of the stationary and the moving. Therefore you are physicians.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—O deities of the waters
- मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*)—you, who are beneficial to men
- अमृक्तं (*amṛktaṃ*)—the unharmed
- ओमानं (*omānaṃ*)—and protecting food
- तोकाय (*tokāya*)—to our son

- शं (*śaṃ*)—happiness
- योः (*yoḥ*)—and freedom from sorrow (produce)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- मातृतमाः (*mātṛtamāḥ*)—better than the mother who gave birth
- भिषजः (*bhiṣajaḥ*)—as the nourishers of our health
- स्थ (*stha*)—you are
- हि (*hi*)—for
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of the whole
- स्थातुः (*sthātuḥ*)—stationary
- जगतः (*jagataḥ*)—and moving, all the worlds
- जनित्रिः (*janitriḥ*)—you are the mothers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities presiding over the waters, you who are beneficial to men, give to our son and to his son unharmed and protecting food. Produce happiness and freedom from sorrow. You are better than the mother who gave birth, nourishers of our health; for you are the mothers of the whole world, all that is stationary and moving.

### Printed p. 286

##### English translation
Waters, friendly to mankind, grant uninterrupted (life)-preserving (food) for (the perpetuatiou of our) sons and grandsons : grant us security and the removal (of all evil), for you are more then meternal physicians ; you are the parents of the stationary and moveable universe.

> प्रकाशयति स सवितेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Savitṛ, the impelling god, who protects, who is "hiraṇyapāṇi", golden-handed, or one whose hand is beneficial and delightful, and who is "yajataḥ", to be worshipped, is to come to us. The god who is possessed of wealth, like the face of Uṣas, to the sacrificer who has given oblations opens up, makes manifest, the desirable riches: he is Savitṛ. This is the construction.

### Printed p. 287

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Savitṛ, the protector, having a hand of gold, venerable and divine, who, being wealthy, makes manifest the desired riches to the sacrificer who offers oblations, like the goddess Uṣas of divine form, graciously come towards us.

##### English translation
May the adorable, golden-handed Savitri, the preserver, come to us; he, the munificent, who, like the opening of the dawn, displays desirable (riches) to the offerer of the oblation.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"And, O son of strength, O Agni, son of might, today, at this time, bring, cause to come, to this sacrifice of ours the gods who are to be worshipped, Indra and the others. - सदमित् (*sadamit*)—always

- स्यां (*syāṃ*)—may I be a fit recipient

- अवसा (*avasā*)—by protection

- स्यां (*syāṃ*)—may I be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of strength, at this time of the sacrifice performed by us, cause the gods to come to our sacrifice. May I always be a fit recipient of your gift of wealth. O Agni, grant that by your protection I may be happy, having obtained excellent sons, grandsons and the like.

##### English translation
And you, son of strength, bring back to-day the deities to this our sacrifice : may I be ever in (the enjoyment of) your bounty : may I through your protection, Agni, be blessed with excellent male descendants.

> शत्रुकृतात्तूर्वतं । अस्मांस्तारयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"And, O wise, O Nāsatyas", of true nature or leaders of truth, O Aśvins, you, the well-known ones, come quickly to this hymn of mine, which is joined with acts of attendance. Having come, as you released the sage Atri from great darkness made by the asuras, so, O leaders, deliver us in battle, when it is at hand, from the suffering caused by enemies.

- तोर्वतं (*torvataṃ*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Aśvin gods, you, the well-known ones, listening to my hymn, I who am joined with your acts of worship, graciously come quickly. As you freed the sage Atri from darkness, free us from great darkness. O Aśvin gods, leaders, protect us in battle from the suffering caused by enemies.

##### English translation
Wise Nasatyas, come quickly to my invocation (united) with holy acts: (extricate us) from thick darkness, as you did extricate Atri: protect us, leaders (of rites), from danger in battle.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते नो॑ रा॒यो द्यु॒मतो॒ वाज॑वतो दा॒तारो॑ भूत नृ॒वतः॑  ॒
> पुरु॒क्षोः ।  
> द॒श॒स्यंतो॑ दि॒व्याः पार्थि॑वासो॒ गोजा॑ता॒ अप्या॑ मृ॒ळता॑ च  
> देवाः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । नः । रायः । द्युमतः । वाजवतः । दातारः । भूत । नृवतः । पुरुक्षोः ।  
> दशस्यंतः । दिव्याः । पार्थिवासः । गोजाताः । अप्याः । मृळत । च । देवाः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 290

> हे देवास्ते यूयं द्युमतो दीप्तिमतो वाजवतो बलयुक्तस्य
> नृवतो नृभिः पुत्रादिभिरुपेतस्य पुरुक्षोर्बहुभिः कीर्तनीयस्य रायो धनस्य
> नोऽस्मभ्यं दातारो भूत । भवत । अपि च दशस्यंतः कामान्प्रयच्छंतो दिव्या दिवि
> भवा आदित्याः पार्थिवासः पृथिव्यां भवा वसवो गोजाताः । गौः पृश्निर्माध्यमिका
> वाक् । तत उत्पन्ना मरुतोऽप्या अप्स्यंतरिक्षे भवा रुद्राश्च ते सर्वे यूयमस्मान्मृळत । सुखयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O gods, you be givers to us of wealth that is "dyumat", radiant, "vājavat", possessed of strength, "nṛvat", accompanied by men, that is, sons and the like, and "purukṣu", to be praised by many. And, granting desires, the celestial ones, the Ādityas who are in heaven; the terrestrial ones, the Vasus who are on earth; "gojātāḥ": "go" is Pṛśni, the speech of the middle region, and the Maruts born from it; "apyāḥ", the Rudras who are in the waters, in the atmosphere: all of you make us happy, give us happiness."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- ते (*te*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- द्युमतः (*dyumataḥ*)—radiant
- वाजवतः (*vājavataḥ*)—mighty
- नृवतः (*nṛvataḥ*)—accompanied by sons and the like
- पुरुक्षोः (*purukṣoḥ*)—praised by many
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- दातारः (*dātāraḥ*)—givers
- भूत (*bhūta*)—be
- दशस्यंतः (*daśasyaṃtaḥ*)—granting desired ends
- दिव्याः (*divyāḥ*)—the Ādityas dwelling in the heavenly world
- पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*)—the Vasus dwelling on earth
- गोजाताः (*gojātāḥ*)—the Maruts, sons of Pṛśni
- अप्याः च (*apyāḥ ca*)—and the Rudras dwelling in the atmosphere
- मृळत (*mṛḷata*)—let them make us happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, be givers to us of wealth that is radiant, mighty, accompanied by sons and the like, and praised by many. Granting desired ends, let the Ādityas dwelling in the heavenly world, the Vasus dwelling on earth, the Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, and the Rudras dwelling in the atmosphere make us happy.

##### English translation
Be unto us, gods, the donors of splendid, invigorating riches, comprising male descendants, and celebrated by many : celestial Adityas, terrestrial Vasus, offspring of Prishni, children of the waters, granting our desires, make us happy.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते नो॑ रु॒द्रः सर॑स्वती स॒जोषा॑ मा॒ळ्हुष्मं॑तो॒ विष्णु॑र्म्ळंतु  ॒
> वायुः ।  
> ऋ॒भु॒क्षा वाजो॒ दैव्यू॑ विधा॒ता प॒र्जन्या॒वाता॑ पिप्यता॒मिषं॑  
> नः ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 291

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । नः । रुद्रः । सरस्वती । सजोषाः । माळ्हुष्मंतः । विष्णुः । मृळंतु । वायुः ।  
> ऋभुक्षाः । वाजः । दैव्यः । विधाता । पर्जन्यावाता । पिप्यतां । इषं । नः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मीळ्हुष्मंतो वर्षणवंतस्ते देवा नोऽस्मान्मृळंतु । मृळयंतु ।
> सुखियंतु । के त इति चेदुच्यते । रुद्रः सरस्वती च सजोषाः सह प्रीयमाणा
> विष्णुर्वायुश्च ऋभुक्षाः । ऋभुर्विभ्वा वाज इति त्रयः सौधन्वनाः । तेषामाद्य
> ऋभुश्च वाजोऽंतिमश्च । उपलक्षणमेतत् । विभ्वा च । दैव्यो देवेभ्यो हितो
> विधाता प्रजापतिश्च । अपि च पर्जन्यावाता पर्जन्यश्च वायुश्चोभौ नोऽस्मभ्यमिषमन्नं पिप्यतां । वर्धयतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those gods, "mīḷhuṣmantaḥ", the rain-givers, are to make us happy. If it is asked who they are, he says: Rudra and Sarasvatī, "sajoṣāḥ", pleased together; Viṣṇu and Vāyu; and "ṛbhukṣāḥ". Ṛbhu, Vibhvā and Vāja are the three sons of Sudhanvan; of them the first, Ṛbhu, and the last, Vāja, are named, and this is by way of indication, so that Vibhvā too is meant. "Daivyaḥ" is Vidhātṛ, beneficial to the gods, that is, Prajāpati. And Parjanya and Vāyu, both of them, are to increase for us "iṣa", food.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मीळ्हुष्मंतः (*mīḷhuṣmaṃtaḥ*)—the rain-makers
- ते (*te*)—the famous
- रुद्रः (*rudraḥ*)—Rudra
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—who attain satisfaction together
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- वायुः (*vāyuḥ*)—Vāyu
- ऋभुक्षाः (*ṛbhukṣāḥ*)—Ṛbhukṣan
- वाजः (*vājaḥ*)—Vāja (Vibhvan)
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळंतु (*mṛḷaṃtu*)—let them make happy
- दैव्यः (*daivyaḥ*)—who is beneficial to the gods
- विधाता (*vidhātā*)—Prajāpati
- पर्जन्यावाता (*parjanyāvātā*)—Parjanya and the god Vāyu
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- पिप्यतां (*pipyatāṃ*)—let them increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Rudra, Sarasvatī, Viṣṇu and Vāyu, who attain satisfaction together, who are the makers of rain and are famous, and Ṛbhu, Vāja and Vibhvan, make us happy. May Prajāpati, who is beneficial to the gods, and Parjanya and the god Vāyu increase our food.

##### English translation
May Rudra and Saraswati, alike well pleased, and Vishnu and Vayu, make us happy, sending rain; and Ribhukshin, and Vaja, and the divine Vidhatri: and may Parjanya and Vata grant us abundant food.

### Printed p. 292
#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त स्य दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता भगो॑ नो॒ऽपां नपा॑दवतु॒ दानु॒ सप्रिः॑ ।  
> त्वष्टा॑ दे॒वेभि॒र्जनि॑भिः स॒जोषा॒ द्यौर्दे॒वेभिः॑ पृथि॒वी स॑मु॒द्रॆः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । स्यः । देवः । सविता । भगः । नः । अपां । नपात् । अवतु । दानु । पप्रिः ।  
> त्वष्टा । देवेभिः । जनिभिः । सजोषाः । दौर्ब्य । देवेभिः । पृथिवी । समुद्रैः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च स्य स यः प्रेरकतया सर्वत्र प्रख्यातः स सविता देवो भगश्चापां
> नपाच्चापां मेघस्थानां पुत्रो माध्यमिकोग्निः स च नोऽस्मानवतु । रक्षतु ।
> कीदृशोपां नपात् । दानु दातव्यं धनं पप्रिः प्राता पूरयिता ॥ प्रा पूरण
> इत्यस्मादादृगमहन इति किनो लिड्वद्भावान्न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः ॥ तथा
> देवेभिर्देवैर्जनिभिस्तत्पत्नीभिश्च सजोषाः सहप्रीतिस्त्वष्टा च देवेभिर्देवैः सह
> प्रीयमाणा दौश्च समुद्रॆः सह प्रीयमाणा पृथिवी चैताश्च सर्वा देवता
> आस्मानवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And that god Savitṛ, who is famed everywhere as the impeller, and Bhaga, and "apāṃ napāt", the son of the waters that stand in the clouds, the Agni of the middle region: may he too protect us. Of what kind is Apāṃ Napāt? "Dānu" is the wealth that is to be given; "papriḥ" is the one who fills it up, who fulfils. Likewise "sajoṣāḥ", sharing delight, with the gods and with their wives ("janibhiḥ"); Tvaṣṭṛ, pleased together with the gods; Dyaus, pleased together with the gods; and Earth, pleased together with the seas: may all these deities protect us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the famous
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—and of divine nature
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—Bhaga
- दानु (*dānu*)—the wealth that is to be given
- पप्रिः (*papriḥ*)—who fills up
- अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*)—Agni, who dwells in the atmosphere
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अवतु (*avatu*)—let him protect
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—with the gods
- जनिभिः (*janibhiḥ*)—and with their wives
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—who is together
- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—Tvaṣṭṛ
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—who is together with the gods
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the heavenly world
- समुद्रॆः (*samudrèḥ*)—who is together with the seas
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth (let her protect us)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the famous and divine Savitṛ, and Bhaga, and Agni, who dwells in the atmosphere and fills up the wealth that is to be given, protect us. May Tvaṣṭṛ, who is together with the gods and with their wives, the heavenly world, which is together with the gods, and the earth, which is together with the seas, protect us.

### Printed p. 293

##### English translation
And may the divinie Savitri and Bhaga, and the grandson of the waters, (Agni), the prodigal of gifts preserve us ; and may Twashtri with the gods, and Earth with the seas, (preserve us).

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नोऽहि॑र्बु॒ध्न्यः॑ शृणोत्व॒ज एक॑पात्पृथि॒वी स॑मु॒द्रः ।  
> विश्वे॑ दे॒वा ऋ॑ता॒वृधो॑ हुवा॒नाः स्तु॒ता मंत्राः॑ कविश॒स्ता  ॑
> अवंतु ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । अहिः । बुध्न्यः । शृणोतु । अजः । एकपात् । पृथिवी । समुद्रः ।  
> विश्वे । देवाः । ऋत्यवृधः । हुवानाः । स्तुताः । मंत्राः । कविशस्त्राः । अवंतु ॥१४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निमारुत उत नोऽहिरित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोतु
> देवानां पत्नीरुशतीरवंतु नः । आ. ५-२० । इति ॥
> उतापि जाहिर्बुध्न्यो नोऽस्माकं स्तोत्रं शृणोतु । अजो जन्मरहितः ।
> एकोऽसहाय एव पद्यते गच्छतीत्येकपात् । एतत्पदद्वयाभिधेयो देवश्च पृथिवी
> समुद्रश्चास्मदीयं स्तोत्रं शृणोतु । अपि च ऋतावृध ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य सत्यस्य वा
> वर्धयितारो हुवाना आस्माभिराहूयमानाः पूर्वर्यषिभिश्च स्तोत्रैः स्तुता
> मंत्रा मंत्रणीया गुप्तं भाषितव्या मंत्रप्रतिपाद्या वा कविशस्ताः कविभिर्मेधाविभिर्युषिभिः शस्त्रैः शंसिता ईदृशा विश्वे देवा अवंतु । अस्मान्रक्षंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse belongs to the Agnimāruta recitation. It is also set down in the sūtra: उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोतु देवानां पत्नीरुशतीरवंतु नः (*uta no 'hirbudhnyaḥ śṛṇotu devānāṃ patnīruśatīravaṃtu naḥ*) (Ā. 5-20). May Ahirbudhnya hear our hymn; "aja" is the birthless one; "ekapāt" is the one who goes ("padyate") alone, unaccompanied; and the god denoted by these two words, and Earth and Ocean, are to hear our hymn. And may the Viśvedevas protect us: "ṛtāvṛdhaḥ", increasers of ṛta, that is, of the sacrifice or of truth; "huvānāḥ", called by us, and praised with hymns by the ancient seers; "mantrāḥ", to be pondered, to be spoken in secret, or those who are set forth by the mantras; "kaviśastāḥ", praised with śastras by poets, the wise ones, and the sages. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- अहिर्बुध्न्यः (*ahirbudhnyaḥ*)—the god Ahirbudhnya
- अज एकपात् (*aja ekapāt*)—the god bearing the name Aja Ekapād
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth
- समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*)—the deity presiding over the ocean
- नः (*naḥ*)—our hymn
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—let them hear
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—the increasers of the sacrifice
- हुवानाः (*huvānāḥ*)—those who are called by us

### Printed p. 294
- स्तुताः (*stutāḥ*)—those who are praised by us
- मंत्राः (*maṃtrāḥ*)—those worthy of our meditation
- कविशस्ताः (*kaviśastāḥ*)—those who are praised by the wise
- विश्वेदे देवाः (*viśvede devāḥ*)—all the Viśvedevas
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—let them protect us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Ahirbudhnya, Aja Ekapād, the earth and the deity presiding over the ocean, let all of them hear our hymn. May all the Viśvedevas, the increasers of the sacrifice, who are called by us, who are worthy of our praise and of our meditation, and deserving of the praise of the wise, protect us.

##### English translation
May Ahirbudhnya, Aja-ekapad, and Earth and Ocean, hear us : may the universal gods, who are exalted by sacrifice, they who are invoked and praised (by us), to whom mystical prayers are addressed, and who have been glorified by (ancient) sages, preserve us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In reciting the Agnimāruta śastra mantras, this Ṛk "uta no 'hiḥ" is to be included and recited; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोतु देवानां पत्नीरुशतीरवंतु नः (*uta no 'hirbudhnyaḥ śṛṇotu devānāṃ patnīruśatīravaṃtu naḥ*) (A. 5-20). **NOTE**
Ahirbudhnya: concerning this deity, see what is written in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 5, p. 588, and Part 14, pp. 142-143.
Aja Ekapād: concerning this deity, see what is written in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 5, p. 588, and Part 15, p. 174.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग्ना हु॒तासो॒ वस॒वोऽधृ॑ष्टा॒ विश्वे॑ स्तु॒तासो॑ भूता यजत्राः॥
