## Sūkta 53 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयमु त्वेति दशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं पौष्टं । यां
> पूषन्नित्यनुष्टुप् शिष्वा गायत्र्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । वयं दश पौष्णं तद्दायत्रं
> वै यां पूषन्ननुष्टुबिति ॥ अर्थार्थिभिः प्रवसद्धिरेतज्जप्यं । सूत्रितं च । वयमु
> त्वा पथस्पत इत्यर्थचर्यां चरिष्यन् । आ. गृ. ३-७-८ । इति । जपेदिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning वयमु त्वा (*vayamu tvā*), of ten Ṛks, is the fourth sūkta; its seer is Bharadvāja and its deity is Pūṣan. The Ṛk beginning यां पूषन् (*yāṃ pūṣan*) is Anuṣṭubh and the rest are Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says so accordingly: वयं दश पौष्णं तद्दायत्रं वै यां पूषन्ननुष्टुबिति (*vayaṃ daśa pauṣṇaṃ taddāyatraṃ vai yāṃ pūṣannanuṣṭubiti*). This sūkta is to be muttered by those who seek wealth and travel abroad, and the sūtra says: वयमु त्वा पथस्पत इत्यर्थचर्यां चरिष्यन् (*vayamu tvā pathaspata ityarthacaryāṃ cariṣyan*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-7-8) **NOTE**. The word "he should mutter" is to be supplied.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta वयमु त्वा (*vayamu tvā*) is the fourth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; the deity is Pūṣan. The eighth Ṛk of this sūkta, यां पूषन् (*yāṃ pūṣan*), is in the Anuṣṭup metre. All the remaining Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated thus: वयं दश पौष्णं तद्दायत्रं वै यां पूषन्ननुष्टुप् (*vayaṃ daśa pauṣṇaṃ taddāyatraṃ vai yāṃ pūṣannanuṣṭup*). Those who travel abroad seeking wealth should mutter this sūkta, as explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra, वयमु त्वा पथस्पते इत्यर्धर्चया चरिष्यन् (*vayamu tvā pathaspate ityardharcayā cariṣyan*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-7-8) **NOTE**.

- Sūkta 53
- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 53
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 8; Varga 17, 18
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10
- Ṛṣi: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Pūṣan
- Chandas: 1-7, 9-10 Gāyatrī; 8 Triṣṭup **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यमु॑ त्वा पथस्पते॒ रथं॒ न वाज॑सातये ।  
> धि॒ये पू॑षन्न युज्महि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वयं । ऊं इति । त्वा । पथः । पते । रथं । न । वाजसातये ।  
> धिये । पूषन् । आयुज्महि ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 336

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पथस्पते मार्गस्य पालयितः पूषन् धिये कर्मार्थं वाजसातयेऽन्नस्य
> लाभाय च वयं रथं न युद्धे रथमिव त्वा त्वामयुज्महि । युंज्महि । अस्मदभिमुखं कुर्मः ॥ उ इति पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pathaspati, protector of the path, Pūṣan, for the sake of the work (dhī) and for the gaining of food (vājasāti), we yoke you, as one yokes a chariot in battle: we turn you towards us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पथस्पते (*pathaspate*)—who are the protector of the paths
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O divine Pūṣan
- धिये (*dhiye*)—for the protection of our work
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—and for the gaining of our food
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- रथं न (*rathaṃ na*)—as one takes refuge in a chariot in battle
- त्वा उ (*tvā u*)—you alone
- आयुज्महि (*āyujmahi*)—we take refuge in, and make you join with us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Pūṣan, protector of all paths, for the protection of our work and for our gaining of food, as a warrior in battle takes refuge in his chariot and makes himself one with it, we take refuge wholly in you and make you one with us.

##### English translation
Pushan, lord of paths, we attach you to us like a chariot, for (the sake of) bringing food, and of (accomplishing our) solemnity.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि नो॒ नर्यं॒ वसु॑ वी॒रं प्रय॑तदक्षिणं ।  
> वा॒मं गृ॒हप॑तिं नय । २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । नः । नर्यं । वसु । वीरं । प्रयत्नदक्षिणं ।  
> वामं । गृहपतिं । नय ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् नर्यं नृभ्यो हितं वसु धनमभि प्राप्तं वीरं दारिद्रस्य
> विशेषेणेरयितारं गमयितारं प्रयतदक्षिणं पूर्वमन्येभ्योऽपि दत्तधनं । यद्वा ।
> प्रयतं शुद्धं दक्षिणं धनं यस्य तादृशं । वामं वननीयमेवंविधं गृहपतिं
> गृहस्थं नोऽस्मान्नय । प्रापय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, wealth that is beneficial to men, that has been attained; one who is a hero, a sender-away (īrayitṛ), a remover in particular, of poverty; one who has given wealth to others before; or else one whose wealth, his gift, is pure; desirable: such a householder, a man of the household, lead us to; bring us to him.

### Printed p. 337

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Pūṣan) नर्यं (*naryaṃ*)—beneficial to men
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- अभि (*abhi*)—for obtaining
- वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—who has the power to destroy poverty
- प्रयतदक्षिणं (*prayatadakṣiṇaṃ*)—who has wealth fit to be given
- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—who has attractive qualities
- गृहपतिं (*gṛhapatiṃ*)—to the master of the house
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- नय (*naya*)—lead and bring together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Pūṣan, lead us and bring us together with a master of the house who has the power to destroy poverty, who has wealth fit to be given and who has attractive qualities, that we may obtain wealth beneficial to all men.

##### English translation
Conduct us to a gracious householder, friendly to man, liberal in (bestowing) wealth, the giver of pious donations.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अदि॑त्संतं चिदाघृणे॒ पूष॒न्दाना॑य चोदय ।  
> प॒णेश्चि॒द्वि म्र॑दा॒ मनः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अदित्संशं । चित् । अघृणे । पूषन् । दानाय । चोदय ।  
> पणेः । चित् । वि । म्रद । मनः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अघृण आगतदीप्ते पूषन् आदित्संतं चित् दातुमनिच्छंतमपि पुरुषं
> दानायास्मद्दानार्थं चोदय । प्रेरय । पणेश्चिद्वणिजोऽपि वार्धुषिकस्य लुब्धस्यापि
> मनो हृदयं वि म्रद । दानार्थं मृदूकुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aghṛṇa, Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you: impel to give to us even the man who does not wish to give. Soften the mind, the heart, even of a trader, a usurer, a miser; make it soft for the purpose of giving.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—who are possessed of exceedingly great radiance
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O divine Pūṣan
- अदित्संतं चित् (*aditsaṃtaṃ cit*)—even a miser who has no nature of giving
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—to give and, as a benefactor of the world,

### Printed p. 338

may he become so.
- चोदय (*codaya*)—impel
- पणेश्चित् मनः (*paṇeścit manaḥ*)—the mind also of the pani (the miser) who has a hard heart
- वि म्रद (*vi mrada*)—make it soft with compassion

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, possessed of exceedingly great radiance, impel even the miser who has no nature of giving, so that he gives and becomes a benefactor of the world. Make the mind of the pani (the miser), whose heart is hard, soft with compassion.

##### English translation
Resplendent Pushan, instigate the niggard to liberality, soften the heart of the miser.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि प॒थो वाज॑सातये चिनु॒हि वि मृधो॑ जहि ।  
> साधं॑तामुग्र नो॒ धियः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । पथः । वाजसातये । चिनुहि । वि । मृधः । जहि ।  
> साधंतां । उग्र । नः । धियः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उग्रोद्गूर्णबल पूषन् पथो मार्गान् वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाय
> वि चिनुहि । शोधितान्नुरु । यैः पथिभिर्गता धनं लभेमहि तादृशान्पथः पृथक्कुर्वित्यर्थः । मृधो बाधकान् तस्करादींश्च वि जहि । बाधस्व । तथा नोऽस्माकं धियः
> कर्माण्यन्नलाभार्थं क्रियमाणानि साधंतां । सिध्यंतु । सफलानि भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, whose strength is raised up and fierce: clear the paths for the winning of food. Make the paths purified, those by which we may go and gain wealth, that is, set such paths apart. Strike down the obstructors, thieves and the like; keep them off. And let our undertakings, the rites performed for the gaining of food, be accomplished and bear fruit.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्र (*ugra*)—O Pūṣan, whose strength is exceedingly great and terrifying to enemies
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—so that food may come to us easily
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—our paths
- वि चिनुहि (*vi cinuhi*)—make them pure, free of thieves and the like
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the violent thieves and the like
- वि जहि (*vi jahi*)—defeat and destroy
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the rites performed for the sake of food
- साधंतां (*sādhaṃtāṃ*)—may they attain the desired object

### Printed p. 339

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, whose strength is exceedingly great and terrifying to enemies, so that food may come to us easily, make our paths pure, free of thieves and the like. Defeat and destroy the violent thieves and the like. May the rites performed for our gain of food attain the fulfilment of their desired objects.

##### English translation
Fierce Pushan, select (fit) roads for the passage of provisions : drive away all obstructors, (thieves, or the like), so that our holy rites may be accomplished.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ तृंधि पणी॒नामार॑या॒ हृद॑या कवे ।  
> अथे॑म॒स्मभ्यं॑ रंधय ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । तृंधि । पणीनां । आरया । हृदया । कवे ।  
> आथ । ईं । आस्मभ्यं । रंधय ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे कवे प्राज्ञ पूषन् पणीनां वणिजां लुब्धानां हृदया हृदयानि
> कठिनान्यारया । सूक्ष्मलोहाग्रो दंडः प्रतोद इत्यारेति चाख्यायते । तया परि
> तृंधि । परिविध्य । हृद्गतं काठिन्यमपनयेत्यर्थः । अथानंतरमीमेनान्पणीनस्मभ्यं
> रंधय । वशीकुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wise Pūṣan, with the goad, the ārā, pierce the hearts of the panis, the traders and misers, which are hard. The ārā is called a rod with a fine metal point, a prod. Pierce through with it, that is, remove the hardness that lies in the heart. Then make these panis subject to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवे (*kave*)—O wise Pūṣan
- पणी नां (*paṇī nāṃ*)—of the panis, who have no nature of giving and are misers
- हृदया (*hṛdayā*)—the hardness that lies in the heart
- आरया (*ārayā*)—with the goad of fierce power
- परि तृंधि (*pari tṛṃdhi*)—destroy (make their hearts soft)
- आथ (*ātha*)—afterwards
- ईं (*īṃ*)—these panis
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- रंधय (*raṃdhaya*)—make them submit and fulfil our prayers

### Printed p. 340

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Pūṣan, destroy with the goad of fierce power the hardness in the hearts of the panis, who have no nature of giving and are misers, and make their hearts soft. Afterwards make these panis submit to us and become helpers to us.

##### English translation
Piercc with a goad the hearts of the avaricious, wise Pushan, and so render them complacent towards us.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि पू॑ष॒न्नार॑या तुद प॒णेरि॑च्छ हृ॒दि प्रि॒यं ।  
> अथे॑म॒स्मभ्यं॑ रंधय ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । पूषन् । आरया । तुद । पणेः । इच्छ । हृदि । प्रियं ।  
> अथ । ईं । अस्मभ्यं । रंधय ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् आरया प्रतोदेन पणेर्वणिजो हृदयं वि तुद । विविध्य । तस्य
> पणेर्हृदि हृदये प्रियमस्मभ्यमनुकूलं धनमिच्छ । दातव्यमितीच्छां जनय ।
> अथानंतरमस्मभ्यमीमेनान्रंधय । वशीकुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, pierce with the goad, the prod, the heart of the pani, the trader. In the heart of that pani, desire for us the dear, favourable wealth; that is, produce in him the wish that it must be given. Then make these men subject to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan
- आरया (*ārayā*)—with your goad of fierce power
- पणेः (*paṇeḥ*)—the heart of the pani
- वि तुद (*vi tuda*)—torment
- हृदि (*hṛdi*)—in that same heart
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—the wish to do us good
- इच्छॆ (*icchè*)—produce the desire
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- ईं (*īṃ*)—these same panis
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- रंधय (*raṃdhaya*)—subdue them and impel them to help us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, torment the heart of the pani with your goad of fierce power. In that same heart produce the desire to do us good. Afterwards subdue these same panis and impel them to help us.

### Printed p. 341

##### English translation
Pierce with a goad. Pushan, the heart of the avaricious ; generate generosity in his heart, and so render him complacent towards us.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ रि॑ख किकि॒रा कृ॑णु पणी॒नां हृद॑या कवे ।  
> अथे॑म॒स्मभ्यं॑ रंधय ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । रिख । किकिरा । कृणु । पणीनां । हृदया । कवे ।  
> अथ । ईं । अस्मभ्यं । रंधय ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे कवे प्राज्ञ पूषन् पणीनां वणिजां हृदया हृदयान्या रिख । आलिख ।
> अलिख्य च किकिरा कीर्णानि प्रशिथिलानि कृणु । कुरु । मृदूनि कुर्वित्यर्थः । अन्यद्गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wise Pūṣan, scratch the hearts of the panis, the traders, and having scratched them make them scattered, loosened; that is, make them soft. The rest has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कवे (*kave*)—O wise Pūṣan
- पणीनां (*paṇīnāṃ*)—of the panis
- हृदया (*hṛdayā*)—the hard hearts
- आ रिख (*ā rikha*)—rub them as one whets on a whetstone
- किकिरा (*kikirā*)—so that they give up their hardness and become soft
- कृणु (*kṛṇu*)—make
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- ईं (*īṃ*)—these same panis
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- रंधय (*raṃdhaya*)—make them submit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise Pūṣan, rub the hard hearts of the panis as one whets on a whetstone. Make them give up their hardness and become soft. Make these same misers submit to our prayer and fulfil our desired objects.

##### English translation
Abrade, wise Pushan the hearts of the avaricious ; relax (their hardness), and so render them complacent towards us.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यां । पूषन् । ब्रह्मचोदनीं । आरां । बिभर्षि । अघृणे ।  
> तया । समस्य । हृदयं । आ । रिख । किकिरा । कृणु ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आफृण आगतदीप्ते पूषन् ब्रह्मचोदनीं ब्रह्मणोऽन्यस्य प्रेरयित्रिं
> यामारां बिभर्षि हस्ते धारयसि तया समस्यॆ सर्वस्य लुब्धजनस्य हृदयमा रिख ।
> आलिण । किकिरा किकिराणि कीर्णानि प्रशिथिलानि च कृणु । कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you: the goad that you carry in your hand, which impels the Brahman (the prayer or food), the ārā, with it scratch the heart of every miserly person, and make the scattered, loosened ones, that is, make them soft.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अघृणे (*aghṛṇe*)—O one possessed of exceedingly great radiance
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan
- ब्रह्मचोदनीं (*brahmacodanīṃ*)—that impels food
- यां (*yāṃ*)—which
- आरां (*ārāṃ*)—goad
- बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*)—you possess
- तया (*tayā*)—with that
- समस्य (*samasya*)—of all the miserly people
- हृदयं (*hṛdayaṃ*)—the heart
- आ रिख (*ā rikha*)—rub it so that they become soft
- किकिरा (*kikirā*)—so that they attain softness
- कृणु (*kṛṇu*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, possessed of exceedingly great radiance, with the very goad that you possess, which impels food, rub the hearts of all the miserly people and make them attain softness, so that they show compassion towards us.

##### English translation
Resplendent Pushan, with that food-propelling goad which you bear, abrade the heart of every miser and render it relaxed.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या ते॒ अष्टा॒ गो॑प॒शापृ॑णे पशु॒साध॑नी ।  
> तस्या॑स्ते सु॒म्म मी॑महे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । ते । अष्टा । गोऽओपशा । आफृणे । पशुसाधनी ।  
> तस्याः । ते । सुम्मं । ईमहे ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आफृण आगतदीप्ते पूषन् ते त्वदीया याष्ट्रारा गोओपशा । उपशेरत
> इत्योपशाः । गाव ओपशा यस्यास्तादृशी । आत एव पशुसाधनी पशूनां साधयित्रि
> भवति ते त्वदीयायास्तस्याः संबंधि सुम्नं सुखमीमहे । याचामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you: that goad of yours, which is gopaśā. Those that lie near are the opaśāḥ; she whose opaśāḥ are cows is of that kind. Therefore she is the accomplisher of cattle, the one who brings cattle about. Of that goad of yours we beg the happiness that belongs to it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—O Pūṣan, of marvellous radiance
- गोपशा (*gopaśā*)—that gives shelter to cows
- पशुसाधनी (*paśusādhanī*)—that is the guide and protector of cattle
- ते (*te*)—your
- या अष्टा (*yā aṣṭā*)—which goad there is
- तस्याः (*tasyāḥ*)—by that goad of yours
- सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)—the happiness to be obtained
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, of marvellous radiance, your goad, which gives shelter to cows and is the guide and protector of cattle: from that same goad we ask the happiness that is to be obtained.

##### English translation
Resplendent Pushan, we ask of you the service of that your weapon, which is the guide of cows, the director of cattle.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नो॑ गो॒षणिं॒ धिय॑मश्व॒सां वा॑ज॒सामु॒त ।  
> न्य॒वत्कृ॑णुहि वी॒तये॑ ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 344

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । गोऽसनिं । धियं । अश्वसां । वाजसां । उत ।  
> स्नवत् । कृणुहि । वीतये ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे पूषन् गोषणिं गवां सनित्रीमश्वसामश्वानां सनित्रीं
> वाजसां वाजानामन्नानां सनित्रीमुतापि च नृवत् नृवतीं यद्वा नृणां वनित्रीं
> दात्रिमेवंभूतां धियं बुद्धिं कर्म वा नोऽस्माकं वीतये खादनायोपभोगार्थं कृणुहि कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And further, O Pūṣan: make our intellect or rite (धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)), which is the bestower of cows, the bestower of horses, the bestower of food, and which is possessed of men (or else: the giver of men), fit for our eating and enjoyment (वीतये (*vītaye*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- गोषणिं (*goṣaṇiṃ*)—that which increases cows
- अश्वसां (*aśvasāṃ*)—that which helps towards the gaining of horses
- वाजसां (*vājasāṃ*)—that which nourishes with food
- उत (*uta*)—and
- नृवत् (*nṛvat*)—that which helps towards sons, grandsons and the like
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—our rite
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—as fit for enjoyment
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, make our rite, which increases cows, helps towards the gaining of horses and nourishes with food, fit for our enjoyment.

##### English translation
Make our pious worship productive of cows, of houses, of food, of
dependants, for our enjoyment.

The fifty-fourth sūkta

## Sūkta 54 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सं पूषन्निति दशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं पौष्णं गायत्रं । सं
> पूषन्नित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ नष्टधनमन्विच्छता पुरुषेणैतज्जप्यं । सूत्रितं च । सं पूषन्विदुषेति नष्टमधिजिगमिषन्मूळ्वो वा । आ. गृ. ३-७-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the fifth sūkta, of ten Ṛks, beginning सं पूषन् (*saṃ pūṣan*), has Bharadvāja as its seer, Pūṣan as its deity, and the Gāyatrī metre. The Anukramaṇī says the same (सं पूषन् (*saṃ pūṣan*)). A man who is seeking lost wealth should mutter this sūkta. It is laid down in the sūtra beginning with सं पूषन्विदुषेति (*saṃ pūṣanviduṣeti*), to be used by one who wishes to find what is lost, or who is bewildered (Ā. Gṛ. 3-7-9)**NOTE**.

### Printed p. 345

Translation (Anuvāda): This sūkta beginning सं पूषन् (*saṃ pūṣan*) is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta, Pūṣan the deity, Gāyatrī the metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said at the beginning, सं पूषन् (*saṃ pūṣan*). That a man who seeks lost wealth should mutter this sūkta is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra सं पूषन्विदुषेति नष्टमधिजिगमिषुनूळ्वो वा (*saṃ pūṣanviduṣeti naṣṭamadhijigamiṣunūḷvo vā*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-7-9)**NOTE**.

Sūkta 54. Maṇḍala 6. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 54. Aṣṭaka 4. Adhyāya 8. Vargas 19, 20. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya. Deity: Pūṣan. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं पू॑षन्वि॒दुषा॑ नय॒ यो अंज॑सानु॒शास॑ति ।  
> य ए॒वेदमिति॒ ब्रव॑त् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । पूषन् । विदुषा । नय । यः । अंजसा । अनुशासति ।  
> यः । एव । इदं । इति । ब्रवत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् पोषक देव विदुषा जानता तेन जनेन सं नय अस्मान्
> संगमय यो विद्वानंजसा ऋजुमार्गेणानुशासति अनुशास्ति नष्टद्रव्यप्राप्त्यपायमुपदिशति । यश्चैवैवमिदं नष्टं भवदीयं धनमिति ब्रवत् ब्रवीति । नष्टं
> धनं दर्शयतीत्यर्थः ! तेन विदुषेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, nourishing god, bring us together with that knowing man who directly, by the straight way, instructs us in the means of regaining what is lost, and who says, "This is your lost wealth", that is, who shows the lost wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan, nourisher of the world
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which wise man
- अंजसा (*aṃjasā*)—walking in the excellent straight path
- अनुशासति (*anuśāsati*)—who teaches us too that same straight path

### Printed p. 346

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which wise man
- एव (*eva*)—in this very manner
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this deed is to be performed
- इति (*iti*)—thus
- ब्रवत् (*bravat*)—says
- विदुषा (*viduṣā*)—with such a man of discerning knowledge
- सं नय (*saṃ naya*)—unite us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, unite us with that wise man who, walking in the excellent straight path, teaches us too that same straight path, and who, saying "In this very manner such a deed is to be performed", makes known the discernment of what is to be done and what is not to be done.

##### English translation
Bring us, Pushan, into communication with a wise man who may
rightly direct us, who may even say, this is so.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समु॑ पू॒ष्णा ग॑मेमहि॒ यो गृ॒हा अ॑भि॒शास॑ति ।  
> इ॒म ए॒वेति॑ च॒ ब्रव॑त् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । ऊं इति । पूष्णा । गमेमहि । यः । गृहान् । अभिशासति ।  
> इमे । एव । इति । च । ब्रवत् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूष्णानुगृहीता वयं सं गमेमहि तेन जनेन संगच्छेमहि यो जनो
> गृहान् येषु गृहेष्वस्मदीया नष्टाः पशवस्तिष्ठंति तान् गृहानभिशासति अभिशास्ति
> अभिमुख्येन बोधयति । यश्चेमे त्वदीया नष्टाः पशव एवैवं तिष्ठंतीति च
> ब्रवत् ब्रूयात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Favoured by Pūṣan, may we meet that man who points out the houses in which our lost cattle stand, shows them to us face to face, and who says, "These cattle of yours stand just so."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which discerning man
- गृहान् (*gṛhān*)—the houses in which our cattle are hidden
- अभिशासति (*abhiśāsati*)—shows to us
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- इमे (*ime*)—these your cattle
- एव (*eva*)—stand thus, having been carried off
- इति (*iti*)—thus
- ब्रवत् (*bravat*)—says; with such a man of discerning knowledge

### Printed p. 347

- पूष्णा (*pūṣṇā*)—we who are favoured by the god Pūṣan
- संगमेमहि (*saṃgamemahi*)—may we come together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May we, favoured by the god Pūṣan, come together with that man of discerning knowledge who shows us the houses in which our cattle are hidden, and who tells us, "Your cattle stand thus, having been carried off."

##### English translation
May we, by the favour of Pushan, come in communication with (the
man) who may direct us to the houses (where our goods are sacreted), and
may say, verily these are they.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पू॒ष्णश्च॒क्रं न रि॑ष्यति॒ न कोशोऽव॑ पद्यते ।  
> नो अ॑स्य व्यथते प॒विः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूष्णः । चक्रं । न । रिष्यति । न । कोशः । अव । पद्यते ।  
> नो इति । अस्य । व्यथते । पविः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूष्णः । पोषकस्य देवस्य चक्रमायुधं । न रिष्यति । न विनश्यति । अस्य चक्रस्य
> कोशश्च नाव पद्यते । न हीयते । अस्य पविर्धारा च नो नैव व्यथते । कुंठीभवति ।
> तेन चक्रेण चोरान्हत्वास्मदीयं धनं प्रकाशयेति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The discus, the weapon, of Pūṣan the nourisher is not destroyed; and the sheath of this discus does not fall away, is not lost; and the edge, the blade, of this weapon does not suffer, that is, does not become blunt. The sense is: with that discus kill the thieves and bring our wealth to light.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूष्णः (*pūṣṇaḥ*)—of the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world
- चक्रं (*cakraṃ*)—the weapon called the discus
- न रिष्यति (*na riṣyati*)—is not destroyed
- कोशः (*kośaḥ*)—the sheath of that weapon also
- न अव पद्यते (*na ava padyate*)—does not come to destruction
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this god Pūṣan
- पविः (*paviḥ*)—the edge of the weapon
- नो व्यथते (*no vyathate*)—does not become blunt

### Printed p. 348

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The weapon called the discus, of the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, is not destroyed. The sheath in which that weapon is placed does not come to destruction either. The edge of this god's weapon does not become blunt.

##### English translation
The discus of Pushan does not destory ; its sheath is not discarded,
its edge harms not us.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो अ॑स्मै ह॒विषावि॑ध॒न्न तं पू॒षापि॑ मृष्यते ।  
> प्र॒थ॒मो विं॑दते॒ वसु॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । अस्मै । हविषा । अविधत् । न । तं । पूषा । अपि । मृष्यते ।  
> प्रथमः । विंदते । वसु ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो यजमानोऽस्मै पूष्टे हविषा चरुपुरोडाशादिनाविधत् परिचरति तं
> यजमानं पूषा नापि मृष्यते । अपिशब्द ईषदर्थे । ईषदपि न हिनस्ति । स च प्रथमो
> मुख्यः सन् वसु धनं विंदते । लभते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificer who serves this Pūṣan with an oblation, cooked grain, cakes and the like, him Pūṣan does not injure even in the least (the word अपि (*api*) has the sense of "slightly"). And that man, being first, the chief, wins wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to this god Pūṣan
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—by offering oblations
- अविधत् (*avidhat*)—offers worship
- तं (*taṃ*)—that sacrificer
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- न अपि मृष्यते (*na api mṛṣyate*)—does not destroy
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same sacrificer
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—as most eminent of all
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- विंदते (*viṃdate*)—obtains

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who offers worship to this god Pūṣan by offering oblations, that sacrificer the god Pūṣan does not destroy. That same sacrificer obtains wealth as the most eminent of all.

### Printed p. 349

##### English translation
Pushan inflicts not the least injury on the man who propitiates him
by oblations : he is the the first who acquires wealth.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पू॒षा गा अन्वे॑तु नः पू॒षा र॑क्ष॒त्वर्व॑तः ।  
> पू॒षां वाजं॑ सनोतु नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूषा । गाः । अनु । एतु । नः । पूषा । रक्षतु । अर्वतः ।  
> पूषां । वाजं । सनोतु । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूषा पोषको देवो नोऽस्मदीया गा अन्वेतु । रक्षणार्थमनुगच्छतु ।
> स च पूषार्वतोऽश्वान्रक्षतु चोरेभ्यः । तथा वाजमन्नं च नोऽस्मभ्यं पूषा
> सनोतु ! प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Pūṣan, the nourishing god, follow our cattle, going after them for their protection. May that same Pūṣan protect our horses from thieves. And may Pūṣan bestow food on us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—cows
- अन्वेतु (*anvetu*)—may he follow for protection
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—that same god Pūṣan
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—our horses
- रक्षिसु (*rakṣisu*)—may he protect
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- सनोतु (*sanotu*)—may he provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, follow our cows for their protection. May that same god Pūṣan protect our horses. May the god Pūṣan provide us with food.

##### English translation
May Pushan come to (guard) our cattle, may Pushan protect our houses : may Pushan give us food.**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पूष॒न्ननु॒ प्र गा इ॑हि॒ यज॑मानस्य सुन्व॒तः ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूषन् । अनु । प्र । गाः । इहि । यजमानस्य । सुन्वतः ।  
> अस्माकं । स्तुवतां । उत ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, go after the cattle of the sacrificer who is pressing the Soma, for their protection; and go also after the cattle of us who sing your praise.

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O god Pūṣan
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—who presses the Soma juice (to offer to you)

- गाः (*gāḥ*)—cows
- अनु प्र इहि (*anu pra ihi*)—follow for their protection
- उत (*uta*)—and

- आस्माकं (*āsmākaṃ*)—follow also for the protection of us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, follow for their protection the cows of the sacrificer who presses the Soma juice to offer to you, and follow also for the protection of us who praise you.

##### English translation
Come, Pushan, to (guard) the cattle of of the institutor of the rite
presenting libations, and also of us repeating (your) praises

> हे पूषन्' अस्मदीयं गोधनं माकिर्नेशत् । मा नश्यतु । माकिर्माकीमि
> त्येत् प्रतिषेधमात्रे वर्तेते । माकीं रिषत् । मा व्याघ्रादिभिर्हिंस्यतां । माकीं
> मा च केवटे कूपे सं शारि । संशीर्णं भूत् । कूपपातेनापि हिंसितं मा भवतु ।
> अथैवं सत्यरिष्वाभिरहिंसिताभिर्गोभिः सहा गहि । सायंकाल आगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, let our cattle-wealth not perish (माकिर्नेशत् (*mākirneśat*)). Let it not be injured by tigers and the like (माकीं रिषत् (*mākīṃ riṣat*)). And let it not be shattered by falling into a well (केवटे (*kevaṭe*)); let it not be harmed even by a fall into a pit. This being so, come in the evening together with the cows that have been left unharmed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- माकिर्नेशत् (*mākirneśat*)—let our cattle-wealth not perish
- माकीं रिषत् (*mākīṃ riṣat*)—let it not be injured by tigers and the like
- केवटे (*kevaṭe*)—in wells
- माकीं सं शारि (*mākīṃ saṃ śāri*)—let it not slip and fall
- अथ (*atha*)—after the protection of these
- अरिष्वाभिः (*ariṣvābhiḥ*)—together with these unharmed cows
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—graciously come at evening time

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, let our cattle-wealth not perish. Let it not be injured by tigers and the like. Let it not slip and fall into wells. After protecting them, come at evening time with the cows left unharmed.

##### English translation
Let not, Pushan, our cattle perish; let them not be injured; let them not
be hurt by falling into a well ; come, therefore, along with them unharmed.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शृ॒ण्वंतं॑ पू॒षणं॑ व॒यमिर्य॒मन॑ष्टवेदसं ।  
> ईशा॑नं रा॒य ई॑महे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शृण्वंतं । पूषणं । वयं । इर्यं । अनष्टवेदसं ।  
> ईशानं । रायः । ईमहे ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 352

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मत्सोत्राणि शृण्वंतमिर्यं दारिद्रस्य प्रेरकमनष्टवेदसमविनष्टधनमीशानं सर्वस्येश्वरमेवंविधं पूषणं देवं वयं रायो धनानीमहे
> याचामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We beg for riches from the god Pūṣan, who hears our hymns, who is the remover of poverty (इर्यं (*iryaṃ*)), whose wealth is undestroyed (अनष्टवेदसं (*anaṣṭavedasaṃ*)), the lord of all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—who hears our praises
- इर्यं (*iryaṃ*)—the destroyer of poverty
- अनष्ट वेदसं (*anaṣṭa vedasaṃ*)—who has wealth that is free of destruction
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—who is the master of all
- पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*)—the god Pūṣan
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—for the sake of wealth
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We ask the god Pūṣan, who hears our praises, who destroys poverty, whose wealth is free of destruction and who is the master of all, for wealth.

##### English translation
We solicit riches of Pushan, who hears (our eulogies); who is the averter (of poverty); the preserver of that which is not lost, the ruler (over all).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पूष॒न्तव॑ व्र॒ते व॒यं न रि॑ष्येम॒ कदा॑ च॒न ।  
> स्तो॒तार॑स्त इ॒ह स्म॑सि ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूषन् । तव । व्रते । वयं । न । रिष्येम । कदा । चन ।  
> स्तोतारः । ते । इह । स्मसि ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्मास्येषु वैश्वदेवे पर्वणि पौष्णस्य हविषः पूषन्तव व्रत इत्येषानुवाक्य । सूत्रितं च । वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वः पूषन्तव व्रते वयं ।
> आ. २-१६ । इति ॥
> हे पूषन्नोषक तव त्वदीये व्रते कर्मणि वर्तमाना वयं कदा चन
> कदाचिदपि न रिष्येम । हिंसिता न भवेम । तादृशाश्च वयमिहास्मिन्कर्मणि ते तव
> स्तोतारः स्मसि । स्मः । भवामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, at the Vaiśvadeva parvan, this Ṛk पूषन्तव व्रते (*pūṣantava vrate*) is the anuvākyā for the oblation to Pūṣan; it is laid down by the sūtra वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वः पूषन्तव व्रते वयं (*vāmamadya savitarvāmamu śvaḥ pūṣantava vrate vayaṃ*) (Ā. 2-16). O nourishing Pūṣan, we who are engaged in your rite shall never at any time be harmed. Such as we are, here in this rite we are your praisers.

### Printed p. 353

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O nourishing god Pūṣan
- तव (*tava*)—your
- व्रते (*vrate*)—engaged in your rite of worship
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- कदा चन (*kadā cana*)—always
- न रिष्येम (*na riṣyema*)—may we not suffer harm
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite
- ते (*te*)—your
- स्तोतारः स्मसि (*stotāraḥ smasi*)—are we not your praisers?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O nourishing god Pūṣan, may we, engaged in your rite of worship, never be subject to harm. In this sacrificial rite are we not your praisers?

##### English translation
May we never suffer detriment when engaged, Pushan, in your worship : we are at this time your adorers.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifice called Cāturmāsya, at the Vaiśvadeva parvan, in the oblation made to the deity Pūṣan, this Ṛk beginning पूषन् तव (*pūṣan tava*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra: this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वः पूषन्तव व्रते वयं (*vāmamadya savitarvāmamu śvaḥ pūṣantava vrate vayaṃ*) (Ā. 2-16).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ पू॒षा प॒रस्ता॒द्दस्तं॑ दधातु॒ दक्षि॑णं ।  
> पुन॑र्नो न॒ष्टमाज॑तु ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । पूषा । परस्तात् । हस्तं । दधातु । दक्षिणं ।  
> पुनः । नः । नष्टं । आ । अजतु ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूषो पोषको देवः परस्तात्परस्मिन्देशे सुसंचारादन्यस्मिन् चोरव्याघ्रादिभिरुषिते देशे गच्छतो गोधनस्य निवारणाय स्वकीयं दक्षिणं हस्तं परि
> दधातु । परिधानं निवारकं करोतु । नोऽस्मदीयं नष्टं च गोधनं पुनराजतु ।
> आगच्छतु । आगमयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the nourishing god Pūṣan place his own right hand around, as a barrier, to keep back our cattle-wealth that goes to a distant place, to another region inhabited by thieves, tigers and the like**NOTE**. And may he bring back to us again our lost cattle-wealth; may he come with it, may he cause it to come.

### Printed p. 354

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- परस्तात् (*parastāt*)—over our cows that roam in forest tracts and the like, full of tigers and others
- दक्षिणं हस्तं (*dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ*)—his right hand
- परि दधातु (*pari dadhātu*)—let him place over them (so that those cows may not go to an unprotected region)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- नष्टं (*naṣṭaṃ*)—the stolen cattle-wealth
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- आजतु (*ājatu*)—let him bring and join it to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Pūṣan place his right hand over our cows that roam in forest tracts and the like, full of tigers and others, to prevent them from going to unprotected regions. May he bring again to us our stolen cattle-wealth.

##### English translation
May Pushan put forth his right hand (to restrain our cattle) from going astray : may he bring again to us that which has been lost.

The fifty-fifth sūkta

## Sūkta 55 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एहि वामिति षडृचं षष्ठं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं गायत्रं पौष्णं ।
> अनुक्रम्यते च । एहि वां षडिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the sixth sūkta, of six Ṛks, beginning एहि वां (*ehi vāṃ*), has Bharadvāja as its seer, the Gāyatra metre, and Pūṣan as its deity. The Anukramaṇī also says so (एहि वां षडिति (*ehi vāṃ ṣaḍiti*)). The use in ritual (viniyoga) has already been stated.

Translation (Anuvāda): This sūkta beginning एहि वां (*ehi vāṃ*) is the sixth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. In it there are six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; the deity is Pūṣan; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said, एहि वां षट् (*ehi vāṃ ṣaṭ*). The use in ritual (viniyoga) has been stated before.

Sūkta 55. Maṇḍala 6. Anuvāka 5. Sūkta 55. Aṣṭaka 4. Adhyāya 8. Varga 21. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya. Deity: Pūṣan. Metre: Gāyatrī.

### Printed p. 355

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एहि॒ वां वि॑मुचो नपा॒दाघृ॑णे॒ सं स॑चावहै ।  
> रथीऋतुतस्य नो भव ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । इहि । वां । विमुचः । नपात् । आघृणे । सं । सचावहै ।  
> रथीः । यतस्य । नः । भव ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विमुचो नपात् । विमुंचति सृष्टिकाले स्वसकाशात्सर्वाः प्रजा विसृजतीति
> विमुक् प्रजापतिः । तस्य पुत्राघृण आगतदीप्ते पूषन् वां । वाति गच्छति स्तुतिं
> प्राप्नोतीति वा स्तोता ॥ वा गतिगंधनयोरित्यस्मादातो मनिन्निति विच् ॥ वां गंतारं
> स्तोतारं मामेहि । आगच्छ । आवां च सं सचावहै । समयाव । संगच्छावहै ।
> तादृशस्त्वं नोऽस्माकमृतस्य यज्ञस्य रथी रंहिता नेता भव । तथा सति तत्रत्यं
> हविस्त्वयापि लभ्यत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O descendant of Vimuc: Vimuk is Prajāpati, who at the time of creation sends out all creatures from himself. O Aghṛṇa, Pūṣan, whose radiance has come to you, son of Prajāpati! वां (*vāṃ*) is the praiser, he who goes, that is, reaches the praise. Come to me, the praiser who goes to you. And let us two be united. Being such, be for us the swift leader (रथीः (*rathīḥ*)) of the rite (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)), the sacrifice; in that case the oblation there will be received by you also.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विमुचः (*vimucaḥ*)—of Prajāpati, who creates all beings at the time of creation
- नपात् (*napāt*)—who are his son
- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—O Pūṣan, who have marvellous radiance
- वां (*vāṃ*)—to me, your praiser
- एहि (*ehi*)—graciously come
- आवां (*āvāṃ*)—we two
- सं सचावहै (*saṃ sacāvahai*)—let us be united and stay together
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- रथीः (*rathīḥ*)—as leader
- भव (*bhava*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, son of Prajāpati, who at the time of creation brings out into the light all beings hidden within himself, and possessed of marvellous radiance: come graciously to me, your praiser. Let us two be united and stay together. Be the leader of our sacrifice.

##### English translation
Come illustrious grandson of Prajapati to (me, your) worshipper :
let us be associated : become the conveyer of our sacrifice.**NOTE**

### Printed p. 356

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अफ्घणे (*aphghaṇe*)—for this word Yāska has given the explanation:
आघृणिरागतहृणिः आघृणे सं सचावहै । आगशहृणे सं सेवावहै ॥ (*āghṛṇirāgatahṛṇiḥ āghṛṇe saṃ sacāvahai | āgaśahṛṇe saṃ sevāvahai ‖*) (Ni. 5-9) **GLOSS**
Durgācārya, commenting on this, has explained the meaning: आगतदीप्तिरागतक्रोधो वाभिधेयः (*āgatadīptirāgatakrodho vābhidheyaḥ*), that is, one who has blazing radiance, or one who has anger. Although the word आफृणि (*āphṛṇi*) is read both among the names expressing radiance, such as हरः हृणिः (*haraḥ hṛṇiḥ*), and among the names expressing anger, such as हेळः हरः हृणिः (*heḷaḥ haraḥ hṛṇiḥ*), here for the word आफृणि (*āphṛṇi*) the meaning "radiance", that is, "one who has radiance", is the fitting one.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> र॒थीत॑मं कप॒र्दिन॒मीशा॑नं॒ राध॑सो म॒हः ।  
> रा॒यः सखा॑यमीमहे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रथितमं । कपर्दिनं । ईशानं । राधसः । महः ।  
> रायः । सखायं । ईमहे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रथीतममतिशयेन रथिनं । यद्वा । अतिशयेन रंहितारं नेतारं कपर्दिनं ।
> कपर्दश्चूडा । तद्वंतं । राध्नोत्यनेनेति राधो धनं । महो महतो
> राधसो धनस्येशानं स्वामिनं सखायमस्माकं मित्रमेवंविधं पूषणं रायो
> धनानीमहे । याचामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

रथीतमं (*rathītamaṃ*) is the one who is the greatest charioteer; or else, the one who is the supreme swift leader. कपर्दिनं (*kapardinaṃ*): kapardaḥ is the hair-knot (cūḍā); he who has it. राधो (*rādho*) is wealth, that by which one prospers. Pūṣan is lord, owner, of great wealth, and our friend; of him, such as he is, we beg riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रथीतमं (*rathītamaṃ*)—the supreme leader
- कपर्दिनं (*kapardinaṃ*)—who has an attractive tuft of hair
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—to great
- राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)—wealth
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—who is the lord
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—who is a friend to us; Pūṣan
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—for the sake of wealth
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We ask the god Pūṣan, the supreme leader, who has an attractive tuft of hair, who is lord of great wealth and a friend to us, for wealth.

### Printed p. 357

##### English translation
We solicit riches of our friend, (Pushan), the chief of charioteers, the wearer of a braid (of hair), the lord of infinite wealth.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रा॒यो धारा॑स्याघृणे॒ वसो॑ रा॒शिर॑जाश्व ।  
> धीव॑तोधीवतः॒ सखा॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रायः । धारा । असि । आघृणे । वसोः । राशिः । अजअश्व ।  
> धीवतःऽधीवतः । सखा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आफृण आगतदीप्ते पूषन् रायो धनस्य धारासि । प्रवाहो भवसि ।
> स्तोतृभ्यो बहु धनं नैरंतर्येण प्रयच्छसीत्यर्थः । अजाश्व । अजाश्चागा एवाश्वा
> अश्वकार्यापन्ना यस्य तादृश पूषन् वसोर्वसुनो धनस्य राशिः संघश्च भवसि ।
> धनसंघश्च त्वय्येव निवसतीत्यर्थः । धीवतो धीवतः सर्वस्य स्तोत्रवतः पुरुषस्य
> सहा मित्रभूतश्च भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, shining one, you are the stream of wealth: that is, you give much wealth to your praisers without interruption. Ajāśva means one whose horses, doing the work of horses, are goats. O Pūṣan, such as you are, you are also the heap and the assembly of wealth; the whole mass of wealth dwells in you alone. You are the companion and friend of every man who offers praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—O Pūṣan, endowed with radiance
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—for all wealth
- धारा असि (*dhārā asi*)—you yourself are the stream
- अजाश्व (*ajāśva*)—O Pūṣan, whose horses have the form of goats
- वसोः (*vasoḥ*)—of wealth
- राशिः (*rāśiḥ*)—you are the heap
- धीवतोधीवतः (*dhīvatodhīvataḥ*)—to every kind of praiser
- सखा (*sakhā*)—you are the friend

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O radiant Pūṣan, for all wealth you yourself are the stream. O Pūṣan, whose horses have the form of goats, for all wealth you yourself are the heap. To every kind of praiser you yourself are the friend.

##### English translation
Illustrious Pushan, you are a torrent of riches: you, who have a goat for your steed, are a heap of wealth ; the friend of every worshipper.

The god Pūṣan who is renowned as the paramour of his sister Uṣas, who has a vehicle in the form of goats, who is possessed of strength and is the nourisher, that god Pūṣan let us now praise and worship.

I praise Pūṣan, the husband of Night, the creator of the world. May Pūṣan, the paramour of his sister Uṣas, hear our praises. May Pūṣan, the brother of Indra, be a friend to me, the praiser.

## Sūkta 56 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य एनमिति षडृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं पौष्णं । अंत्यानुष्टुबादौ पंच गायत्र्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । य एनमंत्यानुष्टुबिति ॥ गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning य एनं (*ya enaṃ*) has six Ṛks and is the seventh sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja, its deity is Pūṣan. The last verse is in the Anuṣṭubh metre, and the first five are Gāyatrī. So the Anukramaṇī says: य एनमंत्यानुष्टुबिति (*ya enamaṃtyānuṣṭubiti*). The application of the sūkta has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning "Ya enam" is the seventh sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; the deity is Pūṣan; the last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The first five Ṛks of the sūkta are in the Gāyatrī metre. The Anukramaṇī says: "Ya enamantyānuṣṭup". The application of the sūkta has been stated before.

- Ṛṣi: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Pūṣan
- Chandas: 1–5 Gāyatrī; 6 Anuṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य ए॑नमा॒दिदे॑शति करं॒भादिति॑ पू॒षणं॑ ।  
> न तेन॑ दे॒व आ॒दिशे॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । एनं । आदिदेशति । करंभत् । इति । पूषणं ।  
> न । तेन । देवः । आदिशे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः स्तोतैनं पूषणं पोषकं करंभात्करंभाणां धृतमिश्राणां यवसक्कूनामत्तेत्यादिदेशति अभिष्टौति तेन पुरुषेणान्यो देवो नादिशे । आदेष्टव्यः
> स्तोतव्यो न भवति । पूष्ण एव सर्वस्याभिमतस्य धनस्य लाभात् देवतांतरं न
> स्तौतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The praiser who declares this Pūṣan, the nourisher, to be the eater of karambha, that is, of barley-meal mixed with ghee, by that man no other god is indicated, no other god is to be directed to or praised. Because all desired wealth is obtained from Pūṣan alone, he does not praise another deity.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the praiser who
- एनं पूषणं (*enaṃ pūṣaṇaṃ*)—with reference to this god Pūṣan
- करंभात् (*karaṃbhāt*)—the eater of barley-meal mixed with ghee
- इति (*iti*)—thus
- आदिदेशति (*ādideśati*)—praises and proclaims
- तेन (*tena*)—by that same praiser
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—any other god than Pūṣan
- न आदिशे (*na ādiśe*)—is certainly not indicated

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praiser who, with reference to this god Pūṣan, praises and proclaims "This god is the eater of karambha", by that praiser no other god than Pūṣan is indicated.

### Printed p. 362

##### English translation
No (other) deity is indicated by him who declares the offering of mixed meal and butter to be intended for Pushan.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त घा॒ स र॒थीत॑मः॒ सख्या॒ सत्प॑तियु॒र्जा ।  
> इंद्रो॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ जिह्नु ते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । घ । सः । रथितमः । सख्या । सत्पतिः । युजा ।  
> इंद्रः । वृत्राणि । जिघ्नते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत घापि च स यः शत्रूणां हंतृत्वेन प्रसिद्धस्तादृशो रथीतमोऽतिशयेन
> रथी महारथः सत्पतिः सतां पालयितैवंगुण इंद्रः सख्या मित्रभूतेन पूष्णा युजा
> सहायभूतेन युक्तः सन् वृत्राणि शत्रून् जिघ्नते । हंति । इंद्रस्याप्ययमेव
> साहाय्यकारीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And that Indra, who is renowned as the slayer of enemies, the greatest of charioteers, the great charioteer, the protector of the good, being joined with Pūṣan as his friend and ally, kills the enemies. The meaning is that Pūṣan is the helper even of Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत घ (*uta gha*)—and
- सः (*saḥ*)—he who is renowned as the destroyer of enemies
- रथीतमः (*rathītamaḥ*)—the one most excellent among charioteers
- सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*)—the protector of good men
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—his friend
- युजा (*yujā*)—who helps him in battle and the like, Pūṣan
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—enemies
- जिह्वते (*jihvate*)—kills

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is renowned as the destroyer of enemies, the great charioteer, the protector of good men, joined with the god Pūṣan, who is his friend and who stays by him and helps him in battle and the like, kills his enemies.

##### English translation
He, the chief of charioteers, the protector of the virtuous, Indra, destroys his foes, with his friend Pushan for his ally.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒तादः प॑रु॒षे गवि॒ सूर॑श्च॒क्रं हि॑र॒ण्ययं॑ ।  
> नै॑रयद्र॒थीत॑मः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । अदः । परुषे । गवि । सूरः । चक्रं । हिरण्ययं ॥  
> नि । ऐरयत् । रथितमः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च सूरः प्रेरको रथीतमोऽतिशयेन रथी नेतृतमो वा पूषा
> परुषे परुषति पर्ववति भास्वति वा गवि । गच्छतीति गौरादित्यः । तस्मिन् हिरण्ययं
> हिरण्मयं सुवर्णनिर्मितमदस्तद्रथस्य चक्रं नैरयत् । नितरां प्रेरयति स्म ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pūṣan, the impeller and the greatest of charioteers, or the supreme leader, drives on in the radiant sun, the gauḥ (the one who goes), that golden wheel of his chariot, made of gold. Parus means that which has joints or which shines; gau is the sun, since it goes. He drives it on continually.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—the impeller
- रथीतमः (*rathītamaḥ*)—the supreme leader, the god Pūṣan
- परुषे (*paruṣe*)—radiant
- गवि (*gavi*)—in the sun
- हिरण्ययं (*hiraṇyayaṃ*)—made of gold
- अदः चक्रं (*adaḥ cakraṃ*)—that wheel of the chariot
- नैरयत् (*nairayat*)—he yokes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Pūṣan, the impeller of all and the supreme leader, yokes in the radiant sun the golden wheel of the chariot.

##### English translation
He, the impeller, the chief of charioteers, (Pushan), ever urges on that golden wheel (of his car) for the radiant sun.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Gavi: in the sun. On the meaning of the word gau as the sun, Yāska says: आदित्योऽपि गौरुच्यते । उतादः परुषे गवि । पर्ववति भास्वतीत्यौपमन्यवः ॥ (*ādityo 'pi gaurucyate | utādaḥ paruṣe gavi | parvavati bhāsvatītyaupamanyavaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 9-6).

### Printed p. 364

Thus he has given the etymology. The sun too has the name gauḥ, because he is of a moving nature and does not stay even for a moment in one place but is always in motion; so gavi means in the sun. Because he shines with a mass of radiance, gauḥ (gauḥ also means a ray) is the sun or Āditya: this is the opinion of the teacher named Aupamanyava, as Yāska explains.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद॒द्य त्वा॑ पुरुष्टुत॒ ब्रवा॑म दस्र मंतुमः ।  
> तत्सु नो॒ मन्म॑ साधय ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अद्य । त्वा । पुरुस्तुत । ब्रवाम । दस्र । मंतुमः ।  
> तत् । सु । नः । मन्म । साधय ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरुष्टुत बहुभिर्यजमानैः स्तुत दस्र दर्शनीय मंतुमो ज्ञानवान्
> पूषन् अद्येदानीं यदुद्दिश्य त्वा त्वां ब्रवाम स्तवाम नोऽस्माकं मन्म
> मननीयं तद्धनं सु साधय उत्पादयॆ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, praised by many sacrificers, beautiful to behold, possessed of knowledge, today we praise you for the sake of a wealth; accomplish for us, produce, that wealth worthy of our thought.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुष्टुत (*puruṣṭuta*)—who is praised by many sacrificers
- दस्र (*dasra*)—who has an attractive form
- मंतुमः (*maṃtumaḥ*)—who has abundant knowledge, O god Pūṣan
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- यत् (*yat*)—for the sake of which wealth
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- ब्रवाम (*bravāma*)—we praise
- मन्म (*manma*)—which is fit for our meditation
- तत् (*tat*)—that same wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- सु साधय (*su sādhaya*)—produce in abundance

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, who are praised by many sacrificers, who have an attractive form and abundant knowledge, at this time of the sacrifice produce for us that same wealth, worthy of our meditation, for the sake of which we praise you. Provide it for us.

##### English translation
Since, intelligent Pushan, of goodly aspect, the praised of many, we celebrate you to-day, therefore grant us the desired wealth.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं च॑ नो ग॒वेष॑णं सा॒तये॑ सीषधो ग॒णं ।  
> आ॒रात्पू॑षन्नसि श्रु॒तः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । च । नः । गोऽविषणं । सातये । सीसधः । गणं ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् नोऽस्माकं सातये लाभायेमं च गणं मनुष्यसंघं
> गवेषणं गवामेषयितारं सीषधः । साधय । हे पूषन् आरात् दूरदेशेऽपि त्वं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, for our gain, accomplish for this company of men, who are seekers of cows, what they desire. O Pūṣan, you are renowned and famous even in a distant place.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the gaining of cows
- गवेषणं (*gaveṣaṇaṃ*)—who are searching for cows
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इमं च गणं (*imaṃ ca gaṇaṃ*)—this company of sacrificers
- सीषधः (*sīṣadhaḥ*)—satisfy
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O god Pūṣan
- आरात् (*ārāt*)—even in very distant places
- श्रुतः (*śrutaḥ*)—renowned
- असि (*asi*)—you are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, satisfy this our company of sacrificers, who are searching for cows for the gaining of cows. O god Pūṣan, you are renowned even in very distant places.

##### English translation
Gratify this our assembly, desirous of cattle by their acquistion : you. Pushan, are renowned afar.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ते॑ स्व॒स्तिमी॑मह आ॒रेअ॑घा॒मुपा॑वसुं ।  
> अ॒द्या च॑ स॒र्वता॑तये॒ श्वश्च॑ स॒र्वता॑तये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । स्वस्तिं । ईमहे । आरेऽअघां । उपवसुं ।  
> अद्य । च । सर्वतातये । श्वः । च । सर्वतातये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् ते त्वदीयां त्वया देयां स्वस्तिं कल्याणीं रक्षामारेअघां ।
> आरे दूरेऽघं पापं यस्यास्तादृशीं । उपावसुमुपगतधनां । ईदृशीं स्वस्तिमद्य
> चास्मिंश्च काले सर्वतातये । सर्वैर्युत्विग्निस्तायत इति सर्वतातिर्यज्ञः । तदर्थं ।
> यद्वा । सर्वेषां भोगानां विस्ताराय । श्वश्च परस्मिन्नपि दिने सर्वतातये सर्वदा
> सर्वतात्यर्थमेमहे । अभियाचामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, we beg of you well-being, that is, welfare and protection to be given by you, far from evil, which is attended by wealth; this we ask today and at the time to come, for the sake of the sacrifice (sarvatāti), the sacrifice being so called because it is extended by all the officiating priests and sacrificers **NOTE**. Or else it is for the spreading of all enjoyments. And tomorrow, on another day also, for the sake of the sacrifice, always, for the sake of all, we ask and entreat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्य च (*adya ca*)—today, in the present
- सर्वतातये (*sarvatātaye*)—for the sake of the sacrifice that is performed
- श्वश्च (*śvaśca*)—in the days to come
- सर्वतातये (*sarvatātaye*)—for the sake of the sacrifices that are performed
- ते (*te*)—to be bestowed by you
- आरेआघां (*āreāghāṃ*)—which is free from sin
- उपावसुं (*upāvasuṃ*)—which is wealth-giving
- स्वस्तिं (*svastiṃ*)—well-being
- आ ईमहे (*ā īmahe*)—we ask abundantly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, so that the sacrifice to be performed today and the sacrifices to be performed in the days to come may be performed without obstacle, we ask abundantly the well-being that is free from sin, that gives wealth and that is bestowed by you.

##### English translation
We deserve of you well-being, remote from evil, approximate to wealth, both for the sake of general sacrifice to-day, for the sake of general sacrifice to-morrow.

## Sūkta 57 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रा नु पूषणेति षडृचमष्टमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं गायत्रमैंद्रापौष्णं । अनुक्रांतं च । इंद्रा न्वैंद्रं चेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning इंद्रा नु पूषणा (*iṃdrā nu pūṣaṇā*) has six Ṛks and is the eighth sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja, its metre is Gāyatrī, its deities are Indra and Pūṣan. The Anukramaṇī says: इंद्रा न्वैंद्रं चेति (*iṃdrā nvaiṃdraṃ ceti*). The application has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning "Indrā nu Pūṣaṇā" is the eighth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; Indra and Pūṣan are the deities; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says: "Indrā nindraṃ ca" **NOTE**. The application has been stated before.

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 57
- Maṇḍala 6, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 57
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 8, Varga 23
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6
- Ṛṣi: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Indra and Pūṣan
- Chandas: Gāyatrī

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॒ नु पू॒षणा॑ व॒यं स॒ख्याय॑ स्व॒स्तये॑ ।  
> हु॒वेम॒ वाज॑सातये ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा । नु । पूषणा । वयं । सख्याय । स्वस्तये ।  
> हुवेम । वाजसातॆये ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इतरेतरयोगादिंद्रपूषण्यब्दयोरुभयत्र द्विवचनं । इंद्रापूषणौ देवौ
> नु अद्य च वयं स्वस्तये सख्याय शोभनाय सखित्वाय वाजसातये वाजस्यान्नस्य
> बलस्य वा सातये संभजनाय च हुवेम । आह्वयाम । स्तवाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The words Indra and Pūṣan are both in the dual because of their mutual conjunction. We now call, that is, invoke and praise, the two gods Indra and Pūṣan, for our well-being, for the sake of an excellent friendship, and for the obtaining and enjoyment of food or strength.

### Printed p. 368

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रापूषणौ (*iṃdrāpūṣaṇau*)—the gods Indra and Pūṣan
- नु (*nu*)—now
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our well-being
- सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)—for the winning of friendship
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the obtaining of food
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we pray and invite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Now we pray to the gods Indra and Pūṣan and invite them, for our well-being, for winning friendship with them and for the obtaining of food.

##### English translation
We invoke you, Indra and Pushan, for your friendship, for our well-being, and for the obtaining of food.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोम॑म॒न्य उपा॑सद॒त्पात॑वे च॒म्वोः॑ सु॒तं ।  
> क॒रं॒भम॒न्य इ॑च्छति ॥ २ ।'

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमं । अन्यः । उप । आसदत् । पातवे । चम्योः । सुतं ।  
> करंभं । अन्यः । इच्छति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चन्नोरधिषवणफलकयोः सुतमभिषुतं सोममन्वोन्वयोरेकतर इंद्रः
> पातवे पातुमुपासदत् । उपसीदति । उपगच्छति । अन्य एकतरः पूषा करंभं
> फृतसिक्तं सक्त्वात्मकं हविर्भक्षयितुमिच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

One of the two, Indra, comes and sits near to drink the Soma pressed on the two pressing-boards. The other, Pūṣan, desires to eat the karambha, an offering of barley-meal sprinkled with ghee.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—of the two, Indra and Pūṣan, one, Indra
- चव्वोः (*cavvoḥ*)—by the pressing-boards
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma juice
- पातवे (*pātave*)—to drink
- उपासदत् (*upāsadat*)—sits down
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the other, Pūṣan
- करंभं (*karaṃbhaṃ*)—the offering mixed with ghee and in the form of barley-meal
- इच्छति (*icchati*)—desires to eat

### Printed p. 369

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Of the two, Indra and Pūṣan, Indra sits down to drink the Soma juice pressed by the pressing-boards that press out the Soma juice. The other, Pūṣan, desires to eat the offering which is mixed with ghee and is in the form of barley-meal.

##### English translation
One (of you) approaches to drink the Soma poured out into ladles, the other desires the buttered meal.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒जा अ॒न्यस्य॒ वह्न॑यो॒ हरी॑ अ॒न्यस्य॒ संभृ॑ता ।  
> ताभ्यां॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ जिघ्नते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अजाः । अन्यस्य । वह्नयः । हरी इति । अन्यस्य । संभृता ।  
> ताभ्यां । वृत्राणि । जिघ्नते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयोरिंद्रापूष्टोरन्यस्यैकस्य पूष्टोऽजाश्चागा वह्नयो वाहका अश्वाः ।
> अन्यस्यापरस्येंद्रस्य संभृता संभृतौ सम्यक् पुष्टौ हरी एतत्संज्ञावश्च वाहकौ ।
> स चेंद्रस्ताभ्यां वृत्राणि शत्रून् जिघ्नते । हंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of these two, Indra and Pūṣan, the one, Pūṣan, has goats as his bearers, his carrying steeds. The other, Indra, has the two well-nourished, strong horses of the name Hari as his bearers. And that Indra, with those two, kills the enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अन्यस्य (*anyasya*)—to Pūṣan (one of the two, Indra and Pūṣan)
- वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)—the vehicles
- अजाः (*ajāḥ*)—are goats
- अन्यस्य (*anyasya*)—to the other, Indra
- संभृता (*saṃbhṛtā*)—well grown
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses called Hari are the vehicle
- ताभ्यां (*tābhyāṃ*)—among the two **NOTE**
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—all enemies
- जिघ्नते (*jighnate*)—kills

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Of the two, Indra and Pūṣan, Pūṣan has vehicles in the form of goats. The other, Indra, has as his vehicle the well-grown horses called Hari. Of the two, Indra kills all enemies.

### Printed p. 370

##### English translation
Goats are the bearers of the one, two well-fed horses, of the other, and with them he destroys his foes.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिंद्रो॒ अन॑य॒द्रितो॑ म॒हीर॒पो वृषं॑तमः ।  
> तत्र॑ पू॒षा भ॑व॒त्सचा॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्रः । अनयत् । रितः । महीः । अपः । वृषन्तमः ।  
> तत्र । पूषा । अभवत् । सचा ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदा वृषंतमोऽतिशयेन वर्षितेंद्रो रितो गंत्रीर्महीर्महतीरपो
> वृष्ट्युदकान्यनयत् इमं लोकं प्रापयति तत्र तदानीं पूषा पोषको देवः
> सचाभवत् । अस्येंद्रस्य सहायो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When Indra, the greatest of showerers, brings to this world the great, flowing waters, that is, the waters of the rain, then Pūṣan, the nourishing god, becomes his companion; he becomes Indra's helper.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वृषंतमः (*vṛṣaṃtamaḥ*)—who sends down rain in abundance
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- रितः (*ritaḥ*)—which flow
- महीः (*mahīḥ*)—and are of great power
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- अनयत् (*anayat*)—he brings to this world
- तत्र (*tatra*)—at that time
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- सजा (*sajā*)—with him
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—is

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Indra, who sends down rain in abundance, brings to this world the flowing waters of great power, at that time the god Pūṣan is with him.

##### English translation
When the showerer Indra sends down the falling and mighty waters, there is Pushan along with him

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तां पू॒ष्णः सु॑म॒तिं व॒यं वृ॒क्षस्य॒ प्र व॒यामि॑व ।  
> इंद्र॑स्य॒ चा र॑भामहे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तां । पूष्णः । सुमतिं । वयं । वृक्षस्य । प्र । वयां इव ।  
> इंद्रस्य । च । आ । रभामहे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूष्णः पोषकस्य देवस्येंद्रस्य च तां प्रसिद्धां सुमतिं कल्याणीं मतिमनुग्रहबुद्धिं वृक्षस्य महीरुहस्य प्र वयां प्रकृष्टां दृढां शाखामिव वयमा
> रभामहे अवलंबामहे । आश्रयाम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We lay hold of, resort to, that renowned good mind, the gracious thought, of Pūṣan the nourisher and of Indra, as one lays hold of a strong, firm branch of a great tree.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृक्षस्य (*vṛkṣasya*)—of a great tree
- प्र वयां इव (*pra vayāṃ iva*)—as one resorts to a firm branch
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- पूष्णः (*pūṣṇaḥ*)—of the god Pūṣan
- च (*ca*)—and
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- तां (*tāṃ*)—that renowned
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—mind of favour
- रभामहे (*rabhāmahe*)—we resort to

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a man caught in a flood and similar calamities resorts to a firm branch of a great tree, so we resort to the renowned gracious mind of the god Pūṣan and of Indra.

##### English translation
We depend upon the good-will of Pushan, and of Indra, as (we cling) to the branches of a tree.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्पू॒षणं॑ युवामहे॒ऽभीशू॑रिव॒ सार॑थिः ।  
> म॒ह्या इंद्रं॑ स्व॒स्तये॑ ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 372

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । पूषणं । युवामहे । अभीशून् इव । सारथिः ।  
> मह्यै । इंद्रं । स्वस्तये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूषणं पोषकं देवमिंद्रं च महै महत्यै स्वस्तये रक्षार्थमुद्युवामहे । उद्योजयामः । उद्योजनमाकर्षणं । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सारथिः
> सूतोऽभीशूनिव । अभीशून्रश्मीनश्वबंधनार्थान्यथाकर्षति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We draw up, that is, we call to ourselves, Pūṣan the nourisher and Indra for great well-being, for protection. Drawing up means pulling. An example is given: as a charioteer, the driver, pulls to him the reins that serve to bind the horses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सारथी (*sārathī*)—the driver of the chariot
- अभीशूनिव (*abhīśūniva*)—as he pulls the reins toward himself
- पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*)—Pūṣan
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—and Indra
- मह्यै (*mahyai*)—great
- स्वत्रये (*svatraye*)—for welfare
- उद्युवामहे (*udyuvāmahe*)—we draw to us and make come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the driver of the chariot pulls the reins (the ropes) toward himself, so we draw Pūṣan and Indra toward us for great welfare and make them come.

##### English translation
We draw to us, for our great welfare, Pushan and Indra, as a charioteer (pulls tight) his reins.

## Sūkta 58 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शुक्रं त इति चतुर्यचं नवमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं पौष्टं । द्वितीया
> जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । शुक्रं चतुष्कं द्वितीया जगतीति ॥
> वैश्वदेवे पर्वणि वैश्वदेवस्य हविषः शुक्रं त इति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । शुक्रं ते
> अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यदिहेह वः स्वतवसः । आ. २-१६ । इति ॥ एकादशिनस्य पौष्टस्य
> पशोर्वपाया एषैव याज्या । सूत्रितं च । शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यत्पथे
> पथामजनिष्ठ पूषा । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥ अमाभिष्टवेऽप्येषा । सूत्रितं च । शुक्रं ते
> अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यदपश्यं गोपामनिपद्यमानं । आ. ४-६ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning शुक्रं त (*śukraṃ ta*) has four Ṛks and is the ninth sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja, its deity is Pūṣan; the second verse is Jagatī, the rest are Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī says: शुक्रं चतुष्कं द्वितीया जगतीति (*śukraṃ catuṣkaṃ dvitīyā jagatīti*). In the Vaiśvadeva parvan, this verse is the yājyā of the Vaiśvadeva oblation; it is laid down in the sūtra शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यदिहेह वः स्वतवसः (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadiheha vaḥ svatavasaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 2-16). For the vapā of the animal of Pūṣan in the Ekādaśina rite this same verse is the yājyā; it is laid down in the sūtra शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यत्पथे पथामजनिष्ठ पूषा (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyatpathe pathāmajaniṣṭha pūṣā*) (Ā. Sū. 3-7). It is used also in the अमाभिष्टवे (*amābhiṣṭave*) **NOTE**; it is laid down in the sūtra शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यदपश्यं गोपामनिपद्यमानं (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadapaśyaṃ gopāmanipadyamānaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-6).

### Printed p. 373

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning "Śukraṃ te" is the ninth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has four Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; Pūṣan is the deity; the second Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Jagatī metre, the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The Anukramaṇī says: "Śukraṃ catuṣkaṃ dvitīyā jagatī". In the Parveṣṭi connected with the Viśvedevas, in the oblation made to Pūṣan, the Ṛk "Śukraṃ te" is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as laid down by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यदिहेह वः स्वतवसः (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadiheha vaḥ svatavasaḥ*) (Ā. 2-16). In the animal oblation made to Pūṣan on the day of the Ekādaśin rite, this Ṛk is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the vapā oblation, as laid down by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यत्पथे पथामजनिष्ट पूषा (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyatpathe pathāmajaniṣṭa pūṣā*) (Ā. 3-7). And this Ṛk is applied also in the abhiṣṭava mantras in the sacrifice called Pravarga, as laid down by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यदपश्यं गोपामनिपद्यमानं (*śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadapaśyaṃ gopāmanipadyamānaṃ*) (Ā. 4-6).

##### Particulars

- Sūkta 58
- Maṇḍala 6, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 58
- Aṣṭaka 4, Adhyāya 8, Varga 24
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 4
- Ṛṣi: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya
- Devatā: Pūṣan
- Chandas: 1, 3, 4 Triṣṭubh; 2 Jagatī

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन् ते तव शुक्रं शुक्लवर्णमन्यदेकमहर्भवति वासरात्मकं । कथा ते
> तव संबंधि यजतं । यजिरत्र संगतिकरणे वर्तते । यजनीयं प्रकाशेन
> संगमनीयं स्वतः कृष्णवर्णमन्यदेकमहर्भवति राताख्यं । इत्थं विसुरूपे
> शुक्लकृष्णतया नानारूपे अहनी तव महिम्मा निष्पद्येते । यद्वा । हे पूषन्
> त्वदीयमन्यदेकं रूपं शुक्रं निर्मलं दिवसस्योत्पादकं । त्वदीयमन्यदेकं
> रूपं यजतं केवलं यजनीयं न प्रकाशकं रात्रेरुत्पादकं । आत एव विषुरूपे
> विषमरूपे अहनी अहश्च रात्रिश्च भवतः । आहोरात्रयोर्निर्माणे सूर्य एव
> कर्ता कथमस्य प्रसक्तिरिति तत्राह । द्यौरिवासि । यथा द्यौरादित्यः प्रकाशयिता तथा त्वं
> प्रकाशकोऽसि । कुत इत्यत आद । हे स्वधावोऽन्नवन्नूषन् विश्वाः सर्वा मायाः
> प्रज्ञा हि यस्मात्कारणादवसि रक्षसि अतः कारणात्त्वं सूर्य इव भवसीत्यर्थः ।
> तादृशस्य ते तव भद्रा कल्याणी रातिर्दानमिहास्मास्वस्तु । भवतु ॥ यास्क स्वाह । शुक्रं
> ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यदृज्जियं ते अन्यदयज्जियं ते अन्यदिति ना विषमरूपे
> अहनी कर्मणा द्यौरिव चासि । सर्वाणि च प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन् । नि. १२-१७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, one of your forms is white, that is, the day. Another, which is yajata (here the verb yaj has the sense of association): to be joined with, that is, in itself dark, and not shining, is the night, called rāta. Thus the two, the day and the night, are of different forms, white and dark, by your greatness. Or else: one form of yours is white, pure, the producer of the day; the other form of yours is only to be worshipped, not shining, the producer of the night. Hence the day and the night are of unequal forms. It may be asked: the making of day and night is the work of the sun, how does it come to Pūṣan? He answers: you are like heaven, that is, as the sun is the illuminator, so you are the illuminator. Why? O lord of svadhā, possessor of food, because you protect all the wisdoms, therefore you are like the sun. May your auspicious gift be here with us. Yāska says (Ni. 12-17): शुक्रं ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यदृज्जियं ते अन्यदयज्जियं ते अन्यदिति ना विषमरूपे अहनी कर्मणा द्यौरिव चासि । सर्वाणि च प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन् । (*śukraṃ te anyallohitaṃ te anyadṛjjiyaṃ te anyadayajjiyaṃ te anyaditi nā viṣamarūpe ahanī karmaṇā dyauriva cāsi | sarvāṇi ca prajñānānyavasyannavan |*) **GLOSS**

- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—one of your forms, the day
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—is of white colour

- ते अन्यत् (*te anyat*)—the other, in dark colour, is in the form of night
- अदनी (*adanī*)—day and night, which are your own forms
- विषुरूपे (*viṣurūpe*)—are of different forms
- द्यौः इव (*dyauḥ iva*)—like the sun
- आसि (*āsi*)—you are
- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—O Pūṣan, possessed of food
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- माया हि (*māyā hi*)—even the creatures
- अवसि (*avasi*)—you protect
- ते (*te*)—your
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, one of your forms, the day, is of white colour. Another form of yours, to be worshipped, is in the form of night, of dark colour. The day and the night, which are your own forms, are of different forms. You are shining like the sun. O Pūṣan, possessed of food, you protect all creatures. May your auspicious gift be with us

##### English translation
One of your forms, (Pushan), is luminous, one is venerable; so that the day is variously complexioned : for you are like the sun: verily. best-

##### English translation
ower of food, you protect all intelligences: may your auspicious liaberality be manifested on this occasion.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On this ṛk Yāska gives an etymological explanation: शुक्रं ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्यज्ञियं ते अन्यद्विषमरूपे अहनी कर्म द्यौरिव चासि सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन् भाजनवती ते पूषन्निह दत्तिरस्तु ॥ (*śukraṃ te anyallohitaṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadyajñiyaṃ te anyadviṣamarūpe ahanī karma dyauriva cāsi sarvāṇi prajñānānyavasyannavan bhājanavatī te pūṣanniha dattirastu ‖*) (Ni. 12-17). O god Pūṣan, one of your forms is of red colour, or exceedingly luminous. Another form is worthy of sacrifice, that is, fit to be worshipped with sacrifices and the like. Your two forms, day and night, are of mutually opposed character: that is, since the day is luminous and the night is accompanied by darkness, the one is opposed to the other. Again, like Āditya, or like the light of Āditya, you are pervasive everywhere. You protect all wise people (or all wisdom, or the Śāstras). Besides, you are the possessor of food, that is, the one who provides food to all. Therefore, O god Pūṣan, may a gift of auspicious food and the like be given to us also: this is the chief purport of the explanation. **NOTE**

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Ajāśva: one whose vehicle is a goat. **NOTE** Paśupāḥ: the protector of animals. Vājapasya: one in whose house, pasya, there are foods, vājāḥ. Dhiyaṃjinva: dhiyaḥ are the worshippers or the rites; he is the one who gratifies them. He has been placed by Prajāpati, as the nourisher, in the whole world. Such a Pūṣan, the nourishing god, brandishing the goad held loosely in his own hand, observing all the worlds or all beings, and illuminating them in the form of the Sun, goes, that is, moves in the sky.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अजाश्वः (*ajāśvaḥ*)—he who has a horse of goat form
- पशुपातिः (*paśupātiḥ*)—the herdsman of animals **NOTE**
- वाजपस्यः (*vājapasyaḥ*)—he whose house is full of abundance of food
- धियंजिन्वः (*dhiyaṃjinvaḥ*)—he who satisfies the worshippers
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—in the whole
- भुवने (*bhuvane*)—world
- अर्पितः (*arpitaḥ*)—he who is placed as nourisher
- पूषा देवः (*pūṣā devaḥ*)—the god Pūṣan
- शिथिरां (*śithirāṃ*)—held loosely
- अष्टां (*aṣṭāṃ*)—the thunderbolt (goad) **NOTE**
- उद्वरीवृजत् (*udvarīvṛjat*)—brandishing all around
- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—all the worlds
- संचक्षणः (*saṃcakṣaṇaḥ*)—observing
- ईयते (*īyate*)—he moves

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Pūṣan, who has a horse of goat form, the herdsman of animals, whose house is full of abundance of food, who satisfies the worshippers, and who is placed as the nourisher in all the worlds, moves about brandishing the loosely held thunderbolt and observing all the worlds.

##### English translation
The rider of the goat, the protector of animals, in whose dwelling food is abundant, the propitiated by sacred rites, who has been placed over the whole (world) the divine Pushan, brandishing his loosened goad, proceeds (in the sky), contemplating all beings.

> पश्वादिविषयेण स्तोतृभिः कृतो वशीकृतोऽसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For the vapā and the puroḍāśa of the animal belonging to Pūṣan, the two ṛks beginning यास्ते पूषन् (*yāste pūṣan*) are anuvākyā verses. This is laid down in the Sūtra (Ā. 3-7). O Pūṣan, those golden, beneficial and delightful ships of yours that move within the ocean, in the sky: with those ships you go on the errand of Sūrya as his messenger. Once, when Sūrya had set out with the gods to slay the Asuras, his wife became anxious about her husband. Sūrya sent Pūṣan to her, and therefore Pūṣan is praised here. Moreover, you desire the food that is the oblation, śravas, and you have been brought under control by the worshippers through their desire, directed to cattle and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O god Pūṣan
- ते (*te*)—your
- हिरण्ययाः (*hiraṇyayāḥ*)—made of gold
- याः नावः (*yāḥ nāvaḥ*)—which vessels
- समुद्रे (*samudre*)—of the ocean
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle
- अंतरिक्षे (*aṃtarikṣe*)—in the sky
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—move
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with those vessels
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of Sūrya
- दूत्यां (*dūtyāṃ*)—the duty
- यासि (*yāsi*)—you carry out
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—the food in the form of the oblation
- इच्छमानः (*icchamānaḥ*)—desiring
- कामेन (*kāmena*)—by the oblation offered willingly
- कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)—you are brought under control

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, with those vessels made of gold that move in the sky, which is as the middle of the ocean, you carry out the duty of Sūrya. Desiring the food in the form of the oblation, you are brought under control by the oblation offered willingly.

##### English translation
With those your golden vessels, which navigate within the ocean-firmament, you discharge the office of messenger of the sun: desirous of the sacrificial food, you are propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.

### Printed p. 378

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the vapā and puroḍāśa offerings are made in the animal sacrifice performed for the deity Pūṣan, the two ṛks beginning यास्ते पूषन् (*yāste pūṣan*) (this ṛk and the next) are to be recited as anuvākyā mantras. This is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: यास्ते पूषन्नावो अंतः समुद्र इति द्वे पूषेमा आशा अनु वेद सर्वाः (*yāste pūṣannāvo aṃtaḥ samudra iti dve pūṣemā āśā anu veda sarvāḥ*) (Ā. 2-7). **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पू॒षा सु॒बंधु॑र्दि॒व आ पृ॑थि॒व्या इ॒ळस्पति॑र्म॒घवा॑ द॒स्मव॑र्चाः ।  
> यं दे॒वासो॒ अद॑दुः सू॒र्याय्यै॒ कामे॑न कृ॒तं त॒वसं॒  ॑
> स्वंचं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूषा । सुबंधुः । दिवः । आ । पृथिव्याः । इळः । पतिः । मघवा । दस्मवर्चाः ।  
> यं । देवासः । अददुः । सूर्यायै । कामेन । कृतं । तवसं । सुअंचं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूषा पोषको देवो दिव आ द्युलोकस्य च पृथिव्याश्च सुबंधुः शोभनो
> बंधुर्भवति । तथेळस्पतिरिळाया अन्नस्य पतिर्मघवा । मघमिति धननाम । तद्वान् ।
> यद्वा । महतेर्दानकर्मणो भावसाधनो मघशब्दः । दानवान् दस्मवर्चाः ।
> वर्च इति रूपनाम । दस्मं दर्शनीयं वर्चो यस्य तादृशः । यं पूषणं देवास ।
> सर्वे देवाः सूर्यय्य सूर्यस्य पत्नि यद्वा सावित्र्यै सूर्याख्यया
> आश्विनोर्वरणायाददुः दत्तवंतः । पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा । ऋग्वे. १०-८५-१४ ।
> इति हि श्रूयते । कीदृशं पूषणं। कामेन पश्वादिविषयेण कृतं स्तोतृभिर्वशीकृतं
> तवसं बलवंतं प्रवृद्धं वा स्वंचं स्वंचनं सुष्टु गच्छंतं । एवंविधं यं पूषणमददुः स पूषा सुबंधुरित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pūṣan, the nourishing god, is a good kinsman of heaven and of earth. Likewise he is the lord of iḷā, food, and maghavā: magha is a name for wealth, and he possesses it; or else the word magha comes from the root mahate, which is in the sense of giving, and the word is formed with the sense of the act itself: he is a giver. He is dasmavarcāḥ: varcas is a name for form, and dasma means to be looked at; he is one whose form is pleasing to look at. Him, Pūṣan, all the gods gave to Sūryā, who is Sūrya's wife, or else to Sāvitrī under the name Sūryā, for the choosing of the Aśvins. **NOTE** It is heard: पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा (*putraḥ pitarāvavṛṇīta pūṣā*) (Ṛgve. 10-85-14). **NOTE** What kind of Pūṣan? One brought under control by the worshippers through desire directed to cattle and the like; strong, or grown great; svañc, that is, moving well. The construction is: the Pūṣan whom they gave, such a Pūṣan is the good kinsman.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—brought under control
- तवसं (*tavasaṃ*)—possessed of strength
- स्वंचं (*svaṃcaṃ*)—possessed of excellent movement
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom, the god Pūṣan
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—all the gods
- सूर्यायै (*sūryāyai*)—to the goddess Sūryā
- अददुः (*adaduḥ*)—offered, such a one
- इळस्पतिः (*iḷaspatiḥ*)—the lord of food
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—possessed of wealth
- दस्यवर्चाः (*dasyavarcāḥ*)—possessed of attractive lustre
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- दिवि आ (*divi ā*)—to the whole heaven
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—to the earth
- सुबंधुः (*subaṃdhuḥ*)—a good kinsman **NOTE**

### Printed p. 379

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Him who has been carried by oblations and the like to the control of the sacrificer **NOTE**, who is full of strength and of excellent movement, the god Pūṣan whom all the gods offered to the daughter of Sūrya: such a Pūṣan, the lord of food, the wealthy one, of attractive lustre, is a good kinsman to the whole heaven and to the earth.

##### English translation
Pushan is the kind kinsman of heaven and earth, the lord of food, the possessor of opulence, of goodly from; whom the gods gave to Surya, vigorous, well-moving, propitiated by (that which is) willingly offered.

## Sūkta 59 (Maṇḍala 6)

The sūkta of ten ṛks: प्र नु वोचेति दशर्चं दशमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षमिंद्राग्निदेवताकं (*pra nu voceti daśarcaṃ daśamaṃ sūktaṃ bharadvājasyārṣamiṃdrāgnidevatākaṃ*). सप्तमाद्याश्चतस्रोऽनुष्टुभः शिष्टाः षट् बृहत्यः (*saptamādyāścatasro 'nuṣṭubhaḥ śiṣṭāḥ ṣaṭ bṛhatyaḥ*). तथा जानुक्रांतं (*tathā jānukrāṃtaṃ*). प्र नु दशैंद्राग्नं तु बार्हतं चतुरनुष्टुबंतमिति (*pra nu daśaiṃdrāgnaṃ tu bārhataṃ caturanuṣṭubaṃtamiti*). गतो विनियोगः (*gato viniyogaḥ*).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning प्र नु वोबा (*pra nu vobā*) **NOTE** is the tenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. There are ten ṛks in it. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; the deities are Indra and Agni. From the seventh ṛk of this sūkta, the following four ṛks are in the Anuṣṭup metre; the remaining six ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: प्र नु दशैंद्राग्नंतु बार्हतं चतुरनुष्टुबंतं (*pra nu daśaiṃdrāgnaṃtu bārhataṃ caturanuṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). The application has been stated before.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 59
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 8; Vargas 25, 26
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 10
- Printed "Yajus": भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*) **NOTE**
- Deity: Indrāgnī
- Metre: 1-6 Bṛhatī; 7-10 Anuṣṭup
