#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र नु वो॑चा सु॒तेषु॑ नां वी॒र्या॒३॒॑ ३ यानि॑ च॒क्रथुः॑ ।  
> ह॒तासो॑ नां पि॒तरो॑ दे॒वश॑त्रव॒ इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ जीव॑थो यु॒वं॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । नु । वोच । सुतेषु । वां । वीर्या । यानि । चक्रथुः ।  
> हतासः । वां । पितरः । देवशत्रवः । इंद्राग्नी इति । जीवथः । युवं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी यानि वीर्या वीर्याणि वीरकर्माणि चक्रथुः कृतवंत् युवां
> सुतेश्वभिषुतेषु सोमेष्मस्मद्यज्ञे नां युवयोस्तानि वीर्याणि नु क्षिप्रं प्र
> वोच । प्रवोचं । प्रब्रवीमि । तदेव वीर्यं दर्शयति । हे इंद्राग्नी देवशत्रवः ।
> देवाः शत्रवः शातयितारो येषां तादृशाः । असुराः पितरो हिंसकाः ॥ पीयतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । तस्यैतद्रूपं ॥ ईदृशा असुरा नां युवाभ्यां हतासो हता आसन् ।
> युवं युवां तु जीवथः । जीवनवंतौ भवथः । असुरैर्न बाधिताविति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the heroic deeds that you two have done, those deeds of yours I quickly proclaim at the Soma pressings, in our sacrifice. He shows that very heroism. O Indra and Agni, the Asuras, whose destroyers, enemies, are the gods, and who are pitaraḥ, injurers (the root pī has the sense of injuring, and this is its form): such Asuras were slain by you two. But you two live: you are living, that is, not harassed by the Asuras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- यानि (*yāni*)—which famous
- वीर्या (*vīryā*)—heroic deeds
- चक्रथुः (*cakrathuḥ*)—you have done
- वां (*vāṃ*)—all those heroic deeds of yours
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—when the Soma juice is pressed
- प्रवोच (*pravoca*)—I recite, O Indra and Agni
- देवशत्रवः (*devaśatravaḥ*)—who are as enemies to all the gods
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—and injurers, the Asuras
- वां (*vāṃ*)—by you two
- हतासः (*hatāsaḥ*)—have been slain; (but)
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- जीवथः (*jīvathaḥ*)—have lived unharmed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, all the famous heroic deeds that you have done, I quickly recite as soon as the Soma juice is pressed. O Indra and Agni, the Asuras, who are as enemies and injurers to all the gods, have been slain by you two. But you two alone have lived unharmed.

### Printed p. 381

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 2

> बळि॒त्था म॑हि॒मा वा॒मिंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ पनि॑ष्ठ॒ आ ।  
> स॒मा॒नो वां॑ जनि॒ता भ्रात॑रा यु॒वं य॒मावि॒हेह॑मातरा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समानः । वां । जनिता । भ्रातरा । युवं । यमौ । इहेहमातरा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी वां युवयोर्महिमा महत्त्वमित्थेत्थमनेन प्रकारेण बट्
> सत्यं । युष्मद्विषयं यज्जन्ममहत्त्वं प्रतिपाद्यते तत्सर्वं यथार्थमित्यर्थः ।
> पनिष्ठ आ पनिष्ठः स्तुत्यतमश्च प्रजापतिः समान एक एव वां युवयोर्जनिता
> जनयिता । अतो युवं युवां भ्रातरा भ्रातरौ स्थः । अपि च यमौ यमलौ
> सहोत्पन्नाविहेहमातरा ! इह चेह च सर्वत्र माता ययोस्तादृशौ स्थः । अदितिर्ह्यनयोर्माता सैव विस्तीर्णा भूमिरितीहेहमातराविति श्रूयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, your greatness is thus; बट् (*baṭ*) means truth. Whatever is declared concerning your birth and greatness is all as it truly is. Panishtha, the most praiseworthy Prajāpati, is one and the same begetter of you both. Therefore you two are brothers. Moreover you are twins, born together, and इहेहमातरा (*ihehamātarā*): you are such that your mother is here and here, that is, everywhere. For Aditi is the mother of these two, and she is the wide earth; thus it is heard, in the word इहेहमातरा (*ihehamātarā*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- महिमा (*mahimā*)—greatness
- इत्था (*itthā*)—is of this kind
- बट् (*baṭ*)—this is indeed true
- पनिष्ठः (*paniṣṭhaḥ*)—the most venerable Prajāpati
- वां (*vāṃ*)—to both of you
- समानः (*samānaḥ*)—the one only
- जनिता (*janitā*)—is the father
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- भ्रातरौ (*bhrātarau*)—are brothers
- यम् (*yam*)—you two, born together
- इहेहमातरा (*ihehamātarā*)—are possessed of mothers who stand everywhere (the earth)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, it is indeed true that your greatness is of this kind. The most venerable Prajāpati is the one and only father of you both. You two are brothers.

### Printed p. 382

You two, born together, are possessed of mothers who stand everywhere. Aditi, the mother of the gods, who pervades everywhere, is your mother.

##### English translation
Your greatness, Indra and Agni, is after this fashion, and is most deserving of praise: the same is your progenitor: twin brothers are you, having a mother everywhere present.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यमौ इहेहमातरा (*yamau ihehamātarā*)—here यमौ (*yamau*) means twins, children born together. Indra and Agni are described here as twins, because Prajāpati himself is the father of Indra and Agni and Aditi, the mother of the gods, is their mother. Therefore Indra and Agni are brothers to each other, and since they were born together at one time, they are twins. Since Aditi is also said to be this wide earth, one may say that the earth is their mother. Yāska, for the subject of twins, has cited as an example the very sentence of this ṛk, यमाविहेहमातरा (*yamāvihehamātarā*) (Ni. 10-21).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ओ॒कि॒वांसा॑ सु॒ते सचा॒ अश्वा॒ सप्ति॑ इ॒वाद॑ने ।  
> इंद्रा॒ न्व१॒ं॑ग्नी अव॑से॒ह व॒ज्रणा॑ व॒यं दे॒वा ह॑वामहे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ओकिवांसा । सुते । सचा । अश्वा । सप्ति इवेति सप्ति इव । आदने ।  
> इंद्रा । नु । अग्नी इति । आवसा । इद । वज्रिणा । वयं । देवा । हवामहे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी सुतेऽभिषुते सोमे युवां सचा सहौकिवांसौकिवांसौ
> समवेत् संगतौ भवतं ॥ उच समवाय इत्यस्यैतद्रूपं । तत्र दृष्टांतः । आदने
> भक्षणीये घासे सप्ति इवाश्वा सर्पणशीलावश्वानिव । नु अद्य वयं तादृशाविंद्राग्नी
> इहास्मिन्यज्ञेवसा रक्षणेन हेतुना हवामहे । आह्वयामहे ॥ इतरेतरयोगादिद्रशब्देऽग्निशब्दे च द्विवचनं ॥ कीदृशाविंद्राग्नी । वज्रिणा वज्रिणावायुधोपेत्
> देवा दानादिगुणयुक्ता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, when the Soma is pressed, you two together come together, are united. An illustration is given: as two swift-moving horses come together at their food, their fodder. Now, today, we here in this sacrifice call such Indra and Agni, for the purpose of protection. What are Indra and Agni like? They are armed with the thunderbolt, as weapon, and they are gods endowed with qualities such as generosity.

### Printed p. 383

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सप्ति (*sapti*)—(O Indra and Agni,) of swift-moving
- अश्वा (*aśvā*)—horses
- आदने (*ādane*)—as they gather together for eating
- सुते (*sute*)—at the time when the Soma juice is pressed
- सचा (*sacā*)—you two come together
- ओकिवांसा (*okivāṃsā*)—and become possessed of one place
- नु (*nu*)—now
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- अवसा (*avasā*)—for protection
- वज्रिणा (*vajriṇā*)—holders of the thunderbolt weapon
- देवा (*devā*)—and of divine nature
- इंद्राग्नि (*iṃdrāgni*)—Indra and Agni
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, as swift-moving horses gather together to eat grass, so at this time when the Soma juice is pressed you two come together and become possessed of one place. Now, in this sacrifice, for our protection, we call with prayer Indra and Agni, the holders of the thunderbolt weapon, who are of divine nature.

##### English translation
You approach together, when the libation is effused, like two fleet coursers to their forage: we invoke to-day Indra and Agni, deities armed with the thunderbolt, to this ceremony for our preservation.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य इं॑द्राग्नी सु॒तेषु॑ वां॒ स्तव॒त्तेष्कृ॑तावृधा ।  
> जो॒ष॒वा॒कं वद॑तः पज्रहोषिणा॒ न दे॑वा भ॒सथ॑श्च॒न ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । इंद्राग्नी इति । सुतेषु । वां । स्तवत् । तेषु । ऋतवृधा ।  
> जोषवाकं । वदतः । पज्रहोषिणा । न । देवा । भसथः । चन ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋतावृधा ऋतस्य सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य वा वर्धयिताराविंद्राग्नी सुतेष्वभिषुतेषु सोमेषु यः स्तोता नां युवां स्तुवत् कुत्सितं स्तूयात् तेषु
> सोमेषु मध्यॆ जोषवाकं वदतो जोषं जोषयितव्यं प्रीतिहेतुत्वेन कर्तव्यं
> स्वयमप्रीतिकरं तादृशं वाकं वाक्यं वदतस्तस्य स्तोतुः सोमं हे पज्रहोषिणा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, augmenters of ṛta, that is, of truth or of the sacrifice: the worshipper who, when the Soma is pressed, praises you ill, in those Soma offerings speaks a जोषवाकं (*joṣavākaṃ*), a speech that is to be made pleasing, that ought to be done as a cause of pleasure, but is itself not pleasing: of that worshipper, of his Soma, O you of famous praise-sound…

### Printed p. 384

> पज्रः प्रार्जितः प्रसिद्धो होषो घोषः स्तोत्रं ययोस्तादृशौ हे देवा देवौ
> युवां न भसथः । न भक्षयथः । चनेति पादपूरणः ॥ अत्र निरुक्तं । जोषवाकमित्यविज्ञातनामधेयं जोषयितव्यं भवति । य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां सोमेषु
> स्तौति तेष्टृतस्य वर्धयितारौ न तस्याश्नीथः । योऽयं जोषवाकं वदति विजंजपः
> प्रार्जितहोषिणौ देवौ न तस्याश्नीथः । नि. ५-२२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…that is, those whose pajra, famous, hoṣa, sound of praise, is such; O gods, you two do not eat, you do not consume his Soma. The word चन (*cana*) is a filler of the line. Here he cites the Nirukta: जोषवाकमित्यविज्ञातनामधेयं जोषयितव्यं भवति । य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां सोमेषु स्तौति तेष्टृतस्य वर्धयितारौ न तस्याश्नीथः । योऽयं जोषवाकं वदति विजंजपः प्रार्जितहोषिणौ देवौ न तस्याश्नीथः । (*joṣavākamityavijñātanāmadheyaṃ joṣayitavyaṃ bhavati | ya iṃdrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ someṣu stauti teṣṭṛtasya vardhayitārau na tasyāśnīthaḥ | yo 'yaṃ joṣavākaṃ vadati vijaṃjapaḥ prārjitahoṣiṇau devau na tasyāśnīthaḥ |*) (Ni. 5-22). **GLOSS**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यतावृधा (*yatāvṛdhā*)—O augmenters of the sacrifice **NOTE**
- पज्रहोषिणा (*pajrahoṣiṇā*)—possessed of famous sound of praise
- देवा (*devā*)—of divine nature
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—at the time when the Soma juice is pressed
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever worshipper
- वां (*vāṃ*)—addressing both of you
- स्तवत् (*stavat*)—praises ill
- तेषु (*teṣu*)—among the worshippers
- जोषवाकं (*joṣavākaṃ*)—a sentence of praise that does not give satisfaction
- वदतः (*vadataḥ*)—among those who recite
- न भसथः (*na bhasathaḥ*)—you do not eat the oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, augmenters of the sacrifice, possessed of famous sound of praise, of divine nature: at the time when the Soma juice is pressed, among those worshippers who praise you both ill, and among those who praise with a sentence of praise that does not give satisfaction, you do not eat the oblation.

##### English translation
Divine Indra and Agni, augmenters of sacrifice, by whom the acclamation (of praise) is received, you partake not of the (Soma) of him who, when the libation is effused, praises you (improperly), uttering unacceptable eulogies.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अप्रीतिकरं वाक्यं (*aprītikaraṃ vākyaṃ*): a sentence without love. To explain the meaning of this word जोषवाकं (*joṣavākaṃ*), Yāska has given an etymological explanation on this ṛk: जोषवाकमित्यविज्ञा तनामधेयं जीषयितव्यं भवति । य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां स्तवत्तेष्टृतावृधा । जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ॥ य इंद्राग्नी सुतेषु वां सोमेषु स्तौति तस्याश्नीथोऽथ योऽयं जोषवाकं वदति विजञ्चपः प्रार्जितहोषिणौ न देवौ तस्माश्नीथः ॥ (*joṣavākamityavijñā tanāmadheyaṃ jīṣayitavyaṃ bhavati | ya iṃdrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ stavatteṣṭṛtāvṛdhā | joṣavākaṃ vadataḥ pajrahoṣiṇā na devā bhasathaścana ‖ ya iṃdrāgnī suteṣu vāṃ someṣu stauti tasyāśnītho 'tha yo 'yaṃ joṣavākaṃ vadati vijañcapaḥ prārjitahoṣiṇau na devau tasmāśnīthaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 5-22). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 385

O Indra and Agni, as soon as the Soma juice is pressed, whichever worshipper praises you both, you accept and eat the oblation, or the Soma, that he offers. But the worshipper who, while praising, recites what is not known to himself or what is not pleasing, and so praises: what he offers you do not accept and eat. This is the chief purport of the explanation.

There is a slight difference between Sāyaṇa's explanation and Yāska's with regard to the first half of this ṛk. Sāyaṇa has taken the meaning to be that they do not eat the oblation of the man who praises Indra and Agni ill, that is, with blame, with fault, in the form of contempt. But Yāska has explained that they eat the oblation of the worshipper who praises after the pressing of the Soma, but that if there is blame in that praise, or sentences without love, they do not eat his oblation. Here there is room for both kinds of meaning.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ को अ॒स्य वां॒ देवौ॒ मर्त॑श्चिकेतति ।  
> विषू॑चो॒ अश्वा॑न्युजा॒न ई॑यत॒ एकः॑ समा॒न आ रथे॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । कः । अस्य । वां । देवौ । मर्शः । चिकेतति ।  
> विषूचः । अश्वान् । युयुजानः । ईयते । एकः । समाने । आ । रथे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवौ द्योतमानाविंद्राग्नी वां युवयोरस्येदं कर्म को मर्तो
> मनुष्यश्चिकेतति । जानीयात् । न कोऽपित्यर्थः । किं तत्कर्म । विषूचो नानांचतो
> गच्छतोऽश्वान् समान उभयार्थ एकस्मिन्प्रथे युवयोरेक इंद्रः सूर्यात्मना
> वर्तमानो युयुजानस्तादृशानश्वान्योजयन् एयते । सर्वं जगदभिगच्छति ।
> यद्वा । विषूचो नानारूपानश्वान् व्यापकान् समान एकरूपे रथे संवत्सरात्मके
> युयुजानो योजयॆन् युवयोरेकः सूर्यात्मेंद्र एयते । आगच्छति ।
> एतद्युवयोः कर्म को यथावज्ञानीयादित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining gods Indra and Agni, which mortal, which man, would know this deed of you two? That is, none would. What is that deed? One of you two, Indra, who exists in the form of Sūrya, yoking horses that go in diverse directions, in a single common path that serves both, goes, that is, approaches the whole world. Or else: yoking horses of diverse forms, pervasive, in a common car of one form, which is in the form of the year, one of you two, Indra in the form of Sūrya, comes, approaches. Who could truly know this deed of yours is the sense.

### Printed p. 386

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवौ (*devau*)—shining
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—one of you two, Indra
- समाने रथे (*samāne rathe*)—seated in the one car common to both of you
- विषूचः (*viṣūcaḥ*)—going everywhere
- आश्वान् (*āśvān*)—horses
- युयुजानः (*yuyujānaḥ*)—having yoked to the car
- आ ईयते (*ā īyate*)—while he travels in the form of Sūrya
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- अस्य (*asya*)—this deed in the form of travelling
- कः मर्तः (*kaḥ martaḥ*)—what man indeed
- चिकेतति (*ciketati*)—can know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Indra and Agni, when one of you two, Indra, seated in the one car common to both of you, having yoked to the car horses that go everywhere, travels in the form of Sūrya, what man indeed can know this deed of yours, in the form of travelling, and its aim?

##### English translation
What mortal, divine Indra and Agni, is a judge of that (your act), when one of you, harnessing his diversely-going horses, proceeds in the common car.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी अ॒पादि॒यं पूर्वागा॑त्प॒द्वती॑भ्यः ।  
> हि॒त्वी शिरो॑ जि॒ह्वया॒ वाव॑द॒च्चर॑त्रिं॒शत्प॒दा न्य॑क्रमीत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । अपात् । इयं । पूर्वा । आ । अगात् । पर्तवतीभ्यः ।  
> हित्वी । शिरः । जिह्वया । वावदत् । चरत् । त्रिंशत् । पदा । नि । अक्रमात् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी अपात्पादरहितेयमुषाः पद्वतीभ्यः पादयुक्ताभ्यः सुप्ताभ्यः
> प्रज्याभ्यः पूर्वा प्रथमभाविनी सत्यागात् । आगच्छति । तथा प्राणिनां शिरो हित्वी प्रेरयित्रि । यद्वा । शिरो हित्वात्यक्त्वा स्वयमशिरस्का सती । जिह्वया प्राणिस्थया तदी-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, this Uṣas, who is footless, comes first, before the footed creatures that are asleep; so, having come first, she sets in motion the heads of living beings. Or else: having given up her head, herself headless, with the tongue that is situated in living beings, her own…

### Printed p. 387

> येन वागिंद्रियेण नावदत् भृशं शब्दं कुर्वती चरत् । एवं चरंत्युषास्त्रिंशत्पदान्यवयवभूतान् त्रिंशन्नुहूर्तान्न्यक्रमीत् । एकेन दिवसेनातिक्रामति । एतच्च
> युवयोः कर्म । तत्की जानीयादिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…by which organ of speech she moves, making a loud sound, not speaking. Thus moving, Uṣas traverses thirty steps, that is, the thirty muhūrtas that are her parts; she passes over them in one day. And this is the deed of you two: who could know it? This is the connection with the preceding verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- आपात् (*āpāt*)—she who is without feet
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this goddess Uṣas
- पद्वतीभ्यः (*padvatībhyaḥ*)—than the creatures that have feet
- पूर्वा (*pūrvā*)—as the one who comes first
- आगात् (*āgāt*)—appears and comes
- शिरः (*śiraḥ*)—her head
- हित्वी (*hitvī*)—having hidden
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—through the speech-organs of living beings
- नावदत् (*nāvadat*)—causing sound to be made
- चरत् (*carat*)—moving
- त्रिंशत् पदा (*triṃśat padā*)—as far as thirty steps (as long as thirty muhūrtas)
- न्यक्रमित् (*nyakramit*)—she becomes visible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, this goddess Uṣas, who is without feet, appears and comes even before the creatures that have feet. Hiding her head, moving and causing sound to be made through the speech-organs of living beings, she becomes visible for thirty muhūrtas. All this is the power of Indra and Agni. What man can know it?

##### English translation
This footless (dawn), Indra and Agni, comes before the footed sleepers, animating the head (of living beings with consciousness), causing them to utter loud sounds with their tongues, and passing onwards she traverses thirty steps.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ आ हि त॑न्व॒ते नरो॒ धन्वा॑नि बा॒ह्वोः ।  
> मा नो॑ अ॒स्मिन्म॑हाध॒ने परा॑ वर्क्तं॒ गवि॑ष्टिषु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । आ । हि । तन्वते । नरः । धन्वानि । बाह्वोः ।  
> मा । नः । अस्मिन् । महाधने । परा । वर्क्तं । गोऽइष्टिषु ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 388

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी नरो योद्धारो मनुष्या बाह्वोऽर्हस्तयोर्धन्वानि
> धनूंष्या तन्वते हि । आततज्यानि कुर्वते हि । युवां चास्मिन्महाधने जेशव्येन
> महाधनेनोपेते संगा मे गविष्टिषु गवामन्वेषणेषु नोऽस्मान् मा परा
> वर्क्तं । मा परित्यजतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the warriors, the men, stretch the bows in their arms, that is, they make them strung. And you two, in this great-wealth combat, one that is endowed with great wealth to be won, in the seekings of cows, do not abandon us. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—men engaged in battle
- बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)—with their arms
- धन्वानि (*dhanvāni*)—the bows
- आ तन्वते हि (*ā tanvate hi*)—have stretched and hold, have they not
- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—(you two)
- आस्मिन् महाधने (*āsmin mahādhane*)—in this battle fought for abundant wealth
- गविष्टिषु (*gaviṣṭiṣu*)—while we are engaged in the effort to seek cows
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा परा वर्क्तं (*mā parā varktaṃ*)—do not abandon, and do not let us fall into the power of enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, men engaged in battle have stretched and hold their bows with their arms, have they not! In this battle fought for the gain of abundant wealth, while we are engaged in the effort to seek cows, do not abandon us and do not let us fall into the power of enemies.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, men verily stretch their bows with their arms, but do not desert us contending for cattle in the great combat.

### Printed p. 389

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी आघा आहंत्रोऽर्योऽभिगंत्रोऽरातयः शत्रुसेना मा
> तपंति । मां बाधंते । ता अपा कृतं । अपाकुरुतं । तथा द्वेषांसि द्वेष्टन्शत्रुन् सूर्यादधि । अधिः पंचम्यर्थानुवादकः । सूर्यदर्शनाद्युयुतं ।
> पृथक्कुरुतं च । यथा ते सूर्यं न पश्यंति तथा कुरुतं । मारयतमित्यर्थः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the murderous ones, the attackers, the enemy armies, harass me. Drive them away. Likewise the haters, the enemies who hate us, separate from the sight of the sun. Separate them, and do so that they do not see the sun; the sense is, kill them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- आघाः (*āghāḥ*)—sinful
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—and attacking
- अरातयः (*arātayaḥ*)—enemies
- मा (*mā*)—me
- तपंति (*tapaṃti*)—harass **NOTE**
- अप आ कृतं (*apa ā kṛtaṃ*)—drive them far away
- द्वेषांसि (*dveṣāṃsi*)—the enemies who hate us
- सूर्यादधि (*sūryādadhi*)—from the sight of the sun
- युयुतं (*yuyutaṃ*)—separate them (make it so that they have neither sight of the sun nor the light of the sun)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, the enemies, who are sinful and fall upon us, harass me. Drive them far away. Separate the enemies who hate us from the sight of the sun, that is, make it so that they have no light of the sun.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, murderous, aggressive enemies harass us: drive away my adversaries: separate them from (sight of) the sun.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी यु॒वोरपि॒ वसु॑ दि॒व्यानि॒ पार्थि॑वा ।  
> आ न॑ इ॒ह प्र य॑च्छतं र॒यिं वि॒श्वायु॑पोषसं ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । युवोः । अपि । वसु । दिव्यानि । पार्थिवा ।  
> आ । नः । इह । प्र । यच्छतं । रयिं । विश्वायुपोषसं ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 390

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी युवोर्युववयोर्दिव्यानि दिवि भवानि पार्थिवा पृथिव्यां
> भवानि लोकद्वयसंबंधीनि वसु वसून्यपि हितानि युवयोरेव वर्तंते । अतः
> कारणादिहास्मिन्यज्ञे नोऽस्मभ्यं रयिं धनमा अभि प्र यच्छतं । कीदृशं रयिं ।
> विश्वायुपोषसं । आयव इति मनुष्यनाम । सर्वेषां मनुष्याणां पोषणाय
> पर्याप्तं । यद्वा । सर्वस्यायुषः पोषणे शक्तं ॥ छांदसो वर्णलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the treasures that are in heaven and those on earth, belonging to the two worlds, all of them are truly yours alone. For that reason, here in this sacrifice, bestow wealth upon us. What kind of wealth? विश्वायुपोषसं (*viśvāyupoṣasaṃ*): आयव (*āyava*) is a name for men; wealth that is sufficient for the nourishment of all men. Or else: able to nourish the whole life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- दिव्यानि (*divyāni*)—that which is in the world of heaven
- पार्थिवा (*pārthivā*)—and that which is on earth
- वसु अपि (*vasu api*)—all the riches as well
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—belong to you two alone
- इह (*iha*)—at the time of this sacrifice
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- विश्वायुपोषसं (*viśvāyupoṣasaṃ*)—nourishing all men
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- आ प्र यच्छतं (*ā pra yacchataṃ*)—provide and give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, all the riches that are in the world of heaven and those that are on earth belong to you two alone. At the time of this sacrifice, provide for us wealth that nourishes all men.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, yours are both celestial and terrestrial treasures: bestow upon us, on this occasion, life-sustaining riches.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी उक्तवाहसा॒ स्तोमे॑भिर्हवनश्रुता ।  
> विश्वा॑भिर्गी॒र्भिरा ग॑तम॒स्य सोम॑स्य पी॒तये॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । उक्तवाहसा । स्तोमेभिः । हवनश्रुता ।  
> विश्वाभिः । गीःभिः । अ । गतं । अस्य । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 391

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उक्तवाहसोक्षैः स्तुतिभिर्वहनीयौ हे हवनश्रुता हवनस्याह्वानस्य
> शोतारौ एवंभूत्था हे इंद्राग्नी स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैर्विश्वाभिः सर्वाभिर्गिर्भिः
> शस्त्ररूपाभिर्वाग्भिश्च हेतुभूताभिरा गतं आगच्छृतं । किमर्थं । अस्यास्मदीयस्य
> सोमस्य पीतये पानार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O you who are borne by loud praises, O you who hear the invocation, the call: O Indra and Agni, such as you are, come with the praises, with all the speeches in the form of śastras, which are the means. For what purpose? For the drinking of this Soma of ours.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उक्तवाहसा (*uktavāhasā*)—you who are borne by the recited mantras
- हवनश्रुता (*havanaśrutā*)—and who hear our praises
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—by praises in the form of stomas
- विश्वाभिः (*viśvābhiḥ*)—by all
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—speeches in the form of śastras (being drawn)
- अस्य (*asya*)—offered in this sacrifice
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of the Soma juice
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for drinking
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—be pleased to come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, who are borne by the recited mantras and who hear our praises, drawn by the praises in the form of stomas and by all the speeches in the form of śastras, be pleased to come to drink the Soma offered in this sacrifice.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, who are to be attracted by hymns; you, who hear our invocation (accompanied) by praises and by all adorations, come hither to drink of this Soma libation.

## Sūkta 60 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्नथद्वृत्रमिति पंचदशर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षमैंद्राग्नं । आदौ
> तिस्रस्त्रिष्टुभश्चतुर्थाद्या नव गायत्र्यस्त्रयोदशी त्रिष्टुप् चतुर्दशी बृहती
> पंचदश्यनुष्टुप् । तथा चानुक्रांतं । श्नथक्पंचोना गायत्रं तु त्रित्रिष्टुबादि
> त्रिष्टुब्बृहत्यनुष्टुबंतमिति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ वरुणप्रघासेष्टैंद्राग्नस्य
> हविषः श्नथदित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च । इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं श्नथद्वृत्रमुत
> सनोति वाजं । आ. २-१७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning श्नथद्वृत्रमिति (*śnathadvṛtramiti*) has fifteen ṛks and is the eleventh sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja; its deity is Indra and Agni. The first three ṛks are in Triṣṭubh, the nine from the fourth are in Gāyatrī, the thirteenth is Triṣṭubh, the fourteenth Bṛhatī, the fifteenth Anuṣṭubh. So it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: श्नथक्पंचोना गायत्रं तु त्रित्रिष्टुबादि त्रिष्टुब्बृहत्यनुष्टुबंतमिति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ वरुणप्रघासेष्टैंद्राग्नस्य हविषः श्नथदित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च । इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं श्नथद्वृत्रमुत सनोति वाजं । आ. २-१७ । इति ॥ अनुवादवु—श्नथद्वत्रं ऎंब ई सूक्तवु ऐदनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हन्नॊंदनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि हदिनैदु ऋक्कुगळिरुवुवु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ भरद्वाजनु ऋषियु, इंद्राग्निगळु देवतॆयु. ई सूक्तद मॊदलिन मूरु ऋक्कुगळु त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्कवु ; नाल्कनॆय ऋक्किनिंद मुंदिन ऒंभत्तु ऋक्कुगळु गायत्री छंदस्कवु. हदिमूरनॆय ऋक्कु त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्कवु. हदिनाल्कनॆय ऋक्कु बृहती छंदस्कवु. हदिनैदनॆय ऋक्कु अनुष्टुप् छंदस्कवु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—श्नथत्पंचोना गायत्रं तु त्रित्रिष्टुबादि त्रिष्टुब्बृहत्यनुष्टुबंतं (*śnathakpaṃconā gāyatraṃ tu tritriṣṭubādi triṣṭubbṛhatyanuṣṭubaṃtamiti ‖ gataḥ sūktaviniyogaḥ ‖ varuṇapraghāseṣṭaiṃdrāgnasya haviṣaḥ śnathadityeṣā yājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ śnathadvṛtramuta sanoti vājaṃ | ā. 2-17 | iti ‖ anuvādavu—śnathadvatraṃ èṃba ī sūktavu aidanèya anuvākadalli hannòṃdanèya sūktavu. idaralli hadinaidu ṛkkugaḷiruvuvu. ī sūktakkè bharadvājanu ṛṣiyu, iṃdrāgnigaḷu devatèyu. ī sūktada mòdalina mūru ṛkkugaḷu triṣṭup chaṃdaskavu ; nālkanèya ṛkkiniṃda muṃdina òṃbhattu ṛkkugaḷu gāyatrī chaṃdaskavu. hadimūranèya ṛkku triṣṭup chaṃdaskavu. hadinālkanèya ṛkku bṛhatī chaṃdaskavu. hadinaidanèya ṛkku anuṣṭup chaṃdaskavu. anukramaṇikèyalli—śnathatpaṃconā gāyatraṃ tu tritriṣṭubādi triṣṭubbṛhatyanuṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). **GLOSS** The application of the sūkta has been given. In the Varuṇapraghāsa offering, for the oblation to Indra and Agni, the ṛk beginning श्नथत् (*śnathat*) is the yājyā. It is set out in the Sūtra: इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं श्नथद्वृत्रमुत सनोति वाजं (*iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ śnathadvṛtramuta sanoti vājaṃ*) (Ā. 2-17).

### Printed p. 392

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning श्नथद्वत्रं (*śnathadvatraṃ*) **NOTE** is the eleventh sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. There are fifteen ṛks in it. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; the deities are Indra and Agni. The first three ṛks of this sūkta are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the nine ṛks from the fourth onwards are in the Gāyatrī metre. The thirteenth ṛk is in Triṣṭubh, the fourteenth in Bṛhatī, the fifteenth in Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: श्नथत्पंचोना गायत्रं तु त्रित्रिष्टुबादि त्रिष्टुब्बृहत्यनुष्टुबंतं (*śnathatpaṃconā gāyatraṃ tu tritriṣṭubādi triṣṭubbṛhatyanuṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). The application of the sūkta has been stated before. In the iṣṭi called Varuṇapraghāsa, in the offering of the oblation made to the deities Indra and Agni, the first ṛk of this sūkta, beginning श्नथत् (*śnathat*), is to be recited as a yājyā mantra. This is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं श्नथद्वत्रमुत सनोति वाजं (*iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ śnathadvatramuta sanoti vājaṃ*) (Ā. 2-17).

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 60
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 8; Vargas 27, 28, 29
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15
- Ṛṣi: भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*)
- Deity: Indrāgnī
- Metre: 1-3, 13 Triṣṭup; 4-12 Gāyatrī; 14 Bṛhatī; 15 Anuṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्नथ॑द्वृ॒त्रमु॒त स॑नोति॒ वाज॒मिंद्रा॒ यो अ॒ग्नी सहु॑री  ॒
> सपर्यात् ।  
> इ॒र॒ज्यंता॑ वस॒व्य॑स्य॒ भूरेः॒ सह॑स्तमा॒ सह॑सा वाज॒यंता॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्नथत् । वृत्रं । उत । सनोति । वाजं । इंद्रा । यः । अग्नी इति । सहुरी इति ।  
> सपर्यात् ।  
> इरज्यंता । वसव्यस्य । भूरेः । सहःतमा । सहसा । वाजयंता ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 393

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स पुरुषो वृत्रमावरकं शत्रुं श्नथत् । हिनस्ति । उतापि च वाजमन्नं बलं
> वा सनोति । लभते । यः पुरुषः सहुरी शत्रूणामभिभविताराविंद्राग्नी सपर्यात्
> परिचरेत् ॥ इतरेतरयोगादुभयत्र पूर्ववद्वि वचनं ॥ कीदृशाविंद्राग्नी । भूरेः
> प्रभूतस्य वसव्यस्य वसुसमूहस्य । यद्वा !! स्वार्थिको यत् ॥ धनस्यॆरज्यंतेशानौ
> स्वामिनौ ॥ इरज्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा ॥ सहसा बलेन सहस्तमातिशयेनाभिभवितार्
> शत्रूणां वाजयंता वाजं दनिर्लक्षणमन्नमात्मन इच्छंत् । यद्वा । वाजं
> सोतृभ्यो दातव्यमन्नं कामयमानौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That man smites (श्नथत् (*śnathat*), he kills) the enemy Vṛtra, the obstructer, and also wins food or strength (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), who would serve Indra and Agni, the two overcomers of enemies. The dual is used in both places by the mutual connection of the two deities, as before. Of what kind are Indra and Agni? They are lords (इरज्यंता (*irajyaṃtā*)) of abundant wealth (वसव्यस्य (*vasavyasya*)), that is, of a multitude of treasures; or the word for wealth is formed with an added suffix, and the two are its masters, since इरज्यति (*irajyati*) is a verb of lordship. They overcome enemies most mightily (सहस्तमा (*sahastamā*)) by strength (सहसा (*sahasā*)). Desiring food (वाजयंता (*vājayaṃtā*)) for themselves **NOTE**; or else, desiring the food that is to be given to the worshippers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भोरेः (*bhoreḥ*)—abundant
- वसव्यस्य (*vasavyasya*)—of the mass of wealth
- इरज्यंता (*irajyaṃtā*)—who are the lords
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—with exceeding strength
- सहस्तमा (*sahastamā*)—who confront the enemies
- वाजयंता (*vājayaṃtā*)—who desire food in the form of oblation
- सहुरी (*sahurī*)—who crush and defeat the enemies
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—the deities who are Indra and Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which man
- सपर्यात् (*saparyāt*)—may worship (that man)
- वृतं (*vṛtaṃ*)—the enemy who has besieged him
- श्नथत् (*śnathat*)—strikes down and kills
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food also
- सनोति (*sanoti*)—obtains

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The man who worships the deities Indra and Agni, who are lords of the whole abundant mass of wealth, who confront enemies with exceeding strength, who desire food in the form of oblation, and who crush and defeat enemies, strikes down and kills the enemy who has besieged him. And he obtains food as well.

##### English translation
He overcomes his enemy, and acquires food, who worships the victorious Indra and Agni, the lords of infinite opulence, most powerful in strength, desirous of (sacrificial) food.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता यो॑धिष्टम॒भि गा इं॑द्र नू॒नम॒पः स्व॑रु॒षसो॑ अग्न  ॒
> ऊळ्हाः ।  
> दिशः॒ स्व॑रु॒षस॑ इंद्र चि॒त्रा अ॒पो गा अ॑ग्ने युवसे नि॒युत्वा॑न् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । योधिष्टं । अभि । गाः । इंद्र । नूनं । अपः । स्वः । उषसः । अग्ने । ऊळ्हाः ।  
> दिशः । स्वः । उषसः । इंद्र । चित्राः । अपः । गाः । अग्ने । युवसे । नियुत्वान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र हे अग्ने ता तौ युवां गा अप उदकानि स्वः सूर्यमुषस
> उषःकालानूळ्हाः पणिभिरपहृता एतान् गवादीनभिलक्ष्य योधिष्टं। शैरसुरैर्युद्धं
> कृतवंतौ । नूनमिति पादपूरणार्थः । हे इंद्र त्वं दिशः प्राच्याद्याः स्वः सूर्यमुषसश्च चित्राश्चायनीया अप उदकानि च गाश्च पणिभिरपहृतानेतान्युवसे । अनेन
> लोकेनायोजयः । यद्वा । असुरैरावृतान्दिगादीनसुरवधेनावरणमपनीय
> पृथक्कृतवानसीत्यर्थः । हे अग्ने नियुत्वान् नियुद्धिरश्वैर्युक्तः सन् त्वमप्येवमकार्षिरीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, O Agni, you two fought (योधिष्टं (*yodhiṣṭaṃ*)) with the Asuras, having in view the cows, the waters, the sun and the dawns, which had been carried off by the Paṇis; the word नूनं (*nūnaṃ*) serves only to fill out the pāda. O Indra, you unite (युवसे (*yuvase*)) the quarters, east and the rest, the sun, the dawns, the wonderful waters and the cows carried off by the Paṇis, with this world. Or else: having slain the Asuras who had enclosed the quarters and the rest, you removed the covering and set them apart; this is the sense. O Agni, possessed of the Niyut horses, you too did the same.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ता (*tā*)—you two
- ऊळ्हाः (*ūḷhāḥ*)—carried off by the Paṇis
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—for the cows
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—for the sake of the waters
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—for the sake of gaining the sun
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—with the aim of obtaining the dawn
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—certainly
- अभि योधिष्टं (*abhi yodhiṣṭaṃ*)—you fight with the enemies
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दितः (*ditaḥ*)—the quarters, east and the rest
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the sun
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the dawns
- चित्राः (*citrāḥ*)—attractive
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows carried off by the Paṇis
- युवसे (*yuvase*)—you set in their respective places
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*)—you, who have the horses named Niyut, have also accomplished the same deeds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, O Agni, you two have certainly fought with the enemies for the cows carried off by the Paṇis, for the waters, for the gaining of the sun, and with the aim of obtaining the dawn. O Indra, you set in their respective places the quarters, east and the rest, the sun, the dawns, the attractive waters and the cows carried off by the Paṇis. O Agni, you too, who have the horses named Niyut, have accomplished the same deeds.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, verily you have combated for (the recovery of) the cows, the waters, the sun, the dawns that had been carried away (by the Asuras): you reunite, Indra, (with the world), the quarters of the horizon, the sun, the wonderful waters, the dawns, the cattle, and so do you, Agni, who have the Niyut steeds.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वृ॑त्रहणा वृत्र॒हभिः॒ शुष्मै॒रिंद्र॑ या॒तं नमो॑भिरग्ने  ॒
> अर्वाक् ।  
> यु॒वं राधो॑भि॒रक॑वेभिरिं॒द्राग्ने॑ अ॒स्मे भ॑वतमुत्त॒मेभिः॑॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वृत्रहना । वृत्रहभिः । शुष्मैः । इंद्र । यातं । नमःभिः । अग्ने । अर्वाक् ।  
> युवं । राधःभिः । अकवेभिः । इंद्र । अग्ने । अस्मे इति । भवतं । उत्तमेभिः ॥३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऐंद्राग्नस्य पशोर्वपाया आ वृत्रहणेत्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । आ वृत्रहणा
> वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरा भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> हे वृत्रहणा वृत्रस्यासुरस्य हंतारौ हे इंद्र हे अग्ने वृत्रहभिर्वृत्रस्य
> हंतृभिवृत्रनहननिमित्तैः शुष्मैर्बलैनमोभिरस्मभ्यं दातवैरन्नैश्च सार्धमर्वागस्मदभिमुखमा यातं । अगच्छतं । हे इंद्र हे अग्ने युवं युवामकवेभिरकुत्सितैर्महद्भिरुत्तमेभिरुत्कष्टतम्म राधोभिधनैः सहास्मे अस्मासु भवतं
> अविर्भवतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This ṛk, आ वृत्रहणा (*ā vṛtrahaṇā*), is the anuvākyā for the vapā-oblation of the animal offered to Indra and Agni. It is laid down in the Sūtra: आ वृत्रहणा वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरा भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू (*ā vṛtrahaṇā vṛtrahabhiḥ śuṣmairā bharataṃ śikṣataṃ vajrabāhū*) (Ā. 3-7). O slayers of Vṛtra, the Asura, O Indra, O Agni, come (यातं (*yātaṃ*)) towards us, facing us, together with strengths (शुष्मैः (*śuṣmaiḥ*)) that are the killers of Vṛtra, that is, that serve to slay Vṛtra, and with the foods that are to be given to us (नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)). O Indra, O Agni, be manifest (भवतं (*bhavataṃ*)) among us together with blameless, great and most excellent riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*)—who are slayers of enemies
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra,
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- वृत्रहभिः (*vṛtrahabhiḥ*)—that destroy enemies
- शुष्मैः (*śuṣmaiḥ*)—with strengths
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—and with the foods that we need, endowed
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—facing us
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be so kind as to come
- इंद्रॆ (*iṃdrè*)—O Indra,
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni,
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- अकवेभिः (*akavebhiḥ*)—not blameworthy
### Printed p. 396
- उत्तमेभिः (*uttamebhiḥ*)—and praiseworthy
- राधोभिः (*rādhobhiḥ*)—with riches
- अस्मे (*asme*)—before us
- भवतं (*bhavataṃ*)—appear and show yourselves

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, slayers of enemies, be so kind as to come facing us, endowed with strengths that destroy enemies and with the foods that we need. O Indra, O Agni, appear and show yourselves before us together with riches that are not blameworthy and are praiseworthy.

##### English translation
Slayers of Vritra, Indra and Agni, come down with foe-subduing energies, (to be invigorated) by (our) offerings: be manifest to us, Indra and Agni, with unblameable and most excellent riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the offering of the vapā in the animal sacrifice made to Indra and Agni, this ṛk beginning आ वृत्रहणा (*ā vṛtrahaṇā*) is to be recited as an anuvākyā mantra; this is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ वृत्रहणा वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरा भरतं शिक्षतं वज्रबाहू (*ā vṛtrahaṇā vṛtrahabhiḥ śuṣmairā bharataṃ śikṣataṃ vajrabāhū*) (Ā. 3-7).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता हु॑वे॒ ययो॑रि॒दं प॒प्ने विश्वं॑ पु॒रा कृ॒तं ।  
> इं॒द्रा॒ग्नी न म॑र्धतः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । हुवे । ययोः । इदं । पप्ने । विश्वं । पुरा । कृतं ।  
> इंद्राग्नी इति । न । मर्धतः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि प्रातःसवनेऽच्छावाकशस्त्रे ता हुवे इति षडहस्तोत्रियस्त्रृचः । सूत्रितं च । ता हुवे ययोरिदमियं वामस्य मन्मनः । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥
> पृष्ट्याभिप्लवषडहयोः स्तोमवृदौ ता हुव इत्याद्या नवर्च आवापार्थाः । सूत्रितं
> च । ता हुवे ययोरिदमिति नवेयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश । आ. ७-५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, in the śastra of the Acchāvāka, the tṛca beginning ता हुवे (*tā huve*) is the ṣaḍaha-stotriya. It is laid down in the Sūtra: ता हुवे ययोरिदमियं वामस्य मन्मनः (*tā huve yayoridamiyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*) (Ā. 7-2). In the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas, for the increase of the stoma, the nine ṛks beginning with ता हुव (*tā huva*) are for insertion (āvāpa). It is laid down: ता हुवे ययोरिदमिति नवेयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश (*tā huve yayoridamiti naveyaṃ vāmasya manmana ityekādaśa*) (Ā. 7-5).

### Printed p. 397

> ता तौ तादृशाविंद्राग्नी हुवे । आह्वये । ययोरिंद्राग्नोः पुरा
> पूर्वस्मिन्काले कृतं विश्वं सर्वमिदं पूर्वास्वक्षु कीर्तितं वीर्यं पप्ने पन्यते
> ऋषिभिः स्तूयते । ताविंद्राग्नी हुव इत्यन्वयः । तौ चेंद्राग्नी न मर्धतः ।
> स्तोत्यन्न हिंस्तः । अतोऽस्थानप्याहूत् रक्षतामिति भावः ॥ मर्धतिर्हिंसाकर्मा :

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I call (हुवे (*huve*)) those two, Indra and Agni, such as they are, of whom all this heroic deed, done in former time and proclaimed in the earlier ṛks, is praised (पप्ने (*papne*)) by the seers. The construction is: I call those Indra and Agni. And may those two not harm (न मर्धतः (*na mardhataḥ*)) the one who praises them; hence may they protect us who have called them; this is the sense. The verb मर्धति (*mardhati*) denotes harming. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—by which Indra and Agni
- पुरा (*purā*)—in all former times
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—performed
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—the heroic deeds described before
- पप्ने (*papne*)—have been praised
- ता (*tā*)—those renowned Indra and Agni
- हुवे (*huve*)—we pray and invoke
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O deities Indra and Agni
- न मर्धतः (*na mardhataḥ*)—do not harm us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We pray and invoke those renowned Indra and Agni, by whom all the heroic deeds performed in all former times and described by the earlier mantras have been praised. Do not harm us.

##### English translation
I invoke those two, the whole of whose deeds of old have been celebrated : Indra and Agni harm us not.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the morning pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, the three ṛks beginning with ता हुवे (*tā huve*) (ṛks 4–6 of this sūkta) are to be recited as the ṣaḍaha-stotriya tṛca; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the Sūtra ता हुवे ययोरिदमियं वामस्य मन्मनः (*tā huve yayoridamiyaṃ vāmasya manmanaḥ*) (Ā. 3-2) **NOTE**. And in the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭha and Abhiplava ṣaḍaha, for the increase of the stoma, the nine ṛks beginning with ता हुवे (*tā huve*) (ṛks 4–12 of this sūkta) are to be recited as āvāpa mantras; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the Sūtra ता हुवे ययोरिदमिति नवेयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश (*tā huve yayoridamiti naveyaṃ vāmasya manmana ityekādaśa*) (Ā. 7-5).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒ग्रा वि॑घ॒निना॒ मृध॑ इंद्रा॒ग्नी ह॑वामहे ।  
> ता नो॑ मृळात ई॒दृशे॑ ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 398

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उग्रा । विघनिना । मृधः । इंद्राग्नी इति । हवामहे ।  
> ता । नः । मृळातः । ईदृशे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उग्रोग्रावुद्गूर्णबलावत एव मृधः शूत्रून्विघनिना विघनिन् विशेषेण
> हतवंताविंद्राग्नी हवामहे । आह्वयामहे । तौ चेंद्राग्नी ईदृशेऽस्मिन् संग्रामे
> नोऽस्मान्मृळातः । सुखयतां । यद्वा ॥ मृळतिरूपदयाकर्मा ॥ नोऽस्माकं
> मृळातः । उपदयां कुरुतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We call (हवामहे (*havāmahe*)) Indra and Agni, who are fierce (उग्रा (*ugrā*)), that is, of uplifted strength, and for that very reason are the special slayers (विघनिना (*vighaninā*)) of enemies (मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)). May those two, Indra and Agni, in such a battle as this, make us happy (मृळातः (*mṛḷātaḥ*)). Or else: the verb मृळति (*mṛḷati*) denotes compassion; may they show compassion to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्रा (*ugrā*)—who have strength terrible to enemies
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies
- विघनिना (*vighaninā*)—and who destroy
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—Indra and Agni
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and invoke
- ता (*tā*)—those same Indra and Agni
- ईदृशे (*īdṛśe*)—in such a battle
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळातः (*mṛḷātaḥ*)—may they make happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We pray and invoke Indra and Agni, who have strength terrible to enemies and who destroy enemies. May those same Indra and Agni make us happy in such a battle.

##### English translation
We invoke the fierce Indra and Agni, the slayers of enemies: may they give us success in similar warfare.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ह॒तो वृ॒त्राण्यार्या॑ ह॒तो दासा॑नि॒ सत्प॑ती ।  
> ह॒तो विश्वा॒ अप॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हतः । वृत्राणि । आर्या । हतः । दासानि । सत्पती इति सत्पती ।  
> हतः । विश्वाः । अप । द्विषः ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 399

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ताविंद्राग्नी आर्यार्यैः कर्मानुष्ठातृभिः कृतानि वृत्राण्युपद्रवजातानि
> हतः । हिंस्तः । तथा सत्पती सतां पालयिताराविंद्राग्नी दासानि । दासाः कर्महीनाः
> शत्रवः । तैः कृतानि चोपद्रवजातानि हतः । अपि च विश्वाः सर्वा द्वेषीः
> शत्रुभूताः।प्रजा अप हतः विनाशयतः । अतोऽस्माकमप्येवमेव कुरुतामिति भावः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those two, Indra and Agni, destroy (हतः (*hataḥ*)) the afflictions (वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)) that have arisen as troubles caused by the Āryas, the performers of rites. Likewise they, as protectors of the good (सत्पती (*satpatī*)), destroy the troubles (दासानि (*dāsāni*)) made by the Dāsas, the enemies who are without rites. And further, they utterly destroy all hostile (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)) creatures who are enemies. The sense is: therefore may they do just so for us also.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नि (*iṃdrāgni*)—Indra and Agni
- आर्या (*āryā*)—done by the Āryas, the performers of rites
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the afflictions
- हतः (*hataḥ*)—they destroy
- सत्पती (*satpatī*)—those same Indra and Agni, protectors of the good
- दासानि (*dāsāni*)—also the troubles caused by enemies who are without rites
- हतः (*hataḥ*)—they destroy
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—the hostile people
- अप हतः (*apa hataḥ*)—they destroy completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra and Agni destroy all the afflictions caused either by the Āryas, the performers of rites, or by the enemies who are in the form of Dāsas, without rites. And they destroy all hostile people.

##### English translation
Counteract all oppressions (committed) by the pious : counteract all oppressions (committed) by the impious : protectors of the virtuous, destroy all those who hate us.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी यु॒वामि॒मे॒३॒॑भि स्तोमा॑ अनूषत ।  
> ।  
> पिब॑तं शंभुवा सु॒तं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । युवां । इमे । अभि । स्तोमाः । अनूषत ।  
> ।  
> पिबतं । शंभुवा । सुतं ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 400

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र इंद्राग्नी युवामिति षडहस्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्विजेत्यच्छावाकस्य । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे स्तोमाः स्तोतारोऽभ्यनूषत अभिष्टुवंति ।
> हे शंभुवा सुखस्य भावयिताराविंद्राग्नी सुतमभिषुतम्मदीयं सोमं पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, in the śastra of the Acchāvāka, the tṛca beginning इंद्राग्नी युवां (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāṃ*) is the ṣaḍaha-stotriya. It is laid down in the Sūtra: इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्विजेत्यच्छावाकस्य (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijetyacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-2). O Indra and Agni, these praisers (स्तोमाः (*stomāḥ*)) glorify (अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)) you. O Śaṃbhuvā, you two who cause happiness, drink (पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)) my Soma that has been pressed (सुतं (*sutaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- युवां (*yuvāṃ*)—both of you
- इमे स्तोमाः (*ime stomāḥ*)—these praisers
- अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)—glorify
- शंभुवा (*śaṃbhuvā*)—O Indra and Agni, who bring happiness
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—this pressed Soma juice
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, these praisers glorify you both. O Indra and Agni, who bring happiness, drink this pressed Soma juice.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, these hymns glorify you both ; drink, bestowers of of happiness, the libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the morning pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, the three ṛks beginning with इंद्राग्नी युवां (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāṃ*) (ṛks 7–9 of this sūkta) are to be recited as the ṣaḍaha-stotriya tṛca; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the Sūtra इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्विजेत्यच्छावाकस्य (*iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime yajñasya hi stha ṛtvijetyacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-2).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या वां॒ संति॑ पुरु॒स्पृहो॑ नि॒युतो॑ दा॒शुषे॑ नरा ।  
> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ ताभि॒रा ग॑तं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> याः । वा । संति । पुरुस्पृहः । नियुतः । दाशुषे । नरा ।  
> इंद्राग्नी इति । शाभिः । आ । गतं ii ८ ।.

### Printed p. 401

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नरा नेताराविंद्राग्नी वां युवयोः स्वभूताः पुरुस्पृहः पुरुभिर्बहुभिः स्पृहणीया दाशुषे हवींषि दत्तवते यजमानार्थमुत्पन्ना या
> नियुतोऽश्वाः संति हे इंद्राग्नी ताभिर्नियुद्भिरा गतं । आगच्छतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leaders, Indra and Agni, those Niyut horses (नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)) that are your own, much desired (पुरुस्पृहः (*puruspṛhaḥ*)) by many, and have come into being for the sacrificer who has given oblations (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)), with those Niyuts, O Indra and Agni, come (आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरा (*narā*)—O leaders of the world
- इंदाग्नी (*iṃdāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- वां (*vāṃ*)—belonging to you
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—horses
- पुरुस्पृहः (*puruspṛhaḥ*)—desired by many
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—produced for the sacrificer who offers oblations
- संति (*saṃti*)—there are
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with those horses
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—be so kind as to come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, leaders of the world, be so kind as to come with those horses of yours that are desired by many and are produced for the sacrificer who offers oblations.

##### English translation
Indra and Agni, leaders (of rites), whose Niyut steeds are desired by many, come with them to the donor (of the libatation.)

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ताभि॒रा ग॑च्छतं न॒रोपे॒दं सव॑नं सु॒तं ।  
> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ताभिः । आ । गच्छतं । नरा । उप । इदं । सवनं । सुतं ।  
> इंद्राग्नी इति । सोमपीतये ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नरा नेताराविंद्राग्नी । सूयतेऽभिषूयत इति सवनः सोमः । इदं
> सवनमिमं सोमं सुतमभिषुतमुप प्रति । यद्वा । इदं प्रातःसवनमुपास्मिन्
> XXI 26
> XXI 26

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leaders, Indra and Agni. Savana is Soma, since it is pressed (सूयते (*sūyate*)). The words इदं सवनं (*idaṃ savanaṃ*) mean this Soma that has been pressed, and उप (*upa*) means towards. Or else: इदं (*idaṃ*) refers to this morning pressing, and the sense is towards the Soma pressed at this pressing,

### Printed p. 402

> सवने सुतमभिषुतं सोमं प्रति ताभिर्नियुद्भिरा गच्छतं । किमर्थ० । सोमपीतये
> तस्य सोमस्य पानार्थ० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

come with those Niyut horses. For what purpose? For the drinking (सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)) of that Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरा (*narā*)—O leaders
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- इदं सवनं उप (*idaṃ savanaṃ upa*)—facing this Soma juice
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with those same horses
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for the drinking of Soma
- आ गच्छतं (*ā gacchataṃ*)—be so kind as to come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, leaders, for the drinking of this Soma that has been pressed and made ready, be so kind as to come, with your horses, facing this juice:

##### English translation
Come with them, leaders (of rites), to the effused libation, to drink, Indra and Agni, of the Soma.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमी॑ळिष्व॒ यो अ॒र्चिषा॒ वना॒ विश्वा॑ परि॒ष्वज॑त् ।  
> कृ॒ष्णा कृ॒णोति॑ जि॒ह्वया॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । ईळिष्व । यः । अर्चिषा । वना । विश्वा । परिस्वजत् ।  
> कृष्णा । कृणोति । जिह्वया ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो स्तोतस्तमग्निमाळिष्ट स्तुहि योऽग्निरर्चिषा ज्वालारूपेण तेजसा विश्वा
> सर्वाणि वनारण्यानि परिष्वजत् परिष्वजति परितो वेष्टयति । यश्च तानि वनानि जिह्वया
> ज्वालया दग्वा कृष्णा कृष्णवर्णानि कृणोति करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, praise (ईळिष्ट (*īḷiṣṭa*)) that Agni who, with his flame, his brilliance in the form of fire, embraces (परिष्वजत् (*pariṣvajat*)) all forests, that is, wraps them round on every side; and who, having burnt those forests with his tongue, the flame, makes them black (कृष्णा (*kṛṣṇā*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni (O praiser)
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—with his brilliance
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- वना (*vanā*)—the forests
- परिष्वजत् (*pariṣvajat*)—envelops (and)
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with his tongue in the form of flame
- कृष्णा (*kṛṣṇā*)—all those forests black in colour
- कृणोति (*kṛṇoti*)—makes
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Agni
- ईळिष्ट् (*īḷiṣṭ*)—praise

### Printed p. 403

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, praise that Agni who with his brilliance envelops all the forests, and with his tongue in the form of flame makes all those forests black in colour.

##### English translation
Glorify that Agni who envelopes all the forests with flame, who blackens them with (his) tongue.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य इ॒द्ध आ॒विवा॑सति सु॒म्म मिंद्र॑स्य॒ मर्त्यः॑ ।  
> द्यु॒म्नाय॑ सु॒तरा॑ अ॒पः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । इद्दे । आविवासति । सुम्नं । इंद्रस्य । मर्त्यः ।  
> द्युम्नाय । सुतराः । अपः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो मर्त्यो मनुष्य इद्दे दीप्तेऽग्नौ सुम्मं सुखकरं हविरिंद्रस्येंद्रायाविवासति परिचरति प्रयच्छति ॥ चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठि ॥ तस्य मर्त्यस्य द्युम्नाय
> द्योतमानायान्नाय तदर्थं सुतराः सुखेन तरणीया अप उदकानि वृष्ट्यात्मकानींद्रः करोतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The mortal, the man, who into the kindled (इद्दे (*idde*)), blazing fire presents (आविवासति (*āvivāsati*)) a pleasing (सुम्मं (*summaṃ*)) oblation for Indra, for that mortal's shining food Indra makes the waters (अपः (*apaḥ*)), that is, rain, easy to cross (सुतराः (*sutarāḥ*)); this is the word to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—mortal, the sacrificer
- इद्दे (*idde*)—when the sacrificial fire is kindled
- सुम्नं (*sumnaṃ*)—a pleasing oblation
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—for Indra
- आविवासति (*āvivāsati*)—presents (to that man)
- द्युम्नायॆ (*dyumnāyè*)—for the attainment of shining food
- सुतराः (*sutarāḥ*)—that carry the sacrificer easily across distress
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters of rain (Indra gives)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To that mortal sacrificer who, when the sacrificial fire is kindled, presents a pleasing oblation to Indra, Indra gives the waters of rain, which carry him easily across distress, for the gaining of shining food.

### Printed p. 404

##### English translation
The mortal who presents the gratifying (oblation) to Indra in the kindled (fire), to him (Indra grants) acceptable waters for his sustenance.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता नो॒ वाज॑वती॒रिष॑ आ॒शून्पि॑पृत॒मर्व॑तः ।  
> इंद्र॑म॒ुग्निं च॒ वोळ्ह॑वे ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । नः । वाजवतीः । इषः । आशून् । पिपृतं । अर्वतः ।  
> इंद्रं । अग्निं । च । वोळ्हवे ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी ता तौ युवां वाजवतीरन्नवतीरिष इष्यमाणा वृष्टिः ।
> यद्वा । वाजो बलं । तद्वतीरिषोऽन्नान्याशून् शीघ्रगानर्वतोऽश्वांश्च नोऽस्मभ्यं
> पिपृतं । पूरयतं । प्रयच्छतं । किमर्थं । इंद्रमग्निं च युवां वोळ्हवे
> वोढुं हविर्भिः प्रापयितुं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, you two, grant us (पिपृतं (*pipṛtaṃ*), fill, bestow) the food-rich (वाजवतीः (*vājavatīḥ*)) wished-for rain (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)). Or else: vāja is strength, and the इषः (*iṣaḥ*) endowed with it are foods; and grant us swift-going (आशून् (*āśūn*)) horses (अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)). For what purpose? In order to carry (वोळ्हवे (*voḷhave*)) Indra and Agni, that is, to convey you with oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता (*tā*)—you, the renowned
- इंद्रमग्निं च (*iṃdramagniṃ ca*)—to you, who are Indra and Agni
- वोळ्हवे (*voḷhave*)—for bearing the oblation
- वाजवतीः (*vājavatīḥ*)—provided with food
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—endowed with strength
- आशून् (*āśūn*)—and swift-going
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—horses
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पिपृतं (*pipṛtaṃ*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, renowned as you are, provide us with horses that are supplied with food, endowed with strength and swift-going, for bearing the oblation to you, who are Indra and Agni.

##### English translation
May those two grant us strengthening food, and swift horses to convey (our offerings).

### Printed p. 405

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒भा वा॑मिंद्राग्नी आहु॒वध्या॑ उ॒भा राध॑सः स॒ह मा॑द॒यध्यै॑ ।  
> उ॒भा दा॒तारा॑वि॒षां र॑यी॒णामु॒भा वाज॑स्य सा॒तये॑ हुवे  
> वां ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उभा । वां । इंद्राग्नी इति । आहुवध्यै । उभा । राधसः । सह । मादयध्यै ।  
> उभा । दातार् । इषां । रयीणां । उभा । वाजस्य । सातये । हुवे । वां ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऐंद्राग्नस्य पशोर्हविषोऽनुवाक्योभा वामित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । उभा
> वामिंद्राग्नी आहुवध्यै शुचिं नु स्तोमं नव जातमद्य । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्राग्नी उभोभौ संहत्य वर्तमानौ नां युवां हुवे । आह्वयामि ।
> किमर्थं । आहुवध्या अभिमुख्येन होतुं । तथोभोभौ युवामाह्वये राधसो
> राधसा राधकेन हविषा सह युगपदेव मादयध्यॆ मादयितुं तर्पयितुं ।
> सर्वेषु देवेषु सत्स्वावयोराह्वाने किं कारणमिति चेदुच्यते । उभोभौ ता
> युवामिषामन्नानां रयाणां धनानां च दातारौ स्थः । अतः कारणादुभोभौ नां
> युवां वाजस्यान्नस्य सातये संभजनाय हुवे । आह्वये ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This ṛk, उभा वां (*ubhā vāṃ*), is the anuvākyā for the oblation of the animal offered to Indra and Agni. It is laid down in the Sūtra: उभा वामिंद्राग्नी आहुवध्यै शुचिं नु स्तोमं नव जातमद्य (*ubhā vāmiṃdrāgnī āhuvadhyai śuciṃ nu stomaṃ nava jātamadya*) (Ā. 3-7). O Indra and Agni, both of you, being together, I call (हुवे (*huve*)) you. For what purpose? In order to sacrifice before you (आहुवध्यै (*āhuvadhyai*)). Likewise I call you both, in order that together, at one and the same time, you may be gratified (मादयध्यै (*mādayadhyai*)) and satisfied with the accomplishing oblation (राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)). If it is asked what is the reason for calling you two when all the gods are present, it is said: both of you are givers of foods (इषां (*iṣāṃ*)) and of riches (रयीणां (*rayīṇāṃ*)). For that reason I call you both for the sharing (सातये (*sātaye*)) of food (वाजस्य (*vājasya*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- उभा (*ubhā*)—who are together
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you both
- आ हुवध्यै (*ā huvadhyai*)—to offer the oblation
- हुवे (*huve*)—I pray and invoke
- राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)—with oblations
- उभा (*ubhā*)—both
- सह (*saha*)—at one time
- मादयध्यै (*mādayadhyai*)—to enjoy satisfaction (I call)
- उभा (*ubhā*)—you both
- इषां (*iṣāṃ*)—of foods
- रयाणां (*rayāṇāṃ*)—and of riches
- दातार् (*dātār*)—are givers
- उभा (*ubhā*)—who are together
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you both
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—of food
- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the attainment (I call)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, I pray and invoke you both, who are together, to offer the oblation. With oblations may you both enjoy satisfaction at one and the same time. You both are givers of foods and of riches. I call you both, who are together, for the attainment of food.

##### English translation

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice made for Indra and Agni, when the oblation is offered, this ṛk beginning उभा वां (*ubhā vāṃ*) is to be recited as an anuvākyā mantra; this is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उभा वामिंद्राग्नी आहुवध्यॆ शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्य (*ubhā vāmiṃdrāgnī āhuvadhyè śuciṃ nu stomaṃ navajātamadya*) (A. 3-7) **NOTE**.

#### Ṛk 14

> आ नो॒ गव्ये॑भि॒रश्व॑र्वस॒वै॒३॒॑ ३ रुप॑ गच्छतं ।  
> सखा॑यौ दे॒वौ स॒ख्याय॑ शं॒भुवें॑द्रा॒ग्नी ता ह॑वामहे ॥१४॥

> सखायौ । देवौ । सख्याय । शंभुवा । इंद्राग्नी इति । ता । हवामहे ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी गव्येभिर्गोसमूहैरश्वैरश्वसमूहैर्वसन्यैर्वसुसमूहैश्च
> सार्धं नोऽस्मानाभिमुख्येनोपा गच्छतं । शेषः परोक्षकृतः । सखायौ समानख्यान् देवौ दानादिगुणयुक्तौ शंभुवा शंभुव् सुखस्य भावयितार् ता
> तादृशाविंद्राग्नी सख्याय सखित्वार्थं वयं हवामहे । आह्वयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, come towards us, facing us, together with herds of cows (गव्येभिः (*gavyebhiḥ*)), troops of horses (अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)) and masses of wealth (वसवैः (*vasavaiḥ*)). You are friends (सखायौ (*sakhāyau*)) of equal renown, gods endowed with qualities such as generosity, Śaṃbhuvā, producers of happiness. Those same Indra and Agni we call (हवामहे (*havāmahe*)) for the sake of friendship (सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)).

- न उप (*na upa*)—facing us

- देव् (*dev*)—divine in nature

> वी॒तं ह॒व्यान्या ग॑तं॒ पिब॑तं सो॒म्यं मधु॑ ॥ १५ ॥

> स्तोत्रं शृणुतं । श्रुत्वा च तदीयानि हव्यानि हवींषि वीतं । कामयेथां ।

Having desired them, come (आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)). And having come, drink (पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)) the sweet Soma (मधु (*madhu*)).

## Sūkta 61 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमददादिति चतुर्दशर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं सरस्वतीदेवताकं । आदितस्तिस्रो जगत्यप्रयोदश्यपि जगती चतुर्दशी त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा
> गायत्र्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इयं षळूना सारस्वतं त्रिजगत्यादि जगतीत्रिष्टुबंतमिति ॥ अत्र शौनकः । इयमित्येतदाद्यं तु सूक्तं सारस्वतं जपेत् । द्विजः प्रातः
> शुचिर्भूत्वा वाग्मी भवति बुद्धिमान् । ऋग्वि. २-२३ । इति ॥ पार्श्विके षष्ठेऽहनि
> प्रलुग इयमददादिति सारस्वतस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । इयमददाद्रभसमृणच्युतमिति
> प्रलुगं । आ. ८-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning इयमददात् (*iyamadadāt*) has fourteen ṛks and is the twelfth sūkta. Its seer is Bharadvāja; its deity is Sarasvatī. The first three ṛks are in Jagatī, the thirteenth is also Jagatī, the fourteenth is Triṣṭubh, and the rest are Gāyatrī. So it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: इयं षळूना सारस्वतं त्रिजगत्यादि जगतीत्रिष्टुबंतं (*iyaṃ ṣaḷūnā sārasvataṃ trijagatyādi jagatītriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). **GLOSS** On this Śaunaka says (Ṛgvi. 2-23) **NOTE**: a twice-born who, purified, recites this Sarasvatī sūkta beginning with इयं (*iyaṃ*) in the morning becomes eloquent and wise. As for its application: on the sixth day of the Pārśvika (Pṛṣṭha) sacrifice, in the Praluga, the tṛca beginning इयमददात् (*iyamadadāt*) is the Sārasvata. It is laid down in the Sūtra: इयमददाद्रभसमृणच्युतमिति प्रलुगं (*iyamadadādrabhasamṛṇacyutamiti pralugaṃ*) (Ā. 8-1).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning इयमददात् (*iyamadadāt*) is the twelfth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. There are fourteen ṛks in it. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Bharadvāja; the deity is Sarasvatī. The first three ṛks of this sūkta and the thirteenth ṛk are in the Jagatī metre. The fourteenth is in Triṣṭubh. All the remaining ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इयं षळूना सारस्वतं त्रिजगत्यादि जगतीत्रिष्टुबंतं (*iyaṃ ṣaḷūnā sārasvataṃ trijagatyādi jagatītriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). **GLOSS** On the application of this sūkta the great sage Śaunaka has said, in his work called Ṛgvidhāna: इयमित्येतदाद्यं तु सूक्तं सारस्वतं जपेत् । द्विजः प्रातः शुचिर्भूत्वा वाग्मी भवति बुद्धिमान् ॥ (*iyamityetadādyaṃ tu sūktaṃ sārasvataṃ japet | dvijaḥ prātaḥ śucirbhūtvā vāgmī bhavati buddhimān ‖*) (Ṛgvidhāna 2-295). That is, if a twice-born man rises at dawn, becomes purified by bathing and the like, and recites this sūkta beginning इयमददात् (*iyamadadāt*), whose deity is Sarasvatī, that man becomes, by the grace of the goddess Sarasvatī,

### Printed p. 409

eloquent, that is, skilled in speaking, and intelligent. And on the sixth day of the Pṛṣṭha sacrifice, when the Praluga śastra mantras are recited, the first three ṛks of the sūkta beginning इयमददात् (*iyamadadāt*) are to be recited as the Sārasvata tṛca; this is set out by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, इयमदद्रादभसमृणच्युतमिति प्रलुगं (*iyamadadrādabhasamṛṇacyutamiti pralugaṃ*) (Ā. 8-1).

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 61
- Aṣṭaka 4; Adhyāya 8; Vargas 30, 31, 32
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 14
- Ṛṣi: भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*)
- Deity: Sarasvatī
- Metre: 1-3, 13 Jagatī; 4-12 Gāyatrī; 14 Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒यम॑ददाद्रभ॒समृ॑ण॒च्युतं॒ दिवो॑दासं वध्र्य॒श्वाय॑  ॒॑
> दाशुषे ।  
> या शश्वं॑तमाच॒खादा॑व॒सं प॒णिं ता ते॑ दा॒त्राणि॑ तवि॒षा  ॑
> सरस्वती ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । अददात् । रभसं । ऋण्च्युतं । दिवःदासं । वध्रिअश्वाय । दाशुषे ।  
> या । शश्वंतं । आचखाद । अवसं । पणिं । ता । ते । दात्राणि । तविषा । सरस्वति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयं सरस्वती रभसं वेगवंतमृणच्युतं वैदिकस्य देवर्षिपितृसंबंधिनो
> लौकिकस्य च ऋणस्य च्यावयितारं दिवोदासमेतत्संज्ञं पुत्रं दाशुषे हवींषि
> दत्तवते वध्यश्चाय्तत्संज्ञाय ऋषयेऽददात् । दत्तवती । या सरस्वती शश्वंतं
> बहुलं पणिं पणनशीलं वणिजमदातृजनमवसं केवलं स्वात्मन एव तर्पकमाचखाद
> आजघान सेयमददादित्यन्वयः । अथ प्रत्यक्षीकृत्य स्तोति । हे सरस्वति देवि ता तानि
> पुत्रदानादीनि ते त्वदीयानि दात्राणि दानानि तविषा तविषाणि महांति भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Sarasvatī gave (अददात् (*adadāt*)) to the sacrificer Vadhryaśva, who had given oblations (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)), a son named Divodāsa, swift (रभसं (*rabhasaṃ*)), a liberator from debt (ऋणच्युतं (*ṛṇacyutaṃ*)), that is, one who frees from the Vedic debt owed to the gods, seers and fathers and from the worldly debt. She is the Sarasvatī who struck down (आचखाद (*ācakhāda*)) the numerous Paṇi, a trader by nature, a man who gives nothing to others, an Avasa, one who gratifies only himself. The construction is: that same Sarasvatī gave. Then, making her present, he praises her: O goddess Sarasvatī, those gifts of yours, such as the giving of a son, are great (तविषा (*taviṣā*)).

- या (*yā*)—which goddess Sarasvatī
- शश्वंतं (*śaśvaṃtaṃ*)—greatly
- अवसं (*avasaṃ*)—who thought only of his own welfare
- पणिं (*paṇiṃ*)—and was a miser, the Asura
- आचखाद (*ācakhāda*)—killed, such

- रभसं (*rabhasaṃ*)—swift
- ऋणच्युतं (*ṛṇacyutaṃ*)—who discharges the debts to gods, seers and fathers
- दिवोदासं (*divodāsaṃ*)—the son named Divodāsa

- वध्रश्वाय (*vadhraśvāya*)—to the seer named Vadhryaśva

- सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—O goddess Sarasvatī

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Sarasvatī who destroyed the Asura who greatly thought only of his own welfare and was selfish and extremely miserly, that same Sarasvatī has given a son named Divodāsa, swift and a discharger of the debts to gods and fathers, to the seer named Vadhryaśva, who offers oblations. O Sarasvatī, the gift of a son and the gift of wealth that are favoured by you bear great fruit.

##### English translation
She gave to the donor of the oblations, Vadhryaswa, a son, Divodasa endowed with speed, and acquitting the debt (due to gods and progenitors); she who destroyed the churlish niggard, (thinking) only of himself : such are your great bounties, Saraswati.

> सरस्वती देवतारूपेण नदीरूपेण च वर्तते । देवतारूपा स्तुता ।
> अधुनानया नदीरूपां सरस्वतीं स्तौति । इयं नदीरूपा सरस्वती शुष्मैः
> शोषकैरात्मीयैर्बलैस्तविषेभिर्महद्भिरूर्मिभिस्तरंगैर्गिरीणां पर्वतानां तीरसंबद्धानां सानु सानून्यरुजत् । भनक्ति । बिसखा इव । बिसं खनतीति बिसखाः ।
> स यथा बिसार्थं पंकं रुजति तद्वत् । तां सरस्वतीं पारावतघ्नीं परावति दूरदेशे
> विद्यमानस्यापि वृक्षादेर्हंत्रीं सुवृक्तिभिः स्तुतिभिर्धितिभिः कर्मभिश्चावसे रक्षणार्थमा
> विवासेम । परिचरेम । यद्वा । पारावतघ्नीं पारावारे पारार्वाची तीरे ।
> तयोर्घातिनीं । उक्तं च । पारावतघ्नीं पारावारघातिनीं । नि. २-२४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sarasvatī exists both in the form of a deity and in the form of a river. In the form of a deity she has been praised; now with this ṛk he praises Sarasvatī in the form of a river. This river-form Sarasvatī, with her own strengths that dry things up (शुष्मैः (*śuṣmaiḥ*)), with great (तविषेभिः (*taviṣebhiḥ*)) waves (ऊर्मिभिः (*ūrmibhiḥ*)), breaks (अरुजत् (*arujat*)) the peaks (सानु (*sānu*)) of the mountains that adjoin her banks, like (बिसखा इव (*bisakhā iva*)) a digger of lotus fibre: as he breaks the mud for the sake of the fibre, so she. Her, the Pārāvataghnī, the destroyer even of a tree and the like that stands in a distant place, we serve (आ विवासेम (*ā vivāsema*)) with praises (सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)) and with rites (धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)) for protection (अवसे (*avase*)). Or else: पारावतघ्नीं (*pārāvataghnīṃ*) means the destroyer of both banks, the far and the near. And it is said: पारावतघ्नीं पारावारघातिनीं (*pārāvataghnīṃ pārāvāraghātinīṃ*) (Ni. 2-24). **GLOSS**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this goddess Sarasvatī in the form of a river
- बिसखा इव (*bisakhā iva*)—easily, as one digs mud for the lotus stalk
- शुष्मेभिः (*śuṣmebhiḥ*)—with her powerful
- तविषेभिः (*taviṣebhiḥ*)—and great
- ऊर्मिभिः (*ūrmibhiḥ*)—waves
- गिरीणां (*girīṇāṃ*)—of the mountains
- सानु (*sānu*)—the lofty places
- अरुजत् (*arujat*)—she breaks through
- पारावतघ्नीं (*pārāvataghnīṃ*)—who brings down trees and the like (or banks) that are in a distant place
- सरस्वतीं (*sarasvatīṃ*)—this goddess Sarasvatī
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with excellent praises
- धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—and with excellent rites
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- आ विवासेम (*ā vivāsema*)—let us worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This goddess Sarasvatī in the form of a river easily breaks through the lofty places of the mountains with her powerful and great waves, as one digs mud for the lotus stalk. Let us worship, for protection, with excellent praises and with excellent rites, this goddess Sarasvatī, who brings down trees and the like and the banks that are in a distant place.

##### English translation
With impetuous and mighty waves she breaks down the precipices of the mountains, like a digger for the lotus fibres : we adore for our protection, with praises and with sacred rites, Saraswati the underminer of both her banks.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this ṛk Yāska has given an etymology: इयं शुष्मैः शोषणैः । शुष्ममिति बलनाम शोषयतीति सतः । बिसं बिस्मतेर्भेदनकर्मणो वृद्धिकर्मणो वा । सानु समुच्च्रितं भवति समुन्नु- (*iyaṃ śuṣmaiḥ śoṣaṇaiḥ | śuṣmamiti balanāma śoṣayatīti sataḥ | bisaṃ bismaterbhedanakarmaṇo vṛddhikarmaṇo vā | sānu samuccritaṃ bhavati samunnu-*) **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 412

न्नमिति वा । महद्भिरूर्मिभिः पारावतघ्नीं पारावारघातिनीं । पारं परं भवति । अवारमवरं । अवनाय सुप्रवृत्ताभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिः सरस्वतीं नदीं कर्मभिः परिचरेम ॥ (*nnamiti vā | mahadbhirūrmibhiḥ pārāvataghnīṃ pārāvāraghātinīṃ | pāraṃ paraṃ bhavati | avāramavaraṃ | avanāya supravṛttābhiḥ śobhanābhiḥ stutibhiḥ sarasvatīṃ nadīṃ karmabhiḥ paricarema ‖*) (Ni. 2-24)

"Śuṣka" means strength. For the word शुष्क (*śuṣka*) is formed from the root शोषयति (*śoṣayati*), which has the sense of pressing down; since it presses down everything by its own strength, the sense "strength" has become established for the word.**NOTE**
बिसं (*bisaṃ*) means lotus stalk. This word is formed from the root बिस्कृति (*biskṛti*), which has the sense of cutting, breaking into pieces, or growing. The word सानु (*sānu*) means a high place, an elevated place, a summit. This river Sarasvatī, with her huge, that is, great waves, breaks away and destroys her two banks, as one easily cuts through the tender lotus stalk. That is, because of the current of the river the two banks collapse and fall and become mingled with the water of the river. पारं (*pāraṃ*) means that which is different (परं (*paraṃ*)) or that which is far away. अवरं (*avaraṃ*) means that which is near. पारावारं (*pārāvāraṃ*) means the two banks, the one far away (the opposite one) and the one near. The chief purport of the etymology is: let us serve with offerings of worship the river Sarasvatī, flowing between such two banks, for our protection, with well-composed praises recited clearly and with proper accents, or with excellently performed rites of worship and the like.

### Printed p. 413

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सर॑स्वति देव॒निदो॒ नि ब॑र्हय प्र॒जां विश्व॑स्य॒ बृस॑यस्य मा॒यिनः॑।  
> उ॒त क्षि॒तिभ्यो॒ऽवनी॑रविंदो वि॒षमे॑भ्यो अस्रवो वाजिनीवति॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सरस्वति । देवनिदः । बर्हय । प्रजां । विश्वस्य । बृहयस्य । मायिनः ।  
> उत । क्षितिभ्यः । अवनीः । अविंदः । विषं । विध्यः । अस्रवः । वाजिनीवति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सरस्वति देवनिदो देवानां निंदकानसुरान्नि बर्हय । न्यबर्हयः ।
> अवधीः । तथा विश्वस्य व्याप्तस्य मायिनो मायाविनो बृसयस्य । बृसय इति
> त्वष्टुर्नामधेयं । त्वष्टुः प्रजां पुत्रं वृत्रासुरं च न्यवधीः । त्वत्साहाय्यादेवेंद्रो हतवानित्यर्थः । उतापि च हे वाजिनीवति अन्नवति सरस्वति त्वं क्षितिभ्यो
> मनुष्येभ्योऽवनीरसुरैरपहृता भूमीरविंदः । अलंभयः । एभ्यो मनुष्येभ्यो
> विषमुदकं चास्रवः । अक्षारयः । यद्वा । क्षितयोऽसुरजनाः । तेभ्यः सकाशादवनीर्भूमीरविंदः । लब्बवानसि । तान् हत्त्वैभ्यश्चासुरेभ्यो विषं मृतिहेतुभूतं
> गरलमस्रवः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Sarasvatī, you have destroyed the Asuras who revile the gods, and you have slain the offspring of the all-pervading Bṛsaya, the possessor of māyā." Bṛsaya is a name of Tvaṣṭṛ; you slew the offspring of Tvaṣṭṛ, that is, his son, the Asura Vṛtra. The meaning is that Indra slew him with your help. And, O Sarasvatī, possessed of food, you obtained for men the lands carried off by the Asuras, and you caused water to flow for these men. Or else: the Asura peoples are meant by क्षितयो (*kṣitayo*); from them you obtained the lands, you gained them; and having slain them, you caused to flow for these Asuras poison, a deadly venom, the cause of death.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—O goddess Sarasvatī
- देवनिदः (*devanidaḥ*)—the Asuras who revile the gods
- नि बर्हयः (*ni barhayaḥ*)—you have destroyed
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of the all-pervading
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—of the one endowed with power
- बृसयस्य (*bṛsayasya*)—of Tvaṣṭṛ
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—you have also slain the son, Vṛtra
- उत (*uta*)—and
- वाजिनीवति (*vājinīvati*)—O Sarasvatī, endowed with food
- क्षितिभ्यः (*kṣitibhyaḥ*)—to men
- अवनीः (*avanīḥ*)—the lands carried off by the Asuras
- अविंदः (*aviṃdaḥ*)—you provided again
- ऐभ्यः (*aibhyaḥ*)—for these men
- विषं (*viṣaṃ*)—water
- अस्रवः (*asravaḥ*)—you caused to flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sarasvatī, you have destroyed the Asuras who revile the gods. You have slain Vṛtra, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, who is all-pervading and endowed with power; and, O Sarasvatī, endowed with food, you have provided again to men the lands carried off by the Asuras. For these very men you have caused water to flow.

##### English translation
Destory, Saraswati the revilers of the gods, the offspring of the universal deluder, Vrisaya : giver of sustenance, you have acquired for men the lands (seized by the Asuras), and have showered water upon them.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र णो॑ दे॒वी सर॑स्वती॒ वाजे॑भिर्वा॒जनी॑वती ।  
> धी॒नाम॑वि॒त्र्य॑वतु ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । नः । देवी । सरस्वती । वाजेभिः । वाजिनीवती ।  
> धीनां । अवित्री । अवतु ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 414

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवी दानादिगुणयुक्ता वाजिनीवती । वाजोऽन्नं यस्यां क्रियायां सा
> वाजिनी । तद्युक्ता । धीनां ध्यातृणां स्तोतृणामवित्री रक्षित्री । एवंभूता सरस्वती
> वाजेभिरन्नॆर्नोऽस्मान्प्रावतु । प्रकर्षेण तर्पयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Devī" means she who is endowed with qualities such as generosity. वाजिनीवती (*vājinīvatī*): vāja is food; the rite in which there is food is vājinī; she is endowed with that. धीनां (*dhīnāṃ*) means of the meditators, that is, of the worshippers; अवित्री (*avitrī*) means the protectress. May Sarasvatī, so characterised, protect us with वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*), that is, with foods; may she satisfy us abundantly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवी (*devī*)—divine
- वाजिनीवती (*vājinīvatī*)—endowed with food
- धीनां (*dhīnāṃ*)—to the worshippers
- आवित्री (*āvitrī*)—the protectress
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī
- वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*)—with foods
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- प्र अवतु (*pra avatu*)—may she protect fully, or may she satisfy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Sarasvatī, who is divine, endowed with food, and the protectress of the worshippers, protect us with foods; may she fully satisfy us.

##### English translation
May the divine Saraswati, the acceptress of (sacrificial) food, the protectress of her worshippers, sustain as with (abundant) viands.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्त्वा॑ देवि सरस्वत्युपब्रू॒ते धने॑ हि॒ते ।  
> इंद्रं॒ न वृ॑त्र॒तूर्ये॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । त्वा । देवि । सरस्वति । उपब्रूते । धने । हिते ।  
> इंद्रं । न । वृत्रतूर्ये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवि सरस्वति यः स्तोता वृत्रतूर्ये संग्रामे धने हिते निहिते
> निमित्तभूते सतींद्रं न इंद्रमिव त्वामुपब्रूते स्तौति तं रक्षेति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O goddess Sarasvatī, the worshipper who, in the battle for wealth, wealth being the occasion, praises you as one praises Indra, him protect": thus the sentence is to be completed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवि (*devi*)—O divine
- सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—O Sarasvatī
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the worshipper who
- वृत्रतोर्ये (*vṛtratorye*)—in battle
- धने हिते (*dhane hite*)—for the sake of wealth
- इंद्रं न (*iṃdraṃ na*)—as one praises Indra
- त्वा उपब्रूते (*tvā upabrūte*)—praises you (protect such a worshipper)

### Printed p. 415

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Sarasvatī, the worshipper who, in battle, for the sake of wealth, praises you just as he praises Indra, protect such a worshipper.

##### English translation
Divine Saraswati, protect him engaged in conflict for the sake of wealth, who glorifies you like Indra.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं दे॑वि सरस्व॒त्यवा॒ वाजे॑षु वाजिनि ।  
> रदा॑ पू॒षेव॑ नः स॒निं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । देवि । सरस्वति । अव । वाजेषु । वाजिनि ।  
> रद । पूषाइव । नः । सनिं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवि दानादिगुणयुक्ते हे वाजिनि । वाजो बलमन्नं वा । तद्युक्ते ।
> हे सरस्वति त्वं वाजेषु संग्रामेष्टव । अस्मान्रक्ष । अपि च नोऽस्मभ्यं पूषेव
> पोषको देव इव सनिं संभजनीयं धनं रद । विलिख । प्रयच्छेति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O goddess, endowed with qualities such as generosity; O वाजिनि (*vājini*)": vāja is strength or food, and she is endowed with that. "O Sarasvatī, protect us in the वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*), that is, in battles. And, like Pūṣan, the nourishing god, रद (*rada*) for us the wealth that is to be shared": रद (*rada*) means विलिख (*vilikha*), that is, bestow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवि (*devi*)—O one endowed with qualities such as generosity
- वाजिनि (*vājini*)—O one endowed with power
- सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—O Sarasvatī
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*)—in battles
- अव (*ava*)—protect us
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पूषेव (*pūṣeva*)—like the nourishing god Pūṣan
- सनिं (*saniṃ*)—wealth fit to be enjoyed
- रद (*rada*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sarasvatī, endowed with qualities such as generosity and endowed with power, protect us in battles. Like Pūṣan, the nourishing god, provide us with wealth fit to be enjoyed.

##### English translation
Divine Saraswati, abounding in food, protect us in combat, and, like Pushan, give us gifts.
