- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—a valiant
- अस्ता इव (*astā iva*)—archer
- शत्र्यान् (*śatryān*)—like one who strikes and drives away enemies
- (उषाः (*uṣāḥ*)—the goddess Uṣas)
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—darkness
- अपेजते (*apejate*)—she strikes and drives away
- अजिरः (*ajiraḥ*)—swift-moving
- वोळ्हा न (*voḷhā na*)—like a leader of an army
- बाधते (*bādhate*)—she afflicts the darkness

### Printed p. 457

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The golden-hued and resplendent rays carry this goddess Uṣas, who is the bestower of auspiciousness, of extensive form and renowned. As a valiant archer strikes and drives away enemies, the goddess Uṣas strikes and drives away the darkness. Like a swift-moving leader of an army, she afflicts the darkness.

##### English translation
Ruddy and resplendent cows bear the auspicious, expanding, illustrious dawn : like a warrior, who, casting his darts, or a swift charger scattering enemies, she drives away the glooms.

> सा न॒ आ व॑ह पृथुयामन्नृष्टे र॒यिं दि॑वो दुहितरिष॒यध्यै॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुगा । उत । ते । सुपथा । पर्वतेषु । अवाते । अपः । तरसि । स्वभानो इति  
> स्वभानो ।  
> सा । नः । आ । वह । पृथुयामन् । ऋष्टे । रयिं । दिवः । दुहितः । इषयध्यै ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषो देवि पर्वतेषूतॆ दुर्गॆष्टप्यवाते गमनसाधनरहिते देशे सुपथा
> सुपथानि मार्गाणि सुगा सुगानि सुखेन गम्यानि ते तव भवंति । स्वभानो हे
> स्वप्रकाशेऽपोऽंतरिक्षमाकाशं । आप इत्यंतरिक्षनामसु पाठात् । सामुद्रिकीरपो वा
> तरसि । पृथुयामन् पृथुरथ ऋष्टे दर्शनीये दिवो दुहितरंतरिक्षुसुते हे उषो
> देवि सा त्वमिषयध्या एषणीयं धनं नोऽस्मभ्यमा वह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O goddess Uṣas, in mountains, that is in inaccessible places, and in places without means of passage, good paths that are easy to travel with ease are yours. O self-luminous one, you cross the "apaḥ", that is the sky, since "āpaḥ" is read among the names of the sky; or else you cross the waters of the ocean. O you of the wide chariot, O beautiful one, O daughter of heaven, that is of the sky, goddess Uṣas: you, such as you are, bring to us the wealth that is to be desired.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Uṣas, the excellent paths and the means of easy travel that exist in the mountains and in the inaccessible strongholds without means of passage belong to you. O self-luminous goddess, you cross the sky. O Uṣas, daughter of the sky, you who have such renowned auspicious qualities, bring to us in your chariot, which has a wide expanse and an attractive form, the wealth that we desire.

##### English translation
Yours are good roads and easy to be traversed in mountains and inaccessible places : you pass self-irradating over the waters : bring to us, daughter of heaven, in your spacious and beatiful chariot, desirable riches.

O goddess Uṣas, you who, unobstructed, bear dear wealth upon your vehicles, which have the form of bulls, such as you are, bring me excellent wealth. ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O goddess Uṣas, when your dawning has taken place, even the birds fly up from their dwelling-place. Those who are sharers in oblations, or earners of food, since "pitu" is read among the names of food, the men, they too rise up. Further, O goddess Uṣas, you bring abundant desired wealth to the mortal who is near, the giver of oblations.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Uṣas, at the time of your manifestation even the birds fly away from their dwelling-places. Men engaged in earning food also awake, rise and move about. O divine Uṣas, bring abundant desired wealth to the sacrificer who is near you and offers oblations to you.

##### English translation
At your dawning, divine Ushas, the birds spring up from their nests, and men who have to gain their sustenance (arise) : you divine Ushas, bring ample wealth to the mortal who is near you, the offerer of the oblation.

## Sūkta 65 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषा स्वेति षडृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । अनुक्रम्यते
> च । एषास्येति । उषस्यं त्विति पूर्वसूक्त उक्तत्वादिदमप्युषोदेवताकं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाशिनशस्त्रयोरुक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning एषा स्वेति (*eṣā sveti*), of six ṛks, the fourth sūkta, is the vision of Bharadvāja and is in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said एषास्येति (*eṣāsyeti*) **GLOSS**. Since उषस्यं त्विति (*uṣasyaṃ tviti*) **GLOSS** has been stated in the previous sūkta, this one too has Uṣas as its deity. Its ritual use in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvina-śastra has been stated.

### Printed p. 461

##### Anuvāda

Translation: this sūkta एषा स्या (*eṣā syā*) is the fourth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has six ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta; the goddess Uṣas is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said एषा स्या (*eṣā syā*) **GLOSS**. It has already been stated earlier that this sūkta is used for the Prātaranuvāka and for the Āśvina-śastra mantras.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 65
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 1; Varga 6
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6
- Ṛṣi: भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*)
- Deity: उषाः (*uṣāḥ*)
- Metre: Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒षा स्या नो॑ दुहि॒ता दि॑वो॒जाः क्षि॒तीरु॒च्छंती॒ मानु॑षीरजीगः।  
> या भा॒नुना॒ रुश॑ता रा॒म्यास्वज्ञा॑यि ति॒रस्तम॑सश्चिद॒क्तून् ॥ - ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषा । स्या । नः । दुहिता । दिवःजाः । क्षितीः । उच्छंती । मानुषीः । अजीगरिति ।  
> या । भानुना । रुशता । राम्यासु । अज्ञायि । तिर॥ । तमसः । चित् । अक्तून् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषा स्या सा दिवोजा दिवो जाता अत एव दुहिता दिवः पुत्र्युषा नोऽस्मदर्थमुच्छंती तमांसि वर्जयंती क्षितीः प्रजाः मानुषीरजीगः । उद्दिरति । जीगर्तिर्गिरतिकर्मा वा । नि. ६-८ । इति यास्कः । प्रकाशयतीति यावत् । या रुशता दीप्यमानेन भानुना युक्ता राम्यासु याम्यासु रात्रिषु ॥ रेफयकारयोर्व्यत्यय॥ ॥ अक्तून्नक्षत्रादितेजांसि तमसश्चित् तमांसि च तिरस्तिरस्कुर्वत्यज्ञायि दृश्यते॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Uṣas is born of heaven and therefore is the daughter, the child of heaven. For us she drives away the darknesses and rouses the human peoples; "ajīgaḥ" means that she makes them manifest, that is she illumines them, and Yāska is cited for this (Ni. 6-8). She who, joined with a shining ray, in the nights, "rāmyā" being explained as "yāmyā", puts into the shade the lights of the stars and the like, and the darknesses as well, is seen as such.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- या (*yā*)—the goddess Uṣas who
- रुशता (*ruśatā*)—with bright
- भानुना (*bhānunā*)—rays
- राम्यासु (*rāmyāsu*)—that were in the night times
- अक्तून् (*aktūn*)—the stars and the like
- तमसश्चित् (*tamasaścit*)—likewise the darkness

### Printed p. 462

- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—concealing
- अज्ञायि (*ajñāyi*)—becomes visible, such as she is
- स्या (*syā*)—the renowned
- दिवोजाः (*divojāḥ*)—born of the heavenly world
- दुहिता (*duhitā*)—and the daughter of the heavenly world
- एषा (*eṣā*)—this goddess Uṣas
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- उच्छंती (*ucchaṃtī*)—destroying the darkness
- मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*) क्षितीः (*kṣitīḥ*)—the human peoples
- अजीगः (*ajīgaḥ*)—she illumines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The renowned goddess Uṣas, born of the heavenly world and daughter of the heavenly world, who becomes visible by her bright rays, concealing the stars and the like that shone in the night time, and likewise the darkness, destroys the darkness for us and illumines the human peoples.

##### English translation
This heaven-bron daughter (of th sky), driving away the darkness for us, makes visible humau beings : she who with bright lustre is perceived dissipating the glooms, and (extinguishing) the planets (shining) in the nights.

> अग्रं । यज्ञस्य । बृहतः । नयंतीः । वि । ताः । बाधंते । तमः । ऊर्म्यायाः ॥२॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चंद्ररथाः कांतिरथाः । चंद्रश्चंदतेः कांतिकर्मणः । नि. ११-५ । इति यास्कः ।
> ता उषसस्तत्तदानीं प्रातःकाले बृहतो बृंहणशीलस्य यज्ञ स्याग्रं मुखं नयंतीः
> संपादयंत्योऽरुणयुग्निररुणवर्णयुक्तैरश्वैर्वि ययुः । विस्तीर्णं यांति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Chandrarathāḥ" means those whose chariots are radiant; Yāska is cited for the sense of "candra" (Ni. 11-5). Those Uṣases, at that time, in the morning, bring forward the front, the head, of the great, growth-natured sacrifice, and go forth widely with horses of red colour.

### Printed p. 463

> चित्रं यथा भवति तथा भांति च । उर्मार्यया रात्रेः । अक्तुरूर्म्येति रात्रिनामसु
> पाशात् । तमो वि बाधंते । सम्यगपनयंति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They also shine wonderfully. "Ūrmyā" is read among the names of night, as is "aktu"; so they drive away the darkness of the night, that is they remove it completely.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चंद्ररथाः (*caṃdrarathāḥ*)—those who have chariots of attractive radiance
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the dawns
- तत् (*tat*)—in the morning time itself
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*)—of vast nature
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—the front part
- नयंतीः (*nayaṃtīḥ*)—securing
- अरुणयुग्भिः (*aruṇayugbhiḥ*)—of red colour
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with horses
- वि ययुः (*vi yayuḥ*)—they move about at will
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—in manifold ways
- भांति (*bhāṃti*)—they shine
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—they
- ऊर्मायाः (*ūrmāyāḥ*)—of the night time
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the darkness
- वि बाधंते (*vi bādhaṃte*)—they destroy completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The dawns, who have chariots of attractive radiance, in the morning time itself, securing the front part of the sacrifice, which is of vast nature, move about at will with horses of red colour. Shining in manifold ways, they destroy completely the darkness of the night time.

##### English translation
The Dawns in beautiful chariots drawn by purple steeds in pairs, shine gloriously as they proceed (along the heaven) : bringing on the commencement of the great (morning) sacrifice, they disperse the darkness of the night.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषसो दाशुषे हविषां दात्रे मर्त्याय श्रवः कीर्तिं वाजं बलमिषमन्नमूर्जं रसं च वहंतीर्वहंत्यो यूयं मघोनीर्धनवत्यः पत्यमाना
> गच्छंत्योऽद्य विधते परिचरते मह्यं वीरवत्पुत्रपौत्रादिसहितमवोऽन्नं । सिनमव
> इत्यन्ननामसु पाठात् । रत्नं धनं च । श्वात्रं रत्नमिति धननामसु पाठात् । नि धात ।
> नितरां धत्त ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣases, to the mortal who gives oblations you bear fame, strength, food and sustenance; being wealthy and going forth today, bestow constantly on me, who serve you, food together with heroes, that is with sons, grandsons and the like, and wealth as well. "Sinam" and "avaḥ" are read among the names of food, and "śvātram" and "ratnam" are read among the names of wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—O goddesses Uṣas
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—who offers oblations
- मर्त्याय (*martyāya*)—to the man
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—fame
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—strength
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—and sap
- वहंतीः (*vahaṃtīḥ*)—you who bear
- मघोनीः (*maghonīḥ*)—as wealthy ones
- पत्यमानाः (*patyamānāḥ*)—going about
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to me also who worship you
- वीरवत् (*vīravat*)—together with heroic sons and the like
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—food
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—and wealth
- नि धात (*ni dhāta*)—give completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddesses Uṣas, you who bear fame, strength, food and sap to the man who offers oblations, going about as wealthy ones, give at this time completely, to me also who worship you, food together with heroic sons and the like, and wealth.

##### English translation
Dawns, bringing fame, and food, and sustenance, and strength to the mortal, the donor (of the oblation). abounding in wealth, and proceeding (through the sky), bestow upon the worshipper to-day food, with male descendants and riches.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दा हि वो॑ विध॒ते रत्न॒मस्ती॒दा वी॒राय॑ दा॒शुष॑ उषासः ।  
> इ॒दा विप्रा॑य॒ जर॑ते॒ यदु॒क्का नि ष्म॒ माव॑ते वहथा पु॒रा  ॑
> चित् ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 465

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदा । हि । वः । विधते । रत्नं । अस्ति । इदा । वीराय । दाशुषे । उषसः ।  
> इदा । विप्राय । जरते । यत् । उक्ता । नि । स्म । मावते । वहथ । पुरा । चित् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषस इदा हीदानीमेव वो युष्माकं विधते परिचरते दातुं रत्नं
> धनमस्ति । इदा हीदानीमेव वीराय प्रेरयित्रे हविषां दाशुषे यजमानाय
> दातुं वो रत्नमस्ति । इदा हीदानीमेव विप्राय प्राज्ञाय जरते स्तुवते
> दातुं वो रत्नमस्ति । यद्यस्मिन्विप्र उक्तोक्तनामकानि स्तोत्राणि विद्यंते मावते
> मत्सदृशाय यजमानाय तद्रत्नं नि वहथ । पुरा चित् पुरापि रत्नं मह्यं दत्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣases, even now, at this very moment, you have wealth to give to the one who serves you. At this very moment you have wealth to give to the hero, the impeller, the giver of oblations, the sacrificer. At this very moment you have wealth to give to the sage, the wise one who praises you. In whom the stotras called ukthas exist, to that sacrificer, who is like me, bring that wealth. Even before this, wealth was given to me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—O goddesses Uṣas
- इदा हि (*idā hi*)—now itself
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to give to the one who offers worship
- रत्नं (*ratnaṃ*)—wealth
- अस्ति (*asti*)—there is
- इदा (*idā*) (हि (*hi*))—now itself
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—who offers oblations
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer (you have wealth to give)
- इदा (*idā*) (हि (*hi*))—now itself
- विप्राय (*viprāya*)—the wise one
- जरते (*jarate*)—and the praiser, to the sacrificer, there is wealth to give
- यत् (*yat*)—in which sacrificer
- उक्था (*ukthā*)—the stotras called ukthas exist
- मावते (*māvate*)—to that sacrificer also, who is like me
- नि वहथ (*ni vahatha*)—fill with wealth
- पुरा चित् (*purā cit*)—you gave to me even before

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddesses Uṣas, now itself there is wealth to give to the one who offers worship to you. Now itself there is wealth to give to the sacrificer who offers oblations. Now itself there is wealth to give to the sacrificer who is wise and a praiser. O Uṣases, to the sacrificer who, like me, has stotras of the called kind, bring and fill wealth, just as you gave it to us before.

##### English translation
Verily, Dawns, there is at present wealth to give to your worshipper, to the man offering (oblations), to the sage repeating your praise ; if the praises (are accepted), then bring to him who is like me such wealth as has been formerly bestowed (upon myself).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दा हि त॑ उषो अद्रिसानो गो॒त्रा गवा॒मंगि॑रसो गृ॒णंति॑ ।  
> व्य१॒॑ १ केण॑ बिभिदु॒र्ब्रह्म॑णा च स॒त्या नृ॒णाम॑भवद्दे॒वहू॑तिः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदा । हि । ते । उषः । अद्रिसानो इत्यद्रिसानो । गोत्रा । गवां । अंगिरसः ।  
> गृणंति ।  
> वि । अर्केण । बिभिदुः । ब्रह्मणा । च । सत्या । नृणां । अभवत् । देवरूतिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषोऽद्रिसानो आदृतसानो ते तव प्रसादादिदा हि सद्य एव गवां गोत्रा
> संघानंगिरसो गृणंति । उत्सृजंति । तथा च निगमांतरं । गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो
> यदंगिरः । ऋग्वे. २-२३-१८ । इति । अर्कॆणार्चनीयेन ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रेण वि
> बिभिदुः । तमांसि विदारयंति च । नृणां नेत्यणां तेषामंगिरसां देवहूतिर्देवविषया स्तुतिः सत्या सत्यफलाभवत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣas, you of honoured summit, by your grace, now itself, the Aṅgirases release the herds of cattle. So another Vedic passage says गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो यदंगिरः (*gavāṃ gotramudasṛjo yadaṃgiraḥ*) (Ṛgve. 2-23-18)**NOTE** **GLOSS**. With the worshipful brahma, that is the stotra, they also split the darknesses. The invocation of the gods, the praise directed to the gods, of those leaders, the Aṅgirases, became true, that is fruitful with truth.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas
- ते (*te*)—by your grace
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—the Aṅgirases
- अद्रिसानो (*adrisāno*)—from the peak regions of the mountain
- इदा हि (*idā hi*)—now itself
- गवां गोत्रा (*gavāṃ gotrā*)—the herd of cattle
- गृणंति (*gṛṇaṃti*)—they release
- अर्केण (*arkeṇa*)—worthy of worship
- ब्रह्मणा च (*brahmaṇā ca*)—with the stotra also
- वि बिभिदुः (*vi bibhiduḥ*)—they have destroyed the darkness
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—of the leaders, the Aṅgirases
- देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)—the praise directed to the gods
- सत्या (*satyā*)—possessing the fruit of truth
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Uṣas, by your grace the Aṅgirases release now itself the herds of cattle from the peak regions of the mountain. With the stotra worthy of worship also they have destroyed the darkness. The praise directed to the gods, of the leaders, the Aṅgirases, became possessed of the fruit of truth.

##### English translation
Verily, Ushas. the Angirasas through your (favour) recover the herd of cattle from the summit of the mountain : by adoration and prayer they

### Printed p. 467

have divided (the rock) : unfailing was the praise of the gods uttered by the leaders (of rites).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒च्छा दि॑वो दुहितः प्रश्न॒वन्नो॑ भरद्वाज॒वद्वि॑ध॒ते म॑घोनि।  
> सु॒वीरं॑ र॒यिं गृ॑ण॒ते रि॑रीह्युरुगा॒यमधि॑ धेहि॒ श्रवो॑ नः ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उच्छृ । दिवः । दुहितरिति । प्रश्नवत् । नः । भरद्वाजवत् । विधते । मघोनि ।  
> सुवीरं । रयिं । गृणते । रिरीहि । उरुगायं । अधि । धेहि । श्रवः । नः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे दिवो दुहितरुषः प्रत्नवत्पुरातनेभ्य इव नोऽस्मदर्थमुच्छ । तमांसि
> वर्जय । हे मघोनि भरद्वाजवद्विधते परिचरते । भरद्वाजवदिति वचनादन्योऽप्यस्ति
> भरद्वाजः । तथा च ब्राह्मणं । प्राणो वै भरद्वाजवदिति । गृणते स्तुतिं कुर्वते
> मह्यं सुवीरं कल्याणपुत्रपौत्रादियुक्तं रयिं धनं रिरीहि । देहि । किंच नोऽस्मभ्यमुरुगायं बहुभिर्गातव्यं श्रवोऽन्नमधि धेहि । अधिकं प्रयच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, as for the ancients, so for us drive away the darkness. O wealthy one, to me who serve you, as to Bharadvāja: the word "bharadvājavat" implies that there is yet another Bharadvāja, and so a Brāhmaṇa says प्राणो वै भरद्वाजवदिति (*prāṇo vai bharadvājavaditi*) **GLOSS**. To me who offer praise give wealth together with excellent sons, grandsons and the like. Further, bestow upon us in abundance food, which is to be sung by many; give more.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवो दुहितः (*divo duhitaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the heavenly world
- प्रत्नवत् (*pratnavat*)—just as you favoured in the past
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us also
- उच्छृ (*ucchṛ*)—disperse the darkness
- मघोनि (*maghoni*)—O goddess Uṣas who are possessed of wealth
- भरद्वाजवत् (*bharadvājavat*)—just as you gave in the past to Bharadvāja
- विधते (*vidhate*)—to me too who offer worship to you
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—and who praise you
- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—together with heroic sons and the like
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- रिरीहि (*rirīhi*)—give
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- उरुगायं (*urugāyaṃ*)—praised by many
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food
- अधि धेहि (*adhi dhehi*)—give in abundance

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the heavenly world, as you favoured in the past, so for us also destroy the darkness and bring about light. O goddess Uṣas, who are possessed of wealth, as you gave in the past to Bharadvāja, so give to me also, who offer worship to you and praise you, wealth together with heroic sons and the like. Provide us also with food that is praised by many.

## Sūkta 66 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वपुर्नु तदित्येकादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं
> मारुतं । कथा चानुक्रम्यते । वपुर्न्वेकादश मारुतमिति ॥ व्यूळ्की दशरात्रे
> षष्ठेऽहन्याग्नि मारुत इदं सूक्तं मारुतनिविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । हविष्कांतं वपुर्नु
> तत् । आ. ८-८ । इति ॥ वैश्वदेवे पर्वणि मारुतसप्तकपालस्य प्र चित्रमर्कमिति याज्या ।
> प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुरायेति नवानुयाज्याः । आ. २-१६ । इति ॥ एकादशिने
> मारुते पशौ प्र चित्रमर्कमित्येपैव याज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते
> तुरायारा इवेदचरमा अहेव । आ. ३ ७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta वपुर्नु तत् (*vapurnu tat*), of eleven ṛks, is the fifth sūkta; it is the vision of Bharadvāja, in the Triṣṭubh metre, with the Maruts as deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said वपुर्न्वेकादश मारुतमिति (*vapurnvekādaśa mārutamiti*) **GLOSS**. In the Daśarātra, on the sixth day, in the Āgnimāruta, this sūkta is placed as the sūkta of the Marut nivid.**NOTE** It is set out in the sūtra हविष्कांतं वपुर्नु तत् (*haviṣkāṃtaṃ vapurnu tat*) (Ā. 8-8). In the Vaiśvadeva parvan, for the Marut offering in seven potsherds, प्र चित्रमर्कमिति (*pra citramarkamiti*) is the yājyā, and the nine anuyājyās begin प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुरायेति (*pra citramarkaṃ gṛṇate turāyeti*) (Ā. 2-16). In the Marut animal sacrifice of the Ekādaśin, this same प्र चित्रमर्कमित्येपैव (*pra citramarkamityepaiva*) is the yājyā; it is set out in the sūtra प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुरायारा इवेदचरमा अहेव (*pra citramarkaṃ gṛṇate turāyārā ivedacaramā aheva*) (Ā. 3-7).

##### Anuvāda

Translation: this sūkta वपुर्नु तत् (*vapurnu tat*) is the fifth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta; the Maruts are the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said वपुर्न्वॆकादश मारुतं (*vapurnvèkādaśa mārutaṃ*) **GLOSS**. On the sixth day of the sacrifice called Vyūḷha Daśarātra, in the middle of the Āgnimāruta śastra mantras, this sūkta is to be recited as the nivid-sūkta of the Marut deity, as is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra हविष्मांतं वपुर्नु तत् (*haviṣmāṃtaṃ vapurnu tat*) (Ā. 8-8).**NOTE** In the Parveṣṭi connected with the Vaiśvadeva, in the Mārutasaptakapāla homa, the ninth ṛk प्र चित्रमर्क० (*pra citramarka0*) is to be recited as yājyā mantra, as is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्र चित्रमर्क० गृणते तुरायेति नवानुयाजः (*pra citramarka0 gṛṇate turāyeti navānuyājaḥ*) (Ā. 2-16).**NOTE** In the Marut animal sacrifice made on the day of the sacrifice called Ekādaśin, the ṛk प्र चित्रमर्क० (*pra citramarka0*) is to be recited as yājyā mantra, as is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्र चित्रमर्क० गृणते तुरायरा इवेद चरमा अहेव (*pra citramarka0 gṛṇate turāyarā iveda caramā aheva*) (Ā. 3-7).

- Metre: Triṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वपु॒र्नु तच्चि॑कि॒तुषे॑ चिदस्तु समा॒नं नाम॑ धे॒नु पत्य॑मानं ।  
> मर्ते॑ष्व॒न्यद्दो॒हसे॑ पी॒पाय॑ स॒कृच्छु॒क्रं दु॑दुहे॒ पृश्नि॒ रूधः॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वपुः । नु । तत् । चिकितुषे । चित् । अस्तु । समानं । नाम । धेनु । पत्यमानं ।  
> मर्तेषु । अन्यत् । दोहसे । पीपाय । सकृत् । शुक्रं । दुदुहे । पृश्निः । ऊधः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्प्रसिद्धं समानमेकरूपं । मरुतः सर्वदा समानरूपाः । तथा च निगमांतरं । अजेष्ठासो अकनिष्ठास एते । ऋग्वे. ५-६०-५ । इति । नाम स्थिराणामपि
> नामकं धेनु प्रीणयित्यु पत्यमानं सर्वदा गच्छद्वपुर्मरुतां रूपं चिकितुषे
> विदुषे स्तोत्रे नु क्षिप्रमस्तु । प्रादुर्भवतु । चिदिति पूरकं । किंच तद्रूपं
> मर्त्येषु मर्त्यलोकेऽन्यदोषधिवनस्पत्यादिकं दोहसे कामान्डोग्गुं पीपाय ।
> आप्याययति । किंच मरुतामेव निर्देशात्पृश्निरंतरिक्षं सकृत्संवत्सरस्य वर्षासु
> शुक्रं शुक्लवर्णमूध उदकं दुदुहे । क्षरति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That well-known form is the same, that is, of one form; the Maruts are always of the same form. So another Vedic passage says अजेष्ठासो अकनिष्ठास एते (*ajeṣṭhāso akaniṣṭhāsa ete*) (Ṛgve. 5-60-5)**NOTE** **GLOSS**. "Nāma" is the namer even of those who are firm. The pleasing, ever-moving form of the Maruts: may it quickly be manifest to the knowing praiser; "cid" is a filler. Further, that form, among mortals, in the mortal world, makes the herbs, trees and the like other than man swell, so as to yield desires. Further, from the mention of the Maruts alone, Pṛśni, the atmosphere, once in the year, in the rains, milks the bright udder, that is the water, that is, lets it flow.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तत् (*tat*)—the renowned
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—having one form
- नाम (*nāma*)—that which makes strong enemies submissive
- धेनु (*dhenu*)—the pleasing
- पत्यमानं (*patyamānaṃ*)—and ever moving
- वपुः (*vapuḥ*)—form of the Maruts
- चिकितुषे (*cikituṣe*)—to the wise praiser
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be visible and appear (that same troop of Maruts)
- मर्तॆषु (*martèṣu*)—in the human world
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—the herbs, trees and the like
- दोहसे (*dohase*)—for the accomplishment of the desired ends of man

### Printed p. 470

- पीपाय (*pīpāya*)—it makes grow (by the will of these Maruts)
- पृश्निः (*pṛśniḥ*)—the atmosphere
- सकृत् (*sakṛt*)—at the respective time of the year
- शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*)—of bright colour
- ऊधः (*ūdhaḥ*)—the water
- दुदुहे (*duduhe*)—milks

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The renowned form of the Maruts, which is of one form, makes powerful enemies submissive, is pleasing and ever moving, becomes visible before the wise praiser. That same troop of Maruts makes the herbs, trees and the like in the human world grow for the accomplishment of the desired ends of man. By the will of these Maruts, the atmosphere also, in the rainy season of the year, milks bright-coloured water.

##### English translation
May the like-formed, benevolent, all-pervading, all-humiliating troop (of the Maruts) be promptly with the prudent man : the troop that ever cherishes, all that amongst mortals is designed to yield (them) advantage and (at whose will) Prishni gives milk from (her) bright udder once (in the year).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts shine like fires that are being kindled; they grow twofold and threefold, that is they increase as they wish. The chariots of these Maruts are free of dust (continued below).

and have golden fittings; that is, the Maruts' chariots are golden and ornamented with gold. Those Maruts appear together with riches and with strengths. So another Vedic passage says ये पृषतीभिर्यष्टिभिः (*ye pṛṣatībhiryaṣṭibhiḥ*) (Ṛgve. 1-37-2)**NOTE** **GLOSS**.

The chariots of the Maruts, who blaze and shine like fires and who increase twofold and threefold, are free of dust and made of gold. Those same Maruts manifest themselves together with riches and with powers.

##### English translation
Unsoiled by dust the golden chariots of those Maruts, who are shining like kindled fires, enlarging themselves (at will) twofold and three-fold, and (charged) with riches and virile energies, are manifest.

> महो महतामेषां माता सा पृश्निर्मही महती । किंच सा पृश्निः सुभ्वे नृणां
> सम्यक् भवनाय गर्भमुदकमाधात् । आदधाति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts who are sons of Rudra, the sprinkler, the supporting Pṛśni, that is the atmosphere, is able to bear them. "Vide hi" means that it is known to all that the mother of these great ones, that Pṛśni, is great. Further, that Pṛśni has conceived the germ, that is the water, for the good existence of men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- माळ्पुषः (*māḷpuṣaḥ*)—of the showerer of rain
- रुद्रस्य (*rudrasya*)—of Rudra
- पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)—who are in the form of sons
- ये (*ye*)—the Maruts who
- संति (*saṃti*)—exist
- यांश्चो नु (*yāṃśco nu*)—whom, the Maruts
- भरध्वै (*bharadhvai*)—to bear
- दाधृविः (*dādhṛviḥ*)—the atmosphere, the supporter, becomes able
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of such great Maruts
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- सा (*sā*)—Pṛśni
- मही (*mahī*)—is of great form
- विदे हि (*vide hi*)—this is a matter known to all
- सा इत् पृश्निः (*sā it pṛśniḥ*)—that same Pṛśni
- सुभ्वे (*subhve*)—to bring about the welfare of all men
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the water
- आधात् (*ādhāt*)—has received and borne

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts who are in the form of sons of Rudra, the showerer of rain, and whom the atmosphere, the supporter, is able to bear: it is a matter known to all that Pṛśni, the mother of such great Maruts, is of great form. That same Pṛśni has received and borne the water to bring about the welfare of all men.

##### English translation
They (who are) the sons of the showerer Rudra, whom the nursing (firmament is able) to sustain, and of whom, the mighty ones, it is known that the great Prishni has received the germ for the benefit (of man).

> निर्यद्दु॒हे शुच॒योऽनु॒ जोष॒मनु॑ श्रि॒या त॒न्व॑मु॒क्षमा॑णाः ॥ ४ ॥

> निः । यत् । दुह्रे । शुचयः । अनु । जोषं । अनु । श्रिया । तन्वं । उक्षमाणाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये प्रसिद्धा मरुतो जनुषो जनान् स्तोत्कृन्यायायेन गमनसाधनेन
> नेषंते न गच्छंति । किं तेषां रक्षणीयत्वाभावाद्यमनाभावो नेत्याह । अंतः
> संतः सर्वेषां हृदि वर्तमाना एवावद्यानि पापानि पुनानाः शोधयंतः । तथा च
> निगमांतरं । प्राणा वै मरुतः स्वापयः । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-१६ । इति । अतः सर्वप्राणिनां
> हृदि वर्तमानत्वात्तेषां गमनं नास्तीति । अध्यात्मं प्राणरूपेणावस्थानं दर्शितं
> भवति शीघ्रगामित्वं तु तेषामधिदैवतरूपेणेति द्रष्टव्यं । यद्यदा शुचयो
> दीप्यमाना मरुतो जोषमनु स्तोत्कृणां काममनु निर्दुहे नितरां दुहंत्युदकं । तथा श्रिया दीप्यान्वनुगतास्तन्वमात्मीयं शरीरं प्रकाशयंत उक्षमाणा
> भूमिं सिंचंतो भवंति । यद्वा । तन्नं विस्तीर्णं यथा भवति तथोक्षमाणा भूमिं
> सिंचंतो भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The well-known Maruts do not go to the people who praise them by any means of going. Is there then no going because there is no one to be protected? He says no: being within, dwelling in the hearts of all, they purify the sins. And so another Vedic passage says प्राणा वै मरुतः स्वापयः (*prāṇā vai marutaḥ svāpayaḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 3-16) **GLOSS**. Therefore, because they dwell in the hearts of all beings, they have no going. Thereby their standing in the self in the form of vital breaths is shown, while their swift-going is to be understood as belonging to their form as deities. When the shining Maruts milk out the water in accordance with the desire of the praisers, then, accompanied by splendour, making their own body shine, they sprinkle the earth. Or else: they sprinkle the earth in such a way that it is broad; this is the meaning.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—the Maruts who
- अंतः संतः (*aṃtaḥ saṃtaḥ*)—being within the hearts of all people
- अवद्यानि (*avadyāni*)—all the sins of each
- पुनानाः (*punānāḥ*)—purify (such purifying Maruts)
- जनुषः (*januṣaḥ*)—facing the praising people
- अया (*ayā*)—in the means of going, chariots and the like
- न ईषंते नु (*na īṣaṃte nu*)—there is no toil of having to go
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)—the shining Maruts
- जोषमनु (*joṣamanu*)—in accordance with the wish of the praisers
- निः दुह्रे (*niḥ duhre*)—milk out rain in abundance, then
- श्रिया (*śriyā*)—with splendour
- अनु (*anu*)—being accompanied
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—making their own body shine
- उक्षमाणाः (*ukṣamāṇāḥ*)—they are those who pour rain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who being within the hearts of all people purify all the sins of each, such purifying Maruts have no toil of having to go to the praising people in chariots, the means of going. When the shining Maruts milk out rain in abundance in accordance with the wish of the praisers, then, accompanied by splendour and making their own body shine, they are those who pour rain.

### Printed p. 474

##### English translation
They who approach not to men by any conveyance, being already
in their hearts, purifying their defects : when brilliant they supply their
milk (the rain) for the gratification (of their worshippers) : they are
watering the earth (manifesting their collective) form with splendour.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न । ये । स्तौनाः । अयासः । मह्ना । नु । चित् । सुदानुः । अव । यासत् ।  
> उग्रान् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> येषु प्रसिद्धेषु मरुत्तु धृष्णु धर्षकं मारुतं नाम मरुत्संज्ञकं
> शस्त्रमा दधाना उच्चारयंतोऽया उपागच्छंतः स्तोतारो मक्षु क्षिप्रं दोहसे
> कामान्दोग्नुं क्षमा भवंति । नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । ये स्तौनाः स्तेनास्तिरोहिता वा
> स्तोतृधनानामपहर्तारोऽयासो गंतारो भवंति । मह्ना महत्वेन युक्ताश्च
> भवंति उग्रांस्तान्कुद्धान् सुदानुः शोभनहविर्दानोऽवयजमानोऽव यासत् ।
> अवयजते । अपगतक्रोधान् करोति । नेति संप्रत्यर्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among those well-known Maruts, the worshippers who approach them and recite the assailing (धृष्णु (*dhṛṣṇu*)) Marut-named śastra are quickly able to milk out, that is, to obtain, their desires. The particle "na" is used here in the sense of "now". Those who are thieves or hidden plunderers of the worshippers' wealth become runaways, and they are also endowed with greatness. Such fierce, angry ones are pacified by the sacrificer, the giver of good oblations: he makes them free of anger. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येषु (*yeṣu*)—in regard to those very Maruts
- धृष्णु (*dhṛṣṇu*)—the enemy-restraining
- मारुतं नाम (*mārutaṃ nāma*)—the Marut-named śastra-mantra
- आ दधानाः (*ā dadhānāḥ*)—reciting
- अयाः (*ayāḥ*)—the approaching worshippers
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- दोहसे (*dohase*)—become able to obtain their desired ends

### Printed p. 475

- ये (*ye*)—which thieves, plunderers of wealth
- अयासः (*ayāsaḥ*)—run away (and)
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by their greatness
- उग्रान् (*ugrān*)—are terrible, such enemies
- सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)—the excellent giver, the sacrificer
- अव यासत् (*ava yāsat*)—becomes able to destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those very Maruts: the worshippers who approach them, reciting the enemy-restraining, Marut-named śastra-mantra, are quickly able to obtain their desired ends. The thieves, plunderers of wealth, who run away, and those who are terrible by their greatness, such enemies the excellent giver, the sacrificer, becomes able to destroy.

##### English translation
Approaching nigh to whom, and repeating the mighty name of the Maruts, (the worshipper is able) quickly to obtain (his wishes): the liberal donor pacifies the angry Maruts, who are otherwise in their might the the resistless plunderers (of their wealth).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त इदु॒ग्राः शव॑सा धृ॒ष्णुषे॑णा उ॒भे यु॑जंत॒ रोद॑सी  ॒॑
> सु॒मेके॑ । ॑ 
> अध॑ स्मैषु रोद॒सी स्वशो॑चि॒राम॑वत्सु तस्थौ॒ न रोकः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । इत् । उग्राः । शवसा । धृष्णुसेनाः । उभे इति । युजंत । रोदसी इति ।  
> सुमेके इति सुमेके ।  
> अध । स्म । एषु । रोदसी । स्वशोचिः । आ । अमवत्सु । तस्थौ । न । रोकः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते मरुत उग्राः शवसा बलेन वेगेन युक्ता धृष्णुषेणा धर्षकसेनाः
> सुमेके सुरूपे उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य युजंत । योजयंति । वृष्टा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those fierce Maruts, endowed with strength and speed and having assailing armies, join together the two beautiful ones, heaven and earth. The intention is that by raining they gratify the earth.

### Printed p. 476

> पृथिवीं तर्पयंतीत्यभिप्रायः । अध स्मापि चैषु येषु मरुत्सु रोदसी रुद्रस्य
> पत्नि माध्यमिकी वाक् स्वशोचिः स्वदीप्तिर्वर्ततेऽमवत्सु बलवत्सु तेषु रोको
> दीप्तिर्बाधको ना ना तस्थौ । न तिष्ठति । न निःसरत्येवेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And moreover, in these Maruts, the two worlds, who are the wife of Rudra, that is, the speech of the middle region, are self-radiant; in these mighty ones the obstructing light does not stand, that is, it does not come forth at all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्राः (*ugrāḥ*)—the terrible to enemies
- धृष्णुषेणाः (*dhṛṣṇuṣeṇāḥ*)—possessed of an army that overcomes enemies
- ते इत् (*te it*)—those very Maruts
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—endowed with strength
- सुमेके (*sumeke*)—of beautiful form
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- युजंत (*yujaṃta*)—they join together
- अध स्म (*adha sma*)—moreover
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—the goddess of the middle region, speech, wife of Rudra
- स्वशोचिः (*svaśociḥ*)—self-radiant
- एषु (*eṣu*)—abides in these very Maruts
- अमवत्सु (*amavatsu*)—in these mighty Maruts
- रोकः (*rokaḥ*)—the power that obstructs light
- न आ तस्थौ (*na ā tasthau*)—cannot exist

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those very Maruts, terrible to enemies and possessed of an army that overcomes enemies, endowed with strength, join together both heaven and earth, which are of beautiful form. Moreover, the goddess of the middle region, the wife of Rudra, self-radiant, abides in these very Maruts. In these mighty Maruts the power that obstructs light cannot exist.

##### English translation
Those fierce and powerfully arrayed (Maruts) unite by their strength
the two beautiful (regions) heaven and earth ; in them, the self-radiant,
heaven and earth abide : the obstruction (of light) dwells not in those
mighty ones.

### Printed p. 477

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो वो युष्माकं संबंधी यामो रथोऽनेनः पापरहितं यथा
> भवति तथास्तु प्रादुर्भवतु । किंच यं याममरथीः । रथिः सारथीः । न रथिररथीः ।
> असारथिरपि स्तोताजति प्रेरयति स रथोऽनश्वश्चिदश्वरहितोऽप्यनवसः पथ्यधनरहितोऽनभीशुः पाशरहितोऽपि रजस्तूरुदकस्य प्रेरकः साधन् स्तोतृणां कामान्
> साधयन् रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ पथ्याः पथोऽंतरिक्षमार्गान् वि याति । विविधं
> गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, may your chariot be free of sin, that is, may it appear free of fault. Moreover, the chariot which a worshipper drives, impels, even though he is no charioteer (a charioteer is one who drives; he who is not is an "arathī"), is without horses, without provisions for the journey, without reins; it urges the water, accomplishes the desires of the worshippers, and travels variously through heaven and earth and the paths of the firmament. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वः (*vaḥ*)—belonging to you
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which chariot
- अरथीः चित् (*arathīḥ cit*)—even though he is not a charioteer
- अजति (*ajati*)—the worshipper impels
- अनश्वः (*anaśvaḥ*)—which is without horses
- अनवसः (*anavasaḥ*)—which travels a road free of grass and the like
- अनभीशुः (*anabhīśuḥ*)—which is without traces
- रजसूः (*rajasūḥ*)—which impels water
- सादन् (*sādan*)—which fulfils the desires of the praisers
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—in heaven and earth
- पथ्याः (*pathyāḥ*)—and on the path of the firmament
- वि याति (*vi yāti*)—which travels especially
- यामः (*yāmaḥ*)—the chariot
- अनेनः (*anenaḥ*)—is free of sin

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, even without a charioteer, the worshipper, by your favour, can impel your chariot. That chariot, which is without horses, travels on a road free of grass and the like, is without traces, impels water, fulfils the desires of the praisers and travels especially in heaven and earth and on the path of the firmament, is free of sin.

##### English translation
May your chariot, Maruts, be devoid of wickedness ; that which (the worshipper) impels, and which without driver without horses, without provender, without traces, scatter watering and accomplishing (desires) traverses heaven and earth and the paths (of the firmament).

> अध द्योः । ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । अस्य । वर्ता । न । तरुता । नु । अस्ति । मरुतः । यं । अवथ । वाजसात् ।  
> तोके । वा । गोषु । तनये । यं । अप्सु । सः । व्रजं । दर्ता । पार्ये ।  
> अध । द्योः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो वाजसात् संग्रामे यमवथ रक्षथ अस्य जनस्य वर्ता प्रेरको
> नास्ति । अस्य तरुता नु हिंसिता च नास्ति । अधापि च तोके पुत्रे तनये पौत्रे धने
> वा गोषु वाप्सु वा निमित्तभूतेषु यमवथ स पार्ये संग्रामे द्योर्दिप्तस्यापि
> विजिगीषोर्वा शत्र्वर्जं गवां संघं दर्ता दारयिता भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, the man whom you protect in battle has no one to impel him (or hinder him), and no destroyer. Moreover, the man whom you protect, with regard to son, grandson, wealth, cows or waters, becomes in the decisive battle the one who breaks up the herd of cattle, the collection of cows, of the enemy, even though that enemy be fiery or eager for victory. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—in battle
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whichever man
- अवथ (*avatha*)—you protect
- अस्य (*asya*)—for such a man
- वर्ता (*vartā*)—a hinderer
- न आस्ति (*na āsti*)—there is not
- तरुता नु (*tarutā nu*)—a destroyer
- न (*na*)—there is not
- आध (*ādha*)—and
- तोके (*toke*)—for the sake of a son
- तनये (*tanaye*)—for the sake of a grandson
- गोषु वा (*goṣu vā*)—or on account of cows
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—for the sake of water
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whomever you protect
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- पार्ये (*pārye*)—in the battle
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—even though the enemy is strong in power
- व्रजं (*vrajaṃ*)—his herd of cattle
- दर्ता (*dartā*)—he is able to scatter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, the man whom you protect in battle has no hinderer and no destroyer. The man whom you protect for the sake of a son, a grandson, or on account of cows, or for the sake of water, is able, even though the enemy in battle is strong in power, to scatter his herd of cattle.

##### English translation
There is no propeller, no obstructer, of him, whom Maruts, you protect in battle : he whom (you prosper) with sons, grandsons, cattle, and water, is war the despoiler of the herds of his ardent (foe).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र चि॒त्रम॒र्कं गृ॑ण॒ते तु॒राय॒ मारु॑ताय॒ स्वत॑वसे भरध्वं ।  
> ये सहां॑सि॒ सह॑सा॒ सहं॑ते॒ रेज॑ते अग्ने पृथि॒वी म॒खेभ्यः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । चित्रं । अर्कं । गृणते । तुराय । मारुताय । स्वतवसे । भरध्वं ।  
> ये । सहांसि । सहसा । सहंते । रेजते । अग्ने । पृथिवी । मखेभ्यः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने गृणते शब्दं कुर्वते स्तूयमानाय वा तुराय त्वरिताय स्वतवसे
> स्वभूतबलाय मारुताय मरुतां गणाय चित्रं दर्शनीयमर्कमन्नं हविः ।
> सधार्क इत्यन्ननामसु पाठात् । प्र भरध्वं । त्वत्सहायभूता ऋत्तिजस्त्वं च सर्वेयूयं प्रभरत ॥ यथा लोके बहुष्टेककार्यकरेषु मुख्यमेकं संबोध्य
> यूयमेवं कुरुतेति प्रार्थना तत्वदत्रापि मुख्यमग्निमेकमेव संबोध्य
> प्रभरध्वमिति बहुवचनप्रयोगः ॥ ये मरुतः सहांसि शत्रोणां बलानि सहसा बलेन
> सहंते अभिभवंति मखेभ्यो मंहनीयेभ्यो मरुद्भो भयात्पृथिवी रेजते ।
> कंपते ॥ मारुतायेति तद्धितवृत्तावंतर्भूतानामपि मरुतां बुद्ध्या प्रविभागात्
> य इति प्रत्यवमर्शः । यथा महाभाष्ये । अथ शब्दानुशासनं । केषां शब्दानां ।
> म. १.१-१ इति । यथा ना लोके । राजपुरुष इत्युक्ते कस्य राज्य इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, to the host of Maruts, who are praising or being praised, swift, and possessed of their own strength, bring forth a wonderful, beautiful अर्कं (*arkaṃ*), that is, food, an oblation, since it is read among the names of food. "Bring forth" is said to Agni and to the priests who are his helpers: all of you bring it forth. As in the world, when many are engaged in one task, a prayer addresses the chief one alone and says "you all do thus", so here too Agni alone, the chief, is addressed and yet the plural is used. The Maruts are those who overcome the powers of enemies by their own strength; from fear of those honourable Maruts the earth trembles. The word for the Maruts' host, though the Maruts are included within it, takes them separately in thought, and so "who" refers back to them. He quotes as an example the Mahābhāṣya, अथ शब्दानुशासनं (*atha śabdānuśāsanaṃ*) followed by केषां शब्दानां (*keṣāṃ śabdānāṃ*) (Ma. 1.1-1) **NOTE**, and the example from the world: when "a king's man" is said, one asks "whose kingdom?"

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ये (*ye*)—those Maruts who
- सहांसि (*sahāṃsi*)—the powers of enemies
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—by their own strength
- सहंते (*sahaṃte*)—defeat
- पृणते (*pṛṇate*)—noise-making
- तुराय (*turāya*)—swift-moving
- स्वतवसे (*svatavase*)—endowed with their own strength
- मारुताय (*mārutāya*)—to the host of Maruts
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—attractive
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—and venerable food (oblation)
- प्र भरध्वं (*pra bharadhvaṃ*)—offer
- मखेभ्यः (*makhebhyaḥ*)—from fear of the venerable Maruts
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth
- रेजते (*rejate*)—trembles

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, to the host of Maruts, those who defeat the powers of enemies by their own strength, such noise-making, swift-moving, endowed with their own strength, the attractive and venerable

### Printed p. 480

food (oblation) that is attractive and venerable: offer it. From fear of the venerable Maruts the earth trembles.

##### English translation
Offer to the loud-sounding, quick-moving, self invigorating company of the Maruts, excellent (sacrificial) food : (to them) who overcome strength by strength : the earth trembles, Agni, at the adorable (Maruts).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्विषीमंतो अध्वरस्येव दिद्युत्तृषुच्यवसोजुहू ३ नाग्नेः  
> अ॒र्चत्र॑यो॒ धुन॑यो॒ न वी॒रा भ्राज॑ज्जनानो म॒रुतो॒  ॑
> अधृष्टाः ॥ १० ॥

> त्विषिमंतः । अध्वरस्य इव । दिद्युत् । तृष्टुच्यवसः । जुह्वः । न । अग्नेः ।  
> अर्चत्रयः । धुनयः । न । वीराः । भ्राजत् जन्मानः । मरुतः । अधृष्टाः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मरुतोऽध्वरस्येव यज्ञस्येव दिद्युत् द्योतमानास्तृषुच्यवसः क्षिप्रगमना
> अग्नेर्जुहू न रश्मय इव त्रिषीमंतो दीप्तिमंतोऽर्चत्रयोऽर्चनीया
> धुनयो न सपत्नान्कंपयंत इव वीराः शूरा भ्राजज्जनानो दीप्तशरीरा अधृष्टाः
> परैरनभिभूताश्व भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts shine like a sacrifice; they are swift-moving. Like the flames of Agni they are radiant and full of splendour; they are venerable. Like shakers of rivals, causing them to tremble, they are heroes, brave ones, of shining body, and they are unassailed, not overcome by others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तैषुच्यवसः (*taiṣucyavasaḥ*)—the swift-moving
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—Maruts
- अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—for the sacrifice
- दिद्युदिव (*didyudiva*)—like those who give light
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- जुह्वो न (*juhvo na*)—like flame-formed rays
- त्रिषीमंतः (*triṣīmaṃtaḥ*)—endowed with lustre
- अर्चत्रयः (*arcatrayaḥ*)—possessing a venerable form
- धुनयो न (*dhunayo na*)—like those who make enemies tremble
- वीराः (*vīrāḥ*)—possessed of valour
- भ्राजज्जन्मानः (*bhrājajjanmānaḥ*)—having a body full of lustre
- अधृष्टाः (*adhṛṣṭāḥ*)—unassailed by enemies, they shine

### Printed p. 481

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The swift-moving Maruts give light to the sacrifice. They possess a venerable form. They make enemies tremble, they are possessed of valour, they have a body full of lustre, and they shine unassailed by enemies.

##### English translation
The Maruts are resplendent as if illuminators of the sacrifice,
(bright) as the flames of Agni, entitled are they to adoration, and like
heroes making (adversaries) tremble : brilliant are they from birth, and
invincible.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं वृ॒धंतं॒ मारु॑तं॒ भ्राज॑दृष्टिं रु॒द्रस्य॑ सू॒नुं ह॒वसा  ॑
> विवासे ।  
> दि॒वः शर्धा॑य॒ शुच॑यो मनी॒षा गि॒रयो॒ नाप॑ उ॒ग्रा  ॑
> अस्पृधन् ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । वृधंतं । मारुतं । भ्राजत् ऽऋष्टिं । रुद्रस्य । सूनुं । हवसा । अ । विवासे ।  
> दिवः । शर्धाय । शुचयः । मनीषाः । गिरयः । न । आपः । उग्राः । अस्पृधन् ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं प्रसिद्धं वृधंतं वर्धमानं भ्राजदृष्टिं भ्राजमानऋष्टिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं
> पुत्रं मारुतं मरुद्दणं हवसा स्तोत्रेणा विवासे । परिचरामि । किंच दिवः स्तोतुः
> शुचयो निर्मला मनीषाः स्तुतय उग्रा उद्यूर्णाः शर्धाय मारुताय
> बलाय । तृक्षः शर्ध इति बलनामसु पाठात् । आप आप्नुवंतो गिरयो न मेघा
> इव । गिरिर्वृज इति मेघनामसु पाठात् । अस्पृध्रन् । अस्पर्धंत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That well-known, growing host of Maruts, who are the sons of Rudra and have shining lances, I serve with praise. Moreover, the pure praises of the worshipper, fierce and uplifted, for the strength of the Maruts (it is read among the names of strength) are pervading, as clouds do (it is read among the names of cloud), and they vie with one another.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तं (*taṃ*)—the well-known
- वृधंतं (*vṛdhaṃtaṃ*)—the one that grows
- भ्राजदृष्टिं (*bhrājadṛṣṭiṃ*)—possessing a shining weapon
- रुद्रस्य सूनुं (*rudrasya sūnuṃ*)—the one in the form of Rudra's sons

### Printed p. 482

- मारुतं (*mārutaṃ*)—the host of Maruts
- हवसा (*havasā*)—with praise
- आ विवासे (*ā vivāse*)—I serve
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the praiser
- शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)—pure
- उग्राः (*ugrāḥ*)—possessed of great strength
- मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*)—praises
- शर्धायॆ (*śardhāyè*)—offered to the host of Maruts
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—pervading it
- गिरियो न (*giriyo na*)—like the clouds that cause rain
- अस्पृधन् (*aspṛdhan*)—they vie

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I serve with praise the well-known host of Maruts, which grows, has shining weapons and is in the form of the sons of Rudra. The praiser's pure praises, possessed of great strength, offered to the host of Maruts and pervading it, vie like the clouds that cause rain.

##### English translation
I worship with oblations that exalted company of the Maruts,
the progeny of Rudra, armed with shining lances: the pure and earnest
praises of the devout (adorer) are emulous in the invigoration (of the
Muruts), as the clouds (vie in the emission of the rain).

## Sūkta 67 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वेषां व इत्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं मैत्रावरुणं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । विश्वेषां मैत्रावरुणमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥
> मैत्रावरुणे पशावा यातं मित्रावरुणेति पशुपुरोडाशस्यानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> आ यातं मित्रावरुणा सुशस्त्या नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> व्यूळ्ळे दशरात्रे सप्तमेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे प्र यद्वामिति मैत्रावरुणस्तृतीयश्चः ।
> सूत्रितं च । प्र यद्वां मित्रावरुणा स्पूर्धन्ना गोमता नासत्या रथेन ।
> आ. ८-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning विश्वेषां व (*viśveṣāṃ va*) has eleven ṛks and is the sixth sūkta. Bharadvāja is its seer, the metre is Triṣṭubh and the deity is Mitra and Varuṇa. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: विश्वेषां मैत्रावरुणमिति (*viśveṣāṃ maitrāvaruṇamiti*) **GLOSS**. The application of the sūkta is by indication. In the animal sacrifice addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa, the ṛk beginning आ यातं मित्रावरुणा (*ā yātaṃ mitrāvaruṇā*) is the anuvākyā of the animal-cake offering; this is laid down in the sūtra beginning आ यातं मित्रावरुणा (*ā yātaṃ mitrāvaruṇā*) (Ā. 3-8). On the seventh day of the Vyūḍha Daśarātra, at the Praüga śastra, the ṛk beginning प्र यद्वां (*pra yadvāṃ*) is the third triplet for Mitra and Varuṇa; this is laid down in the sūtra beginning प्र यद्वां (*pra yadvāṃ*) (Ā. 8-9).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta विश्लेषां वः (*viśleṣāṃ vaḥ*) is the sixth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta; Mitra and Varuṇa are the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: विश्लेषां मैत्रावरुणं (*viśleṣāṃ maitrāvaruṇaṃ*) **GLOSS**. The application of the sūkta is by indication. In the animal offering addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa, the third ṛk of this sūkta, beginning आ यातं मित्रावरुणा (*ā yātaṃ mitrāvaruṇā*), is to be recited as anuvākyā mantra when the animal-cakes are offered; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: आ यातं मित्रावरुणा सुशस्त्या नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं (*ā yātaṃ mitrāvaruṇā suśastyā no mitrāvaruṇā havyajuṣṭiṃ*) (Ā. 3-8) **GLOSS**. On the seventh day of the sacrifice called Vyūḍha Daśarātra, when the Praüga śastra mantra is recited, the three ṛks of this sūkta beginning प्र यद्वां (*pra yadvāṃ*) (ṛks 9-11) are to be recited as the third triplet addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: प्र यद्वां मित्रावरुणा स्पूर्धन्ना गोमता नासत्या रथेन (*pra yadvāṃ mitrāvaruṇā spūrdhannā gomatā nāsatyā rathena*) (Ā. 8-9) **GLOSS**.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 67
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 1; Varga 9, 10
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 11
- Ṛṣi: भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*)
- Deity: मित्रावरुणौ (*mitrāvaruṇau*)
- Metre: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*)

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वे॑षां वः स॒तां ज्येष्ठ॑तमा गी॒र्भिर्मि॒त्रावरु॑णा वावृ॒धध्यै॑ ।  
> सं या र॒श्मेव॑ य॒मतु॒र्यमि॑ष्णा॒ द्वा जनौ॒ अस॑मा बा॒हुभिः॒  
> स्वैः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वेषां । वः । सतां । ज्येष्ठतमा । गीभिः । मित्रावरुणा । ववृधध्यै ।  
> सं । या । रश्म्याइव । यमतुः । यमिष्ठा । द्वा । जनान् । असमा । बाहुभिः ।  
> स्वैः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वेषां सतां मध्ये जेष्ठतमा जेष्ठतमौ मित्रावरुण् वो वां गीर्भिः
> स्तुतिभिर्ववृधध्यै वर्धयितुं ग्रवृत्तोऽस्मि । या यौ द्वा द्वौ सहितावसमा विषमे ।
> त्रिरश्रिं हंति चतुरश्रिरुग्रः । ऋग्वे. १-१५२-२ । इति निगमांतरेणासाम्यं दर्शितं ।
> यमिषा यंतृतमौ स्वैरात्मीयैर्बाहुभी रश्मेव रश्मनेवाश्वान् जनान् सं
> यमतुः संयच्छतः । बाहुभिरिति बहुवचनं पूजार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among all existing beings, O Mitra and Varuṇa, the most senior, I have set about to increase you with praises. You two together are "uneven", that is, unequal; that your unevenness is another matter is shown by another passage: त्रिरश्रिं हंति चतुरश्रिरुग्रः (*triraśriṃ haṃti caturaśrirugraḥ*) (Ṛgve. 1-152-2) **GLOSS** **NOTE**. You two, the best restrainers, hold the people together with your own arms, as one holds horses with a rein; the plural "arms" is used for honour.

- विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*)—of all
- सतां (*satāṃ*)—among beings that are real
- ज्येष्ठतमा (*jyeṣṭhatamā*)—the most excellent
- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- या द्वा (*yā dvā*)—you two who
- असमा (*asamā*)—though not of equal form
- यमिष्णा (*yamiṣṇā*)—as the best controllers of the world
- स्वैः (*svaiḥ*)—your
- बाहुभिः (*bāhubhiḥ*)—with arms
- रश्मेव (*raśmeva*)—as one keeps horses under control with bridles
- जनान् (*janān*)—all the people
- सं यमतुः (*saṃ yamatuḥ*)—you keep under control, such as you
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you

- ववृदध्यै (*vavṛdadhyai*)—I cause to increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, the most excellent among all beings that are real, you two, though not of equal form, as the best controllers of the world, keep all the people under control with your arms, as one keeps horses under control with bridles. I cause you to increase with praises.

##### English translation
(I proceed) by my praises to exalt you, Mitra and Varuna, the
eldest of all existing things : you two, though not the same, are the firmest
restrainers with your arms, and hold men back (from evil) as they check
(horses) with reins.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ वां युवां मत् ममेयं मनीषा स्तुतिः प्र स्तृणीते ।
> प्रच्छादयति । प्रिया हे प्रियौ युवां नमसान्नेन हविषा सहोप गच्छति च ।
> युवयोर्बर्हिर्यज्ञमच्छाभिगच्छति च । हे मित्रावरुणौ नोऽस्मभ्यमधृष्टमनभिभूतं छर्दिर्गृहं यंतं । प्रयच्छतं । हे सुदानू शोभनदान् वां युवयोः
> संबंधि युवाभ्यां देयं यद्गृहं वरूथ्यं शीतवातातपानां वारयित्य भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this praise of mine spreads over you and covers you. O beloved ones, it goes to you with the food, the oblation, and goes to your sacrificial grass. O Mitra and Varuṇa, grant us an unassailed, unconquered house. O good givers, the house given by you is to be a protector against cold, wind and heat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणौ (*mitrāvaruṇau*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- वां (*vāṃ*)—both of you
- मत् (*mat*)—my
- इयं मनीषा (*iyaṃ manīṣā*)—this praise
- प्र स्तृणीते (*pra stṛṇīte*)—pervades
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—O beloved Mitra and Varuṇa
- नमसा (*namasā*)—together with the oblation
- उप (*upa*)—that praise approaches you
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—the seat of darbha grass
- अच्छ (*accha*)—is spread for you
- सुदानू (*sudānū*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, excellent givers
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आधृष्टं (*ādhṛṣṭaṃ*)—unassailed
- वां (*vāṃ*)—given by you
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- वरूथ्यं (*varūthyaṃ*)—a protector against cold, wind and the like
- छर्दिः (*chardiḥ*)—the house
- यंतं (*yaṃtaṃ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this praise of mine joins you both and pervades. O beloved Mitra and Varuṇa, that same praise, together with the oblation, approaches you. The seat of darbha grass is spread out for you. O Mitra and Varuṇa, excellent givers, give us a house that is unassailed, given by you, and a protector against cold, wind and the like.

##### English translation
This my praise is addressed to you both, and proceeds, to you beloved (deities) together with the oblation : the sacred grass is spread before you : grant us, Mitra and Varuna, unassailable dwelling, that through your favour, munificent divinities, may be a (secure) shelter.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, invoked with good praise, with the food, the oblation, or the song of praise, beloved of the whole world, come near. You two, endowed with greatness, hold in check the people who desire food or fame for themselves, as a man engaged in a rite does by his work. The word for "rite" is read among the names of work.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- अप्पस्थः (*appasthaḥ*)—a man devoted to rites

- महित्वा चित् (*mahitvā cit*)—by your greatness itself
- यौ (*yau*)—you who
- श्रुधीयतः (*śrudhīyataḥ*)—desiring food
- जनान् (*janān*)—men
- सं यतथः (*saṃ yatathaḥ*)—join with their accomplishments, such as you
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—dear to all
- सुशस्ति (*suśasti*)—with good praise
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with a hymn of praise
- हूयमाना (*hūyamānā*)—being invoked, you
- उप आ यातं (*upa ā yātaṃ*)—be gracious and come to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, as a man devoted to rites obtains his position by his own work, so you, by your greatness, join men who desire food with their accomplishments. You are dear to all and are invoked with a hymn of good praise; be gracious and come to us.

##### English translation
Come, Mitra and Varuna, beloved by all, and invoked with reverence to the propitious rite, you who by your bounty support men labouring for sustenance as a workman (maintains himself) by work.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या यावश्वा नाश्चाविन वाजिना वाजिनौ बलिनौ पूतबंधू पूतस्तोत्रावृता
> सत्यौ च । यत् यौ गर्भं गर्भभूतावदितिर्देवी भरध्यै बभार ! किंच या यौ
> जायमाना जायमानावेव महि महतो महांता महत्तरौ प्रभूत् मित्रावरुणौ
> मर्ताय मर्ताय रिपवे हिंसकाय घोरा घोरौ घातकौ नि दीधः निदधारादितिः
> स्टोदरे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two who are like horses, strong, whose praises are pure, and who are truthful: Aditi, the goddess, bore them as an embryo. Moreover, these two, Mitra and Varuṇa, were greater than the great even as they were being born; they are terrible to the mortal, the harming enemy, and are his slayers. Aditi bore them in her own womb. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्वा न (*aśvā na*)—like horses

- पूतबंधू (*pūtabaṃdhū*)—possessed of pure praises
- ऋता (*ṛtā*)—who are of the nature of truth
- यत् (*yat*)—whom
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—Aditi
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—in the form of an embryo
- भरध्यै (*bharadhyai*)—she bore
- या (*yā*)—who
- जायमाना (*jāyamānā*)—at the very time of being born
- महि (*mahi*)—than those who have greatness
- प्रमहांता (*pramahāṃtā*)—such Mitra and Varuṇa as had attained very great majesty
- मर्ताय (*martāya*)—for the benefit of man
- रिपवे (*ripave*)—of the harming enemy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those Mitra and Varuṇa who, like horses, are strong, worthy of pure praises and of the nature of truth, whom Aditi bore in her womb, who even when born had attained greater majesty than those who have greatness

such Mitra and Varuṇa Aditi obtained as her sons, for the benefit of man, to be destroyers of the harming enemy.

##### English translation
Who (are) strong as horses, accepters of pious praise, observers of truth, whom Aditi conceived : whom, mighty of the mighty at your birth and formidable to mortal foes, she bore.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All the gods, united in mutual affection, delighting in your greatness, that is, praising you, laid strength in you. Moreover, since you two encompass the wide heaven and earth, your rays, unharmed and undeluded, are there. **NOTE**

- क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)—strength
- अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—they established in you

- यत् (*yat*)—you who
- उर्वी (*urvī*)—the wide
- रोदसी चित् (*rodasī cit*)—both heaven and earth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you, whom all the gods, assembling together, praising you, for your greatness, established your strength in, you who pervade and overpower both the wide heaven and earth, such as you have rays that are unharmed and free of obstruction.

##### English translation
Inasmuch as all the gods equally pleased and rejoicing in your greatness conferred strength upon you, and since you are pre-eminent over the wide heaven and earth, your courses are unobstructed, unimpeded.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता हि क्ष॒त्रं धा॒रये॑थे॒ अनु॒ द्यून्दृं॒हेथे॒ सानु॑मुप॒मादि॑व॒ द्योः ।  
> दृ॒ळ्हो नक्ष॑त्र उ॒त वि॒श्वदे॑वो॒ भूमि॒माता॒न्द्यां धा॒सिना॒योः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । हि । क्षत्रं । धारायेथे इति । अनु । द्यून् । द्यंहेथे इति । सानुं । उपमात् इव ।  
> द्योः ।  
> दृढः । नक्षत्रः । उत । विश्वदेवः । भूमिं । आ । आतान् । द्यां । धासिना । आयोः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता तौ मित्रावरुण् युवामनु द्यून् दिवसे दिवसे क्षत्रं बलं धारयेथे
> हि । द्योरंतरिक्षस्य सानुः समुच्च्रितप्रदेशं मेघं सूर्यं वा दृंहेथे ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you indeed hold strength day by day. You make firm the ridge of the sky, the lofty region of the atmosphere, that is, the cloud or the sun.

### Printed p. 490

> दृढीकुरुतं । उपमादिव । उपमीयते प्रक्षिप्यत इत्युपमात्सूणा । सा यथा
> वत्सं धारयति तद्वदित्यर्थः। दृळ्हो युवाभ्यां दृढीकृतश्च मेघो नक्षत्रोऽन्तरीक्षं
> व्याप्नुवान उतापि च विश्वदेवः सूर्यो भूमिं द्यां दिवं चायोर्मनुष्यस्य ।
> द्रुह्यव आयव इति मनुष्यनामसु पाठात् । धासिनान्नेन हविषा । क्षुत् धासिरित्यन्ननामसु पाठात् । आप्यायितः सन् आतान् । आतनोति युवाभ्यां दृढीकृत एव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As a post, that which is set up, holds a calf, so do you hold: this is the meaning. The cloud, made firm by you, filling the atmosphere, and the sun, the All-god, nourished by the food, the oblation, of man (the words for "man" and for "food" are read among the names of man and the names of food), spread out earth and heaven, made firm by you alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता (*tā*)—you, the well known
- अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*)—every day
- क्षत्रं (*kṣatraṃ*)—strength
- धारयेथे हि (*dhārayethe hi*)—you indeed hold
- द्योः (*dyoḥ*)—of the atmosphere
- सानुं (*sānuṃ*)—the lofty region
- उपमादिव (*upamādiva*)—as with a firm pillar
- दृंहेथे (*dṛṃhethe*)—you make endowed with firm strength
- नक्षत्रः (*nakṣatraḥ*)—the cloud that pervades the atmosphere
- वृळः (*vṛḷaḥ*)—and is firm
- उत (*uta*)—and
- विश्वदेवः (*viśvadevaḥ*)—the sun
- आयोः (*āyoḥ*)—given by man
- धासिना (*dhāsinā*)—satisfied by the food in the form of the oblation
- भूमिं (*bhūmiṃ*)—the earth
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—and the heaven
- आ आतान् (*ā ātān*)—cause to be abundant

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you, the well known, hold great strength every day. You make the lofty region of the atmosphere endowed with firm strength, like a firm pillar. The cloud that pervades the atmosphere and is firm, and the sun, satisfied by the food in the form of the oblation given by man, cause the earth and the heaven to be abundant.

##### English translation
You manifest vigour daily, you strengthen the summit of the sky as
if with a pillar; the solid firmament and the universal deity (the sun)
replenish earth and heaven with the food of man.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता शौ मित्रावरुण् युवां विग्रं प्राज्ञं यजमानं । विप्रो विग्र इति
> मेधाविनामसु पाठात् । धैथे धारयथो जठरमुदरं पृणध्यॆ सोमेन
> पूरयितुं । यद्यदा सभृतयः सह भ्रियमाणा ऋत्तिजः सद्म यज्ञसदनमा पृणंति

> युवतयो नद्यो दिशो वा न मृष्यंते । रजसा नाभिभूयंते । अवाता अशुष्काश्च
> वि भरंते । विभूतिं धारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you hold the wise sacrificer (the word for "wise" is read among the names of the intelligent) in order to fill the belly with Soma. When the priests, who are supported together with him, fill the sacrificial seat, the house of the sacrifice, then, O sustainers of all, when the water sent by you comes, the young women, that is, the rivers or the quarters, are not harmed, not overcome by dust, and, not dried up, bear abundance. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सभृतयः (*sabhṛtayaḥ*)—the priests
- सद्म (*sadma*)—in the house of sacrifice
- आ पृणंति (*ā pṛṇaṃti*)—fill it, then
- ता (*tā*)—you, the well known
- जठरं (*jaṭharaṃ*)—your belly
- पृणध्यॆ (*pṛṇadhyè*)—to fill with Soma juice
- विप्रं (*vipraṃ*)—the wise sacrificer
- धैथे (*dhaithe*)—you support (you become his refuge)
- विश्वजिन्वा (*viśvajinvā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, who are pleasing to the whole world
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—you send water, then
- युवतयः (*yuvatayaḥ*)—the rivers
- न मृष्यंते (*na mṛṣyaṃte*)—are not obstructed by anyone
- अवाताः (*avātāḥ*)—not drying up in the least
- वि भरंते (*vi bharaṃte*)—spread abundance of water

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the priests fill the house of sacrifice, then you, the well known, take refuge in the wise sacrificer in order to fill your belly with Soma juice; that is, you become his refuge. O Mitra and Varuṇa, pleasing to the whole world, when you send water, then the rivers are not obstructed by anyone, and spread around an abundance of water that does not dry up.

##### English translation
You two support the sage (worshipper), filling his belly when he and
his dependants fill the sacrificial chamber ; when, sustainers of all, the

rain (is sent down by you), and the young (rivers) are not obstructed, but,
undried, diffuse (fertility) around.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता जि॒ह्वया॒ सद॒मेदं सु॑मे॒धा आ यद्वां॑ स॒त्यो अ॑र॒तिर्ऋ॒ते  
> भूत् ।  
> तद्वां॑ महि॒त्वं धृ॑तान्नावस्तु यु॒वं दा॒शुषे॒ वि च॑यिष्ट॒मंहः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

> तत् । वां । महित्वं । धृत्यअन्नौ । अस्तु । युवं। दाशुषे । वि । चयिष्टं । अंहः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता तौ मित्रावरुणौ युवां सुमेधाः प्राज्ञो जिह्वया वाचा सदं
> सर्वदेदं जलमा याचते । आ इत्युपसर्गदर्शनाद्योग्यक्रियाध्याहाराद्याचत
> इत्याध्याह्रियते। पूर्वस्यामृचि जलस्य प्रकृतत्वात् बुद्धि विपरिवर्तमानं जलमिदंशब्देन परामृश्यते । यद्यदा वां युवयोररतिरभिगंता ऋते यज्ञे सत्यो
> मायारहित आ भूत् आभवति हे धृतान्सौ तन्महित्वमपेक्षितप्रदातृत्वलक्षणं वां
> युवयोरस्तु । किंच युवं युवां दाशुषे दाशुषो यजमानस्य ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे
> चतुर्थी ॥ अ०हः पापं वि चयिष्टं । विनाशयतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, the wise man always asks you, with his tongue, that is, with speech, for this water. The word "ā" is seen as a preverb, so the fitting verb "asks" is supplied; because water was the subject of the previous ṛk, the water turning in the mind is referred to by the word "this". When your approacher, truthful and free of deceit, comes to the sacrifice, O you whose food is ghee, may that greatness of yours, which consists in giving what is desired, be yours. Moreover, you two destroy the sin of the sacrificer who gives the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- आरतिः (*āratiḥ*)—worshipper
- ऋते (*ṛte*)—in the sacrifice
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—sincere
- आ भूत् (*ā bhūt*)—he approaches you, then
- ता (*tā*)—you
- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—the wise sacrificer
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with his speech
- सदं (*sadaṃ*)—always
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—water
- आ याचते (*ā yācate*)—asks for
- धृतान्नौ (*dhṛtānnau*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, whose food is ghee
- वां (*vāṃ*)—in you
- महित्वं (*mahitvaṃ*)—the greatness of giving generously

- अस्तु (*astu*)—may be
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—of the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—the sin
- वि चयिष्टं (*vi cayiṣṭaṃ*)—destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when your worshipper approaches you sincerely in the sacrifice, then the wise sacrificer always asks you with his speech for water. O Mitra and Varuṇa, whose food is ghee, may the greatness of giving generously be in you. May you two destroy the sin of the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

##### English translation
The wise man always (solicits) you with his prayers for this (supply of water), when approaching you sincerely in sacrifice : may your magnani- mity be such that you, the feeders upon ghi, may exterminate sin in the donor (of the oblation).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ वां युवयोः प्रिया प्रियाणि धाम धामानि कर्माणि
> युवधिता युवाभ्यां विहितानि यद्येऽयजंतो जनाः स्पूर्धन् स्पर्धमानाः प्र
> मिनंति हिंसंति! ये च देवासो देवा ओहसा वहनसाधनेन स्तोत्रेण न युज्यंते ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, your dear deeds, ordained by you, are those which the non-sacrificing people, vying with you, harm; and the gods who are not joined with the praise that carries the oblation

### Printed p. 494

> मर्ता मनुष्याश्च हसा न युज्यंते । ये चाप्यः । अपः कर्म । तद्वंतोऽयज्ञसाचो न यज्ञयुक्ताः । वृथाकर्माणि कुर्वंत इत्यर्थः । ये च न पुत्राः ।
> पृणंतीति पुत्राः । न पुत्रा अपृणंत इत्यर्थः । तान् सर्वान्वि चयिष्टमित्यनुषज्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The mortals, men, are not joined with हसा (*hasā*) **NOTE**. And those who have चाप्यः (*cāpyaḥ*) **NOTE**, that is, work (अपः कर्म (*apaḥ karma*)): possessing it, they are अयज्ञसाचः (*ayajñasācaḥ*), not joined with sacrifice; the meaning is that they perform fruitless works. And those who are न पुत्राः (*na putrāḥ*): they who fill (पृणंतीति (*pṛṇaṃtīti*)) are sons (पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)); those who are not sons are those who do not fill (the gods with offerings). "Destroy all of them" (वि चयिष्ट (*vi cayiṣṭa*)) is to be carried on from the preceding.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वां (*vāṃ*)—to you
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—which are agreeable
- युवधिता (*yuvadhitā*)—and are directed to you
- धाम (*dhāma*)—the rites
- यत् (*yat*)—which men devoid of rites
- स्पर्धन् (*spardhan*)—vying
- प्र मिनंति (*pra minaṃti*)—harm
- ये देवासः (*ye devāsaḥ*)—which gods
- ओहसा (*ohasā*)—by the praises that extol you
- न (*na*)—are not (joined)
- मर्ताः (*martāḥ*)—which mortals
- न (*na*)—are not joined
- ये (*ye*)—those who
- अप्पः (*appaḥ*)—though possessed of rites
- अयज्ञ साचः (*ayajña sācaḥ*)—are devoid of sacrifice (and)
- न पुत्राः (*na putrāḥ*)—those who do not worship and satisfy you, destroy all of them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, the rites that are directed to you and agreeable to you, which men devoid of rites harm, vying with you; the gods who are not joined with the praises that extol you; the mortals who are not joined with those same praises; those who, though possessed of rites, are devoid of sacrifice; and those who do not worship and satisfy you: destroy them all.

##### English translation
(Exterminate also), Mitra and Varuna, those who, emulously
contending, disturb the rites that are agreeable and beneficial to you both :
those divinities, those mortals, who are not diligent in adoration,
those who performing works perform not sacrifices. those who do not
propitiate you.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि यद्वाचं॑ की॒स्तासो॒ भरं॑ते॒ शंसं॑ति॒ के चि॑न्नि॒ विदो॑  ॒
> मनानाः ।  
> आद्वां॑ ब्रवाम स॒त्यानु॒, क्था नकि॑र्दे॒वेभि॑र्यतथो महि॒त्वा ॥

### Printed p. 495

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । यत् । वाचं । कीस्तासः । भरंते । शंसंति । के । चित् । निविदः । मनानाः ।  
> आत् । वां । ब्रवाम । सत्यानि । उक्ता । नकिः । देवेभिः । यतथः । महित्वा ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदा कीस्तासो मेधाविन उद्गातारः । उशिजः कीस्तास इति मेधाविनामसु
> पाठात् । वाचं स्तुतिं वि भरंते पृथक् उच्चारयंति तदा के चिद्ब्रह्मचा मनाना
> अग्न्यादीन् स्तुवंतो निविदः शंसंति । अत्तथा सति वां युवाभ्यां सत्यान्न्युक्थानि
> स्तोत्राणि वयं ब्रवाम । महित्वा महत्वेन देवेभिरनैर्देवैः सह नकिर्यतथः ।
> न गच्छथः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the कीस्तासः (*kīstāsaḥ*), the intelligent udgātṛs (the word is read among the names of the intelligent: उशिजः कीस्तास (*uśijaḥ kīstāsa*)), utter the praise (वाचं (*vācaṃ*)) separately, then some ब्रह्मचा (*brahmacā*) **NOTE**, meditating on Agni and the others and praising them, recite the Nivid mantras. This being so, we utter to you two true praises. By your greatness you two do not go together with the other gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- कीस्तासः (*kīstāsaḥ*)—intelligent udgātṛs
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—the praise
- वि भरंते (*vi bharaṃte*)—recite
- ते चित् (*te cit*)—some **NOTE**
- मनानाः (*manānāḥ*)—meditating on Agni and the others
- निविदः (*nividaḥ*)—the mantra called Nivid
- शंसंति (*śaṃsaṃti*)—they recite
- आत् (*āt*)—on that occasion
- वां (*vāṃ*)—addressing you two
- सत्यानि उक्ता (*satyāni uktā*)—true mantras of praise
- ब्रवाम (*bravāma*)—we recite
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—through the loftiness of your greatness
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—with other gods
- नकिः यतथः (*nakiḥ yatathaḥ*)—you neither join nor go along

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the intelligent udgātṛs recite the praise addressed to you, then some Ṛgvedic priests, meditating on Agni and the others, recite and praise with the mantra called Nivid. On that occasion we recite true mantras of praise addressed to you two. Through the loftiness of your greatness you neither join nor go along with the other gods.

##### English translation
When the intelligent priests offer praise, then some of them, glorify-
ing (Agni and other deities), recite the Nivid hymns; such being the case,
we address to you sincere adoration, for in consequence of your greatness
you do not associate with (other) divinities
