#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒वोरि॒त्था वां॑ छ॒र्दिषो॑ अ॒भिष्टौ॑ यु॒वोर्मि॑त्रावरुणा॒  ॑
> वस्कृ॑धोयु ।  
> अनु॒ यद्गावः॑ स्फु॒रानृ॑जि॒प्यं धृ॒ष्णुं यद्रणे॒ वृष॑णं यु॒नज॑न् ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अवोः । इत्था । वां । छर्दिषः । अभिष्वा । युवोः । मित्रावरुण् । अस्कृधोयु ।  
> अनु । यत् । गावः । स्पुरान् । ऋजिप्यं । धृष्णुं । यत् । रणे । वृषणं । युनजन् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणाववोरवतोर्वां युवयोरभिष्टावभिगमने छर्दिषो
> गृहाय सुखाय वा ॥ चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी ॥ युवामभिगतेषु स्तोतृषु युवोर्युवयोः संबंधि युवाभ्यां देयं तद्गृहादिकमस्कृधोय्वविच्छिन्नं भवति ।
> तथा च यास्कः । अस्कृधोयुरकृध्वायुः । कृध्विति ह्रस्वनाम निकृत्तं भवति । नि. ६-३ ।
> इति । इत्था सत्यमेव । कदा मित्रावरुणयोरभिगमनमित्यत आह । यद्यद गावः
> स्तुतयोऽनु स्पुरान् अनुस्पुरेयुः। यदा च ऋजिष्यमृजुगामिनं धृष्णुं शत्रूणां
> धर्षकं वृषणं कामानां वर्षितारं सोमं रणे रमणे यज्ञे युनजन्
> यजमाना युंज्युः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, protectors, at your approach (अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)), for the house or for happiness: among the singers who have come to you, whatever of yours is to be given by you, that house and the rest, becomes अस्कृधोयु (*askṛdhoyu*), uninterrupted. So Yāska: अस्कृधोयुरकृध्वायुः । कृध्विति ह्रस्वनाम निकृत्तं भवति । (*askṛdhoyurakṛdhvāyuḥ | kṛdhviti hrasvanāma nikṛttaṃ bhavati |*) (Ni. 6-3) **GLOSS**. इत्था (*itthā*) means "truly". When is your approach? He says: when the गावः (*gāvaḥ*), the praises, ring out after (अनु स्पुरान् (*anu spurān*)), and when the sacrificers yoke (युनजन् (*yunajan*)) in the rite, in the sacrifice (रणे (*raṇe*)), the Soma that is ऋजिष्यं (*ṛjiṣyaṃ*), going straight, धृष्णुं (*dhṛṣṇuṃ*), the assailer of enemies, and वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*), the showerer of desires.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the praises
- अनु स्पुरान् (*anu spurān*)—are recited (and)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ऋजिष्यं (*ṛjiṣyaṃ*)—the Soma that goes straight
- धृष्णुं (*dhṛṣṇuṃ*)—that assails enemies
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—and that showers desires
- रणे (*raṇe*)—in the sacrifice
- युनजन् (*yunajan*)—the sacrificers offer, then
- छर्दिषः (*chardiṣaḥ*)—to the house
- अवोः (*avoḥ*)—protectors
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)—as the result of the approach
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—the houses and the rest given by you
- अस्कृधोयु (*askṛdhoyu*)—remain unbroken and eternal, or great
- इत्था (*itthā*)—this is true

### Printed p. 497

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the praises addressed to you are recited, when the sacrificers offer in the sacrifice the Soma that goes straight, assails enemies and showers desires, then, as the result of the approach of you, the protectors of the house, the houses and the rest given by you remain unbroken and eternal, or great.

##### English translation
Upom your approach, Mitra and Varuna, protectors of the dwelling,
your (bounty) is unlimited; when (your) praises are uttered, and the
sacrificers add in the ceremony the soma that inspires straight-forwardness
and resolution, and is the showerer (of benefits)

## Sūkta 68 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्रुष्टि वामित्येकादशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रावरुणं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । श्रुष्टि वामैंद्रावरुणमुपांत्ये जगत्याविति । प्र
> सम्राज इंद्रावरुणा सुतपावित्येते जगत्यौ शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । इंद्रावरुणौ देवता ॥
> अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु तृतीयसवने होत्रकशस्त्रेषु स्तोमवृद्दौ मैत्रावरुणस्येदमावापार्थं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । श्रुष्टि नां यज्ञो युवां नरा । आ. ७-९ ।
> इति ॥ तृतीयसवन इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतमिति प्रशास्तुः प्रस्थितयाज्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतमिंद्रश्च सोमं पिबतं बृहस्पते ।
> आ. ५-५ । इति ॥ उक्थ्ये तृतीयसवन इंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्यॆति मैत्रावरुणस्य
> शस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । इंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्यॆति याज्या । आ. ६-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning श्रुष्टि वां (*śruṣṭi vāṃ*) has eleven ṛks and is the seventh sūkta; its seer is Bharadvāja, its metre Triṣṭubh and its deity Indra and Varuṇa. So it is given in the Anukramaṇikā: श्रुष्टि वामैंद्रावरुणमुपांत्ये जगत्याविति (*śruṣṭi vāmaiṃdrāvaruṇamupāṃtye jagatyāviti*) **GLOSS**. The two ṛks प्र सम्राज (*pra samrāja*) and इंद्रावरुणा सुतपा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapā*) are in the Jagatī metre; the rest are Triṣṭubh. The deity is Indra and Varuṇa. In the Abhiplava ukthya rites, at the third pressing, among the śastras of the hotṛ's assistants, when the stoma is increased, this sūkta is the one to be inserted (āvāpa) for the Maitrāvaruṇa. It is laid down in the sūtra: श्रुष्टि नां यज्ञो युवां नरा (*śruṣṭi nāṃ yajño yuvāṃ narā*) (Ā. 7-9) **GLOSS**. At the third pressing the ṛk इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ*) is the prasthita yājyā of the Praśāstṛ. It is laid down: इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतमिंद्रश्च सोमं पिबतं बृहस्पते (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutamiṃdraśca somaṃ pibataṃ bṛhaspate*) (Ā. 5-5) **GLOSS**. In the ukthya, at the third pressing, the ṛk इंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्य (*iṃdrāvaruṇā madhumattamasya*) is the śastra yājyā of the Maitrāvaruṇa. It is laid down: इंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्यॆति याज्या (*iṃdrāvaruṇā madhumattamasyèti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-1) **GLOSS**.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta श्रुष्टि वां (*śruṣṭi vāṃ*) is the seventh sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta; Indra and Varuṇa are the deities; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: श्रुष्टि वामैंद्रावरुणमुपांत्ये जगत् (*śruṣṭi vāmaiṃdrāvaruṇamupāṃtye jagat*) **GLOSS**. The ninth and tenth ṛks of this sūkta, प्र सम्राजे (*pra samrāje*) and इंद्रावरुणा सुतपौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapau*), are in the Jagatī metre. The remaining nine ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre. In the ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava

### Printed p. 498

at the time of the third pressing, the priests of the hotṛ group are to recite this sūkta, for the increase of the stoma, as an āvāpa sūkta addressed to Maitrāvaruṇa; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra श्रुष्टी वां यज्ञो युवां नरा (*śruṣṭī vāṃ yajño yuvāṃ narā*) (Ā. 7-9) **GLOSS**. And at the time of the third pressing the tenth ṛk of this sūkta, इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ*), is to be used for the prasthita yājyā mantra recited by the priest called Praśāstṛ; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra इंद्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतमिंद्रश्च सोमं पिबतं बृहस्पते (*iṃdrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutamiṃdraśca somaṃ pibataṃ bṛhaspate*) (Ā. 5-5) **GLOSS**. In the ukthya sacrifice also, at the time of the third pressing, the eleventh ṛk of this sūkta, इंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्य (*iṃdrāvaruṇā madhumattamasya*), is to be used as a yājyā mantra among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra इंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्यॆति याज्या (*iṃdrāvaruṇā madhumattamasyèti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-1) **GLOSS**.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 88 **NOTE**
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 1; Varga 11, 12
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 11
- Ṛṣi: भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*)
- Deity: इंद्रावरुणौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇau*)
- Metre: 1-8, 11: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*); 9, 10: जगती (*jagatī*)

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रु॒ष्टी वां॑ य॒ज्ञ उद्य॑तः स॒जोषा॑ मनु॒ष्वद्वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषो॒  ॑
> यज॑ध्यै ।  
> आ य इंद्रा॒वरु॑णावि॒षे अ॒द्य म॒हे सु॒म्नाय॑ म॒ह आ॑व॒वर्त॑त् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रुष्टी । वां । यज्ञः । उत्यतः । सजोषाः । मनुष्वत् । वृक्तबर्हिषः ।  
> यजध्यै ।  
> आ । यः । इंद्रावरुणौ । इषे । अद्य । महे । सुम्नाय । महे । आववर्तत् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 499

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महे मंहनीयौ हे इंद्रावरुण् वां युवयोरर्थे श्रुष्टि क्षिप्रः ।
> तथा च यास्कः । श्रुष्टिति क्षिप्रनामाशु अष्टीति । नि. ६-१२ । यज्ञः सोमः सजोषा
> ऋत्विग्निः सहितोऽद्या समंतादुद्यतः प्रवृत्तः । यः सोमो मनुष्यत् मनोरिव
> वृक्तबर्हिषः स्तीर्णबर्हिषो यजमानस्येषेन्नार्थं महे महते सुम्नाय
> सुखाय च यजध्यै यष्टुं वामाववर्तत् आवर्तयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, honourable ones (महे (*mahe*)), for you two the sacrifice is श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*), swift. So Yāska: श्रुष्टिति क्षिप्रनामाशु अष्टीति (*śruṣṭiti kṣipranāmāśu aṣṭīti*) (Ni. 6-12) **GLOSS**. The Soma, the sacrifice, accompanied by the priests (सजोषा (*sajoṣā*)), is today set out, started, all around. That Soma, like Manu, for the sacrificer who has spread the sacred grass (वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)), for food (इषे (*iṣe*)), for great happiness (सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*)), for worshipping you, आववर्तत् (*āvavartat*), brings you here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महे (*mahe*)—O venerable
- इंद्रावरुणौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇau*)—Indra and Varuṇa
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- मनुष्यत् (*manuṣyat*)—like Manu
- वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)—for the sacrificer who has spread the well prepared seat of darbha grass
- इषे (*iṣe*)—for food
- महे (*mahe*)—and for great
- सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*)—happiness
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—to worship you
- आववर्तत् (*āvavartat*)—is made ready
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—that Soma
- श्रुष्टि (*śruṣṭi*)—swiftly
- नां (*nāṃ*)—addressed to you **NOTE**
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—accompanied by the priests
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- आ (*ā*)—everywhere
- उद्यतः (*udyataḥ*)—is offered (is engaged in your worship)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O venerable Indra and Varuṇa, for the sacrificer who, like Manu, has spread the well prepared seat of darbha grass and worships you, the Soma that is made ready to worship you, for food and for great happiness, is now offered everywhere, swiftly, addressed to you, by the priests; and it is engaged in your worship.

##### English translation
Mighty Indra and Varna promptly has the soma returned, engaged conscientiously (with the priests) to offer sacrifice to you to obtain food, for him by whom, like Manu. the sacred grass has been clipped; he who (invited you hither) to-day for exceeding happiness.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता हि श्रेष्ठा॑ दे॒वता॑ता तु॒जा शूरा॑णां॒ शवि॑ष्ठा॒ ता हि भू॒तं।  
> म॒घोनां॒ मंहि॑ष्ठा तुवि॒शुष्क॑ ऋ॒तेन॑ वृत्र॒तुरा॒ सर्व॑सेना ॥

### Printed p. 500

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । हि । श्रेष्ठा । देवताता । तुजा । शूराणां । शविष्ठा । ता । हि । भूतं ।  
> मघोनां । मंहिष्ठा । तुविशुष्मा । ऋतेन । वृत्रतुरा । सर्वसेना ॥ २ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ ता तौ प्रसिद्धौ युवां श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठौ देवताता देवतात्
> यज्ञे । इष्टिर्देवतातेति यज्ञनामसु पाठात् । तुजा धनानां प्रेरकौ हि भूतं ।
> भवतं । किंच ता तौ हि युवां शूराणां मध्यॆ शविष्ठातिशयेन बलवंतौ भूतं ।
> किंच मघोनां दानवतां मंहिष्ठा दातृतमौ तुविशुष्मा बहुबलावृतेन सत्येन
> वृत्रतुरा शत्रूणां हिंसकौ सर्वसेना कृत्ससेनौ च भूतमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two, those well known, are the best (श्रेष्ठा (*śreṣṭhā*)) देवताता (*devatātā*) **NOTE** in the sacrifice, since इष्टिर्देवतातेति (*iṣṭirdevatāteti*) is read among the names of sacrifice. You are तुजा (*tujā*), impellers of wealth: be so. Moreover, among heroes you two are शविष्ठा (*śaviṣṭhā*), exceedingly strong. Moreover, among the मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*), those who give, you are मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*), the greatest givers; तुविशुष्मा (*tuviśuṣmā*), of great strength; through ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), truth, वृत्रतुरा (*vṛtraturā*), destroyers of foes; and सर्वसेना (*sarvasenā*), possessed of whole armies: be so.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता हि (*tā hi*)—you two, the well known
- देवताता (*devatātā*)—in the sacrifice that worships the gods
- श्रेष्ठा (*śreṣṭhā*)—the best
- तुजा (*tujā*)—as givers of wealth
- भूतं (*bhūtaṃ*)—you are
- ता हि (*tā hi*)—you two
- शूराणां (*śūrāṇāṃ*)—among heroes
- शविष्ठा (*śaviṣṭhā*)—of exceeding strength
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—among those who possess wealth
- मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*)—most generous givers
- तुविशुष्मा (*tuviśuṣmā*)—you yourselves, of abundant strength
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—through truth
- वृत्रतुरा (*vṛtraturā*)—destroyers of foes
- सर्वसेना (*sarvasenā*)—and also in the form of all armies **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, in the sacrifice that worships the gods, you two, the well known, are the best givers of wealth. You two alone are of exceeding strength among heroes, and the most generous givers among those who possess wealth. You yourselves, of abundant strength, through truth are destroyers of foes and are also in the form of all armies.

##### English translation
You two are the principal (divinities) at the worship of the gods;
the distributors of wealth; the most vigorous of heroes; the most liberal
among the opulent; possessed of vast strength; destroyers of foes by truth;
entire hosts (of yourselves).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता गृ॑णीहि नम॒स्ये॑भिः शू॒षैः सु॒म्नेभि॒रिंद्रा॒वरु॑णा चका॒ना ।  
> वज्रे॑णा॒न्यः शव॑सा॒ हंति॑ वृ॒त्रं सिष॑क्त्य॒न्नो वृ॒जने॑षु॒ विप्रः॑ ॥३॥

### Printed p. 501

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । गृणीहि । नमस्येभिः । शूषैः । सुम्नेभिः । इंद्रावरुणा । चकाना ।  
> वज्रेण । अन्यः । शवसा । हंति । वृत्रं । सिसक्ति । अन्यः । वृजनेषु । विप्रः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे भरद्वाज नमस्येभिः स्तुत्यैः शूषैर्बलैः । शूषमिति बलनामसु पाठात् ।
> सुम्मेभिः सुखैश्च सर्वैश्च काना स्तुतौ ॥ कायतिः शब्दकर्मा । तस्य लिटः कानचि
> रूपमिदं ॥ ता ताविंद्रावरुण् गृणीहि । स्तुहि । अन्यस्तयोरन्य इंद्रो वृत्रं
> वृत्रनामकमसुरं वज्रेण हंति । अन्नो वरुणो विप्रः प्राज्ञो वृजनेषु
> स्तोत्थणामुपद्रवेषु रक्षितुं शवसा बलेन सिषक्ति । संगच्छते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Bharadvāja, praise Indra and Varuṇa with praiseworthy (नमस्येभिः (*namasyebhiḥ*)) strengths (शूषैः (*śūṣaiḥ*); the word for "śūṣa" is read among the names of strength) and with pleasures (सुम्मेभिः (*summebhiḥ*)) **NOTE**. Praise (गृणीहि (*gṛṇīhi*), that is, extol) those two, Indra and Varuṇa. Of the two, the one, Indra, slays Vṛtra, the demon of that name, with the thunderbolt. The other, Varuṇa, the wise (विप्रः (*vipraḥ*), that is, the knowing), joins (सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*), that is, comes together) with strength to protect the praisers in their troubles (वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नमस्येभिः (*namasyebhiḥ*)—venerable
- शूषैः (*śūṣaiḥ*)—with strengths
- सुम्मेभिः (*summebhiḥ*)—with pleasures
- चकाना (*cakānā*)—renowned
- ता इंद्रवरुणा (*tā iṃdravaruṇā*)—those same Indra and Varuṇa
- गृणीहि (*gṛṇīhi*)—praise
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—one of the two, Indra
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra
- वज्रेण (*vajreṇa*)—with the thunderbolt
- हंति (*haṃti*)—slays
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the other, Varuṇa
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—being wise
- वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*)—in times of trouble, to protect the praisers
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—with strength
- सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*)—joins

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bharadvāja, praise those same Indra and Varuṇa, renowned for venerable strengths and pleasures. Of the two, Indra slays Vṛtra with the thunderbolt. The other, Varuṇa, being wise, joins with strength to protect the praisers in times of trouble.

##### English translation
Praise Mitra and Varuna, renowned for all glorious energies and
enjoyments: one of whom slays Vritra with the thunderbolt, the other,
intelligent by his might, comes to the aid (of the pious when) in difficulties.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग्नाश्च॒ यन्नर॑श्च वावृ॒धंत॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ न॒रां स्वगू॑र्ताः ।  
> प्रैभ्य॑ इंद्रावरुणा महि॒त्वा द्यौश्च॑ पृथिवि भूत॒र्मुवी ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 502

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ग्नाः । च । यत् । नरः । च । ववृधंत । विश्वे । देवासः । नरां । स्वगूर्ताः ।  
> प्र । एभ्यः । इंद्रावरुणा । महित्वा । द्यौः । च । पृथिवि । भूतं । उर्वी इति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नरां नृणां मनुष्याणां मध्यॆ ग्नाश्च स्त्रीयश्च । मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां ।
> नि. ३-२१ । इति यास्कवचनात् । नरश्च पुरुषाश्च विश्वे सर्वॆ देवासो देवाः ॥
> देवास इत्यत्र पुमान् स्त्रियेत्येकशेषात् देव्यश्च देवाश्च देवास इति निर्देशः
> पुंवन्निर्दॆशः ॥ स्वगूर्ताः स्वयमुद्यता यद्यदा ववृधंत स्तुतिभिर्वर्धयंते
> तदा हे इंद्रावरुण् महित्वा महत्त्वयुक्तावेभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः प्र भूतं । प्रभवतं । हे द्यौः पृथिवि चोभे उर्वि विस्तीर्णे युवामेभ्यः प्रभूतमित्यनुषंगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among men (नरां (*narāṃ*), that is, mankind) there are ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*), women, from Yāska's statement: मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां (*menā gnā iti strīṇāṃ*) (Ni. 3-21) **GLOSS**; and नरः (*naraḥ*), men; and all the gods (देवासः (*devāsaḥ*); here the word means both gods and goddesses, and the masculine form is used for both). They are स्वगूर्ताः (*svagūrtāḥ*), self-impelled. When (यत् (*yat*)) they make you grow (ववृधंत (*vavṛdhaṃta*)) with praises, then, O Indra and Varuṇa, you two, endowed with greatness, surpass (प्र भूतं (*pra bhūtaṃ*), that is, prevail over) these praisers. And O heaven and earth, both wide and extensive, the words "you two surpass them" are to be carried on to you also.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- नरां (*narāṃ*)—among mankind
- ग्नाश्च (*gnāśca*)—women
- नरश्च (*naraśca*)—and men
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods also
- स्वगूर्ताः (*svagūrtāḥ*)—self-impelled
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ववृधंत (*vavṛdhaṃta*)—they cause your increase with praises, then
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—you, endowed with greatness
- ऐभ्यः (*aibhyaḥ*)—than all these praisers
- प्र भूतं (*pra bhūtaṃ*)—become of more abundant greatness
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—O deity of the heavenly world
- पृथिवि च (*pṛthivi ca*)—and O earth (you two)
- उर्वी (*urvī*)—being of extensive form, are above all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, when, among mankind, women, men and all the gods, self-impelled, cause your increase with praises, then you, endowed with greatness, become of more abundant greatness than all these praisers. O deity of the heavenly world, O earth, you two also, being of extensive form, are above all.

##### English translation
When amongst mankind, both males and females, and when all the
gods spontaneously striving glorify you, Indra and Varuna, you become
pre-eminent in greatness over them, as do you, wide heaven and earth
(surpass them also).

### Printed p. 503

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स इत्यु॒दानुः॒ स्ववा॑ ऋ॒तावेंद्रा॒ यो वां॑ वरुण॒ दाश॑ति॒  
> त्मन् ।  
> इ॒षा स द्वि॒षस्त॑रे॒द्दास्वा॒न्वंस॑द्र॒यिं र॑यि॒वत॑श्च॒ जना॑न् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । इत् । सुदानुः । स्ववान् । ऋतवा । इंद्रा । यः । वां । वरुणा । दाशति ।  
> त्मन् ।  
> इषा । स ॥ द्विषः । तरेत् । दास्वान् । वंसत् । रयिं । रयिवतः । च । जनान् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रेंद्रौ वरुणा हे वरुणौ ॥ इतरेतरयोगादुभयत्र द्विवचनप्रयोगः । वरुणेत्यत्र संहितायां ह्रस्वश्चांदसः ॥ नां युवाभ्यां यो यजमानस्त्मन्
> आत्मनैव दाशति हवींषि ददाति स इत् स एव सुदानुः शोभनदानो भवति । स्ववान्
> धनवांश्च ऋतावान् यज्ञवांश्च भवति । किंचॆ स दास्वान् दानवान् द्विषो
> द्वेष्टुरिषान्नेन जयलच्छेन सह तरेत् । प्राप्येत् । अपि च रयिं धनं रयिवतो
> धनवतो जनान् पुत्रांश्च वंसत् । संभजेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, both addressed in the dual. Whichever sacrificer, of his own accord (त्मन् (*tman*)), offers (दाशति (*dāśati*), that is, gives) oblations to you two, he alone (स इत् (*sa it*)) becomes सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*), of fine giving. He becomes स्ववान् (*svavān*), wealthy, and ऋतावान् (*ṛtāvān*), possessed of sacrifice. Moreover, he, दास्वान् (*dāsvān*), the giver, with food (इषा (*iṣā*)) won by victory from the hater (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)) would cross over, that is, attain. And also he would obtain (वंसत् (*vaṃsat*), that is, share) wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)), and sons and people who are wealthy (रयिवतः (*rayivataḥ*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- वां (*vāṃ*)—addressing you
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- त्मन् (*tman*)—of his own accord
- दाशति (*dāśati*)—offers oblations
- स इत् (*sa it*)—he alone
- सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)—becomes an excellent giver
- स्ववान् (*svavān*)—wealthy
- ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*)—and possessed of sacrifice
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- दास्वान् (*dāsvān*)—being generous
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—of the enemy
- इषा (*iṣā*)—united with food
- तरेत् (*taret*)—will cross over hardships
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- रयिवतः (*rayivataḥ*)—possessed of wealth
- जनान् च (*janān ca*)—and sons also
- वंसत् (*vaṃsat*)—will obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, whichever sacrificer, addressing you, offers oblations of his own accord, he alone becomes an excellent giver, wealthy and possessed of sacrifice.

### Printed p. 504

He, being generous, obtains food won from his enemies and is delivered from hardship. He obtains wealth and sons possessed of wealth.

##### English translation
He who spontaneously presents you, Indra and Varuna (oblatious), is liberal, wealthy and upright: he shall prosper with the food of his adversary, and possess riches, and opulent descendants.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं यु॒वं दा॒श्व॑ध्वराय देवा र॒यिं ध॒त्तो वसु॑मंतं  ॒
> पुरुक्षुं ।  
> अ॒स्मे स इं॑द्रावरुणा॒वपि॑ ष्वा॒त्र यो भ॒नक्ति॑ व॒नुषा॒मश॑स्तीः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । युवं । दाशुअध्वराय । देवा । रयिं । धत्थः । वसुमंतं । पुरुक्षुं ।  
> अस्मे इति । सः । इंद्रावरुणौ । अपि । स्यात् । प्र । यः । भनक्ति । वनुषां । अशस्तीः ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा देवौ स्तूयमानौ हे इंद्रावरुणौ युवं युवां दाश्वध्वराय
> दत्तहविष्काय वसुमंतं धनानुबंधिनं पुरुक्षुं बह्वन्नं पूर्णयशस्वं वा यं
> यादृशं रयिं धनं धत्थः प्रयच्छथः । योऽपि च वनुषां हिंसकानामशस्तीरकीर्तिः । शत्रुकृतान्ययशांसीत्यर्थः । प्र भनक्ति प्ररुजति स तादृशो रयिरस्मे
> अस्मासु स्यात् । भूयात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two, who are praised (देवा (*devā*), the two gods), to the sacrificer who has given the oblation (दाश्वध्वराय (*dāśvadhvarāya*)), you bestow (धत्थः (*dhatthaḥ*), that is, give) such wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) as is वसुमंतं (*vasumaṃtaṃ*), accompanied by riches, and पुरुक्षुं (*purukṣuṃ*), abundant in food or full of fame. And that which breaks (प्र भनक्ति (*pra bhanakti*), that is, shatters) the ill-fame (अशस्तीः (*aśastīḥ*)) of the harming enemies (वनुषां (*vanuṣāṃ*)), the meaning being the dishonours wrought by foes, may such wealth be in us (अस्मे (*asme*), that is, in us).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवा (*devā*)—you who are divine in nature
- इंद्रावरुणौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇau*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you
- दाश्वध्वराय (*dāśvadhvarāya*)—to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which
- वसुमंतं (*vasumaṃtaṃ*)—accompanied by riches
- पुरुक्षुं (*purukṣuṃ*)—abundant food
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—and wealth
- धत्थः (*dhatthaḥ*)—you give, those, and
- यः अपि (*yaḥ api*)—which riches and the like
- वनुषां (*vanuṣāṃ*)—of harming enemies
- अशस्तिः (*aśastiḥ*)—the ill-fame
- प्र भनक्ति (*pra bhanakti*)—destroy
- सः (*saḥ*)—such wealth
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- स्यात् (*syāt*)—may it be full

### Printed p. 505

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, divine in nature, the food accompanied by riches and abundant, and the wealth, which you give to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation, those, and such wealth and the like as destroys the ill-fame of harming enemies, may it be full in us.

##### English translation
May that opulence comprising treasure and abundant food, which
you bestow, deities, upon the donor (of the oblation), that, Indra and
Varuna, which baffles the calumnies of the malevolent, be ours.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नः॑ सुत्रा॒त्रो दे॒वगो॑पाः सू॒रिभ्य॑ इंद्रावरुणा र॒यिः  ॑
> ष्यात् ।  
> येषां॒ शुष्मः॒ पृत॑नासु सा॒ह्वान् स॒द्यो द्यु॒म्ना ति॒रते॒  ॑
> ततुरिः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । सुत्रात्रः । देवगोपाः । सूरिभ्यः । इंद्रावरुणा । रयिः । ष्यात् ।  
> येषां । शुष्मः । पृतनासु । साह्वान् । प्र । सद्यः । द्युम्ना । तिरते । ततुरिः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि चंद्रावरुणा हे इंद्रावरुणौ सूरिभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो नोऽस्मभ्यं
> सुत्रात्रः सुरक्षो देवगोपाः । देवा गोपा गोप्तारो यस्य स तथाविधः ।
> रयिर्धनं स्यात् । भूयात् । किंच येषामस्माकं शुष्मो बलं पृशनासु
> युद्धेषु साह्वान् शक्रूणामभिभविता ततुरिर्हिंसकश्च सन् द्युम्ना यशांसि सद्य
> एव प्र तिरते सम्यक्तिरस्कुर्यात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And also, O Indra and Varuṇa, to us, the praisers (सूरिभ्यः (*sūribhyaḥ*)), may wealth be सुत्रात्रः (*sutrātraḥ*), well guarded, and देवगोपाः (*devagopāḥ*), that is, of which the gods are the guardians. Moreover, ours, whose strength (शुष्मो (*śuṣmo*)) in battles, being the overcomer of enemies and a destroyer, would at once completely overshadow (प्र तिरते (*pra tirate*)) the glories (द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*), that is, the fames) of those enemies. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- येषां (*yeṣāṃ*)—whose, ours
- शुष्कः (*śuṣkaḥ*)—the strength
- पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)—in battles
- साह्वान् (*sāhvān*)—defeats enemies

### Printed p. 506

- ततुरिः (*taturiḥ*)—and being the destroyer of enemies
- द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*)—all their fame
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once
- प्र तिरते (*pra tirate*)—completely covers, such
- सूरिभ्यः (*sūribhyaḥ*)—to the praisers
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सुत्रात्रः (*sutrātraḥ*)—well protected
- देवगोपाः (*devagopāḥ*)—and guarded by the gods
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—wealth
- स्यात् (*syāt*)—may be obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, may wealth, well protected and guarded by the gods, be obtained by us, the praisers, whose strength in battles defeats enemies and destroys them and at once completely covers all their fame.

##### English translation
May that opulence, Indra and Varuna, which is a sure defence, and of which the gods are the guardians, be ours, celebrating your praise, whose destroying prowess in battles victorious (over foes) speedily obscures (their) fame.

> इत्था । गृणंतः । महिनस्य । शर्धः । अपः । न । नावा । दुःऽइता । तरेम ॥ ८ ॥

> हे इंद्रावरुणेंद्रावरुणौ गृणाना स्तूयमानौ युवां नोऽस्मभ्यं
> सौश्रवसाय । सुश्रवसो भावः सौश्रवसं । तस्यॆ सुश्रवस्त्वाय रयिं धनं नु क्षिप्रं
> पृंकं । प्रयच्छतं । किंच हे देवा देवौ महिनस्य महतोर्युवयोः शर्धो

> तरेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two who are praised (गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)), to us, for good fame (सौश्रवसाय (*sauśravasāya*), that is, the state of having good fame), quickly (नु (*nu*)) bestow (पृंकं (*pṛṃkaṃ*), that is, give) wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)). Moreover, O gods, the strength (शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)) of you two, the great (महिनस्य (*mahinasya*)), thus praising it, we would cross the evils (दुरिता (*duritā*)) as one crosses waters by a boat.

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)—you who are praised by us

- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- पृज्ञं (*pṛjñaṃ*)—give
- देवा (*devā*)—O divine ones
- नावा (*nāvā*)—by a boat
- अपो न (*apo na*)—as one crosses water
- महिनस्य (*mahinasya*)—of you who are great
- शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)—the strength
- इत्या (*ityā*)—in this manner

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, you who are praised by us, quickly give us wealth for the gaining of excellent happiness. O divine ones, praising in this manner the strength of you who are great, may we cross our sins as one crosses water by a boat.

##### English translation
Divine and glorified Indra and Varuna, quickly bestow upon us wealth for our felicity ; and thus eulogising the strength of you two, mighty (deities), may we pass over all difficulties as (we cross) the waters with a boat.

> हे स्तोतः सम्राज अज्ञया राज्ञां शासकाय बृहते परिवृढाय देवाय
> द्योतमानाय वरुणाय प्रियं मनोहरं सप्रथः सर्वतः पृथु । तथा च यास्कः ।
> सप्रथाः सर्वतः पृथुः । नि. ६-७ । इति । मन्म स्तोत्रं नु आद्य प्रार्थ । प्रोच्चारय ।

> विस्तीर्णे द्यावापृथिव्य विभाति विभासयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, to Varuṇa, the सम्राज (*samrāja*), the ruler of kings by his command; बृहते (*bṛhate*), the great, the grown; देवाय (*devāya*), the shining; recite now a hymn (मन्म (*manma*), a praise) that is प्रियं (*priyaṃ*), pleasing, and सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*), broad on every side. So Yāska: सप्रथाः सर्वतः पृथुः (*saprathāḥ sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*) (Ni. 6-7) **GLOSS**. This Varuṇa who, endowed with greatness (महिना (*mahinā*)), महिव्रतः (*mahivrataḥ*), of great works, and endowed with insight (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) and with radiance (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)), and as one free from old age, illumines (विभाति (*vibhāti*)) the two wide worlds, heaven and earth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः आयं (*yaḥ āyaṃ*)—this same Varuṇa who
- महिना (*mahinā*)—united with his greatness
- महिव्रतः (*mahivrataḥ*)—possessed of great works
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—endowed with insight
- अजरो न (*ajaro na*)—and free from decay
- उर्वि (*urvi*)—the wide heaven and earth
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with his radiance
- विभाति (*vibhāti*)—causes to shine, such
- सम्राजे (*samrāje*)—the universal ruler
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—the grown
- देवाय (*devāya*)—and the shining
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to Varuṇa
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—pleasing
- सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*)—and extensive
- मन्म (*manma*)—a hymn
- नु (*nu*)—at once
- प्र अर्च (*pra arca*)—recite and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, this same Varuṇa who, united with his greatness, possessed of great works, endowed with insight and free from decay, causes both the wide heaven and earth to shine with his radiance: to that universal ruler, the grown, the shining Varuṇa, at once recite and worship with a hymn that is pleasing and extensive.

##### English translation
Repeat acceptable and all-comprehensive praise to the imperial mighty divine Varuna, he who, endowed with greatness. with wisdom, and with splendour, illumes the spacious (heaven and earth).

> यु॒वो रथो॑ अध्व॒रं दे॒ववी॑तये॒ प्रति॒ स्वस॑र॒मुप॑ याति  ॒॑
> पीतये ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 509

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवोः । रथः । अध्वरं । देववीतये । प्रति । स्वसरं । उप । याति । पीतये॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रावरुणा हे इंद्रावरुणौ सुतपौ सुतस्य सोमस्य पातारौ युवां
> मद्यं मदकरं सुतमभिषुतमिमं सोमं पिबतं । किंच हे धृतव्रता धृतकर्माणौ
> युवोर्युववयो रथोऽध्वरमुद्दिश्य देववीतये! देवानां पानार्थं पीतये
> युवयोरपि सोमपानार्थं स्वसरं मार्गं प्रत्युप याति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, सुतपौ (*sutapau*), drinkers of the pressed Soma, drink this pressed Soma, the intoxicating (मद्यं (*madyaṃ*), that which gladdens). Moreover, O धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*), upholders of rites, your chariot comes along the road (स्वसरं (*svasaraṃ*), the way) towards the sacrifice, for the drinking (देववीतये (*devavītaye*)) of the gods, and also for the drinking of the Soma by you two (पीतये (*pītaye*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रा वरुणा (*iṃdrā varuṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- सुतपा (*sutapā*)—you who drink the pressed Soma
- मद्यं (*madyaṃ*)—that which satisfies
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—and has been pressed
- इमं सोमं (*imaṃ somaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink
- धृतव्रता (*dhṛtavratā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa, upholders of rites
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—your
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—chariot
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- देववीतये (*devavītaye*)—for the drinking of the gods
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—and for your drinking
- स्वसरं प्रति (*svasaraṃ prati*)—following the road of the sacrifice
- उप याति (*upa yāti*)—comes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, you who drink the pressed Soma, drink this Soma juice that is satisfying and has just been pressed. O Indra and Varuṇa, upholders of rites, your chariot comes following the road of the sacrifice, for the drinking of the gods and for your drinking.

##### English translation
Indra and Varuna, observant of holy duties, drinkers of the Soma juice, drink this exhilarating effused libation: your chariot approaches along the road to the sacrifice, (that you may partake) of the food of the gods, aud drink (the Soma).

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑वरुणा॒ मधु॑मत्तमस्य॒ वृष्णः॒ सोम॑स्य वृष॒णा वृ॑षेथां ।  
> इ॒दं वा॒मंधः॒ परि॑षिक्तम॒स्मे आ॒सद्या॒स्मिन्ब॒र्हिषि॑ मादयेथां॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रावरुणा । मधुमत्कतमस्य । वृष्णः । सोमस्य । वृषणा । आ । वृषेथां ।  
> इदं । वां । अंधः । परिसिक्तं । अस्मे इति । आसद्य । अस्मिन् । बर्हिषि । मादयेथां॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रावरुणा हे इंद्रावरुणौ वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारौ युवां
> मधुमत्तमस्यातिशयेन मधुमंतं रसवंतं वृष्णो वर्षितारं सोमस्य
> सोममा वृषेथां । अश्नीतं । तथा च शतपथब्राह्मणं । यथाभागमावृषायध्वमिति यथाभागमश्नीतेत्येवैतदाह । २-४-२-२० । इति । नां युवयोरर्थ
> इदमंधः सोमरूपमन्नमस्मे आस्माभिः परिषिक्तं पात्रेषु । आत आसद्योपविश्यास्मिन्बर्हिषि यज्ञे मादयेथां सोमपान इति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*), showerers of desires, partake (आ वृषेथां (*ā vṛṣethāṃ*), that is, eat) of the Soma, the sweetest (मधुमत्तमस्य (*madhumattamasya*), exceedingly sweet and full of juice), the showerer (वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)). So the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa: यथाभागमावृषायध्वमिति यथाभागमश्नीतेत्येवैतदाह । (*yathābhāgamāvṛṣāyadhvamiti yathābhāgamaśnītetyevaitadāha |*) (2-4-2-20) **GLOSS**. For you two this food (अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)), in the form of Soma, has been poured round (परिषिक्तं (*pariṣiktaṃ*)) into the vessels by us. Then, having sat down on this sacred grass at the sacrifice, may you be exhilarated, that is, at the Soma drinking; this is the remainder to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—you, showerers of desires
- मधुमत्तमस्य (*madhumattamasya*)—of the most sweet
- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—and juicy
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- आ वृषेथां (*ā vṛṣethāṃ*)—partake
- वां (*vāṃ*)—for you
- इदं अंधः (*idaṃ aṃdhaḥ*)—this Soma juice
- अस्मे (*asme*)—by us
- परिषिक्तं (*pariṣiktaṃ*)—has been filled into the vessel
- अस्मिन् बर्हिषि (*asmin barhiṣi*)—on this seat of darbha grass
- आसद्य (*āsadya*)—sitting down
- मादयेधां (*mādayedhāṃ*)—be satisfied

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, you who shower desires, partake of the Soma juice that is exceedingly sweet and juicy. For you this Soma juice has been filled into the vessel by us. Sitting down on this seat of darbha grass, be satisfied.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra and Varuna, showerers (of benefits), of the most sweet
soma the shedder (of blessings): this, your beverage, is poured forth by
us: sitting on the sacred grass, be exhilarated (by the draught).

## Sūkta 69 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सं वां कर्मणेत्यष्टर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रावैष्णवं । अनुक्रम्यते च । सं वामष्टावैंद्रावैष्णवमिति ॥ उक्ते तृतीयसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्र्यते हि । सं वां कर्मणेंद्राविष्णू मदपती
> मदानामिति याज्ञा । आ. ६-१ । इति ॥ सोमातिरेके प्रातःसवने नैमित्तिके शस्त्रे
> परिहिते सति गाणगारिमते सं वामिति तस्य शस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । ऐंद्रावैष्णव्येति
> गाणगारिद्वैवतप्रधानत्वात्सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमि । आ. ६-७ । इति ॥
> सोमातिरेके माध्यंदिनसवने या विश्वासामित्येषा शस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । या
> विश्वासां जनितारा मतीनामिति याज्ञा । अ. ६-७ । इति ॥ उक्ते तृतीयसवनेच्छावाकस्येंद्राविष्णू मदपती इति शस्त्रयाज्या । सूत्रं तूदाहृतं ॥ तृतीयसवनेच्छावाकस्येंद्राविष्णू पिबतमिति प्रस्थितयाज्या । सूत्रितं च । इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं
> मध्वो अस्येमं स्तोममर्हते जातवेदसे । आ. ५-५ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning सं वां कर्मणा (*saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā*) has eight ṛks and is the eighth sūkta. Bharadvāja is its seer, the metre is Triṣṭubh, and the deity is Indra and Viṣṇu. So it is given in the Anukramaṇikā: सं वामष्टावैंद्रावैष्णवमिति (*saṃ vāmaṣṭāvaiṃdrāvaiṣṇavamiti*) **GLOSS**. In the ukthya rite, at the third pressing, this sūkta is used in the śastra of the Acchāvāka. It is laid down: सं वां कर्मणेंद्राविष्णू मदपती मदानामिति याज्ञा (*saṃ vāṃ karmaṇeṃdrāviṣṇū madapatī madānāmiti yājñā*) (Ā. 6-1) **GLOSS**. When there is an excess of Soma and, at the morning pressing, an occasional śastra has been set aside, then, according to the view of Gāṇagāri, the ṛk सं वां (*saṃ vāṃ*) is its śastra yājyā. It is laid down: ऐंद्रावैष्णव्येति गाणगारिद्वैवतप्रधानत्वात्सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमि (*aiṃdrāvaiṣṇavyeti gāṇagāridvaivatapradhānatvātsaṃ vāṃ karmaṇā samiṣā hinomi*) (Ā. 6-7) **GLOSS**. When there is an excess of Soma at the midday pressing, the ṛk या विश्वासां (*yā viśvāsāṃ*) is the śastra yājyā. It is laid down: या विश्वासां जनितारा मतीनामिति याज्ञा (*yā viśvāsāṃ janitārā matīnāmiti yājñā*) (A. 6-7) **GLOSS** **NOTE**. In the ukthya, at the third pressing, for the Acchāvāka the ṛk इंद्राविष्णू मदपती (*iṃdrāviṣṇū madapatī*) is the śastra yājyā; the sūtra has been quoted above. At the third pressing, for the Acchāvāka, the ṛk इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं (*iṃdrāviṣṇū pibataṃ*) is the prasthita yājyā. It is laid down: इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्वो अस्येमं स्तोममर्हते जातवेदसे (*iṃdrāviṣṇū pibataṃ madhvo asyemaṃ stomamarhate jātavedase*) (Ā. 5-5) **GLOSS**.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta सं वां कर्मणा (*saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā*) is the eighth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta; Indra and Viṣṇu are the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: सं वामष्टावैंद्रावैष्णवं (*saṃ vāmaṣṭāvaiṃdrāvaiṣṇavaṃ*) **GLOSS**. At the time of the third pressing of the sacrifice called Ukthya, this sūkta is to be recited among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra सं वां कर्मणेंद्राविष्णू मदपती मदानामिति याज्या (*saṃ vāṃ karmaṇeṃdrāviṣṇū madapatī madānāmiti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-1) **GLOSS**. On the occasion when, at the time of the morning pressing, on account of an excess of Soma, the śastra mantras are to be recited, the ṛk सं वां (*saṃ vāṃ*) is to be recited as the śastra yājyā mantra according to the view of the teacher called Gāṇagāri; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra ऐंद्रावैष्णव्येति गाणगारिद्वैवतप्रधानत्वात् सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमि (*aiṃdrāvaiṣṇavyeti gāṇagāridvaivatapradhānatvāt saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā samiṣā hinomi*) (Ā. 6-7) **GLOSS**. Likewise at the time of the midday pressing also, on account of an excess of Soma, the second ṛk, या विश्वासां (*yā viśvāsāṃ*), is to be recited as the śastra yājyā mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra या विश्वासां जनितारा मतीनामिति याज्या (*yā viśvāsāṃ janitārā matīnāmiti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-7) **GLOSS**. In the ukthya sacrifice also, at the time of the third pressing, the third ṛk, इंद्राविष्णू मदपती (*iṃdrāviṣṇū madapatī*), is to be recited by the priest called Acchāvāka as the śastra yājyā mantra; this is said in the sūtra above. And at the time of the third pressing the seventh ṛk, इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं (*iṃdrāviṣṇū pibataṃ*), is to be recited by the priest called Acchāvāka as the prasthita yājyā mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra

इंद्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्वो अस्येमं स्तोममर्हते जातवेदसे (*iṃdrāviṣṇū pibataṃ madhvo asyemaṃ stomamarhate jātavedase*) (Ā. 5-5) **GLOSS**.

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 69 **NOTE**
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 1; Varga 13
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 8

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं वां॒ कर्म॑णा॒ समि॒षा हि॑नो॒मींद्रा॑विष्णू॒ अप॑सस्पा॒रे  ॒
> अस्य ।  
> जु॒षेथां॑ य॒ज्ञं द्रवि॑णं च धत्त॒मरि॑ष्टैर्नः प॒थिभिः॑ पा॒रयं॑ता ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । वां । कर्मणा । सं । इषा । हिनोमि । इंद्राविष्णू इति । अपसः । पारे । अस्य ।  
> जुषेथां । यज्ञं । द्रविणं । च । धत्तं । अरिष्टैः । नः । पथिभिः । पारयंता ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राविष्णू नां युवां कर्मणा स्तोत्रेणेषा हविषा च सं हिनोमि ।
> सम्यक् प्रेरयामि । अपसः कर्मणोऽस्योक्तस्य पारे समाप्ता यज्ञं जुषेथां ।
> सेवेथां । किंचारिष्टैरनुपद्रवैः पथिभिर्मार्गैर्नोऽस्मान्पारयंता पारं नयंतौ
> युवां द्रविणं धनं धत्तं । अस्मभ्यं दत्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Viṣṇu, I well impel you two (सं हिनोमि (*saṃ hinomi*), that is, I urge duly) with the rite (कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*), the praise) and with the oblation (इषा (*iṣā*)). At the end (पारे (*pāre*)), at the completion, of this work (अपसः (*apasaḥ*), the rite) that has been recited, enjoy (जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*), that is, be served by) the sacrifice. Moreover, leading us across (पारयंता (*pārayaṃtā*), taking us to the further shore) by safe paths (अरिष्टैः (*ariṣṭaiḥ*), free from disturbance), bestow (धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*), give) wealth (द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)) on us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*)—with the rite in the form of praise
- इषा (*iṣā*)—and with the oblation
- सं हिनोमि (*saṃ hinomi*)—I worship

- अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—of my rite (and)
- अस्य (*asya*)—of the recitation of this ukta mantra
- पारे (*pāre*)—at the end
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*)—enjoy
- अरिष्टैः (*ariṣṭaiḥ*)—free from harm
- पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)—by paths
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पारयंता (*pārayaṃtā*)—lead and show us the shore
- द्रविणं च (*draviṇaṃ ca*)—wealth also
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu, I worship you with the rite in the form of praise and with the oblation. At the end of my rite and of this recitation of the ukta mantra, enjoy the sacrifice. Lead us by paths free from harm. And without trouble show us the shore. Give us wealth.

##### English translation
I earnestly propitiate you, Indra and Vishnu, by worship and (sacrificial) food : upon the completion of the rite, accept the sacrifice, and grant us wealth, conducting us by safe paths.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two well-known Indra and Viṣṇu who are the जनितारा (*janitārā*), generators, of all (विश्वासां (*viśvāsāṃ*)) the मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*), the praises.

### Printed p. 514

> इत्यस्माद्घातोरेव तृचि जनिता मंत्र इति निपातनाण्णिलोपः ॥ कलशा कलशौ
> सोमधाना सोमस्य निधानभूतौ च स्यातां । अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । हे इंद्राविष्णू
> वां युवां शस्यमाना उच्चार्यमाणाः शस्त्ररूपा गिरो वाचः प्रावंतु ।
> प्राप्नुवंतु । अर्कैः स्तोतृभिर्गीयमानासो गीयमानाः स्तोमासः स्तोमाः
> स्तोत्राणि च प्रावंतु । प्राप्नुवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the two also be कलशा (*kalaśā*), vessels, and सोमधाना (*somadhānā*), receptacles of the Soma. Now a direct address: O Indra and Viṣṇu, may the utterances (गिरः (*giraḥ*), the words) in the form of śastras, which are being recited (शस्यमाना (*śasyamānā*)) to you, reach you (प्रावंतु (*prāvaṃtu*), that is, attain). And may the stomas (स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*)), the hymns of praise that are being sung (गीयमानासो (*gīyamānāso*)) by the praisers (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)), reach you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu
- या (*yā*)—you who
- विश्वासां (*viśvāsāṃ*)—for all
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—praises
- जनितारा (*janitārā*)—are the place of origin
- कलशा (*kalaśā*)—and are in the form of vessels
- सोमधाना (*somadhānā*)—in the form of receptacles in which Soma is placed, such
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- शस्यमानाः (*śasyamānāḥ*)—that praise you
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the words of praise
- प्र अवंतु (*pra avaṃtu*)—may they come and reach you
- अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—by the praisers
- गीयमानासः (*gīyamānāsaḥ*)—that are chanted
- स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*)—the stomas also
- प्र (अवंतु) (*pra (avaṃtu)*)—may they come and reach you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the place of origin of all praises and are in the form of vessels, in the form of receptacles in which Soma is placed: may our words of praise that praise such as you come and reach you. May the stomas that are chanted by the praisers also come and reach you.

##### English translation
May the prayers that are repeated to you reach you Indra and Vishnu : may the praises that are chanted reach you : you are the generators of all praises, pitchers recipient of the Soma libation.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑विष्णू मदपती मदाना॒मा सोमं॑ यातं॒ द्रवि॑णो॒  ॑
> दधाना ।  
> सं वा॑मंजंत्व॒क्तुभि॑र्मती॒नां सं स्तोमा॑सः श॒स्यमा॑नास  ॒
> उ॒क्थैः ।

### Printed p. 515

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राविष्टू इति । मदपती इति मदपती । मदानां । आ । सोमं । यातं ।  
> द्रविणो इति । दधाना ।  
> सं । वां । अजंतु । अक्तुभिः । मतीनां । सं । स्तोमासः । शस्यमानासः ।  
> उक्थैः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राविष्णू मदानां सोमानां मदपती स्वामिन् । मदपती इत्यत्र
> मदकब्दोऽनुवादः । द्रविणो द्रविणानि धनान्यपि ॥ द्रविणा उ इति पदद्वयमेकीभूय द्रविणो इति पदं निष्पन्नं ॥ दधाना ददानौ युवां सोममभ्या यातं ।
> मतीनां स्तोतृणां स्तोमासः स्तोत्राण्युक्थैः शस्त्रैः सार्थं शस्यमानास
> उच्चार्यमाणा वां युवामक्तुभिस्तेजोभिः समंजंतु । समर्थयंतु । सं
> समिति द्विरुक्तिरादरार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Indra and Viṣṇu as the lords of the exhilarations, that is, of the Somas; the word "exhilaration" in the compound meaning "lords of exhilaration" is only a restatement. The wealths are the riches that the two bestow. The two of them, bestowing wealth, are to come to the Soma. The hymns of the praisers, the stomas, being recited together with the śastras (the recitations accompanying the uktha), are to anoint you with radiance, that is, to support and strengthen you. The doubling of the prefix expresses regard.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu
- मदानां (*madānāṃ*)—of all the Somas
- मदपती (*madapatī*)—you who are the lords
- द्रविणो (*draviṇo*)—of wealths also
- दधाना (*dadhānā*)—you who hold, you
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—towards the Soma
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—be pleased to come
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—of the praisers
- स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*)—the hymns
- उत्थैः (*utthaiḥ*)—together with the śastra-mantras
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- शस्यमानासः (*śasyamānāsaḥ*)—praising
- अक्तुभीः (*aktubhīḥ*)—with radiances
- सं अंजंतु (*saṃ aṃjaṃtu*)—may they fill and make you grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you who are the lords of all the Somas and lords of wealths also: be pleased to come towards the Soma. May the hymns of the praisers, joined with the śastra-mantras, praise you, fill you with radiance and make you grow.

##### English translation
Indra and Vishnu, lords of the exhilaration, of the exhilarating
juices, come to (drink) the Soma, bringing (with you) wealth : may the
encomiums of the praises repeated along with the prayers anoint you
completely with radiance.

### Printed p. 516
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वा॒मश्वा॑सो अभिमाति॒षाह॒ इंद्रा॑विष्णू सध॒मादो॑  
> वहंतु ।  
> जु॒षेथां॒ विश्वा॒ हव॑ना मती॒नामुप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि शृणुतं॒ गिरो॑  
> मे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वां । अश्वासः । अभिमाति सहः । इंद्राविष्णू इति । सधर्मादः । वहंतु ।  
> जुषेथां । विश्वा । हवना । मतीनां । उप ब्रह्माणि । शृणुतं । गिरः । मे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राविष्णू वां युवामभिमातिषाहोऽभिमातीनां हिंसकानामभि
> भवितारः सधमादः सह माद्यंतोऽश्वासोऽश्वा आ वहंतु । मतीनां स्तोत्थाणां
> विश्वा विश्वानि हवना हवनानि स्तोत्राणि जुषेथां । सेवेथां । तदर्थं मे मदीयानि
> ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि गिरः शस्त्ररूपा वाचश्चोप शृणुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Viṣṇu, your horses, who overcome the hostile harmers (the abhimātis) and who rejoice together, are to bring you hither. Be pleased with, that is, accept, all the invocations, the hymns of the praisers. For that purpose hear my hymns and my utterances in the form of śastras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu deities
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- अभिमातिषाहः (*abhimātiṣāhaḥ*)—that fell the harmful enemies
- सधमादः (*sadhamādaḥ*)—that rejoice together
- अश्वासः (*aśvāsaḥ*)—horses
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—may they bring you
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—of the praisers
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- हवना (*havanā*)—the hymns
- जुषेथां (*juṣethāṃ*)—be pleased to accept
- मे (*me*)—recited by me
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—the hymns
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the utterances in the form of śastras
- उपशृणुतं (*upaśṛṇutaṃ*)—listen and hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu deities, may your horses, which overcome the harmful enemies and rejoice together, bring you. Accept all the hymns of the praisers. Listen to the hymns recited by me and to the utterances in the form of śastras.

##### English translation
May your equally-spirited steeds. Indra and Vishnu the triumphant over enemies, bear you hither : be pleased with all the invocations of your worshippers : hear my prayers and praises

### Printed p. 517
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑विष्णू॒ तत्प॑न॒याय्यं॑ वां॒ सोम॑स्य॒ मद॑ उ॒रु च॑क्रमाथे ।  
> अकृ॑णुतमं॒तरि॑क्षं॒ वरी॒योऽप्र॑थतं जी॒वसे॑ नो॒ रजां॑सि॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राविष्णू इति । तत् । पनयाय्क्यं । वां । सोमस्य । मदे । उरु । चक्रमाथे  
> इति ।  
> अकृणुतं । अंतरिक्षं । वरीयः । अप्रथतं । जीवसे । नः । रजांसि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रादिष्णू वां युवयोस्तत्कर्म पनयाय्यं स्तुत्यं । किं तत्कर्मेत्यत आह । सोमस्य मदे सति यदुरु विस्तीर्णं चक्रमाथे । विचक्रमाथे । यद्यपि
> विष्णोरेव विक्रमस्तथाप्येकार्थत्वादुभयोरित्युच्यते । यच्चांतरिक्षं वरीय
> उरुतरमकृणुतं अकुरुतं । यदपि च रजांसि लोकान् सर्वान् । लोका
> रजांस्युच्यंत इति यास्कः । नोऽस्माकं जीवसे जीवनायाप्रथतं अप्रथयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Viṣṇu, that deed of yours is praiseworthy. What deed? When there is exhilaration from the Soma, you strode widely and far; although the striding belongs to Viṣṇu alone, it is said of both because the two are of one purpose. And you made the atmosphere wider, and you spread out the rajas, all the worlds (Yāska says that the worlds are called rajas), for our life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu deities
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by drinking the Soma-juice
- मदे (*made*)—when exhilaration arose
- उरु (*uru*)—most extensively
- चक्रमाथे (*cakramāthe*)—you strode over the universe
- नां (*nāṃ*)—your
- तत् (*tat*)—that deed of striding
- पनयाय्यं (*panayāyyaṃ*)—is most praiseworthy
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the atmosphere
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—so that it became extensive
- अकृणुतं (*akṛṇutaṃ*)—you have made
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—all the worlds
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—as fit for life
- अप्रथतं (*aprathataṃ*)—you have manifested

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu deities, that deed of yours, that when exhilaration arose from drinking the Soma-juice you strode over the universe most extensively, is exceedingly praiseworthy. You have made the atmosphere extensive. You have manifested all the worlds as fit for our life.

### Printed p. 518

##### English translation
Indra and Vishnu, that (exploit) is to be glorified, by which, in the
exhilaration of the Soma, you have strode over the wide (space): you have
traversed the wide fimameut : you have declared the worlds (fit) for our
existence.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑विष्णू ह॒विषा॑ वावृधा॒नाग्रा॑द्वाना॒ नम॑सा रातहव्या ।  
> घृता॑सुती॒ द्रवि॑णं धत्तम॒स्मे स॑मु॒द्रः स्थः॑ क॒लशः॑ सोम॒धानः॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राविष्टू इति । हविषा । वावृधाना । अग्रआद्वाना । नमसा । रातहव्या ।  
> घृतासुती इति घृतआसुती । द्रविणं । धत्तं । अस्मे इति । समुद्रः । स्थः । कलशः ।  
> सोमधानः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> घृतासुती घृतान्नाविंद्राविष्णू युवां हविषा सोमेन वावृधाना
> वर्धमानावग्राद्वाना सोमाग्रस्य शुक्रस्यात्तारौ नमसा नमस्कारेण रातहव्या
> दत्तहविष्क यजमानैरस्मे अस्मभ्यं द्रविणं धनं धत्तं । प्रयच्छतं । किंच युवां
> समुद्र उदधिरिव स्थः । भवथः । यतः सोमधानः सोमनिधानः कलशो भवथः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Viṣṇu, fed with ghee, you who grow by the oblation, that is, the Soma, who are the eaters of the first, the pure part of the Soma, to whom the sacrificers have given oblations with reverence: bestow wealth upon us. Moreover, you are like the ocean, the sea; for you are a pitcher, the receptacle of the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu deities
- धृतासुती (*dhṛtāsutī*)—you who have food in the form of ghee
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—by the oblation in the form of Soma
- वावृधाना (*vāvṛdhānā*)—who grow
- आग्राद्वाना (*āgrādvānā*)—who eat the first part of the Soma
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with reverence
- रातहव्या (*rātahavyā*)—who have oblations offered
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—wealth
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give
- समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*)—deep like the ocean
- स्थः (*sthaḥ*)—you are
- सोमधानः (*somadhānaḥ*)—in which the Soma is placed
- कलशः (*kalaśaḥ*)—in the form of a pitcher vessel, you are

### Printed p. 519

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu deities, you who have food in the form of ghee, who grow by the oblation in the form of Soma, who eat the first part of the Soma, and who have oblations offered with reverence: give us wealth. You two are deep like the ocean. You are also in the form of pitcher vessels in which the Soma is placed.

##### English translation
Indra and Vishnu, feeders upon clarified butter, drinking of the
fermented Soma, thriving upon oblations, accepting them offered with
reverence, bestow upon us wealth : for you are an ocean, a pitcher, the
receptacle of the libation.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑विष्णू॒ पिब॑तं॒ मध्वो॑ अ॒स्य सोम॑स्य दस्रा ज॒ठरं॑  
> पृणेथां ।  
> आ वा॒मधां॑सि मदि॒राण्य॑ग्म॒न्नु प॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि शृणुतं॒ हवं॑ मे ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राविष्णू इति । पिबतं । मध्वः । अस्य । सोमस्य । दस्रा । जठरं । पृणेथां ।  
> आ । वां । अंधांसि । मदिराणि । अग्मन् । उप । ब्रह्माणि । शृणुतं । हवं । मे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दस्रा हे दर्शनीयाविंद्राविष्णू युवां मध्वोऽस्य मदकरमिमं सोमस्य
> सोमं पिबतं । किंच जठरमुदरं पृणेथां । सोमेन पूरयेथां । हे इंद्राविष्णू वां युवां मदिराणि मदकराण्यंधांसि सोमात्मकान्यन्नान्याग्मन् ।
> अभिगच्छंतु । मे मदीयानि ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि हवं मदीयमाह्वानं चोप
> कृणुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Viṣṇu, beautiful to behold, drink this intoxicating Soma. And fill your belly, your stomach, with the Soma. O Indra and Viṣṇu, may the exhilarating foods, which are Soma in nature, come to you. Do also what concerns my hymns and my invocation.**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दस्रा (*dasrā*)—you who have an attractive form
- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Viṣṇu
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—intoxicating
- अस्य सोमस्य (*asya somasya*)—of this Soma-juice
- पिबतं (*pibataṃ*)—drink

- जठरं (*jaṭharaṃ*)—your belly
- पृणेथां (*pṛṇethāṃ*)—fill yourselves with this juice (O Indra and Viṣṇu)
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- मदिराणि (*madirāṇi*)—intoxicating
- अंधांसि (*aṃdhāṃsi*)—the foods in the form of Soma
- आ अग्मन् (*ā agman*)—may they come near
- मे (*me*)—my
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—hymns
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—and invocation
- उप शृणुतं (*upa śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu, of attractive form, drink this intoxicating Soma-juice. Fill your bellies with this juice. O Indra and Viṣṇu, may the intoxicating foods in the form of Soma approach you. Hear my hymns and my invocation.

##### English translation
Indra and Vishnu, agreeable of aspect, drink of this sweet Soma ;
fill with it your bellies : may the inebriating beverage reach you : hear my
prayers, my invocation.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒भा जि॑ग्यथु॒र्न परा॑ जयेथे॒ न परा॑ जिग्ये कत॒रश्च॒न्नैनोः॑ ।  
> इंद्र॑श्च विष्णो॒ यदप॑स्पृधेथां त्रे॒धा स॒हस्रं॒ वि तद्वै॑रयेथां ॥ ८ ॥

> उभा । जिग्यथुः । न । परा । जयेथे इति । न । परा । जिग्ये । कतरः । चन । एनोः ।  
> इंद्रः । च । विष्णो इति । यत् । अपस्पृधेथां । त्रेधा । सहस्रं । वि । तत् । ऐरयेथां ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राविष्णू उभोभौ युवां जिग्यथुः । शत्रूनजैष्टं । न परा जयेथे ।
> न पुनः कदाचन पराजयेथे । एनोरेनयोर्युववयोर्मध्यॆ कतरश्चनैकशरोऽपि
> न परा जिग्ये । न पराजैष्ट । हे विष्णो इंद्रश्च त्वं च युवां यद्यद्वस्तु प्रत्यपस्पृधेथां असुरैः सहास्पृधेथां त्रेधा लोकवेदवागात्मना त्रिधा स्थितं सहस्रममितं च वि तदैरयेथां । व्यक्रमेथामित्यर्थः ॥ तथा च ब्राह्मणं । उभा जिग्यथुरित्यच्छावाकस्योभौ हि तौ जिग्यतुर्न परा जयेथे न परा जिग्य इति न हि तयोः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you both were victorious: you conquered the enemies. You are not defeated again, ever. Of the two of you, neither one was defeated. O Viṣṇu, and Indra, whatever thing you two contended for with the asuras, standing threefold as world, Veda and speech, and a thousand without measure, that you strode through, that is the meaning. So also the Brāhmaṇa: उभा जिग्यथुरित्यच्छावाकस्योभौ हि तौ जिग्यतुर्न परा जयेथे न परा जिग्य इति न हि तयोः (*ubhā jigyathurityacchāvākasyobhau hi tau jigyaturna parā jayethe na parā jigya iti na hi tayoḥ*)

### Printed p. 521

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कतरश्चन पराजिग्य इंद्रश्च विष्णो यदपस्पृधेथां त्रेधा सहस्रं वि तद्वैरयेथामितींद्रश्च ह वै विष्णुश्चासुरैर्युयुधाते तान् ह स्म जित्वोचतुः कल्पामहा इति ते
> ह तथेत्यसुरा ऊचुः सोऽब्रवीदिंद्रो यावदेवायं विष्णु स्त्रिविक्रमते
> तावदस्माकमथ युष्माकमितरदिति स इमाल्लोकान्विचक्रमेऽथो वेदानथो वाचं
> तदाहुः किं तत्सहस्रमितीमे लोका इमे वेदा अथो वागिति ब्रूयादैरयेथामैरयेथां । ऐ. ब्रा. ६-१५ । इति ॥ यद्वा । तत्सहस्रं गवां सहस्रं त्रेधा
> वैरयेथामित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The passage of the Brāhmaṇa continues: Indra and Viṣṇu fought the asuras, and having conquered them they said, "Let us make an arrangement." The asuras agreed. Indra said, "As far as this Viṣṇu strides in his three strides, that much shall be ours, and the rest yours." Viṣṇu then strode over these worlds, then over the Vedas, then over speech. They ask, "What is that thousand?" One should answer: these worlds, these Vedas and speech. (Ai. Brā. 6-15) **GLOSS** Or else, the thousand is a thousand cows, and the sense is that they strode through it threefold.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उभा (*ubhā*)—you both
- जिग्यथुः (*jigyathuḥ*)—always conquer the enemies
- न परा जयेथे (*na parā jayethe*)—you have never been defeated
- एनोः (*enoḥ*)—of the two of you
- कतरश्चन (*kataraścana*)—even any one
- न परा जिग्यॆ (*na parā jigyè*)—does not suffer defeat
- विष्णू (*viṣṇū*)—O Viṣṇu (you)
- इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*)—and Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—in whatever battle
- अपस्पृधेथां (*apaspṛdhethāṃ*)—you contend with the asuras, in all of them
- त्रेधां (*tredhāṃ*)—that is of three kinds
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—and is without measure
- वि तत् ऐरयेथां (*vi tat airayethāṃ*)—having won the victory, you make a full stride

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Viṣṇu, you both always conquer the enemies. You have never been defeated. Neither of you two suffers defeat. O Viṣṇu, in whatever battles you and Indra contend with the asuras, in all of them, having won the victory that is of three kinds and without measure, you make a full stride.

##### English translation
You have both (ever) been victorious : never have been conquered ; neither of you two has been vanquished : with whomsoever you have contended you have thrice conquered thousands.

## Sūkta 70 (Maṇḍala 6)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धृतवती भुवनानामिति षडृचं नवमं सूक्तं भरद्वाजस्यार्षं जागतं
> द्यावापृथिवीदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । धृतवती षट् द्यावापृथिवीयं

### Printed p. 522

> जागतमिति ॥ अभिप्लविके, पंचमेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र आद्यस्तृचो द्यावापृथिव्यनिविद्धानार्थः । सूत्रितं च । धृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियेंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिरिति
> तृचौ । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥ बृहस्पतिसवेऽपि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र एष स्तृचः । सूत्रितं च ।
> आ. ९-५ ॥ अभिप्लविके तृतीयेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे धृतेन द्यावापृथिवी इति तिस्रो
> द्यावापृथिव्यनिविद्धानार्थाः । सूत्रितं च । धृतेन द्यावापृथिवी इति तिस्रोऽनश्वो
> जातः । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning धृतवती भुवनानां (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāṃ*) has six ṛks and is the ninth sūkta. Bharadvāja is its seer, the metre is Jagatī, and the deity is Heaven and Earth. So it is given in the Anukramaṇikā: धृतवती षट् द्यावापृथिवीयं जागतं (*dhṛtavatī ṣaṭ dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ jāgataṃ*) **GLOSS**. In the Abhiplava rite, on the fifth day, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the first tṛca is used as the nivid-dhāna of Heaven and Earth. It is laid down: धृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियेंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिरिति तृचौ (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyeṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhiriti tṛcau*) (Ā. 7-7) **GLOSS**. In the Bṛhaspatisava also this tṛca is used in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra. It is laid down: (Ā. 9-5) **NOTE**. In the Abhiplava, on the third day, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the three ṛks beginning धृतेन द्यावापृथिवी (*dhṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī*) are used as the nivid-dhāna of Heaven and Earth. It is laid down: धृतेन द्यावापृथिवी इति तिस्रोऽनश्वो जातः (*dhṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī iti tisro 'naśvo jātaḥ*) (Ā. 7-7) **GLOSS**.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta धृतवती भुवनानां (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāṃ*) is the ninth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has six ṛks. Bharadvāja is the seer of this sūkta; Heaven and Earth are the deity; the metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: धृतवती षट् द्यावापृथिवीयं जागतं (*dhṛtavatī ṣaṭ dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ jāgataṃ*) **GLOSS**. In the Abhiplava sacrifice, on the fifth day, at the time of reciting the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, the first three ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as the nivid-dhāna tṛca having Heaven and Earth as deity; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra धृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियेंद्र ऋभुभिर्वाजवद्भिरिति तृचौ (*dhṛtavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyeṃdra ṛbhubhirvājavadbhiriti tṛcau*) (Ā. 7-7) **GLOSS**. In the sacrifice called Bṛhaspatisava also, the above tṛca is to be recited for the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 9-5). And in the Abhiplava, on the third day, when reciting the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, the ṛks 4, 5, 6 beginning धृतेन द्यावापृथिवी (*dhṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī*) are to be recited; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra धृतेन द्यावापृथिवी इति तिस्रोऽनश्चू जातः (*dhṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī iti tisro 'naścū jātaḥ*) (Ā. 7-7) **GLOSS**.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 6; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 70 **NOTE**
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 1; Varga 14
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6
- Ṛṣi: भरद्वाजो बार्हस्पत्यः (*bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ*)
- Deity: द्यावापृथिव्यौ (*dyāvāpṛthivyau*)
- Metre: जगती (*jagatī*)

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> घृ॒तव॑ती॒ भुव॑नानामभि॒श्रियो॒र्वी पृ॒थ्वि म॑धु॒दुघे॑ सु॒सेश॑सा ।  
> द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी वरु॑णस्य॒ धर्म॑णा॒ विष्ण॑भिते अ॒जरे॒ भूरि॑रेतसा ॥

### Printed p. 523

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> घृतवती इति घृतवती । भुवनानां । अभिश्रिया । उर्वी इति । पृथ्वि इति । मधुदुघे इति मधुदुघे । सुपेशसा ।  
> द्यावापृथिवी इति । वरुणस्य । धर्मणा । विस्कभिते इति विस्कभिते । अजरे इति । भूरिS  
> रेतसा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्यावापृथिवी हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ घृतवती दीप्तिमत्यावुदकवत्यौ वा । वनं
> घृतमित्युदकनामसु पाठात् । भवत इति शेषः । भुवनानां भूतानामभिश्रियाभिश्रयणीये भवत इति सर्वत्रानुसंबंधनीयं । उर्वि विस्तीर्णे पृथ्वी बहुकार्यरूपेण प्रथिते च मधुदुघे मधुन उदकस्य दोग्न्य सुपेशसा सुरूपे
> वरुणस्य सर्वस्य नियामकस्य धर्मणा धारणेन विष्कभिते पृथग्धारिते अजरे नित्ये
> भूरिरेतसा बहुरेतस्के बहुकार्ये वा भवतः । अत्र साक्षात् द्यावापृथिव्योः
> स्तुतिप्रसंगाद्वर्णुणस्येति दृष्टव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Heaven and Earth, you two are घृतवती (*ghṛtavatī*), radiant or full of water, for घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*) is read among the names of water. The words "you two are" are to be supplied. You are अभिश्रिया (*abhiśriyā*), to be resorted to by all beings. You are wide and widely known for your many works, and you yield honey, that is, water; you are of fair form. You are held apart by the upholding of Varuṇa, the controller of all; you are unageing, eternal, rich in seed or of many functions. Here, since the occasion is the direct praise of Heaven and Earth, "of Varuṇa" is to be so understood. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृतवती (*dhṛtavatī*)—the two that are full of radiance
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—Heaven and Earth, both
- भुवनानां (*bhuvanānāṃ*)—of all the worlds
- अभिश्रिया (*abhiśriyā*)—being the givers of refuge
- उर्वी (*urvī*)—and having a wide form
- पृथ्वि (*pṛthvi*)—and having wide fame
- मधुदुघे (*madhudughe*)—and milking water
- सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*)—and having an excellent form
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—by the work that upholds the world
- निष्कभिते (*niṣkabhite*)—who attain separate existence
- अजरे (*ajare*)—who are free from decay
- भूरिरेतसा (*bhūriretasā*)—and are of very great vigour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiant Heaven and Earth, both being givers of refuge to all the worlds, having a wide form, having wide fame, milking water, having an excellent form, and, by the work of Varuṇa that upholds the world, having separate existence, are free from decay.

##### English translation
Radiant Heaven and Earth, the asylum of created beings, you are spacious, manifold, water-yiding, lovely, separately fixed by the functions of Varuna, undecaying, many-germed.

### Printed p. 524

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस॑श्चंती॒ भूरि॑धारे॒ पय॑स्वती घृ॒तं दु॑हाते सु॒कृते॒ शुचि॑व्रते ।  
> राजं॑ती अ॒स्य भुव॑नस्य रोदसी अ॒स्मे रेतः॑ सिंचतं॒ यन्मनु॑र्हितं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असश्चंती इति । भूरिधारे इति भूरिधारे । पयस्वती इति । धृतं । दुहाते इति ।  
> सुकृते । शुचिव्रते इति शुचिव्रते ।  
> राजंती इति । अस्य । भुवनस्य । रोदसी इति । अस्मे इति । रेतः । सिंचतं । यत् ।  
> मनुःहितं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> असश्चंती असज्यमाने व्युदस्यंत्या वा भूरिधारे बहुधारे । दिवो
> वृष्टिधाराः पृथिव्याश्चाहुत्युद्भूतरसधाराः । एवमुभयोरपि बहुधारत्वं ।
> पयस्वती उदकवत्यौ । तथा च यास्कः । असज्यमाने इति ना व्युदस्यंत्याविति वा
> बहुधारे उदकवत्यौ । नि. ५-२ । इति । शुचिव्रते शुचिक्रिये द्यावापृथिव्य सुकृते
> शोभनकारिणे यजमानाय धृतं सस्यादिसमृद्धिहेशूदकं दुहाते । अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । रोदसी हे द्यावाप्यथिव्यावस्य भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य राजंती ईशाने
> युवामस्मे आस्मासु रेतः प्रजननसमर्थं वीर्यं सिंचतं । यद्रेतो मनुर्हितं
> मनुष्येभ्यो हितं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two are असश्चंती (*asaścaṃtī*), not clinging, or not falling apart, and भूरिधारे (*bhūridhāre*), of many streams: the streams of rain from heaven and the streams of juice produced by the oblations on earth; thus both have many streams. They are पयस्वती (*payasvatī*), watery. So Yāska says: असज्यमाने इति ना व्युदस्यंत्याविति वा बहुधारे उदकवत्यौ (*asajyamāne iti nā vyudasyaṃtyāviti vā bahudhāre udakavatyau*) (Ni. 5-2) **GLOSS**. Heaven and Earth, pure in their works, milk for the sacrificer who does good works the घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*), the water that brings about the prosperity of crops and the like. Then follows direct praise: O Heaven and Earth, rulers of this world, of all that has come to be, pour into us the vigour, seed capable of generating offspring, which is beneficial to men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- असश्चंती (*asaścaṃtī*)—those who are free from falling
- भूरिधारे (*bhūridhāre*)—who bear many kinds of vigour
- पयस्वती (*payasvatī*)—who are rich in water
- शुचिव्रते (*śucivrate*)—who have pure works and rites, Heaven and Earth
- सुकृते (*sukṛte*)—for the sacrificer who does good works
- घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)—water
- दुहाते (*duhāte*)—they milk
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—O Heaven and Earth
- अस्य भुवनस्य (*asya bhuvanasya*)—of all that has come to be
- राजंती (*rājaṃtī*)—you who are the lords
- यत् (*yat*)—which vigour
- मनुर्हितं (*manurhitaṃ*)—is beneficial to men
- रेतः (*retaḥ*)—that vigour
- अस्मे (*asme*)—in us
- सिंचतं (*siṃcataṃ*)—pour and establish

### Printed p. 525

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and Earth, who are free from falling, who bear many kinds of vigour, who are rich in water and whose works and rites are pure, milk water for the sacrificer who does good works. O Heaven and Earth, you who are the lords of all that has come to be, pour and establish in us that vigour (water or strength) that is beneficial to men.

##### English translation
Uncollapsing, many-showering water-retaining, yielding moisture,
beneficent, pure in act : you two Heaven and Earth, rulers over created
beings, grant us vigour. that may be favourable to (the increase of)
mankind.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो वा॑मृ॒जवे॒ क्रम॑णाय रोदसी॒ मर्तो॑ द॒दाश॑ धिषणे॒  ॑
> स साधति ।  
> प्र प्र॒जाभि॑र्जायते॒ धर्म॑ण॒स्परि॑ यु॒वोः सि॒क्ता विषु॑रूपाणि॒  ॑
> सव्रता ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । वां । यजवे । क्रमणाय । रोदसी इति । मर्तः । ददाश । धिषणे इति । सः ।  
> साधति ।  
> प्र । प्रजाभिः । जायते । धर्मणः । परि । युवोः । सिक्ता । विषुरूपाणि । सव्रता॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धिषणे धृष्टे सर्वस्य भुवनस्य निवासभूते वा हे रोदसी वां युवाभ्यां
> यो मर्तो मर्त्य ऋजवे क्रमणाय युवयोः सुखगमनाय ददात हवींषि
> ददाति स मर्त्यः साधति । कामान् साधयति । किंच प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः प्र
> जायते । प्रवृद्दो भवति । धर्मणः कर्मणः पर्युपरि युवोर्युवयोः सिक्ता
> सिक्तानि रेतांसि विषुरूपाणि नानावर्णानि सव्रता समानकर्माणि भूतानि जायंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*), firm, or the abode of all beings, O Heaven and Earth: the mortal who gives you oblations for your easy, straight course, that mortal accomplishes his desires. Moreover, he is born forth, that is, he prospers, with progeny, sons, grandsons and the rest. Above the rite, the vigours sprinkled by you two, of various colours and of like work, come into being as creatures.

### Printed p. 526

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*)—you who have a firm standing
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—O Heaven and Earth
- वां (*vāṃ*)—for you
- यः मर्तः (*yaḥ martaḥ*)—the man who
- ऋजवे क्रमणाय (*ṛjave kramaṇāya*)—for your easy coming
- ददाश (*dadāśa*)—offers an oblation
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same man
- साधति (*sādhati*)—obtains his desired ends
- प्रजाभिः (*prajābhiḥ*)—with sons, grandsons and the rest
- प्र जायते (*pra jāyate*)—prospers
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—your
- धर्मणः परि (*dharmaṇaḥ pari*)—as the fruit of the upholding work
- सिक्ता (*siktā*)—by the sprinkled vigours
- विषुरूपाणि (*viṣurūpāṇi*)—having many kinds of forms
- सव्रता (*savratā*)—and yet of like work, the beings (creatures) come into being

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Heaven and Earth, you who have a firm standing: the man who, for your easy coming, offers an oblation to you, that same man obtains all his desired ends. He prospers with sons, grandsons and the rest. From the vigours sprinkled as the fruit of your upholding work, creatures that have many kinds of forms and yet are of like work come into being.

##### English translation
Firm-set Heaven and Earth, the mortal who has offered (oblations) for your straight-forwad course, accomplishes (his objects), he prospers with progeny, and invigorated by your operation, many beings of various forms, but similar functions, engendered.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> घृ॒तेन॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॒भीवृ॑ते घृत॒श्रिया॑ घृत॒पृचा॑ घृता॒वृधा॑ ।  
> उ॒र्वि पृ॒थ्वी हो॑तृ॒वूर्ये॑ पु॒रोहि॑ते॒ ते इद्विप्रा॑ ईळते  ॒॒॑
> सुम्ममिष्टये ॥ ४ ॥
